The ULisboa GitHub organization publishes open-source Java libraries focused on Erasmus Without Paper (EWP) data exchange. There is no single self-service commercial API program; most interfaces are open metadata endpoints or affiliation-gated systems.

providers.name: Alkira
providers.description: Alkira delivers Network Infrastructure as a Service (NaaS) through its Cloud Services Exchange, letting enterprises build, deploy, and manage a global multi-cloud network from a unified portal without provisioning physical hardware. The platform connects clouds, sites, remote users, and SaaS through Cloud Exchange Points (CXPs) with built-in segmentation, routing, integrated firewall/security services (Palo Alto, Fortinet, Check Point, Cisco, Zscaler, Infoblox, F5), and full-stack visibility. Everything provisioned in the portal is driven by the Alkira Portal REST API and exposed as infrastructure-as-code via an official Terraform provider, a Go client library, and a published Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents.

providers.name: Beem
providers.description: Beem is a consumer fintech mobile app (trybeem.com) offering instant cash advances of up to $1,000 through its Everdraft feature with no credit check and no interest, alongside personal loans up to $100,000, high-yield savings accounts paying up to 5% APY, AI-powered budgeting, credit building, cashback rewards, identity-theft protection, and insurance products. It supports non-traditional income (gig, freelance, government benefits) and can transfer funds to Cash App or a bank account. Backed by Techstars and used by more than five million people, Beem is consumer-facing and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Bloomberg Media Platforms
providers.description: Bloomberg Media Platforms encompass Bloomberg's digital news and content distribution channels including Bloomberg.com, Bloomberg Businessweek, Bloomberg Markets, Bloomberg Technology, Bloomberg Opinion, and Bloomberg Quicktake. Bloomberg provides news APIs for distributing financial news, market data updates, and editorial content to institutional clients and media partners.

providers.name: Bun
providers.description: Bun is a fast, all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit built by Oven (oven-sh). A single self-contained binary bundles a Node.js-compatible runtime, a package manager (a drop-in, dramatically faster replacement for npm/yarn/pnpm), a native bundler and single-file executable compiler, and a Jest-compatible test runner. Bun is designed as an incrementally adoptable drop-in replacement for Node.js, emphasizing startup speed, install speed, and elegant built-in APIs. It is open source, distributed as a binary via an install script, Homebrew, Docker, and npm, and is surfaced here as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company. Bun exposes no hosted REST API; the CLI and the runtime/bundler APIs are the developer surface.

providers.name: C.H. Robinson
providers.description: C.H. Robinson is one of the world's largest third-party logistics (3PL) providers, offering global freight transportation, supply chain management, customs brokerage, and sourcing of fresh produce. Its Navisphere transportation management system provides end-to-end supply chain planning, purchase order management, execution, freight payment, and business intelligence. C.H. Robinson exposes APIs that allow shippers and carriers to integrate quoting, booking, tracking, documents, and payment workflows directly into their own TMS or ERP platforms.

providers.name: Climeworks
providers.description: Climeworks AG is a Swiss carbon dioxide removal company founded in 2009 as an ETH Zurich spin-off by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher. It designs, builds and operates direct air capture (DAC) plants that filter CO2 out of ambient air through an adsorption-desorption cycle and then permanently mineralize it underground with storage partners such as Carbfix in Iceland - the Orca and Mammoth facilities. Through Climeworks Solutions it also sells risk-mitigated carbon removal portfolios that blend its own DAC removals with certified third-party suppliers, delivered within seven years of purchase and tracked by corporate buyers in an online customer platform. Climeworks is a supplier of carbon removal rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its removals reach programmatic buyers through third-party carbon marketplaces instead.

providers.name: Control4
providers.description: Control4 is a smart home and building automation platform, now part of Snap One / ADI Global (Resideo), headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah. It unifies control of lighting, audio/video, home theater, climate, security, shades, and voice across residential and commercial spaces through a single interface on smartphones, touchscreens, and on-wall keypads. Control4 is delivered through a network of certified integrators rather than direct-to-consumer sales, and interoperates with more than 25,000 third-party devices. For developers it offers the DriverWorks SDK (a Lua-based framework for building device drivers), the Control4 Developer Portal for OAuth application registration against the Control4 cloud, and public first-party libraries on GitHub.

providers.name: Cyberpsyc
providers.description: CyberPsyc Software Solutions, operating as WellTrack Boost (now part of ProtoCall Services), builds self-guided, clinically-supported digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools for behavioral health and wellness. The platform lets users assess and understand their mental health on their own devices and schedule through MoodCheck mood tracking, the Zen Room, a Thought Diary, an Activity Scheduler, Fun and Achievement planning, and guided modules for stress, anxiety, and depression. WellTrack Boost is deployed by college counseling centers and certified community behavioral health clinics, offering institutional single sign-on through a SAML integration surface. No public developer REST API or OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: DistillerSR
providers.description: Behind every new scientific discovery, every new device, every new drug and new policy guideline, there are literature reviews. DistillerSR's software enables customers to securely automate the management of evidence-based research and the analysis of its data faster, more accurately, and more transparently at scale. Leading healthcare research organizations rely on DistillerSR for their literature and systematic reviews.

providers.name: Energy Robotics
providers.description: Energy Robotics GmbH, now trading as Korial, is a Darmstadt, Germany enterprise AI platform (spun out of TU Darmstadt robotics research) for fully autonomous industrial operations. It is hardware-agnostic, unifying mixed-vendor robots, legged and tracked ground robots, drones, fixed cameras, and field sensors into a single governed AI operating layer that turns live telemetry into verified insight and orchestrated action across oil & gas, chemicals, power & utilities, and critical infrastructure. The platform spans four modules: Kore (the AI core with LLM, agentic workflows, embedded AI skills, and fleet/device supervision), Connect (an integration backbone exposing bidirectional governed APIs into ERP, EAM, SCADA, historians and ICS/OT systems), Recreate (digital twins and mission simulation), and Sustain (support, onboarding, and managed mission execution). Korial reports 1,000,000+ autonomous inspections, 100+ global deployments, and named customers including Shell, bp, Repsol, Petrobras, Pluspetrol, Chevron, E.ON, Evonik, BASF, and Merck. Rebranded from Energy Robotics GmbH on 4 May 2026.

providers.name: FastMCP
providers.description: FastMCP is the fast, Pythonic framework for building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, clients, and apps. Originally created by Jeremiah Lowin and maintained by PrefectHQ, FastMCP 1.0 was adopted into the official Anthropic MCP Python SDK in 2024, and the standalone FastMCP project (now at v3) remains the most widely used way to ship MCP servers in Python — the project reports powering roughly 70% of MCP servers across all languages. FastMCP turns ordinary Python functions into MCP tools, resources, prompts, and apps via decorators, auto-generates JSON Schemas from type hints, handles transport negotiation (stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE), and ships first-class OAuth/OIDC authentication, server composition and proxying, OpenAPI/FastAPI import, a CLI for running and installing servers into Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor / ChatGPT / Gemini CLI / Goose, middleware, lifespan management, elicitation, sampling, progress reporting, OpenTelemetry, and a client library and apps runtime for building interactive UIs rendered inside MCP host conversations.

providers.name: Gem
providers.description: Gem is an AI-first recruiting platform that bundles a next-generation ATS, recruiting CRM, AI outbound sourcing, scheduling, talent marketing, application review, and talent rediscovery into a single agentic AI hiring system used by more than 1,200 talent acquisition teams. Gem ships a Chrome extension for sourcing, a public REST API (v0) documented at api.gem.com/v0/reference, an integrations marketplace at integrations.gem.com/gem covering ATS, HRIS, scheduling, assessments, background checks, and job distribution, plus a status page and academy.

providers.name: Leiden University
providers.description: Leiden University (Universiteit Leiden) is the oldest university in the Netherlands, founded in 1575, and ranks #141 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-accessible developer footprint is modest and centered on its libraries rather than a central developer portal. Leiden University Libraries operates an OAI-PMH metadata harvesting endpoint for its Scholarly Publications repository and maintains an active open-source GitHub organization (LeidenUniversityLibrary) with library, Islandora, and IIIF tooling. There is no centrally documented public REST API program; most institutional and student systems are gated behind SSO.

providers.name: Level
providers.description: Level is a stablecoin protocol that issued lvlUSD, a stablecoin fully backed by USDC and USDT which were deployed into blue-chip lending protocols (Aave and the Morpho Steakhouse USDC vault) to generate yield. Lending yield was passed back to holders through an ERC-4626 staking mechanism: lvlUSD could be staked for slvlUSD, a yield-accruing token that appreciates as the protocol distributes yield into the staking contract. Both tokens were transferable and integrated across DeFi venues including Morpho, Pendle, Spectra and Curve, with LayerZero OFT adapters bridging them to Base. Level exposes no public HTTP API — its programmable surface is a set of audited Ethereum mainnet smart contracts (lvlUSD, slvlUSD, LevelMinting, LevelStakingPool, LevelUsdPointsFarm, LevelReserveLens) documented in GitBook and published on GitHub. In September 2025 the team announced it was joining the Sky (fka MakerDAO) ecosystem as part of Grove and that the Level protocol is being sunset: mints paused, redemptions made public and fixed 1:1, cooldowns cut to two seconds, final yield distribution on 2025-10-02, and the front end retired on 2025-12-15 with contract-level redemption remaining available indefinitely.

providers.name: Linte
providers.description: Linte is a Brazilian legal-technology company offering an AI-powered contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform for large enterprises. Its product family spans Linte CLM for document automation and contract lifecycle governance, Linte AI for contract review that summarizes versions and flags risk against a customer playbook, Linte BI for contract analytics dashboards, and Linte Intake for legal demand intake and triage. The platform integrates natively with digital signature providers including ClickSign, DocuSign and D4Sign, and is sold to enterprise legal, procurement and compliance teams primarily in Brazil. Linte publishes no public API program, developer portal or API reference; its only public developer-facing artifacts are npm-published embeddable "Linte Docs" form components.

providers.name: Media Radar
providers.description: MediaRadar (now incorporating the data and capabilities of Vivvix) is a marketing and advertising intelligence platform that tracks advertising investment, creative, and brand activity across streaming and linear TV, digital and programmatic, social, retail media, out-of-home, radio, podcast, and print. It serves brands, agencies, publishers, platforms, and consultancies with competitive, commercial, creative, market, and political ad intelligence used to inform mission-critical marketing and sales decisions. MediaRadar delivers its data through a web UX, data feeds, and a client REST API. The MediaRadar Client API Portal is a private Azure API Management developer portal gated behind client sign-in; API endpoints and schemas are not published publicly, and integrations authenticate with a per-client API Key. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Mythical Games
providers.description: Mythical Games is a Web3 game-technology studio and platform company (an a16z portfolio company) that builds games with player-owned digital items and a secondary marketplace economy. Its business has two sides: consumer game titles (FIFA Rivals, Pudgy Party, Blankos) and the Mythical Platform, a B2B toolkit that lets any game add a secondary economy of tradeable items and currencies. The platform is exposed to integrating studios primarily through gRPC/Protobuf SDKs — the Saga SDK and the earlier IVI SDK — published for Java, C++, and Python, rather than a public REST/OpenAPI surface. The Saga gRPC API covers items, item types, currencies, currency types, listings, offers, player wallets, reservations, an NFT bridge, and metadata, with cursor-based queries and a server-streaming status channel for confirming asynchronous writes. Assets settle on the Mythos chain, a Polkadot/Substrate gaming parachain (MYTH token) whose node software is open source.

providers.name: National Hockey League
providers.description: The National Hockey League (NHL) is the premier professional ice hockey league in North America, comprised of 32 franchises across the United States and Canada. The NHL produces the Stanley Cup playoffs and is one of the major North American professional sports leagues. The NHL does not publish an officially documented developer portal; the league operates undocumented JSON endpoints used by its first-party web and mobile apps (api-web.nhle.com) and provides advanced statistics through NHL EDGE. Commercial data feeds are licensed through SMT, Sportradar, and other approved partners.

providers.name: OneAPM
providers.description: OneAPM (Beijing Blueware Technology / 北京蓝海讯通科技) is a Chinese application performance management and intelligent IT operations vendor founded in 2008. Its product suite instruments applications and infrastructure end to end: Application Insight (server-side, code-level tracing for Java, .NET, PHP, Python, Node.js, Ruby and Go), Browser Insight and Mobile Insight (real user monitoring), Infrastructure Insight and Network Insight, LogInsight for log analytics, Cloud Alert (OneAlert) for intelligent alerting, Cloud Test for performance testing, OneITSM for IT service management, and the Intelligence Insight (I²) AIOps platform. It serves over 60,000 enterprise users across telecommunications, finance, government, transportation, energy and e-commerce, delivered as SaaS or on-premise, and instruments applications via language-specific agents (SDKs) published to npm, RubyGems and a private index.

providers.name: OpenTofu
providers.description: Open-source infrastructure as code tool forked from Terraform, providing a community-driven alternative for provisioning and managing cloud infrastructure using declarative configuration files.

providers.name: Pipe Network
providers.description: Pipe Network is a decentralized storage and content-delivery network built on Solana, marketed as "Firestarter" storage. It offers content-addressed (Blake3) object storage with client-side AES-256-GCM and post-quantum (Kyber-1024 / Dilithium5) encryption, deterministic public URLs of the form /{account}/{hash}, prepaid-USDC billing funded via Solana Pay, and first-party TypeScript / Python / Rust SDKs plus a Rust CLI. The SDKs ship native agent- framework tool adapters (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, Cloudflare AI Workflows, AutoGen, CrewAI) and x402 machine-to-machine payment support. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Playroll
providers.description: Playroll is a global HR platform providing Employer of Record (EOR), contractor management, and global payroll across 180+ countries. It runs local payroll, statutory benefits, and compliance for distributed teams, and offers a partner/enterprise integration surface - native HRIS connectors (HiBob, BambooHR), an "Open API" for bi-directional HR data sync, and custom/embedded integration builds. The developer API is partner- and enterprise-gated; sandbox access and documentation are provided to integration partners rather than published on a public developer portal.

providers.name: Qatar University
providers.description: Qatar University is the national public research university of the State of Qatar, located in Doha, and ranked #122 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is concentrated in QSpace, the university's institutional repository running on DSpace 7.6, which exposes a public OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting endpoint and a public DSpace REST/HAL API for scholarly output and academic records. Most other institutional systems (Self-Service Banner SIS, library discovery, SSO/MFA) are gated behind authentication and do not publish open developer documentation.

providers.name: Quartet Health
providers.description: Quartet Health is a value-based behavioral healthcare enablement and delivery platform that identifies, engages, and connects patients with mental health services across 39 states. It serves health plans, health systems, and community mental health centers with care coordination, patient-to-provider matching, and direct delivery of behavioral health care through its own medical group, focused on whole-person care for individuals with serious mental illness and other behavioral health needs. Quartet was acquired by NeuroFlow. Added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile; the public site exposes no developer or API surface, but does publish a substantive security and compliance program.

providers.name: Runscope
providers.description: Runscope is an API monitoring and testing platform that lets teams create, schedule, and run automated tests against their APIs to catch performance problems, uptime issues, and functional regressions before customers do. Originally an independent, a16z-backed startup, Runscope was acquired by CA Technologies in 2017 and is now delivered as the API Monitoring capability of BlazeMeter (a Perforce company). The product exposes a REST API for managing buckets, tests, environments, and test results, along with scheduled runs, integrations, and real-user Radar monitoring.

providers.name: Self
providers.description: Self (Self Financial, Inc.) is a fintech platform that helps people build credit, savings, and access to cash through a small set of consumer financial products. Its Credit Builder Account pairs a small installment loan with a locked savings deposit and reports on-time payments to all three major credit bureaus; the Self Secured Credit Card requires no credit check, and Rent & Bills Reporting and Self Cash round out the lineup. Self serves several million members and is a Techstars portfolio company. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Subaru of America
providers.description: Subaru of America, Inc. is the United States subsidiary of Subaru Corporation (Japan), headquartered in Camden, New Jersey. SOA sells, services, and supports the Subaru lineup through more than 600 U.S. dealers and operates the MySubaru / STARLINK connected-vehicle platform that powers the MySubaru mobile app, owner portal, remote vehicle commands, safety and security services, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, and dealer integration. None of these surfaces are exposed as a public developer API; all known interfaces are private, OEM-internal, or partner-only.

providers.name: Supafax
providers.description: Supafax is an AI email assistant and autonomous inbox agent from Veriad, Inc. (Y Combinator Winter 2026) that lives inside Gmail and Outlook to proactively manage email and calendar. It drafts context-aware replies in your writing style, auto-labels and prioritizes messages, schedules and books meetings through back-and-forth coordination, answers inbox queries, and runs custom automation rules defined in plain English. Founded in 2025 in San Francisco by Rohan Mahendraker and Anton Muratov, Supafax sells a Professional plan and an Enterprise tier with SSO/SCIM, custom integrations, and dedicated support. It is a consumer/B2B productivity product with no public developer API at this time; its security posture (security.txt, CASA Tier 2, ICO registration, GDPR) is its most developer-relevant public surface.

providers.name: Synop
providers.description: Synop is a software platform for commercial electric vehicle fleet charging and energy management, describing itself as "the operating system for commercial EV fleets." Its hardware- and software-agnostic platform integrates vehicles, chargers, and the grid across the U.S. and Europe, spanning charge management (remote charger control, real-time alerts, EVSE interoperability across 100+ charging station models), energy management (AI-based load and time-of-use optimization, curtailment, demand response, and vehicle-to-grid events), vehicle management (state-of-charge and efficiency via telematics), payment management (billing, driver reimbursement, and transaction reporting), utility management, and SynopLink edge connectivity for site-level operations. Synop cites 500+ MWh under management across 800+ commercial depots. Its API integrations surface live time-of-use rate data and export reimbursement data to accounting and expense systems, though the developer documentation is a password-gated ReadMe admin guide rather than a public developer portal.

providers.name: The Beard Club
providers.description: The Beard Club is a men's grooming and beard-care brand selling beard oils, balms, washes, aftershave, grooming kits, trimmers, and subscription grooming boxes through its Shopify-powered online store at thebeardclub.com. Beyond the consumer storefront, the store is agent-commerce ready: it implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP 2026-04-08) with a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp, a machine-readable /llms.txt and /agents.md, UCP service discovery at /.well-known/ucp, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication, and read-only product and collection JSON endpoints — so AI shopping assistants can search the catalog, build carts, and complete buyer-approved checkouts programmatically.

providers.name: The Vanguard Group
providers.description: The Vanguard Group is an American investor-owned asset manager headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, and is "the largest provider of mutual funds in the world" and the second-largest exchange-traded fund (ETF) provider after BlackRock's iShares. Vanguard manages approximately $12 trillion in assets as of 2025 and employs roughly 20,000 people (the "crew") as of December 31, 2024. The firm was founded on May 1, 1975 by John C. ("Jack") Bogle and is structured as a mutual: "Vanguard is owned by the funds managed by the company and is therefore owned by its customers." Salim Ramji was appointed Chief Executive Officer in July 2024. Vanguard's business spans index and active mutual funds, ETFs, personal advisor services, retirement plan recordkeeping (Vanguard Retirement Plan Services), institutional asset management, fixed income, and a financial-advisor channel served through Vanguard Financial Advisor Services. Vanguard operates across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Despite that scale, Vanguard does not publish a public developer API program — there is no public OpenAPI specification, no SDKs, no CLI, no public webhooks, and no Vanguard-published public RSS feed. Investor, advisor, recordkeeping, and distribution-platform integrations are delivered through authentication-gated portals (investor.vanguard.com, advisors.vanguard.com, institutional.vanguard.com), PDF reporting, brokerage/custodian rails, fund-administrator data feeds, and industry recordkeeping interfaces.

providers.name: Tohoku University
providers.description: Tohoku University is a national research university in Sendai, Japan, founded in 1907 and ranked #107 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on scholarly infrastructure rather than a central developer portal: the TOUR (TOhoku University Repository) institutional repository runs on NII's JAIRO Cloud (WEKO3) and exposes a live OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint for metadata harvesting. The library also operates a public OPAC. No central, self-service API developer portal, open-data platform, or SSO/OAuth client-registration program was found publicly documented; most research-code APIs live in individual lab GitHub organizations.

providers.name: Tremor Video
providers.description: Tremor Video DSP is the demand-side platform originally built by Tremor Video and Tremor International; following the consolidation of Tremor Video DSP and Amobee it is now marketed as the Nexxen DSP, part of the unified Nexxen advertising stack (DSP, SSP, Ad Server and Data Platform). It offers a REST API for programmatic and connected-TV (CTV) advertising operations, letting partners manage advertisers, insertion orders, line items, packages and creatives. The Nexxen DSP API authenticates with OAuth2 client-credentials (client ID and client secret) and is documented publicly through a Nexxen Postman workspace.

providers.name: University of Aberdeen
providers.description: The University of Aberdeen is a public research university in Aberdeen, Scotland, United Kingdom, founded in 1495 and ranked #236 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centred on the Aberdeen University Research Archive (AURA), an open-access institutional repository running DSpace 8 that exposes both a DSpace REST API and an OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata-harvesting endpoint. The university also operates an Elsevier Pure research portal and maintains a verified GitHub organization. No general-purpose public developer portal with course, timetable, or student-information-system APIs was found; integration-style APIs appear to be internal/gated.

providers.name: University of Liverpool
providers.description: The University of Liverpool is a public research university in Liverpool, United Kingdom, a founding member of the Russell Group, ranked #165 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on scholarly and research-data infrastructure rather than a unified developer portal: the EPrints-based University of Liverpool Repository and the DataCat research data catalogue both expose live OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interfaces. No general-purpose public API developer portal, course/timetable API, or self-service API key program was found to be publicly documented at the time of review; most institutional systems (SSO/IdP, student administration, mobile backends) sit behind authentication and are not publicly cataloged.

providers.name: 360 VUZ
providers.description: VUZ (360 VUZ) is an immersive social video platform delivering live and on-demand 360-degree and VR content across sports, concerts, entertainment, celebrities, travel, and master classes. Viewers get exclusive immersive access to top events on mobile, tablet, desktop, and VR headsets including Apple Vision Pro. Founded in the MENA region with headquarters in Riyadh (KAFD) and offices in Dubai, Amman, and Los Angeles, VUZ is backed by 500 Global among other investors. For content partners and creators, VUZ exposes a Creator API (documented via a public Postman collection at creatorapi.360vuz.com) used to publish and manage immersive video. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Actively
providers.description: Actively AI delivers "Intelligence-Led Revenue" — an AI revenue-intelligence platform whose Per-Account Agents work every prospect and customer account 24/7, surfacing next-best-actions and helping go-to-market teams execute them across the full lifecycle. The product spans an Agent Inbox, an Assistant, Watchtower, an API for embedding GTM intelligence into internal tools and workflows, and a hosted MCP server that connects its per-account agents into ChatGPT, Claude, and Cowork. Actively is backed by Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: AiVF
providers.description: AIVF develops AI-powered software for in vitro fertilization (IVF) clinics, embryology laboratories, and patients. Its EMA platform applies computer vision and machine learning to embryo evaluation (AIVF Day-3 and Day-5), genetics, outcomes analytics, and clinic-patient communication to improve embryo selection and IVF success rates, alongside ART Compass by AIVF for fertility-lab benchmarking. AIVF holds a CE mark and names ISO 27001, ISO 27799, ISO 13485, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance; in the US an AI component is an investigational device. AIVF was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API — this profile captures the company's identity, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Apple Safari
providers.description: Apple's web browser available across macOS, iOS, and iPadOS, providing a fast, efficient, and private browsing experience with features like Intelligent Tracking Prevention, iCloud syncing, and web standards support.

providers.name: Bloomberg ESG Products
providers.description: Bloomberg ESG Products provide environmental, social, and governance data, analytics, and scores to help investors assess sustainability risks and opportunities. Bloomberg collects ESG data from thousands of companies globally, offering ESG scores, climate data, green bond data, and sustainable finance analytics through the Bloomberg Terminal and API.

providers.name: Bloomberg Indices
providers.description: Bloomberg Indices are a comprehensive family of fixed income, equity, commodity, and multi-asset benchmark indices used by institutional investors worldwide. The Bloomberg Global Aggregate Bond Index, US Aggregate Bond Index, and related indices serve as key benchmarks for fixed income markets. Bloomberg provides index data, analytics, and constituent information through its Terminal and data delivery platforms.

providers.name: Bloomberg Sustainable Finance Products
providers.description: Bloomberg Sustainable Finance Products provide comprehensive data, analytics, and tools for sustainable investing, green bond markets, ESG integration, and climate risk assessment. Bloomberg serves as a key data provider for sustainable finance markets, offering green bond data, ESG scores, climate analytics, and impact measurement tools aligned with major regulatory frameworks including SFDR, EU Taxonomy, and TCFD.

providers.name: Clara 2
providers.description: Clara is an AI-powered primary care and longevity practice, founded by the team behind Circle Medical and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and A.Capital. Clara pairs deep clinical AI with board-certified clinician review: it securely imports and analyzes a patient's medical records, surfaces health trends, assists with symptom assessment, medication refills, lab ordering, and longevity/biomarker goals, and routes every medical recommendation to a licensed clinician for review and approval before it reaches the patient. The company operates as a fully licensed primary care practice across all 50 U.S. states and is a HIPAA-covered entity. Clara is a consumer telehealth product (subscription plans on askclara.com) and currently publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity, trust, and compliance surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ConverseNow
providers.description: ConverseNow is an Austin, Texas voice AI company, founded in 2018, that builds conversational AI virtual assistants which automate restaurant order taking across high-volume voice channels — inbound phone, drive-thru, SMS, and kiosk. The platform uses large language models to understand natural-language orders, suggest upsells, and confirm items in real time, and it markets an "Order Injection API" that pushes completed orders into restaurant point-of-sale and order-management systems. ConverseNow lists integrations with Brink POS, Fiserv, Focus, ItsaCheckmate, NCR Aloha, Olo, PAR, Qu, Xpient, Adora POS, and Deliverect, and reports processing more than two million conversations per month across national QSR brands. It publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; API access is reached through a sales consultation.

providers.name: Crunched
providers.description: Crunched is an AI Excel analyst for power users in management consulting, investment banking, private equity, and corporate finance. Working as a native Microsoft Excel add-in (Mac and PC) and a companion PowerPoint deck reviewer, it builds fully linked financial models (DCFs, LBOs, cohort and scenario analyses) from plain-English instructions, error-checks entire workbooks, extracts and structures data from PDFs and web sources, formats spreadsheets, and generates client-ready slides with full workbook context. Every edit is tracked with a full audit trail and cited sources. Founded by Philip Borge and Michael Sakowski (ex-McKinsey private equity), Crunched is ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certified and GDPR compliant, and is backed by Y Combinator, First Round Capital, and 20VC. It is distributed through the Microsoft AppSource marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Dayforward
providers.description: Dayforward is a New York-based life insurance technology and services group founded in 2019 by Aaron Shapiro. It owns Commercial Travelers Life Insurance Company (NY-domiciled carrier) and Dayforward Insurance Agency LLC (licensed in all 50 states), and sells income-replacement term life insurance direct to consumers at dayforward.com. Since pivoting to B2B at dayforward.io it licenses Workbench — a SaaS platform covering the full life insurance lifecycle from agent selling and automated underwriting through policy administration and service — plus managed distribution, underwriting and administration services to other carriers and distributors. Workbench is marketed as including "APIs, plug-and-play widgets, single sign-on support, and robust administration tools", but Dayforward publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition or SDKs.

providers.name: Department of Labor
providers.description: The U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) is the federal department that fosters, promotes, and develops the welfare of wage earners, job seekers, and retirees, improves working conditions, advances opportunities for profitable employment, and assures work-related benefits and rights. DOL exposes a portfolio of public APIs and data feeds including the modernized DOL APIv4 served from the DOL Open Data Portal, the Bureau of Labor Statistics Public Data API, the DOL Enforcement Data site, and Data.gov.

providers.name: Disclo
providers.description: Disclo is a workplace-accommodations software platform that powers end-to-end management of ADA, FMLA, and state-leave requests, medical-certification verification, and the interactive accommodation process for employers. The HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant portal automates accommodation workflows and compliance documentation, adds AI-assisted medical-certification review (Disclo Verify) and candidate accommodations for recruiting (Disclo Hire), and integrates with 50+ HRIS and ATS systems. Disclo is a private B2B SaaS company backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst; it operates a secure customer portal (secure.disclo.com) and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. Access is enterprise, demo/sales-led rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Eclypsium
providers.description: Eclypsium is a supply-chain and infrastructure security company that delivers firmware, hardware, and low-level software assurance for enterprise and national infrastructure. Its cloud-based platform continuously scans laptops, servers, network gear, and other devices for firmware implants, rootkits, backdoors, vulnerable components, and integrity drift below the operating system, giving security teams device-level visibility, threat detection, and supply-chain risk management across the hardware and firmware lifecycle. Eclypsium integrates with SIEM, SOAR, and IT workflows and is used to defend against firmware-level attacks, enforce device integrity, and meet supply-chain security and compliance requirements. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and is profiled here in the API Evangelist network. No public self-service developer API is currently published; enrichment captured the company's security, trust, and disclosure posture.

providers.name: F6S
providers.description: The API Design Management Platform powering the world's leading API first companies.

providers.name: Foreman
providers.description: Foreman (foreman.co) is an all-in-one, AI-powered project management and estimating platform built for construction contractors and the trades. It consolidates the full lifecycle of a construction job into one place: AI-assisted blueprint takeoffs and scoped estimates, branded proposals and e-signature, invoicing and online payments with QuickBooks sync, scheduling with critical-path task dependencies, and centralized document management for plans, permits, photos, change orders, and RFI communications. A Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company founded by Nolan Rossi, Foreman aims to keep contractors on the job site instead of behind a desk. As an early-stage product it currently exposes no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched with published company identity and link properties.

providers.name: Geordie AI
providers.description: Geordie AI is an enterprise AI governance platform that gives organizations visibility into and control over the autonomous AI agents deployed across their environments. It discovers agents across code, cloud, endpoints, and SaaS; maps each agent's posture (permissions, tools, MCP connections, and system prompts); provides behavioral observability with continuous audit trails and anomaly detection; delivers risk intelligence mapped to standards such as OWASP, NIST, ISO 42001, and the EU AI Act; and offers Beam, a real-time remediation layer that applies deterministic controls at the agent level. Geordie raised a $30M Series A and is used by enterprises including Xapo Bank, Fitch Group, Synthesia, AlphaSense, Owkin, OakNorth, and A+E Global Media. The company is SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and GDPR compliant. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and General Catalyst and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Geordie publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Guidde
providers.description: Guidde is an AI-powered digital adoption and knowledge-capture platform that turns any on-screen workflow into professional step-by-step video documentation and how-to guides. Its Magic Capture browser extension, desktop, and mobile apps record a process, then AI generates a structured script, an AI voiceover (200+ voices), and an editable walkthrough that teams can translate into 50+ languages and embed wherever work happens. Guidde targets onboarding, customer education, support deflection, and internal process documentation for enterprises, and integrates with tools like Slack, Zendesk, Confluence, Notion, Salesforce, SharePoint, and ServiceNow. Guidde is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Guidde does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: ICAO
providers.description: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations that codifies the principles and techniques of international air navigation and fosters the planning and development of international air transport. ICAO's API Data Service provides 50+ continuously updated APIs covering states, airports, operators, airspace, occurrences, and aircraft, including official reference datasets such as DOC7910 location indicators, DOC8585 operator three-letter codes, and DOC8643 aircraft type designators.

providers.name: JetBlue
providers.description: JetBlue Airways (IATA code B6) is a New York-headquartered low-cost United States carrier flying across the U.S., Caribbean, Latin America and Europe, with hubs and focus cities at JFK, Boston, Fort Lauderdale, Orlando and San Juan. In the travel distribution chain JetBlue sits as an inventory owner that sells through three channels: its own direct consumer surface (jetblue.com, the JetBlue app and the TrueBlue loyalty program), the legacy GDS channel where it files fares, seats and EMDs and settles through ARC in the U.S. and IATA BSPs internationally, and an IATA New Distribution Capability program that reaches agencies through GDS/NDC aggregators, corporate booking tools and online booking platforms. JetBlue publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no downloadable OpenAPI or NDC schema: developer.jetblue.com, developers.jetblue.com and docs.jetblue.com do not resolve, api.jetblue.com answers 404 at every probed path, and the 361-URL public sitemap contains no developer or API page. The only published distribution surface is the travel-agent policy section at jetblue.com/travel-agents, including an NDC program page that states JetBlue supplies NDC API documentation, schema and message samples and certification guidelines to onboarded partners only, after business use-case submission, onboarding and certification testing. Selling JetBlue requires ARC accreditation in the U.S. or IATA accreditation plus local BSP participation abroad; JetBlue states it works with only a few OTAs and is not accepting new applications. Public docs, accreditation required, no self-serve access, and no exit path.

providers.name: Joor
providers.description: JOOR is a New York-based SaaS company (founded 2010) operating a leading B2B wholesale fashion commerce platform and digital marketplace that connects fashion brands with retailers to run their wholesale business end to end. The platform digitizes wholesale buying with online linesheets, lookbooks, virtual showrooms, order management, and the JOOR Marketplace, alongside products such as JOOR Pay (wholesale payments), JOOR Passport (virtual trade shows), and Retail data/analytics. JOOR connects thousands of brands with hundreds of thousands of retail doors globally. Its production platform is fronted by a Kong API gateway and secured with Keycloak-based OpenID Connect authentication; API access is partner/integration-oriented rather than a self-serve public developer program. This profile was enriched from JOOR's live public surface (OIDC discovery, GitHub organization, and status page).

providers.name: Mabel
providers.description: Mabel is a healthcare technology company (Irvine, California; backed by 500 Global) that helps Medicare accountable care organizations (ACOs) enroll and engage beneficiaries. Its platform is a market leader in voluntary alignment, used by roughly one in three ACOs, and spans four core solutions: Voluntary Alignment (campaign execution, response processing, analytics, and compliance auditing for LEAD, ACO REACH, and GUIDE programs), Health Surveys (social determinants of health screenings, NPS, and custom surveys with CMS-formatted reporting), Beneficiary Notifications (compliance notices via email, mail, or SMS with audit-ready tracking), and Letters From Your Doctor (provider-based outreach for enrollment, surveys, and appointments). Mabel is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. No public developer API or SDK surface is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, compliance posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: MagicSchool
providers.description: MagicSchool is an AI platform for K-12 education, used by schools and districts to save teachers time and personalize learning. It offers 80+ AI-powered teacher tools (lesson and unit planning, rubrics, IEP support, differentiation, assessment writing, communication) and 50+ student tools delivered through a moderated, student-safe AI assistant, alongside district-level administration with enterprise controls, data dashboards, and single sign-on. The platform emphasizes responsible AI and privacy for education, and integrates with the major classroom ecosystems (Google, Clever, Canvas, ClassLink, Schoology, Microsoft). MagicSchool is a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio company. No public developer API is offered at this time; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: Meitre
providers.description: Meitre is the leading online reservations, guest, and revenue management platform for the world's top restaurants, with a strong presence across Latin America. It provides a hardware-agnostic, white-label toolkit that lets restaurants manage reservations, availability, waitlists, and guest relationships from a single centralized system. Meitre's algorithms automatically manage table availability by analyzing the setup of each area of a restaurant and demand for each slot, and can require credit-card guarantees to virtually eliminate no-shows. Restaurants pay a fixed monthly fee (no commission), and Meitre exposes a partner integration API at meitre-api.com plus an MCP server for AI-powered natural-language restaurant booking.

providers.name: Nilo Health
providers.description: Nilo Health (nilo.health) is a Berlin-based employee mental health platform that helps businesses support their workforce's mental well-being. Founded in 2019 by Ines Raeth, Catalina Turlea and Jonas Keil, nilo gives teams access to 500+ psychologists for 1:1 video counseling in 50+ languages, alongside self-guided digital programs, group roundtables, and an HR analytics dashboard. It is delivered to employers as a company benefit (SaaS) rather than through a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time. nilo integrates with HR platforms such as Personio and Lano via partner marketplaces, and publishes a trust center citing ISO/IEC 27001. The company is backed by Speedinvest and was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio company.

providers.name: Orum
providers.description: Orum is an AI-powered sales calling and performance platform, marketed as "The Calling Performance System for Sales Teams" and "the AI-powered Live Conversation Platform to supercharge sales activity, connect teams, and drive more revenue." Its products are a parallel Dialer (up to 5 lines on the Launch plan, 10 on Ascend), Salesfloor for virtual co-selling, a Coaching and Enablement suite, Orum AI trained on a claimed one billion-plus sales calls, and Scout, a set of AI data agents. It positions itself as purpose-built for maximizing live conversations and explicitly distinct from the dialers built into CRMs and sales-engagement platforms, integrating instead with Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Salesloft, Gong Engage and Apollo. Pricing is two named plans, Launch and Ascend, both contact-sales with a three-seat minimum and no published figures, plus a free trial capped at 500 dials; AI Coaching and Webhooks are paid add-ons. As of this profiling pass Orum publishes NO public developer surface — no OpenAPI, no API reference, no docs host, no SDKs, no MCP server and no llms.txt (see x-evidence). Webhooks are sold as an add-on but are not publicly documented. It does publish a status page, a trust portal, a responsible-disclosure policy, and SOC 2 Type 2 plus ISO 27001:2022, 27017:2015, 27018:2019 and 27701:2019 attestations.

providers.name: Payform
providers.description: PayForm is a no-code payment form builder that lets creators and small businesses accept one-time and recurring credit-card payments without writing code. Users design customizable checkout forms with flexible fields, run recurring billing with trial periods and setup fees, and deliver digital content such as e-books, videos, and music through a members-only area. It supports 50+ currencies and 30+ languages, connects to the Stripe and PayPal payment gateways, and provides a subscriber self-service portal, Zapier automation to 2,000+ apps, and webhooks for custom integrations. Payform is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Rezonant
providers.description: Rezonant is a London-based product development workspace, founded by former Stripe UK engineering leader Emma Burrows, that captures product intent and carries it all the way through tasks, coding agents, and shipped code. It helps product managers and engineering teams turn product vision into engineering-ready work by connecting to their existing stack (Jira, Linear, GitHub, and docs), shaping intent into buildable tasks, and delivering code while keeping teams in control. Rezonant exited stealth in 2026 with $6M in seed funding from General Catalyst and firstminute Capital. It is offered as a credit-metered SaaS with Free, Business, and Enterprise (SSO/SCIM) plans plus a Chrome extension. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio; the company publishes a product help center but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Rivet Health
providers.description: Rivet Health is a cloud-based revenue cycle management (RCM) platform for healthcare providers, spanning practices, specialty groups, and hospitals. Its software brings together three core modules: Revenue Diagnostics (AI-driven revenue forecasting, real-time reporting, and denial prevention), Payer Performance (contract management, payer benchmarking, and fee-schedule administration), and Patient Pricing (automated patient cost estimates and No Surprises Act Good Faith Estimates). Rivet describes itself as an agnostic platform that integrates with 30+ practice-management systems, EHRs, and clearinghouses — including Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, Veradigm, ModMed, Greenway Health, Nextech, Availity, and Change Healthcare. The company is backed by Menlo Ventures. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation; integrations are delivered through its partner network. Rivet publishes a trust center documenting SOC 2 and HIPAA posture.

providers.name: Scratchpad
providers.description: Scratchpad is an AI-powered workspace for sales teams that sits on top of Salesforce, reducing the friction of keeping the CRM up to date. Reps manage notes, opportunities, tasks, and pipeline from a fast, lightweight interface that syncs everything back to Salesforce, with AI-native sheets and Kanban boards, an AI notetaker and call recorder, automated field updates, executive summaries, and CRM hygiene monitoring. The product connects to Salesforce via API and inherits its permissions and guardrails, and integrates with Slack, Zoom, and Gong. Founded in 2019 by Pouyan Salehi and Cyrus Karbassiyoon in San Francisco, and backed by Accel and Craft Ventures. Scratchpad does not publish its own public developer API; it is a Salesforce-native application. This profile captures its identity, commercial surface, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Slingshot Aerospace
providers.description: Slingshot Aerospace is a space operations intelligence and autonomy (SOIA) company that turns sensing, data fusion, and simulation into operational action for satellite operators, defense, and civil space agencies. Its Portal platform and Developer Suite expose orbital intelligence through APIs — the GSN Data API for near-real-time observations, state vectors, and tracking metrics from the Global Sensor Network and Sovereign Space Object Tracking (SSOT); the Seradata API for global satellite and launch intelligence, mission metadata, reliability history, and operator context; and a forthcoming MCP Insights Server exposing analytics, fusion results, and AI-derived insights from the Agatha AI and TALOS AI pipelines. API access is managed through the Portal with API-key credentials and RBAC, and usage is metered in Slingshot Processing Units (SPUs).

providers.name: Streaming
providers.description: Streaming is a topic catalog of the protocols, platforms, and processing engines used to move and transform real-time, high-volume, often bidirectional data over the network. It indexes the canonical log-structured and broker systems (Apache Kafka, Apache Pulsar, Redpanda, NATS JetStream, AWS Kinesis, GCP Pub/Sub + Dataflow, Azure Event Hubs, Confluent Cloud, StreamNative), the over-the-wire streaming protocols exposed to API consumers (Server-Sent Events, WebSocket, gRPC streaming, GraphQL subscriptions), the change-data capture and connector frameworks that feed them (Kafka Connect, Debezium), and the stream-processing engines that consume them (Apache Flink, Spark Structured Streaming, Materialize, Tinybird, Bytewax, Apache Beam). This topic is distinguished from `events` and `async-apis`: streaming emphasizes real-time, high-throughput, partitioned, and often bidirectional pipes, rather than discrete event envelopes or static contract documents.

providers.name: Subsplash
providers.description: Subsplash is an all-in-one church and ministry engagement platform - custom mobile and TV apps, websites, media hosting and delivery, online giving, and church management (People, Groups, Events, Volunteers). Subsplash publishes a REST developer API (OAuth 2.0, hosted on core.subsplash.com) for programmatic access to media, giving records, people, groups and messaging, and event registrations. Access is gated - full API documentation is released only after submitting the developer documentation-access form, and API credentials (Client ID / Client Secret) must be provisioned by a Subsplash representative on a qualifying paid plan (Pro / Enterprise). Because the documented endpoint surface is behind that gate, the APIs listed here are modeled from Subsplash's public product, support, and integration material rather than transcribed from an open reference, and are flagged endpointsModeled.

providers.name: Superduper
providers.description: Superduper (formerly SuperDuperDB) is an open-source Python framework for building database-integrated AI agents and applications directly on top of existing databases - MongoDB, SQL databases, Snowflake, and Redis - without separate vector stores or ETL. It supports semantic / vector search, RAG, transformer and PyTorch model integration, LLM serving, and distributed ML workflows. The commercial side, Superduper Agents, is an enterprise AI agent orchestration platform for BI and data operations, distributed via the Snowflake Marketplace and self-hosted enterprise installs.

providers.name: Symmetrical
providers.description: Symmetrical.ai is a Polish-British HR and payroll fintech, founded in 2019 in Warsaw with offices in London and Barcelona and backed by Partech. It provides payroll and HR bureau outsourcing plus an HR platform automating wage calculation, digital document management, onboarding, leave and time tracking, and real-time analytics, alongside employee financial wellbeing tools such as earned-wage / salary-on-demand access. Symmetrical is ISO/IEC 27001 certified. The company operates an authentication-gated developer documentation portal (developer.symmetrical.ai) but publishes no public OpenAPI, API reference, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity plus probed security posture.

providers.name: Synchronoss
providers.description: Synchronoss Technologies is a global provider of white-label, operator-branded Personal Cloud and messaging solutions for telecommunications carriers and service providers. Its platform lets subscribers back up, store, manage, and share photos, videos, documents, contacts, messages, and call logs, delivered as a branded cloud experience for operators such as Verizon, AT&T, SoftBank, and BT. Product lines include Personal Cloud, Cloud Insurance, the engageX engagement suite, Advanced Messaging (RCS), and ExpenseNX financial analytics. Synchronoss exposes an API and SDK framework to carrier partners rather than a public self-serve developer portal, so this profile captures the company's public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Tdaycom
providers.description: tday (tday.com) is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) AI platform that turns a software product into on-brand marketing content. It connects to a company's GitHub repository or live website, and on every release automatically produces a launch package — an end-to-end demo video generated from real product flows, feature showcases, and on-brand social graphics and ads — then publishes that creative to social and ad channels and measures how it performs, closing the loop from what a team ships to what it posts. tday operates through the browser like a user, with no SDK embedded in the customer's product, using isolated per-run workspaces, scoped repository access, secure credential storage, and secret redaction. tday exposes a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://tday.com/api/mcp secured with OAuth 2.1 (PKCE, dynamic client registration, RFC 8414 / RFC 9728 discovery), making it the agent-facing surface of the platform.

providers.name: Thomson Reuters
providers.description: Thomson Reuters provides over 137 APIs across legal, tax and accounting, risk and fraud, and trade and supply industries through their global developer portal. APIs cover Westlaw legal research, Checkpoint tax content, ONESOURCE tax software, HighQ document management, Legal Tracker matter management, and risk and fraud solutions including identity verification and adverse media screening.

providers.name: TODO Group
providers.description: The TODO Group is an open community of practitioners under the Linux Foundation who collaborate on best practices, tools, and guidance for running successful Open Source Program Offices (OSPOs). It provides open source tooling including Repolinter for repository linting, the OSPO Landscape mapping OSPO adopters and tools, comprehensive OSPO guides and case studies, and OSPOlogy community programs. The TODO Group serves organizations managing enterprise open source strategies across 120+ member organizations.

providers.name: AccessFintech
providers.description: AccessFintech operates Synergy, a post-trade data and workflow network for capital markets that connects buy-side firms, broker-dealers, custodians, hedge funds, order management systems and vendors onto a shared view of trade, settlement and collateral data. The platform normalizes fragmented data across securities, derivatives and alternatives, detects breaks and exceptions across counterparties, and lets the parties to a trade resolve them collaboratively on a single record instead of by email and reconciliation files. AccessFintech describes Synergy as API-first, with bi-directional integrations, ingestion of JSON, XML, CSV and delimited text over push or pull, and Snowflake-native data sharing on AWS. The API surface is not self-serve: the Synergy application and its GraphQL and REST endpoints sit behind an Okta-backed customer login at login.accessfintech.com, and no public developer portal, reference or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: Alma
providers.description: Alma is a technology-enabled U.S. immigration law firm for companies and individuals, combining licensed immigration attorneys with a platform that learns from every case it files. Alma takes end-to-end ownership of the employment-based immigration process — from initial assessment through approval — across temporary work visas (E-2, E-3, H-1B, L-1A, L-1B, O-1A, O-1B, TN) and employment-based green cards (EB-1A, EB-1B, EB-1C, EB-2 NIW, EB-2 PERM, EB-3). For employers it offers a case-management platform with real-time visibility, LCA/compliance tooling, spend forecasting, SSO, and HRIS/ATS integrations (Workday, ADP, BambooHR, UKG, and more). Alma publishes no public developer API; system integration is delivered through its enterprise plan on SOC 2 Type II infrastructure. This profile was surfaced via VC-portfolio discovery and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Beefy Finance
providers.description: Beefy Finance is a decentralized, multichain yield optimizer platform that allows users to earn compound interest on their crypto holdings through automated vaults and strategies.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health (which also operates as "Clipboard" / Clipboard Works) is a Y Combinator (W17) and Andreessen Horowitz backed healthcare workforce marketplace that connects healthcare facilities with qualified, credentialed professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post open shifts and Clipboard matches them with local nurses, CNAs, caregivers, and allied professionals, handling scheduling, replacement coverage when a worker cancels, credential verification, and payments. The platform serves long-term care, home health and hospice, hospitals, and dental practices, with more than 6,500 workplaces and roughly one million workers across the United States. Clipboard Health is a marketplace/product company rather than an API-first developer platform; it publishes no public product API, OpenAPI, or developer portal, but it does operate an active open-source engineering presence (the ClipboardHealth GitHub organization and the @clipboard-health npm scope) and a published security contact. This profile was surfaced as an a16z / Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health (now branded simply "Clipboard", at clipboardworks.com) is a U.S. healthcare workforce marketplace that connects workplaces — long-term care facilities, home health and hospice agencies, hospitals, dental practices, and travel assignments — with vetted, independent professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post shifts and Clipboard matches, credentials, schedules, and pays qualified workers, with the platform handling documentation, compliance, and instant pay for pros. The company reports serving more than 6,500 workplaces and over a million workers nationwide. Backed by Initialized Capital and IVP, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Clipboard Health publishes no public consumer API; its public developer surface is limited to open-source TypeScript utility libraries on npm (the @clipboard-health scope, from github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils) and a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Cloaked
providers.description: Cloaked is a consumer privacy and identity-protection platform that lets people create unlimited unique identities to shield their real personal data. Each identity bundles a masked email address, a virtual phone number, an auto-generated password, and virtual payment cards so users can sign up for services without handing over their real contact information. The platform adds a built-in password manager, AI-powered spam call screening (Call Guard), dark web and SSN monitoring, automated data-broker removal across 120+ sites, and up to $1M in identity theft insurance. Cloaked emphasizes a zero-knowledge architecture with end-to-end encryption and is SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, and PCI DSS compliant. Backed by General Catalyst, Cloaked ships consumer apps (iOS, Android, web, browser extension) and a Cloaked Enterprise offering for businesses; it is a consumer-facing product with no publicly documented developer API at this time.

providers.name: Columbia Sportswear
providers.description: Columbia Sportswear is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of outdoor, active, and everyday lifestyle apparel, footwear, accessories, and equipment under the Columbia, Mountain Hardwear, SOREL, and prAna brands. Columbia Sportswear Digital operates a partner-focused developer portal on Microsoft Azure API Management at columbia.portal.azure-api.net, exposing APIs for Order Management, Consumer Management, Product Lifecycle Management, Cognitive, Weather, and Translation. The developer portal is gated: registered partners create an account, browse products and APIs, request subscription keys, and integrate against the published endpoints. The company also exchanges traditional EDI documents (POs, ASNs, invoices) with retail trading partners through providers like TrueCommerce and eZCom.

providers.name: Double Robotics
providers.description: Double Robotics builds telepresence robots for hybrid work and education, best known for the self-driving Double 3 videoconferencing robot and the earlier iPad-based Double 2. Its developer program spans three surfaces: the Double 3 SDK (a local command-and-event API exposed over a Unix domain socket on the robot, covering base movement, navigation, PTZ cameras, depth sensors, WebRTC calling, and standby/sidebar apps), iOS SDKs for the Double 2 (Basic Control and Camera Kit), and a Fleet REST API for programmatic access to fleet-management data such as robots, users, call logs, and visitor passes. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched against the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: edX
providers.description: edX is an online learning platform now operated by 2U; the underlying Open edX software is open source. Open edX exposes a comprehensive REST API surface (Enrollment, Courses, Users, Catalog, Discussion, Grades, LTI, Enterprise) and hosts a public API at api.edx.org for partners.

providers.name: Facets
providers.description: Facets is a platform engineering and infrastructure automation platform that unifies provisioning, deployment, and configuration into a single declarative model for governed, secure, and self-serve cloud operations. The Facets Control Plane exposes a REST API for managing blueprints, environments, releases, resources, and integrations across the platform.

providers.name: Fearn
providers.description: Fearn is the AI-native patent prosecution firm built for startups. It pairs former Big Law patent attorneys with proprietary, hallucination-resistant AI models built in-house by PhD computer scientists to take an invention from disclosure to a filing-ready provisional or non-provisional patent draft in minutes rather than the 50+ hours typical of traditional firms, at flat-rate pricing with automated labeled-figure generation and a money-back guarantee tied to claim allowance. Fearn self-hosts its entire AI infrastructure and uses no third-party model APIs, keeping invention disclosures confidential and compliant with SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, and GDPR. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco; backed by Kindred Ventures and a16z speedrun. Fearn is a legal-services company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Fiddler
providers.description: Fiddler by Telerik (Progress Software) is a suite of HTTP debugging proxy tools for capturing, inspecting, modifying, and replaying HTTP and HTTPS traffic between computers. The product family includes Fiddler Everywhere (cross-platform), Fiddler Classic (Windows), and Fiddler Jam (browser-based collaboration tool) for API debugging, performance testing, and web development workflows.

providers.name: Ghent University
providers.description: Ghent University (Universiteit Gent, UGent) is a major public research university in Ghent, Belgium, ranked #169 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer footprint centers on the Ghent University Library: the Academic Bibliography (biblio.ugent.be) exposes a documented REST search API plus OAI-PMH, SRU, unAPI and bulk data dumps under an ODbL license, and the library catalog (lib.ugent.be) offers OAI-PMH, SRU, IIIF and OpenSearch interfaces. The university maintains official GitHub organizations (ugent, ugent-library), and the student computer-science group Zeus WPI publishes the open Hydra Resto API for student-restaurant menu data. There is no single centralized, gateway-style institutional developer portal; APIs are documented per service.

providers.name: Greenlite
providers.description: GreenLite Technologies is a construction permitting and plan-review platform that uses AI-powered technology and expert services to streamline building-permit approval for builders, developers, and jurisdictions. Its products include Atlas (a real-time permit tracking and management dashboard), LiteTable (AI-assisted plan review and code-compliance analysis), Private Plan Review (PPR), and Code Compliance & Pre-Check. GreenLite claims to reduce permitting timelines from 90-120+ days to 21-45 days and serves national QSR, retail, healthcare, education, and financial-institution brands. Backed by Craft Ventures and Insight Partners. GreenLite currently exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its company identity and security posture.

providers.name: Guideline
providers.description: Guideline (now offered as "Gusto 401(k) powered by Guideline") is a retirement benefits provider that delivers full-service, low-cost 401(k) and IRA plans to small and mid-sized businesses, tightly integrated with payroll so employee deductions and employer contributions sync automatically. Through its SEC-registered investment adviser subsidiary it offers managed, low-cost index-fund portfolios, recordkeeping, compliance and plan administration. Guideline reports serving 40,000+ businesses and 700,000+ savers with $10B+ in assets under management. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and machine-readable surfaces (security.txt, llms.txt) for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kaizo
providers.description: Kaizo is an AI-powered quality assurance, coaching, and performance management platform for customer support teams working in Zendesk and Salesforce. Its AutoQA engine automatically scores 100% of support conversations in real time, analyzing sentiment and empathy, generating conversation summaries, surfacing escalation risks, and turning support data into performance insights. AI coaching builds data-driven improvement roadmaps for agents, while dashboards and reporting help support leaders compare team and individual outcomes. Kaizo delivers its product primarily as native apps for the Zendesk Marketplace and Salesforce AppExchange rather than as a public developer API. The company is SOC 2 certified, ISO 27001 certified, GDPR compliant, and continuously monitored by Secureframe. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Kodable
providers.description: Kodable is a San Diego, California based educational technology company that makes self-guided coding, computer science, and digital literacy games for elementary school students in grades K-5. Its product line includes Kodable Basics (an introduction to programming concepts for pre-readers), Kodable Creator (game design and coding with AI-assisted tutoring), Kodable Typing (keyboarding practice), and Bug World (JavaScript and object-oriented programming). Kodable sells to elementary schools and districts as well as directly to parents, pairing the student games with a teacher dashboard, K-5 curriculum, lesson plans, and professional development. The company is a Student Privacy Pledge signatory and a member of the Student Data Privacy Consortium, and publishes a privacy center covering COPPA, its EULA, terms of service, and district Data Privacy Agreement review. Kodable was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Kodable publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts - it is a consumer and school facing application rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Laserhub
providers.description: Laserhub is a Stuttgart-based digital procurement platform for custom-manufactured metal and plastic parts, founded to replace the traditional RFQ cycle for sheet metal, tube and machined components with instant online quoting. Buyers register at app.laserhub.com, upload CAD files, and receive an automated feasibility check plus an instant quote covering laser cutting, plasma and flame cutting, tube laser cutting, bending, CNC turning and milling, weldments, and secondary processes such as threading, deburring, galvanising, powder coating and engraving. Laserhub is itself the contracting party and allocates each order algorithmically across a network of roughly 100 ISO 9001:2015 certified producers in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, serving both SMEs and DAX40 manufacturers with framework agreements, a parts library, sample parts, inspection certificates and design guidelines. Laserhub publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation as of this profile: api.laserhub.com is a private AWS API Gateway that rejects unauthenticated requests, and the only machine-adjacent ordering channel the company documents is an email-based ordering flow (anfrage@laserhub.com) that its own release notes describe as still in a test phase for a subset of customers.

providers.name: Lavender
providers.description: Lavender is an AI email intelligence company for sales teams. Its Email Coach is a browser extension and Outlook add-in that scores and coaches outbound sales email in real time — subject line, structure, tone, length and personalization — using models trained on billions of sales emails, and its newer product Ora is an AI sales agent that drafts email and pushes reasoned prospect research into Salesforce CRM records. Lavender is distributed as an end-user extension and a Salesforce integration rather than as a public developer API: as of this profile the company publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI definition, and no client SDKs. It is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and GDPR compliant. Lavender is backed by Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Membrane
providers.description: Membrane is an AI-powered platform for building product integrations using natural language. It connects to any API with 282+ pre-built packages and is compatible with AI coding assistants via MCP. There is also a separate open source Membrane API Gateway for REST, SOAP, and GraphQL.

providers.name: ModernLoop
providers.description: ModernLoop is an automated interview scheduling and recruiting-operations platform for talent-acquisition teams, now paired with "Taylor AI," a configurable AI recruiting agent. It coordinates interviewer calendars, balances load, and schedules complex interview loops across time zones to cut time-to-hire and improve candidate experience. ModernLoop integrates deeply with applicant tracking systems (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, SmartRecruiters, Avature), calendar and video tools (Google, Microsoft Outlook/Teams, Zoom, Google Meet), communication (Slack, Gmail), coding assessment (CoderPad, CodeSignal, Codility, HackerRank), and SSO providers (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID). The platform is delivered as SaaS: it consumes partner APIs but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or MCP server. Backed by Accel. This profile was enriched from ModernLoop's public site, trust center, and status page.

providers.name: Nara Organics
providers.description: Nara Organics is a direct-to-consumer organic infant-formula brand, surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network. It is not a traditional API provider, but its Shopify storefront at nara.com exposes a modern agent-native commerce surface: a published Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout; a Shopify Customer Account OIDC provider; and /llms.txt + /agents.md agent instructions covering the read-only product surface and the Shop Pay flow. The company is currently managing a voluntary infant-formula recall communicated through its storefront.

providers.name: Newsela
providers.description: Newsela is a K-12 content and assessment platform that provides research-backed, engaging, differentiated reading content and AI-powered tools across ELA, social studies, STEM, and writing to support educators and drive student growth in grades 3-12. Newsela publishes no public developer API; it integrates with school systems as a certified 1EdTech (IMS Global) product supporting OneRoster 1.1 rostering, LTI v1.3 launch, and Data Privacy certification, and handles student data under FERPA, COPPA, and state student-privacy laws. Added to the API Evangelist network as a techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: Numina
providers.description: Numina is a New York City-based urban street-intelligence company (founded 2014, backed by 500 Global and SOSV) whose privacy-first, edge-processing computer-vision sensors measure how people, bicycles, and vehicles move through the public right-of-way. Its "Know Your Streets" platform turns anonymous, aggregated activity into multimodal mobility data for urban planners, municipal departments of transportation, and facilities managers, and exposes that data through the Numina Graph GraphQL API and a developer sandbox. (This profile was seeded as a 500 Global portfolio stub under the placeholder label "CTY"; its Website pointer and 500 Global backing identify it as Numina / numina.co.)

providers.name: One Model
providers.description: One Model is an HR and people-analytics software platform that unifies fragmented workforce data from HRIS, ATS, payroll, engagement, performance, and finance systems into a governed data mesh, then applies AI to turn it into insights for HR leaders and executives. Its products include Data Mesh (unify, govern, and activate data across sources), Data Stories (dashboards and reporting), One AI (a transparent predictive-modeling pipeline plus a natural-language assistant), and enterprise AI connections — including an MCP Server Access option — that let governed people data feed tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and Claude with role-based access controls.
