InkSoft exposes a documented but license-gated developer surface, the InkSoft API 2, a per-store RPC-style HTTP API returning XML or JSON with CORS support. It lets partners and store owners build custom storefronts, product catalog pages, design galleries, cart and checkout flows, and single sign-on against a specific web store. API access requires an InkSoft Unlimited license and an additional monthly fee, so the reference is public but production use is account-gated.

providers.name: John Deere
providers.description: John Deere is a manufacturer of agricultural, construction, and forestry machinery, equipment, and technology. Through its Operations Center and Precision Tech developer programs, John Deere exposes APIs that allow authorized partners and customers to access organization, field, machine, field operations, and webhook data tied to connected equipment and farm management workflows.

providers.name: Kayak
providers.description: KAYAK is a free travel metasearch engine that searches hundreds of travel sites at once so travelers can compare and find the lowest available prices on flights, hotels, rental cars, and vacation packages, with an extensive filtering system for narrowing results. Founded in 2004 and part of Booking Holdings, KAYAK operates a family of global travel brands (including momondo, Cheapflights, HotelsCombined, SWOODOO, checkfelix and Mundi) across 60+ international sites in 25+ languages. Beyond consumer metasearch it offers KAYAK for Business, a Flight Tracker, an Explore destination-discovery tool, and KAYAK AI trip-planning. KAYAK is a metasearch and price-comparison engine rather than an online travel agency — bookings are completed with the airline, hotel, car-rental company, or travel agency. This profile documents KAYAK's public discovery, AI, and security surface; KAYAK does not currently operate a public self-serve developer API program.

providers.name: KRY
providers.description: KRY is a Swedish digital healthcare provider headquartered in Stockholm that operates internationally under the Livi brand. It delivers primary care through video and chat consultations with doctors, nurses, psychologists, physiotherapists, dietitians and midwives via its iOS and Android apps, and also runs physical primary care centres (vardcentraler), child health clinics and midwifery clinics across Sweden. KRY operates as Kry in Sweden (kry.se) and Norway (kry.no) and as Livi in the United Kingdom (livi.co.uk) and France (livi.fr). Services span digital consultations, prescription renewal, medical certificates, vaccination and testing, mental health programmes, occupational health for employers, and regional public healthcare contracts. KRY publishes no public developer program, partner API or SDK surface; the platform is consumer- and clinician-facing, so this profile captures the company identity plus its legal and security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Literati
providers.description: Literati is an Austin, Texas based children's book company founded by Jessica Ewing that operates three connected consumer and school businesses: personalized monthly Book Clubs for Kids that ship five curated books matched to a child's reading level and interests starting at $11.95 per month, Clubs for Classrooms for teachers, and a school book fair business (in-person and online) run through the OpenBook coordinator dashboard at openbook.literati.com and the year-round Literati Store, which returns a share of proceeds to participating schools. The company draws on 150+ publishers, combines expert curation with data science to personalize book selection, and reports more than one million books donated to Title I schools and underserved communities since 2019. Literati publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; its public technical surface is limited to consumer and school-facing web applications, iOS and Android apps, and an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-reporting contact.

providers.name: Molekule
providers.description: Molekule is a consumer air-quality hardware company that makes FDA-cleared HEPA air purifiers for homes and businesses. It sells direct-to-consumer through molekule.com, a Shopify-hosted storefront. While Molekule does not publish a traditional developer API, its store exposes a live agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp for AI shopping agents, OpenID Connect buyer authentication via the Shopify Customer Account API, and published agent instructions at /agents.md and /llms.txt. This profile captures that machine-readable commerce surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Neros
providers.description: Neros Technologies is an American defense manufacturer founded in 2023 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, that designs and mass-produces low-cost, attritable first-person-view (FPV) drones and ground control stations for Western military forces. Its product line includes the ARCHER FPV airframe, ARCHER STRIKE, and the CROSSBOW and LONGBOW ground control stations, built on in-house flight control, powertrain, and radio hardware for electronic-warfare resistance. Neros publishes no public web API; its machine-readable interface contribution is APEX (Adaptive Payload EXchange), an open, MIT-licensed, plug-and-play UART protocol and mechanical connector standard for drone host/payload interoperability, with a C99 reference implementation and a hardware development kit published on GitHub.

providers.name: Noda
providers.description: Noda (formerly Infogrid) is an agentic AI platform for commercial real estate building operations. It functions as an always-on AI virtual building engineer that connects to a portfolio's building management systems (BMS), IoT, weather, and utility data, continuously detects faults and energy waste, identifies root causes, generates quantified savings recommendations, and executes authorized setpoint and load adjustments — tying every action to measured, audit-ready ROI. The platform processes 100M+ data points daily and reports 15-25% annual energy reduction across deployed assets. Trusted by owners and operators of 400M+ square feet including Hilton, JLL, CBRE, Macerich, Cousins, DivcoWest and Salesforce. ISO 27001 certified and hosted on AWS in the United States. Backed by Northzone. Noda exposes no public developer API; onboarding is enterprise/demo-based.

providers.name: ObjectBox
providers.description: ObjectBox is a high-performance, low-footprint, offline-first on-device database with built-in data synchronization and on-device vector search, designed for mobile, IoT, embedded, and edge computing applications. It is delivered as native language bindings (Java, Kotlin, C/C++, Go, Swift, Flutter/Dart, and Python) rather than a hosted REST API, giving apps ACID-compliant local persistence that works reliably offline and is described as up to 10x faster than SQLite. ObjectBox was the first on-device vector database on the market, targeting Edge AI use cases such as semantic search, recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation, and offers optional bi-directional Data Sync between devices and the cloud, including a direct connector to MongoDB. Founded in Germany and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Otterize
providers.description: Otterize is an open-source, Kubernetes-native platform for intent-based access control (IBAC). Application teams declare which services need to talk to which other services using ClientIntents, and Otterize automatically calculates, provisions, and enforces the underlying access controls: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies, AWS/GCP/Azure IAM, Istio Authorization Policies, Kafka ACLs, and MySQL/PostgreSQL grants. It ships three open-source operators (intents operator, credentials operator, network mapper) deployed via Helm, a Go CLI, and a managed Otterize Cloud. Its developer surface is the CLI, Kubernetes Custom Resources, and Helm/Terraform tooling rather than a public REST API. Otterize was surfaced as an Index Ventures portfolio company; otterize.com now redirects to Cyera following acquisition, while the open-source components, documentation, and CLI remain live.

providers.name: Pachyderm
providers.description: Pachyderm is an open-source (Apache-2.0) platform for data-centric pipelines and data versioning, widely used for MLOps. It provides immutable, git-like data lineage through the Pachyderm File System (PFS) and data-driven, containerized pipelines that reprocess only changed data through the Pachyderm Pipeline System (PPS), all running on Kubernetes. The platform is driven by a gRPC/protobuf API with first-party Python, Go, Ruby and Rust clients and the pachctl command-line tool. Pachyderm was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in January 2023; the standalone marketing, documentation and hosted (Pachyderm Hub) sites have since been retired, but the source, releases, SDKs and CLI remain actively published on GitHub and the language package registries (latest release v2.12.2, January 2025).

providers.name: Panorama Education
providers.description: Panorama Education is a K-12 education technology company whose student success platform is used by thousands of school districts to turn student data into action across academics and behavior (MTSS/RTI), universal screening, social- emotional learning (SEL) and survey instruments, attendance, graduation planning, and family and staff engagement. The platform ingests data nightly from 24+ student information systems, learning management systems, and 100+ benchmark and state assessments using the OneRoster standard and secure file transfer. Panorama does not publish a public self-service developer API; integrations are delivered as managed B2B data synchronization. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 attested, 1EdTech Data Privacy certified, ESSA Level II/IV rated, and a Student Privacy Pledge signatory (FERPA/COPPA/PPRA/CCPA aligned).

providers.name: Piper Inc.
providers.description: Piper (Piper Learning, Inc. / Piper LLC) is an educational-technology company that makes hands-on STEM learning kits — most notably the Piper Computer Kit, a buildable wooden computer that teaches circuitry and coding through Minecraft, and Piper Make, a browser-based platform for exploring electronics and Python. Its consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with an MCP endpoint plus Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect, letting AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and check out with explicit buyer approval. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its live public agent/discovery surface.

providers.name: PrimeRevenue
providers.description: PrimeRevenue is a global financial technology company providing working capital and B2B payment solutions through a bank-agnostic, ERP-integrated platform. Its offerings include Supply Chain Finance (buyers extend payment terms while suppliers are paid early), Receivables Finance (suppliers sell invoices for early payment without buyer disclosure), Dynamic Discounting (early payment at variable discount rates), and Payments as a Service (a modern B2B payment layer). The platform manages more than $25B in daily assets, has accelerated over 12.5M invoices, and supports 30+ languages. PrimeRevenue does not publish a public developer portal or API documentation; this profile captures its corporate, security, and compliance surface. Backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Thesis
providers.description: Thesis Care is a healthcare AI company that deploys clinical support agents backed by expert clinicians — nurses and care managers — to help physician groups, health systems, and health plans scale care management, care delivery, and clinical operations. Its platform pairs automation with human clinical oversight so work gets done end-to-end to deliver outcomes rather than create more work, handling the complex cases and edge scenarios that pure technology cannot. The company is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant and has announced a Series A round. Thesis Care publishes no public API or developer surface at this time; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's identity, security posture, and published compliance program.

providers.name: Thread AI
providers.description: Thread AI builds AI orchestration infrastructure for the enterprise. Its platform, Lemma, is a composable AI infrastructure and workflow-orchestration layer for building and running production-grade AI agents and workflows in regulated, mission-critical operations. Lemma pairs a drag-and-drop workflow builder with a code-first SDK and REST, gRPC, and GraphQL API access, adding full audit trails, governance, human-in-the-loop approvals, and reliability controls across email, voice, text, transcription, document extraction, and system-update worker functions. Deployment options span VPC, on-premises, and multi-tenant SaaS, and the platform is SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, GDPR, CJIS, and CMMC 2.0 Level 1 aligned (CMMC 2.0 Level 2 and FedRAMP underway). Thread AI is backed by Homebrew and Index Ventures.

providers.name: Traive
providers.description: Traive is a Brazilian agri-fintech that connects agribusiness with financial investors, using AI and data analytics to simplify credit access in the agricultural sector. Its Traive Agro product handles agricultural credit commercialization with risk analysis, process automation, and financing access, while Traive Finance provides credit risk analysis and access to qualified agricultural assets with traceability. The platform serves 160K+ registered producers and manages over R$6B in structured recurring credit operations. Traive publishes no public developer API; its platform authenticates via a Keycloak OpenID Connect provider whose public discovery documents reveal an internal service estate (credit, farmers, retailers, ERP integration, GraphQL) captured in this profile.

providers.name: Urtopia
providers.description: Urtopia designs and sells smart carbon-fiber electric bikes, pairing lightweight frames and premium components with a connected riding experience through the companion Urtopia App. The company is backed by DCM Ventures and sells direct through its Shopify-powered storefront at newurtopia.com (with regional stores for Europe and Australia and a B2B dealer portal), where the store exposes an agent-ready commerce surface: a published llms.txt with agent instructions, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, and live MCP endpoints for catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout.

providers.name: Workrise
providers.description: Workrise - which returned to its original RigUp brand in September 2024 - is an Austin-based source-to-pay platform for the energy industry, combining vendor management, contingent workforce staffing, bid management, capital management, and field-service payments for upstream and midstream oil and gas operators. Backed by a16z and Founders Fund. The company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; platform access is through accounts.rigup.com (OpenID Connect via Auth0), and its engineering org open-sources utilities at github.com/rigup.

providers.name: Wynd Network
providers.description: Wynd Network (now operating as Wynd Labs) is the company behind Grass, a decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) on Solana that rewards users for sharing their unused internet bandwidth. The Grass Network routes and verifies web traffic through a network of nodes, routers, and validators to collect and structure public web data for AI training and business intelligence. Grass ships consumer apps and a node network rather than a public developer API; its documentation covers network architecture, the GRASS token, staking, and points.

providers.name: Wyze Labs
providers.description: Wyze Labs (wyze.com, formerly wyzecam.com) is a Seattle-area smart home company backed by Norwest Venture Partners, selling affordable security cameras, doorbells, locks, lighting, and sensors. Wyze publishes an official Developer API Console where users generate an API key (one per account, valid one year) to obtain access and refresh tokens for third-party integrations such as Home Bridge, and its Shopify storefront exposes an agent-ready commerce surface: llms.txt/agents.md instructions, OpenID Connect discovery, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint.

providers.name: Zinc
providers.description: Zinc is a UK-founded, Y Combinator and Seedcamp-backed background checking platform that automates pre-employment screening for HR and talent teams. It runs criminal record checks across 195 countries, employment and reference verification, financial and adverse-media screening, right-to-work and qualification checks, delivering results in hours rather than weeks with an average three-day turnaround. Zinc integrates with major ATS and HRIS platforms (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters, HiBob, SAP SuccessFactors and others) and is ISO 27001, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials, GDPR and FCRA aligned. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched from Zinc's public web surface; no public developer API or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Zulily
providers.description: Zulily is an online retailer of daily deals on apparel, home, toys, and lifestyle goods. After its 2023 shutdown the brand was acquired and relaunched as a Shopify-hosted store. The relaunched storefront is agent-native: it implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) with a JSON-RPC MCP shopping endpoint, exposes OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 authentication via the Shopify Customer Account API (including a customer-account-mcp-api scope), and publishes an llms.txt / agents.md describing how AI shopping agents can discover products and run buyer-approved checkouts. This profile was surfaced as an a16z / Trinity Ventures portfolio company and enriched from Zulily's real public agent-commerce surface.

providers.name: Aatmunn
providers.description: Aatmunn (formerly Guardhat, founded 2014 in Detroit and headquartered in Livonia, Michigan) is an industrial safety and asset intelligence platform for frontline and deskless workers. Its SPANR / Industrial Internet of People (IIoP) platform unifies workers, workplaces, and assets into one real-time system, connecting devices from any manufacturer and layering AI-driven insights for predictive hazard detection, emergency response, inspections, and compliance. Products include Inspections, Lone Worker Safety, Human Condition Monitoring, Gas Detection, Control Access Zoning, and Asset Tracking, serving 250+ companies across high-risk industries such as oil & gas, chemicals, mining & infrastructure, manufacturing, utilities, and warehousing & logistics. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and is maintained by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; Aatmunn publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Accord
providers.description: A UK-based financial services company operating within the Allianz group, providing insurance and financial products to retail and business customers across the United Kingdom.

providers.name: Accrual
providers.description: Accrual is an augmented accounting intelligence platform for accounting firms and growing service businesses, offering what it calls the complete accounting workspace spanning engagement management, document intake, data processing, tax return generation, assurance workflows, and client collaboration. Backed by General Catalyst, the company emphasizes secure, US-hosted infrastructure with AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS in transit, data isolation, and SOC 2 Type II attestation, and states that customer data is not used to train AI models. Accrual does not publish a public API or developer program at this time; this profile captures the company identity and its published security posture.

providers.name: Admiral Group
providers.description: Admiral Group plc is a FTSE 100 personal-lines insurance group headquartered in Cardiff, Wales, and listed on the London Stock Exchange since 2004. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where it is one of the largest motor insurers, trading through the Admiral, Bell, Diamond, elephant.co.uk and Veygo brands and underwriting through EUI Limited and Admiral Insurance Company Limited. Beyond UK motor it writes household, travel and pet insurance (expanded by the 2024 acquisition of RSA's UK home and pet book, including the MORE THAN brand), runs the Admiral Money consumer lending arm, owns the Confused.com price comparison site, and operates internationally as ConTe.it in Italy, L'olivier in France and Admiral Seguros in Spain. Its Admiral Pioneer venture arm builds new businesses including Veygo, Admiral Business and the API-first embedded insurance venture Connect by Admiral, and in 2026 it agreed to acquire the commercial fleet insurtech Flock. Admiral's API posture is honestly recorded here as closed: it is a direct-to-consumer and price-comparison distributor, not a broker-channel or platform carrier. No developer, developers, docs or api subdomain resolves on admiralgroup.co.uk; the corporate site is bot-blocked to automated probes; admiral.com publishes 837 sitemap URLs with no developer, API, partner or integration page; and the only API hosts that resolve (api.admiral.com, api.veygo.com) are undocumented private mobile and web backends that return 502 and 403 respectively. No public self-serve API, no OpenAPI, no Postman collection, no GraphQL surface, no webhook or event catalog, and no ACORD, AL3 or NGDS reference was found. Distribution integration runs through price-comparison-website connections and partner agreements, not through a published developer program.

providers.name: AES Corporation
providers.description: The AES Corporation is a Fortune 500 global energy company that generates and distributes electrical power. AES operates a diverse portfolio of renewable, thermal, LNG, and battery storage facilities across multiple countries, serving utilities, industrial facilities, and end users. AES is the largest global supplier of clean energy to corporations in the Americas and operates 34.7 GW globally with $12.2 billion in annual revenue. The company serves 18.7 million household equivalents through utilities in Indiana, Ohio, and El Salvador. AES also co-founded Fluence Energy, a leading energy storage and software platform company.

providers.name: AiFi
providers.description: AiFi is a spatial-intelligence platform that uses camera-only computer vision to understand human behavior in physical spaces. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, it powers autonomous checkout, frictionless identity and entry, real-time fraud prevention, historical journey analytics and an operational co-pilot across retail, stadiums and arenas, quick-service restaurants, travel hubs, healthcare, campuses and government border control. The platform needs no shelf sensors or RFID and tracks shoppers with anonymous skeletal keypoint detection rather than facial recognition by default. AiFi publishes a suite of retailer-facing OASIS APIs that bridge its platform to POS (NCR, Oracle, Square) and payment (Stripe, Adyen) systems, but the developer documentation is served only to authenticated accounts through an AiFi Keycloak single sign-on.

providers.name: Alt
providers.description: Alt (alt.xyz) is an alternative-asset platform for high-value graded trading cards, founded by Leore Avidar, who previously co-founded the address and print API company Lob. Alt lets collectors and investors research, value, buy, sell, vault, and borrow against slabbed cards in one place, spanning baseball, basketball, football, hockey, soccer, golf, tennis, racing and combat-sports cards as well as Pokemon and other trading-card games. The platform combines a fixed-price marketplace, timed and "Liquid" auctions, an Instant Pricer, market-trend and research views, a physical vault in Delaware that removes sales tax from transactions, and card-backed lending. Its pricing engine, Alt Value, is a machine-learning model tuned by card-pricing specialists that produces a real-time value for every BGS, PSA and SGC card vaulted with Alt, and that value underwrites every trade, loan and product on the platform. Alt raised a $75M Series B in November 2021 led by Spearhead with Seven Seven Six and a group of professional athletes. Alt publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, CLI, sandbox or self-service API signup. Its programmatic surface is the private backend behind the alt.xyz web and mobile applications (a FastAPI/GraphQL platform service, with the engineering organisation on GitHub as github.com/onlyalt), which integrates payment, identity-verification, authentication, lending-servicing and shipping vendors but is neither documented nor offered to third parties.

providers.name: AMI Paris
providers.description: AMI Paris is a French contemporary ready-to-wear fashion house founded in 2011 by Alexandre Mattiussi and headquartered in Paris, known for its "Ami de coeur" heart logo. It sells menswear, womenswear, and accessories direct-to-consumer through amiparis.com, an online store built on Shopify. The store exposes a real agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, ucp.dev) MCP endpoint advertised in /.well-known/ucp, a published /llms.txt and /agents.md with agent instructions, Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth2 authentication, and read-only product/collection JSON endpoints. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of HongShan (Sequoia China) and profiled by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Anduin Transactions
providers.description: Anduin builds digital fund operations software for private markets, serving venture capital, private equity, and hedge funds. Its platform streamlines investor onboarding and fund administration through products including Fund Subscription, Data Room, Investor Data Management, Engagement Hub, Integration Hub, a Data Extraction Service, and Investor Access/Portal. Anduin reports 1,305+ funds served, $244B+ capital raised, and 74,000+ investors subscribed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile Anduin publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI; this record captures the company's public identity, security posture, and compliance program for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Athena
providers.description: Athena is an executive assistant service that pairs entrepreneurs, founders, and executives with dedicated, full-time remote executive assistants, along with the recruiting, training, and delegation coaching needed to work with them effectively. Athena screens a large global applicant pool and accepts only a small fraction, then equips its assistants with proprietary in-house AI tooling to maximize productivity across email, scheduling, research, travel, and day-to-day operations. The company is headquartered in San Juan, Puerto Rico and is backed by investors including Khosla Ventures. Athena is a services company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Aura
providers.description: Aura is an all-in-one consumer digital-safety company that protects individuals and families from identity theft, financial fraud, scams, and online threats. Its subscription service bundles credit and identity monitoring with up to millions in identity-theft insurance, suspicious-transaction alerts, dark-web monitoring, a privacy assistant that removes personal data from data brokers, parental controls and safe-gaming alerts, an encrypted vault and password manager, spam-call protection, a VPN, and antivirus. Aura is a direct-to-consumer product with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and compliance surface. Backed by Accel, Cowboy Ventures, General Catalyst, and Partech.

providers.name: Beep
providers.description: Beep (Just Beep It!) is a visual feedback and web collaboration platform that helps teams review live websites, report bugs, run user testing, and collect ideas directly on the page. Delivered primarily as a browser extension, it lets users annotate any web page, leave comments, attach files, and record their screen so feedback moves faster and projects ship sooner. The product targets agencies, product teams, and builders, offers a free tier plus a paid SuperBeeper plan and enterprise pricing, and is built on Wix. It exposes no bespoke developer REST API, but its Wix-powered site publishes an llms.txt and a public Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CandyClub
providers.description: CandyClub is a premium candy and confectionery brand founded in 2015, best known for its direct-to-consumer candy subscription boxes and its wholesale program that supplies curated specialty candies to boutique shops, hotels, resorts, and national retailers. The candyclub.com storefront runs on Shopify and is agent-commerce ready: it publishes an llms.txt agent guide, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint that lets AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, apply discounts, and complete buyer-approved checkouts. CandyClub was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; this profile is enriched from its public storefront, well-known discovery documents, and UCP/agent surface.

providers.name: Complyance
providers.description: Complyance is an AI-powered Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform for enterprise security, risk, and compliance teams. It automates manual GRC workflows across controls management, policy management, risk management, third-party and vendor risk management (TPRM), and customer trust, using purpose-built AI agents for evidence review, control advice, policy drafting, and vendor questionnaire and risk scoring. Complyance ships 100+ ready-made frameworks (including SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, NIST CSF 2.0, CMMC, and GDPR) plus 100+ enterprise integrations to centralize evidence and support audits at scale.

providers.name: Cyberhaven
providers.description: Cyberhaven is a data security company that unifies Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Insider Risk Management, and AI Security into a single AI and data security platform. Its data lineage-first architecture traces data from origin to exfiltration across endpoints, cloud, on-prem, SaaS, and AI tools, coaching users and blocking leaks across email, web, cloud, removable storage, and AI assistants. Cyberhaven exposes a REST API (v1 and v2) that lets teams pull incidents into third-party security tools using API-key authentication, and integrates with directory services, SIEM/SOAR platforms, and cloud applications. Backed by Costanoa Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Dabba
providers.description: Dabba (Wifi Dabba) is a Web3-powered decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) that brings affordable internet connectivity to emerging markets, starting in India. It deploys low-cost Dabba Lite WiFi hotspots through a network of local cable operators (LCOs) and rewards hotspot owners, location owners, backhaul providers, and hardware manufacturers with DBT tokens as data is consumed. Network activity — NFTs, subscriber revenue, and bandwidth usage — is reported onchain, and the token flows through a mint, buyback, and burn model. Surfaced as a Multicoin Capital portfolio company; profiled here from public developer, documentation, and onchain surfaces.

providers.name: Debitura
providers.description: Debitura is an API-first international debt collection platform covering cross-border B2B and B2C receivables. It publishes three separate public REST APIs, one per role in the network rather than one API with role-gated endpoints: the Customer API for creditors uploading invoices to collection and tracking cases, the Referral Partner API for platforms embedding collection as a referral and tracking revenue share, and the Collection Partner API for collection agencies operating cases on the platform. All three are OpenAPI 3.0.4, each on its own host, and each authenticates with an API key in the XApiKey header; the Customer API additionally accepts a bearer token, and the Referral Partner API exposes OAuth operations for minting them. Webhooks appear in all three, each with a paired test surface for exercising events before going live. Debitura publishes its own APIs.json at docs.debitura.com, which is how this profile was built.

providers.name: Earnin
providers.description: Earnin (formerly Activehours) is a consumer financial technology company offering earned wage access (EWA) that lets workers tap the pay they have already earned before their scheduled payday. Its mobile app products include Cash Out (access earned wages up to $150/day and $1,000/pay period with no mandatory fees), Live Pay and the EarnIn Card, Early Pay, Balance Shield overdraft protection, credit monitoring, FDIC-insured Savings Jars, and an EarnIn Payroll offering for businesses. Earnin is a consumer app rather than an API platform; it publishes no public developer portal or API, but does operate a vulnerability-disclosure program (security.txt via Inspectiv) and a trust center. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, Felicis, Matrix Partners, Ribbit Capital, and Trinity Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Earthly
providers.description: Earthly is an open source build automation tool that combines the best of Dockerfiles and Makefiles into a single, consistent build system, providing reproducible builds that run the same way on a developer laptop as they do in CI. Earthly Cloud and Earthly Lunar extend the open source CLI with hosted runners and code governance guardrails. No public REST or GraphQL API has been published; integration is via the Earthly CLI and Earthfile build definitions.

providers.name: EigenDA
providers.description: EigenDA is a secure, high-throughput, decentralized data availability (DA) service built on top of Ethereum using EigenLayer restaking primitives. Developed by Eigen Labs and operated as the flagship product of EigenCloud, EigenDA accepts blobs of rollup data from rollup sequencers, erasure-codes them, distributes the chunks across a network of EigenLayer-restaked operators, and produces aggregate BLS signatures that anchor data availability on Ethereum L1. The service is positioned as a hyperscale DA layer for rollups, advertising 1 GB/s of design throughput and is secured by 4M+ ETH restaked through EigenLayer with validators that include Coinbase, Google, Nethermind, and Puffer. EigenDA is consumed today by rollups and chains including Celo, MegaETH, and Aevo, with integrations available for Arbitrum Orbit, OP Stack, Nitro, and the Sovereign SDK. The protocol exposes a gRPC API surface across a Disperser (blob ingest and status), Relays (blob and chunk retrieval), Retriever (reconstructive retrieval), Churner (operator registration), and Validator/Node endpoints. v2 of the protocol introduces a payment vault and the GetPaymentState RPC on the Disperser, replacing per-account static throughput reservations with a programmatic payments surface. The reference implementation is open source in Go (with a Rust client and SDKs in Rust and TypeScript), licensed Apache-2.0 / MIT, and developed in the open on GitHub.

providers.name: Entropy
providers.description: Entropy is a threshold-signature network for trustless, programmable key management and distributed key generation (DKG). Positioned as "the Autonomous Agent Network," Entropy lets users and agents produce cryptographic signatures without any single party ever holding the private key, using on-chain WASM "programs" that define the exact conditions under which a signature may be generated. Built as a Substrate-based blockchain with a network of Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS) servers running inside Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), Entropy delivers secure crypto custody, programmable signing, and distributed key management for Web3 and autonomous-agent use cases. Backed by a16z and surfaced into the API Evangelist network via the venture-portfolio pipeline.

providers.name: Exactera
providers.description: Exactera is a corporate tax technology and advisory company that pairs AI-powered software with expert tax professionals to help multinational corporations manage the full corporate tax lifecycle. Its SaaS platform and services span transfer pricing compliance and benchmarking, R&D tax credits, fixed-asset depreciation, indirect (sales and use) tax advisory, tax provision, and the RoyaltyStat royalty-rate and transfer-pricing data platform. Exactera automates documentation, benchmarking studies, and regulatory reporting so tax and finance teams can reduce audit exposure and meet global compliance requirements. Backed by Insight Partners, the company serves enterprise tax departments and advisory firms worldwide.

providers.name: Frax Finance
providers.description: Frax Finance is a fractional-algorithmic stablecoin protocol featuring FRAX (a stablecoin), FXS (Frax Shares governance token), and Fraxswap — a TWAMM-based AMM DEX. The protocol is deployed across multiple chains and exposes its on-chain data via The Graph subgraphs.

providers.name: Gable
providers.description: Gable is an all-in-one workplace management platform that connects people, spaces, and data with AI-driven insights for hybrid and in-office teams. The platform provides desk and room booking, room scheduling, visitor management, and event planning, plus on-demand access to a global network of 20,000+ premium coworking spaces across 900+ cities. Gable surfaces office-utilization analytics that compare intended versus actual attendance to inform real estate and cost decisions, and integrates with Slack, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Google Calendar, Okta, Workday, Brivo, and Rippling. A Gable booking API plus SSO and SCIM support enable programmatic and enterprise administration of the workplace estate.

providers.name: Gameforge
providers.description: Gameforge AG is a German publisher of free-to-play online and browser games, headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany. Its catalog includes long-running titles such as OGame, Ikariam, Metin2, AION, NosTale, and other strategy and MMO games played across dozens of localized game servers. Gameforge's flagship title OGame exposes a public read-only game-data API that returns highscores, player and alliance rosters, universe/planet layouts, and per-server metadata as XML feeds (with an opt-in JSON representation), plus a separate access-controlled API that approved third-party tool developers can request for combat and report data. Gameforge also runs a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program through Bugcrowd. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Genie AI
providers.description: Genie AI is a legal-AI platform that helps business and legal teams draft, review, edit, and negotiate contracts autonomously. Founded in 2017 by founders trained by Google DeepMind, Genie is built on a patent-pending architecture called Eidetic Intelligence that gives its agents effectively unlimited memory across documents, negotiations, and organizational knowledge to reduce hallucination. The product ships autonomous contract drafting and review, multi-document deal management, risk analysis against organizational playbooks, tracked-changes negotiation, template automation, and one of the world's largest open legal libraries (500+ customizable templates and thousands of clauses across 150+ jurisdictions). Genie exposes an API and MCP connectors plus native integrations with email, CRM, cloud storage, and eSign on its Enterprise tier. The company is ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 certified, does not train on customer data, and raised a Series A led by GV (Google Ventures) with Khosla Ventures.

providers.name: Gin
providers.description: Gin is a high-performance HTTP web framework for Go that provides a fast and productive way to build microservices and APIs.

providers.name: Groundswell
providers.description: Groundswell is a corporate social responsibility (CSR) platform that lets companies run employee giving, volunteering, grants, employee assistance funds, and corporate donor-advised funds from a single integrated system. The platform provides instant donation matching and payroll giving, volunteer event management and volunteer grants, AI-assisted grant application scoring and workflow configuration, confidential employee assistance fund applications with rapid funding, tax-efficient corporate DAFs, enterprise impact reporting and analytics, and web plus mobile employee experiences. Groundswell is backed by Felicis and GV and runs on AWS infrastructure with a published trust center and SOC 2 Type I and Type II attestations. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; no public developer portal, API, or specification is currently published by the company.

providers.name: HireRight
providers.description: HireRight is a leading global provider of employment background screening, drug and health screening, and workforce verification services, helping more than 28,000 organizations across 200+ countries and territories run and manage their screening programs. Founded in 1990 and headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, HireRight offers 250+ products and services spanning criminal, financial, identity, education and employment verification, compliance, driving records, and Form I-9 checks, and screened roughly 85 million people in 2025. HireRight does not publish a public developer REST API or developer portal; its integration surface is partner- and contract-based, delivered through 70+ prebuilt connectors with 45+ HCM and ATS partners (including Workday, ADP, Oracle, and UKG) and the Applicant Center candidate experience. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public, machine-readable, and security/compliance surface (llms.txt, trust center, disclosure, domain security) rather than an open API.

providers.name: hubs
providers.description: Hubs, now operating as Protolabs Network and formerly known as 3D Hubs, is an on-demand digital manufacturing platform founded in Amsterdam in 2013 and acquired by Protolabs in 2021. It gives engineers and product teams instant online quoting, automated design-for-manufacturing analysis, and access to a vetted global network of more than 250 manufacturing partners for CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal fabrication, and injection molding, from low-volume prototyping through production-scale runs. Hubs was backed by Balderton Capital prior to the Protolabs acquisition.

providers.name: Hummingbird
providers.description: Hummingbird is an AI-powered compliance operations platform for financial institutions and fintechs. It automates customer screening (sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media checks), transaction monitoring for financial crime, investigations and case management, and regulatory reporting including automated SAR, STR, and CTR filing. Hummingbird orchestrates risk and anti-money-laundering (AML) workflows across a connected app marketplace of 50+ integrations, and exposes custom two-way integration APIs provisioned through its partnerships team. The company is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified and backed by Homebrew.

providers.name: Interplay Learning
providers.description: Interplay Learning is an Austin, Texas edtech company delivering always-on, immersive skilled trades training through online video courses, 3D simulations, and VR for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, facilities maintenance, and solar. Its SkillMill platform has trained more than 500,000 workers to be job-ready, pairing hands-on simulations with custom learning paths, certification prep, and skill assessments. For employers, Interplay exposes an enterprise data-integration API plus SSO and LMS integrations so training data can flow into an organization's own systems; it publishes no public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI. Backed by Sierra Ventures. This profile was enriched from the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Johrh
providers.description: Johrh (جوهره للعبايات, "Johrh for Abayas") is a Saudi Arabian direct-to-consumer women's fashion retailer specializing in abayas, jalabiyas, niqabs, scarves (طرح), bags, and complementary modest-wear. The brand operates an Arabic-language online storefront hosted on the Zid e-commerce platform, selling across price tiers (99 SAR, 199 SAR, and premium occasion pieces) with checkout through Saudi payment and buy-now-pay-later gateways (Tabby, Tamara, Madfu, Emkan, ZidPay, Tap, MisPay). It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network; its public web surface is served by the Zid "Vitrin" storefront application, whose OpenAPI is published at johrh.com/openapi.json.

providers.name: Khalifa University
providers.description: Khalifa University of Science and Technology is a research-intensive university in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, ranked #202 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates colleges of Engineering and Physical Sciences, Computing and Mathematical Sciences, and Medicine and Health Sciences, along with multiple research centers. No central public, documented developer or API program was found; student and administrative systems (KU Connect portal, Banner registration, e-Learn, library discovery) are gated behind institutional authentication. The only confirmed public code footprint is the GitHub organization of its Center for Autonomous Robotic Systems (KUCARS), which publishes open-source robotics research repositories rather than a managed, documented API.

providers.name: Lessen
providers.description: Lessen is a Scottsdale, Arizona based property services and facilities management technology company that connects commercial and residential property owners and managers with a nationwide network of vetted service providers for repairs, maintenance, turns, make-readies and capital projects. The company operates a technology platform stack — One by Lessen for work-order, vendor-sourcing and invoicing workflow, Lessen 360 for multifamily maintenance, Lessen Pro for affiliate contractors, Aiden for AI-assisted work-order creation, and the Lessen Marketplace for procurement — supported by mobile apps for tenants, property managers and vendors. Lessen serves retail, financial services, healthcare, food service, industrial, hospitality and education properties alongside single-family and multifamily residential portfolios. Lessen acquired SMS Assist in 2023 and is backed by Fifth Wall and General Catalyst. Lessen publishes no public developer portal, API reference or OpenAPI definition; its named platform integrations are delivered as private partner connections rather than a self-serve API program.

providers.name: LifeSite
providers.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

providers.name: Litify
providers.description: Litify is a legal operating system built on Salesforce that provides REST APIs for managing matters, intakes, documents, tasks, time tracking, billing, and client communications for law firms and legal departments. Integrators access Litify functionality via the Salesforce REST API and the Litify Docrio API under the terms of the Litify API Integration Agreement.

providers.name: MakerDAO
providers.description: MakerDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind the Maker Protocol, an Ethereum-based smart-contract system that lets anyone, anywhere generate the Dai (DAI) stablecoin by locking crypto collateral into Vaults. The protocol governs collateral types, stability fees, the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), collateral liquidation auctions, and oracle price feeds through on-chain governance by MKR token holders. Rather than a hosted REST API, developers integrate directly with the Maker Protocol smart contracts and through the official Dai.js JavaScript / TypeScript SDK, the multicall state-management library, and published developer guides. MakerDAO has since rebranded to the Sky Ecosystem (USDS / SKY). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Paradigm and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Metadata
providers.description: Metadata (metadata.io) is a B2B marketing automation and demand-generation platform that uses AI agents to plan, execute, and optimize paid advertising campaigns across LinkedIn, Meta (Facebook and Instagram), Google Search and Display, Reddit, and Bing. Its core products are Metadata Campaigns (automated full-funnel paid campaign execution), Metadata Audiences with the patented MetaMatch B2B audience engine for precision targeting, and Metadata Insights for real-time, revenue-focused performance analytics. The platform connects to ad channels, CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot), and marketing automation platforms (Marketo, Pardot) to run multivariate campaign testing at scale and optimize for pipeline and revenue rather than lead volume. Backed by 500 Global and Partech. Metadata does not publish a public developer REST API; its integration surface connects the platform to third-party ad and CRM APIs.

providers.name: Modeinspect
providers.description: Modeinspect (operated by Acreom Inc.) is an AI-native design tool that runs inside your codebase. Branded "Mode", it turns a product's real code into editable canvas frames so design engineers can shape production-grade UI on a visual canvas using the actual shipping components, design tokens, live data, breakpoints, and interaction states, then explore variants with AI and hand off pixel-perfect changes as a merge-ready pull request rather than throwaway mockups. The product is in early access / private beta. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and profiled in the API Evangelist network; enriched 2026-07-20. No public developer API, OpenAPI, docs portal, or SDK surface was found at this stage.

providers.name: Mutiny
providers.description: Mutiny (mutinyhq.com) is the GTM assistant built for customer-facing work and workflow automation — vertical AI built specifically for sales execution. Founded in 2018 as part of Y Combinator's S18 batch by Jaleh Rezaei (CEO) and Nikhil Mathew (CTO) and headquartered in New York City, Mutiny helps B2B revenue teams generate on-brand, deal-ready assets (self-updating deal rooms, pitch decks, pricing proposals, business cases, competitive comparisons, and AI-generated ABM campaigns) and automate the repetitive work around deals through agents, skills, and routines. The platform advertises Model Context Protocol (MCP) interoperability with Claude and other MCP-compatible tools and integrates with common GTM systems (CRM, email, the wider revenue stack). It is used by revenue teams at Snowflake, Uber, Rippling, GitLab, Figma, and BMC. Mutiny has raised $72M from Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, Tiger Global, Cowboy Ventures, and Y Combinator. Note: Mutiny publishes no public REST API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time — this profile captures its identity, provider-authored LLM information, and probed security posture. (Its earlier website-personalization / A/B-testing product has been retired.)

providers.name: Oatfi
providers.description: OatFi is a fintech infrastructure company that describes itself as "The Modern Credit Network for B2B Payments." It provides embedded credit, lending, and working-capital products that platforms and marketplaces can offer inside their own payment workflows. Its product surface spans Accounts Payable (flexible payment terms for buyers), Accounts Receivable (guaranteed or early supplier payouts), and Commercial Charge Cards (scaled credit and capital for commercial card programs), backed by modular components for KYB and fraud verification, underwriting, origination, loan management, capital-markets access, and collections. OatFi exposes these capabilities through APIs for approvals, settlements, and reconciliation. The developer documentation (docs.oatfi.com, a ReadMe hub) and dashboard are access-gated, so no public OpenAPI or API reference is available for cataloging at this time. Backed by QED Investors.

providers.name: Outset
providers.description: Outset is an AI-powered qualitative research platform, operated by Parnassus Labs, Inc., that lets enterprise research and product teams run large-scale AI-moderated interviews across video, voice, and text in 85+ countries and many languages. Its AI moderators conduct conversational interviews, an AI-driven synthesis layer produces summaries, themes, quotes, and highlight reels, and a Visual Intelligence suite analyzes visual cues during sessions. The platform includes participant recruitment against a large panel plus an AI fraud-detection agent. Customers include Microsoft, HubSpot, Nestle, Glassdoor, Coinbase, and Indeed. Outset publishes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 42001, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance posture but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Planera
providers.description: Planera is a modern construction scheduling platform for builders and general contractors, purpose-built around the Critical Path Method (CPM). It lets teams build, manage, and optimize project schedules through a visual, collaborative interface with drag-and-drop editing, a digital whiteboard (Canvas), Gantt views, DCMA quality checks, resource planning, and an AI scheduling assistant (Manny) for scenario analysis and risk identification. Planera spans pursuits, preconstruction, operations, and enterprise portfolio management, offers an iPad field app, and integrates with Procore, Autodesk, Primavera P6, and Microsoft Project. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 certified and is backed by Sierra Ventures.

providers.name: Pontera
providers.description: Pontera (formerly FeeX; legal entity Pontera Solutions Inc.) is a wealthtech platform that lets financial advisors securely manage, rebalance, and report on clients' held-away workplace-sponsored retirement accounts — 401(k), 401(a), 403(b), 457, TSP, and certain 529 plans — without a rollover. Accounts connect through a client-permissioned, credential-free workflow designed to avoid triggering custody under SEC Rule 206(4)-2, with an un-editable audit log for supervision. Pontera integrates with portfolio-management, reporting, billing, and supervision systems (Orion, Addepar, Black Diamond, Morningstar and others) but publishes no public developer API. Backed by ICONIQ Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Prepared
providers.description: Prepared is an AI-powered emergency response platform for 911 communications, now operating as the intelligence layer of Axon 911. Its assistive AI helps call-takers, dispatchers, and supervisors across the emergency response lifecycle with non-emergency call triage and deflection, real-time transcription and automated detail capture, live translation (40+ spoken languages and 200+ for text), multi-channel dispatch monitoring, and real-time quality assurance and training. The company reports supporting 1,000+ PSAPs (public safety answering points) and protecting 90M+ people, with claims of up to 50% faster call processing. Prepared is backed by a16z and General Catalyst and was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-portfolio pipeline. The company runs a hosted dispatch console at preparedapp.com but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: QuEra Computing
providers.description: QuEra Computing is a Boston-based neutral-atom quantum computing company (founded 2018) that operates Aquila, a 256-qubit Analog Hamiltonian Simulation QPU available publicly through Amazon Braket, and Gemini-class, a 260-qubit gate-model neutral-atom system used for fault-tolerant logical-qubit research with Harvard and MIT. QuEra has no native public REST API; developers submit programs to Aquila through the AWS Braket task API using QuEra's Bloqade SDKs (bloqade-analog for Python hardware submission, Bloqade.jl for Julia emulation, bloqade-circuit for gate-model programs), built on the Kirin compiler IR. Additional open-source tools include tsim (QEC circuit sampling), bloqade-shuttle, bloqade-lanes, and bloqade-decoders for the Dynamic Qubit Array compilation stack.

providers.name: Rattle
providers.description: Rattle is a sales-execution platform that positions itself as "the AI layer your CRM always needed," connecting Salesforce and Slack so revenue teams can automate RevOps workflows, keep CRM data accurate, and surface deal insights in real time. AI agents drive alerts, data validation, deal-risk assessment, and meeting intelligence from inside Slack. Rattle is backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of this enrichment pass Rattle exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or API reference; this profile captures the company's public web, security/compliance, and operational-transparency surface.

providers.name: Rezo
providers.description: Rezo.ai is an enterprise customer-experience (CX) company building a unified, agentic-AI contact-center platform. Founded in 2018 in Noida, India by Dr. Rashi Gupta and Dr. Manish Gupta, Rezo automates and augments customer interactions across voice, chat, email, and social channels with AI voice agents, speech and sentiment analytics, real-time agent assist, and robotic process automation, supporting 30+ languages. Its Agentic AI Suite spans customer support, sales, and marketing use cases for enterprises across banking, telecom, e-commerce, and other verticals, with product surfaces including the "Central Data Hub" (my.rezo.ai) and the "Autonomous Conversation Matrix" (az-converse.rezo.ai). Rezo operates offices in India, the USA, and the UAE, and holds ISO 27701:2019 with GDPR compliance. Rezo does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures its public identity, trust/compliance posture, and vulnerability disclosure program.

providers.name: Standard Operating Procedures
providers.description: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are documented step-by-step instructions for routine operations and processes to ensure consistency, quality, and compliance across an organization. They are essential for regulated industries such as healthcare, pharmaceuticals, finance, food service, aviation, and manufacturing. SOPs establish clear responsibilities, document institutional knowledge, support regulatory compliance, enable process auditing, and facilitate employee onboarding. Software platforms for SOP management include SweetProcess, Trainual, Guru, Document360, and Notion; many offer developer APIs for embedding SOP workflows into other business systems.

providers.name: Sungkyunkwan University
providers.description: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) is a private research university in Seoul and Suwon, South Korea, with roots dating to 1398, and is ranked #123 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its digital footprint centers on the Kingo Portal single sign-on environment, the iCampus learning system, the university library, and the KINGO-M mobile app. As of this review SKKU publishes no public, documented developer API or open-data portal; integration and identity services (Kingo SSO, eduroam) are gated to enrolled students, faculty, and staff. Public software activity exists mainly through research-lab and student developer-community GitHub organizations rather than a central institutional developer program.

providers.name: Supio
providers.description: Supio is an agentic legal AI platform built for plaintiff and personal-injury law firms, supporting a case from intake to verdict. Its Supio Agent automates labor-intensive legal work — case intake, medical-record analysis and medical chronologies (MedChrons), demand-letter drafting, case-economics analysis, and litigation document drafting — and adds firm-level intelligence across cases. Supio publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI, but offers a customer-available API for building custom integrations, dashboards, and workflows on the structured case data it generates, and integrates with case management systems (Litify, SmartAdvocate, CasePeer, MyCase, Smokeball), document stores (Box, Dropbox, OneDrive, SharePoint), and Westlaw via a Thomson Reuters partnership. The platform is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA, PHIPA, and GDPR compliant.

providers.name: Swimm
providers.description: Swimm is a codebase-understanding and modernization platform that combines deterministic static analysis, AI agents, and senior engineers to help teams understand, document, and safely transform large or legacy codebases. Its core product is an AI coding assistant that helps developers understand complex code and capture that knowledge as code-coupled documentation that stays in sync with the source, with IDE integrations, CI verification, and an agentic context layer that feeds validated knowledge to tools like Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code. Swimm also runs large-scale modernization engagements (.NET, Java, monolith-to-microservices, and mainframe/COBOL). Swimm publishes product documentation, a getting-started guide, IDE and CI integrations, and a GitHub organization, but does not expose a public REST/developer API, SDK packages, or OpenAPI specification at this time.

providers.name: Tech Soft 3D
providers.description: Tech Soft 3D builds developer SDKs and enterprise applications that power 3D data exchange, visualization, and analysis across engineering, manufacturing, and design. Its HOOPS toolkits (Exchange for CAD data translation and access, Visualize for high-performance 3D graphics, Access, Mesh, Solve, and Envision) are licensed to OEMs and independent developers building CAD, CAM, CAE, and PLM software, and it also distributes Siemens Parasolid and Polygonica. Alongside the native toolkits it publishes the HOOPS Visualize Web Components (open, first-party npm packages), SpinFire enterprise viewing/conversion apps, and OEM technologies such as AutoCAD OEM, Inventor OEM, and RealDWG. Tech Soft 3D is backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Tendo
providers.description: Tendo is a healthcare software company founded in 2020 by siblings Dan and Jen Goldsmith (previously of Veeva Systems and Instructure) and headquartered in the Philadelphia area. Tendo builds a cloud, purpose-built healthcare platform and a suite of applications that connect patients, clinicians, providers, and caregivers across the care journey — spanning digital patient engagement, quality and clinical documentation improvement, hospital quality rankings analytics, and the Care Connect marketplace for employers, providers, and patients. The company raised a $50M Series B led by Lux Capital (with General Catalyst). Tendo runs public trust and status surfaces (a SafeBase trust center with SOC 2 and HIPAA, an Atlassian Statuspage) but does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI; API integration is delivered under private partner agreements. Surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Thinglink
providers.description: Thinglink is an educational technology company offering a no-code, AI-powered platform for creating and deploying immersive, interactive learning experiences. Users enrich images, videos, and 360deg / virtual-tour media with clickable "tags" that surface text, audio, links, and embedded content, producing multimodal content for XR, AR, and 360deg training that runs on any device. Thinglink serves K-12 and higher education as well as corporate learning and safety-training teams, and integrates with learning-management systems. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Thinglink publishes a public trust center (ISO 27001, GDPR) but exposes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: TransCrypts
providers.description: TransCrypts is a blockchain-based identity and credential verification platform that lets individuals own, encrypt, and share verified records — employment and income history, background checks, and (with HIPAA certification) health and education credentials — directly with employers, background checkers, and other verifiers. Encrypted data is stored off-chain while cryptographic hashes are anchored on-chain, so users can prove authenticity without exposing personal data. The company reports 5M+ verifications across 4M+ users and 450+ enterprise clients, and connects to HR and payroll systems such as ADP, BambooHR, and Namely. It raised a $15M seed round led by Pantera Capital, with Techstars, Lightspeed Faction, Alpha Edison, Motley Fool Ventures, Mark Cuban, and Protocol Labs participating.

providers.name: University of Copenhagen
providers.description: The University of Copenhagen (Københavns Universitet, UCPH), founded in 1479, is Denmark's oldest and largest university and one of the leading research institutions in the Nordic region, ranked #53 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It has no centralized public developer portal or documented open-data API program. Its public technical footprint consists of the ku-kom GitHub organization (TYPO3 CMS extensions and front-end styleguide used to build the ku.dk web platform) and the CURIS research information system on researchprofiles.ku.dk, an Elsevier Pure platform that conventionally supports OAI-PMH metadata harvesting and the Pure web service though these endpoints could not be confirmed reachable from the public internet at review time.

providers.name: University of Twente
providers.description: The University of Twente (Universiteit Twente, UT), founded in 1961 in Enschede, Netherlands, is a public technical research university and ranks #233 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its publicly confirmable developer/API footprint is modest. The university runs a Pure-based research information system, UT Research Information (research.utwente.nl), which is documented as exposing an OAI-PMH metadata harvesting endpoint, though that endpoint is not openly reachable from the public web front-end at time of review. Source code from the university and its research groups is published across several GitHub organizations. The University of Twente is also a co-founding member of the 4TU.ResearchData repository (data.4tu.nl), which is hosted and governed by TU Delft rather than operated by UT itself.

providers.name: Von
providers.description: Von (vonlabs.ai) is an AI RevOps agent from Rattle Software, the Insight Partners and Sequoia backed team behind gorattle.com, positioned as an AI data scientist for revenue teams. Von connects to CRMs, data warehouses, call recorders, and sales engagement tools - Salesforce, HubSpot, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Gong, Outreach, Salesloft, and more, plus 100+ integrations consumed via MCP - to automate pipeline forecasting, win/loss analysis, churn detection, sales coaching, and Salesforce administration. Von publishes no public API or developer program; its security posture is documented at trust.vonlabs.ai (SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, CASA Tier 2).

providers.name: Wochit
providers.description: Wochit is an enterprise-grade, cloud-based video creation platform that helps organizations produce professional, on-brand videos at scale. It offers three products: Studio, an AI-powered video creation workspace paired with one of the world's largest licensed content libraries; Frame, a white-label, embeddable video editor that SaaS platforms and marketplaces integrate into their own products; and WAVE, an automated video engine that mass-produces videos from templates and data. Wochit serves media companies, publishers, nonprofits, and enterprises that need repeatable, high-volume video production. Wochit does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Yalo
providers.description: Yalo is an intelligent sales platform that uses AI agents to help consumer brands sell through conversational channels like WhatsApp, mobile apps, and phone calls, managing complete customer journeys across more than 40 countries. Its Oris AI sales agent, conversational commerce platform, and cross-platform Chat SDK (Flutter, Android, iOS, and web, with a published gRPC/protobuf message contract) serve CPG, financial services, telco, and eCommerce customers including Nestle, Coca-Cola FEMSA, Mondelez, PepsiCo, and Unilever.

providers.name: Zend
providers.description: Zend is the enterprise PHP platform business of Perforce Software, providing production-grade PHP runtimes, tooling, and long-term support for mission-critical applications. Its portfolio spans ZendPHP (a hardened, enterprise-supported PHP runtime with LTS builds for end-of-life PHP versions), ZendHQ (PHP application observability and monitoring), Zend Server, Zend Studio, and Zend Guard, along with migration, modernization, performance auditing, and Black Belt support services for Laravel, Symfony, CodeIgniter, and CakePHP teams. Zend ships product tooling and a documentation surface rather than a public REST API.

providers.name: AccessHope
providers.description: AccessHope is a Los Angeles-area health benefits company, founded in 2019 and wholly owned by City of Hope, that delivers remote cancer expertise as an employer-sponsored benefit. Its subspecialist teams review a member's pathology, imaging, molecular testing and treatment plan against the latest evidence from a coalition of National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers — City of Hope, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Emory Winship, Fred Hutch, Johns Hopkins Kimmel, Northwestern Medicine Lurie, and UT Southwestern Simmons — and return guidance to the member's own local oncologist rather than moving the patient. AccessHope reports roughly 9 million covered members across 700+ employer and health-plan clients, including 70+ Fortune 500 companies. Delivery is business-to-business: employers, benefits consultants, health plans and navigation partners onboard through an eligibility file feed and an implementation-managed workflow, while members and clinical staff use credentialed web portals. AccessHope publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AfterShoot
providers.description: Aftershoot is a Techstars-backed company building desktop AI software for professional photographers that automates the post-shoot workflow. Its applications cull large photo sets by detecting duplicates, blinks, blur, and composition to pick the best frames, apply personalized AI editing that learns a photographer's style, and perform AI retouching, plus tools for building client galleries and selects. Aftershoot integrates with Adobe Lightroom Classic and Capture One and runs locally on macOS and Windows. There is no public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface; the public code presence is internal Rust/Kotlin tooling on GitHub.

providers.name: Artsy
providers.description: Artsy is the world's largest online art marketplace, connecting collectors with artists and galleries worldwide. The platform features over 1 million artworks from 100,000+ artists and provides access to galleries, art fairs, and auction houses globally. Artsy offers a Public API providing access to images of historic artwork and related information for educational and non-commercial purposes, with access limited to public domain works. The API provides resources for artists, artworks, galleries, shows, sales, and gene (classification) data. Note that the public API may be retired; partner integrations are handled through a separate partner API program.

providers.name: Authentic8
providers.description: Authentic8 is a cybersecurity company best known for Silo, a cloud-based secure browser and digital investigations platform. Silo isolates web activity in the cloud so analysts, investigators, and enterprise users can browse the surface, deep, and dark web anonymously with managed attribution, region masking, and full audit and governance controls. The company serves intelligence, law enforcement, financial crime, fraud, and corporate security teams, and delivers its service as a FedRAMP-authorized SaaS with SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance. Authentic8 is backed by Foundry Group and does not currently publish a public developer API. This profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bambu Lab
providers.description: Bambu Lab is a consumer 3D-printing company (X-series, P-series, and A-series printers, the AMS multi-material system, and the MakerWorld model platform) that connects its printers to the Bambu Handy app and Bambu Studio slicer over a cloud and LAN control plane. There is no open, self-service public REST API: machine control runs over an MQTT interface (us/cn.mqtt.bambulab.com:8883, TLS, authenticated with a Bambu account user id and MQTT token), and a firmware-level "printer control authorization" mechanism now gates binding, firmware updates, camera streams, and print/movement commands. Third parties integrate through Bambu Connect, LAN Developer Mode, or by applying for SDK access; the practical API surface today is community-reverse-engineered (OpenBambuAPI, Bambu-Lab-Cloud-API, and Python/Rust client libraries). Added to the API Evangelist network from the IDG Capital portfolio and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: BetterView Marketplace
providers.description: Betterview is a market-leading Property Intelligence platform that delivers actionable insights to property & casualty insurance underwriters, agents, and insureds to increase efficiency and profitability. Its API lets carriers order and retrieve property profiles enriched with the Roof Spotlight Index (RSI), peril risks, flags, and third-party Partner Connect data, subscribe properties to PropertyPulse monitoring, and query PropertyNow pre-processed datasets by address or coordinates. Betterview integrates with core insurance systems including Guidewire (a Marketplace accelerator for PolicyCenter 10), Duck Creek, and Socotra, and supports SSO, Secure FTP, ImageRight drop, an embeddable geospatial iframe UI, and an External Data Warehouse (EDW) SQL connection.

providers.name: Boundless
providers.description: Boundless is a Seattle-based technology-enabled immigration company that pairs an intuitive online platform with licensed immigration attorneys to help individuals and businesses navigate U.S. immigration. Its consumer products cover family-based green cards, marriage and fiancé (K-1) visas, naturalization and citizenship, and employment-based visas such as H-1B, EB-1, O-1, and E-2, while its business offering adds corporate case management, workflow automation, employee engagement, compliance management, HR-system integration, and global mobility support for immigration teams. Boundless is backed by Foundry Group and Seedcamp. No public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs are published at this time.

providers.name: CardinalOps
providers.description: CardinalOps is a cybersecurity company delivering agentic detection engineering for security operations centers (SOCs). Its Threat Coverage Optimization Platform continuously assesses detection posture across SIEM and EDR tools (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Cortex, Elastic and others), maps existing detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, surfaces coverage gaps, and automatically remediates broken or noisy rules. The Agentic Fleet and Cardinal AI use large language models to extract atomic TTPs from threat intelligence and generate new, validated detection rules. CardinalOps is backed by Battery Ventures and serves enterprise SOC teams. It publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public developer-adjacent, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Champions Oncology
providers.description: Champions Oncology (NASDAQ: CSBR) is a global preclinical and clinical oncology contract research organization (CRO) supporting pharmaceutical and biotech drug development from discovery through the clinic. It maintains a living bank of more than 1,400 patient-derived tumor models and primary hematological models, and offers proprietary in vivo and ex vivo platforms, next-generation sequencing (WES/RNASeq), quantitative and phospho-proteomics, flow cytometry, and other analytical assays. Its Lumin Bioinformatics platform is an integrated, no-code analytics and visualization solution built on precisely curated multi-omics oncology data assembled from over 12,000 cancer patients, exposing gene networks, molecular signatures, target discovery, and AI-driven predictive analytics to researchers. Champions was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Clad Labs
providers.description: Clad Labs is a San Francisco developer-tools startup (Y Combinator, Fall 2025) building Chad IDE, a desktop development environment that orchestrates multiple AI coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor CLI, and OpenAI Codex — from a single interface. Developers spin up teams of parallel agents, keep each task isolated in its own workspace, then merge clean changes back together, while a built-in analytics dashboard tracks coding habits and productivity metrics. The IDE also fills AI-inference downtime with an in-app "Chad Browser" for entertainment that automatically hands focus back to the code when generation completes. Clad Labs ships a downloadable macOS and Windows application rather than a public web API; it exposes no REST/OpenAPI developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Copa (Project Copacetic)
providers.description: Project Copacetic (Copa) is an open source command line tool that patches container images directly using BuildKit, without requiring a full image rebuild. Copa parses vulnerability scan reports from Trivy and other scanners, applies the corresponding OS package updates via the appropriate package manager (apt, apk, dnf, tdnf, yum, zypper), and produces a new container image with a patched layer.
