AI agents draft petition narratives, assemble supporting evidence and anticipate USCIS objections, with every filing reviewed by a licensed attorney before submission. LegalOS is delivered as a service through a customer web application at app.legalos.ai; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Lightning Labs
providers.description: At Lightning Labs, we develop software that powers the Lightning Network. Our open source, secure, and scalable Lightning systems enable users to send and receive money more efficiently than ever before. We also offer a series of verifiable, non-custodial Lightning-based financial services. We bridge the world of open source software and the next-generation of bitcoin financial software.

providers.name: Linker Finance
providers.description: Linker Finance Inc is a US financial technology company providing a digital banking and CRM platform for community and regional retail and commercial banks. Its platform covers digital account opening with embedded KYC and fraud checks, business and commercial onboarding with KYB, AML and beneficial-owner KYC, retail digital banking, and commercial banking features including positive pay, treasury management, remote deposit capture, team management and payment approvals. The platform runs on AWS, ships as responsive web plus native iOS and Android apps published under the bank's own app store accounts, and integrates with bank core systems directly or through integration partners. Linker Finance is a certified PREMIUM partner on the Fiserv AppMarket. Backed by Techstars and Alloy Labs, the company raised a $5M seed round. It publishes no public developer portal or API; its "API Connectivity" is a partner- and customer-scoped integration capability rather than an open API program.

providers.name: Make the Dot
providers.description: Make the Dot is an AI-powered product development platform for fashion and apparel teams. It unifies design, development, and merchandising workflows so brands can build production-ready collections digitally — reducing physical sampling, accelerating time to market, and connecting the tools teams already use (PLM, Shopify, NuOrder, Airtable, Google Suite, Salesforce, Coloro, fabric mills, and Browzwear). It serves everyone from independent Shopify brands to billion-dollar apparel companies. Make the Dot is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a web application and a help center but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Metromile
providers.description: Metromile is a pay-per-mile auto insurance platform powered by telematics and data science. Customers attach the Pulse OBD device to their vehicle to track mileage; premiums consist of a base monthly rate plus a per-mile charge, rewarding low-mileage drivers with significant savings. Beyond consumer insurance, Metromile Enterprise offers a cloud-based REST API platform for property and casualty insurers covering touchless claims automation, accident reconstruction (Replay), fraud detection (Detect), digital FNOL reporting (Report), and back-office workflow automation (Streamline). Metromile was acquired by Lemonade in July 2022.

providers.name: Mountain Protocol
providers.description: Mountain Protocol is the issuer of USDM, a regulated, institutional-grade yield-bearing stablecoin backed by short-term US Treasury securities that pays daily rewards to holders through an ERC20 rebasing token. The company operated a Primary-User account platform with a private REST API for depositing and withdrawing USDM and USDC, querying account balances, and checking USDC liquidity, alongside on-chain proof-of-reserves and a smart-contract security program audited by OpenZeppelin with an Immunefi bug bounty. As of 2025 the protocol entered an orderly wind-down: the primary market closed on August 22, 2025, redemptions moved to secondary markets, and Phase 3 provides on-chain proof-of-reserves so holders can independently verify USDM backing. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Openly
providers.description: Openly is an independent agent home insurance platform founded in 2017 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. The company provides REST APIs for generating homeowners insurance quotes, binding policies, managing endorsements, and processing renewals. Openly operates as a general agency and program administrator, enabling tech-savvy independent agencies to build custom interfaces and plug into the Openly platform on the backend. The platform leverages actuarial science, machine learning, and advanced technology to provide fully underwritten quotes in seconds, supporting primary residences, secondary and seasonal homes, and landlord (rented-to-others) policies with coverage up to $5M guaranteed replacement cost.

providers.name: Pasito
providers.description: Pasito is an AI-native workspace for employee benefits that helps benefits consultants, insurance carriers, and employers simplify every part of the benefits journey — from proposal and quoting through enrollment to year-round employee engagement — using agentic AI workflows. The platform turns unstructured plan documents and census data into a structured data layer that powers a conversational AI benefits assistant, automated proposal/RFP intake, benefits guides and microsites, decision support, and communications. Pasito reports supporting over 6.6 million employees, managing $106B in premiums, and serving 3,600+ employers, integrating with 950+ TPA systems and 260+ HRIS platforms. Backed by Google, Y Combinator, and Core Innovation Capital, the company is building a public-facing API but does not yet publish a developer portal, documentation, or API reference.

providers.name: Pie Insurance
providers.description: Pie Insurance is a small business workers compensation insurance platform that provides a REST API for approved partners to quote, bind, and manage workers comp policies. The partner API supports appetite checking, price indication, quote submission, document upload, and retrieval of bindable quotes, enabling agencies, aggregators, and technology platforms to embed workers comp quoting directly into their own workflows. Pie targets small businesses across 39 states and Washington D.C., using data-driven underwriting to offer savings of up to 30% versus traditional carriers. Payroll-based premium calculations and policy management including certificates of insurance are central to the platform.

providers.name: Probe Information
providers.description: Probe Information Services (Probe42) is an Indian company-intelligence and business-data platform that collects, cleans, and curates information on roughly one million Indian companies from 743 public-domain sources through a five-step verification process. Its products — Probe42 Business, Probe42 Banking, and the Probe42 API — deliver company profiles, financials, director and charge data, and risk signals used by banks, NBFCs, fintechs, and sales teams for onboarding, KYC/due-diligence, credit assessment, and lead intelligence. The Probe42 API lets developers embed this company data directly inside their own applications. Surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the public API surface is gated behind developer-portal authentication.

providers.name: RPC
providers.description: RPC, Inc. is an oilfield services company providing specialized well services to independent and major oil and gas companies engaged in the exploration, production, and development of oil and gas properties. Operating through subsidiaries including Cudd Energy Services, Patterson Services, Spinnaker Oilwell Services, and Thru Tubing Solutions, RPC offers pressure pumping, wireline, downhole tools, coiled tubing, cementing, snubbing, nitrogen services, well control, rental tools, and tubular services. RPC does not currently offer a public developer API.

providers.name: ST Labs
providers.description: ST Labs (Standard Template Labs, stlabs.com) is an AI-native IT service management platform that turns historical ticket data, knowledge bases, and enterprise integrations into instant resolutions, automated workflows, and a living graph of the organization. Its capabilities span smart ticket enrichment (auto-classify, prioritize, attach resolution context), AI clustering into self-healing workflows, AI-agent self-service, and a "Digital Twin" / Axiom context graph that maps real-time relationships between people, applications, infrastructure, and processes and is queryable in natural language. The product connects to 100+ systems (ServiceNow, Okta, AWS, Datadog, Slack, Workday, and more) across ITSM, identity, cloud, security, and collaboration. As of mid-2026 the company is in early-access/waitlist stage with no public developer API, and is backed by CRV and ICONIQ Capital.

providers.name: Successfactors
providers.description: SuccessFactors is a cloud-based human capital management (HCM) company founded in 2001 and an early Canaan Partners portfolio company that IPO'd in 2007 and was acquired by SAP in 2012. It is now delivered as the SAP SuccessFactors HXM (Human Experience Management) Suite, covering core HR (Employee Central), Recruiting, Onboarding, Performance & Goals, Compensation, Learning (LMS), Succession & Development, and Workforce Analytics. SuccessFactors exposes an extensive integration surface through OData v2 and OData v4 APIs (the SFAPI/OData platform) documented on the SAP Business Accelerator Hub, using OAuth 2.0 SAML bearer-assertion and basic authentication per customer datacenter instance.

providers.name: Summation
providers.description: Summation is an enterprise AI analyst platform that automates recurring business work — financial reviews, forecasts, models, and executive-ready decks — by connecting to a company's data sources (ERPs, data warehouses, and spreadsheets) and producing verified, source-traced reports in the format teams already use. Its AI agent "Addison" runs playbooks across finance, operations, and sales, tracing every number back to its source so outputs are audit-ready and SOC 2 Type II compliant. Founded by Ian Wong (CEO) and Ramachandran "RC" Ramarathinam (CTO), formerly of Opendoor, Summation is backed by Battery Ventures. The company operates a customer application, product documentation, and a public Trust Center, but does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Tilda Research
providers.description: Tilda Research deploys AI Teammates that perform the operational work of clinical trials for sponsors, CROs, and research sites — automating study workflows, data capture, trial monitoring, and regulatory compliance. Founded by Ram Yalamanchili and backed by 8VC, the company operates the Tilda Sense clinical-research platform (sense.tilda.bio) and advertises SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance via a Vanta-hosted trust center, but publishes no public developer program or API documentation.

providers.name: Token
providers.description: Token Security is a cybersecurity company that secures non-human identities (NHIs) and AI agents across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments. Its platform continuously discovers every AI agent, service account, and machine identity, maps ownership and security posture, detects identity threats, and automates remediation. Capabilities span NHI inventory, security posture management, lifecycle management, secrets, and identity threat detection and response. The company also ships the Token MCP Server and a native Token AI Agent so security teams can query and act on NHI data conversationally from Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Cursor. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, GGV Capital, and Qiming, Token Security serves enterprise security teams, CISOs, and IAM professionals governing machine and agent identity at scale.

providers.name: Urban SDK
providers.description: Urban SDK is a geospatial AI and data analytics company serving the public sector, delivering hourly road-speed and traffic data, analytics, and AI tools that help cities, counties, and transportation agencies prioritize issues, pinpoint trends, and act on traffic management, public safety, emergency response, and infrastructure planning. A Techstars portfolio company based in Jacksonville, Florida, Urban SDK delivers its data through a web platform and automated Workflows reports rather than a public API, and currently publishes no developer documentation or client SDKs.

providers.name: 9am Health
providers.description: 9amHealth (join9am.com) is a US virtual cardiometabolic clinic delivering specialized care for type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight loss, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol entirely from home. Founded in 2021 in San Diego by mySugr co-founders Frank Westermann and Anton Kittelberger, the company pairs at-home lab test kits, asynchronous and synchronous telehealth visits with obesity specialists, pharmacists, dietitians, and behavioral health experts, mail-order pharmacy for prescriptions including GLP-1 receptor agonists, and optional connected devices such as continuous glucose monitors into individualized care plans. It sells direct to individuals and through employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers. 9amHealth is a consumer and enterprise telehealth brand and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Accordance Ai
providers.description: Accordance (operated by Agnetic Labs Inc.) is a San Francisco frontier AI platform built for tax, audit, and accounting professionals. Founded by researchers from the Stanford AI Lab, it provides a firmwide agentic AI platform that performs tax research with authoritative code, context, and citations, complex accounting analysis, and audit insight — with visible reasoning and verifiable source citations. Accordance is SOC 2 Type II certified, never trains on customer data, and is backed by Menlo Ventures, Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and New Enterprise Associates. The product surface is the Accordance application (app.accordance.ai); no public developer API is currently documented.

providers.name: Accountable
providers.description: Accountable is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: crypto. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Aerodrome
providers.description: Aerodrome Finance is the central trading and liquidity marketplace on the Base network — a next-generation MetaDEX (automated market maker inspired by Solidly and Velodrome) that pairs a vote-escrow ve(3,3) tokenomics model with gauge-directed AERO emissions. It offers basic volatile (vAMM) and stable (sAMM) pools plus concentrated-liquidity Slipstream pools, letting liquidity providers, voters, and traders coordinate incentives on Base. Aerodrome is a smart-contract protocol rather than a hosted API: developers integrate through its onchain Solidity contracts, the shared open-source "Sugar" SDK (JavaScript and Python) that reads pool/veNFT/relay data and builds unsigned transactions, and GraphQL subgraphs for analytics. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public sources.

providers.name: Allstate
providers.description: Allstate is a personal lines insurer in the United States offering auto, home, life, and other insurance products through agents, call centers, and direct channels. The Allstate Developer Portal provides partner APIs for agency management, policy quoting, claims integration, and telematics data exchange for authorized business partners.

providers.name: Amgen
providers.description: Amgen is committed to unlocking the potential of biology for patients suffering from serious illnesses by discovering, developing, manufacturing and delivering innovative human therapeutics. As a pioneer in biotechnology since 1980, Amgen uses living cells to make biologic medicines addressing cardiovascular metabolic conditions, oncology, inflammation, rare diseases, and bone health, operating in approximately 100 countries worldwide.

providers.name: Apache Lucene
providers.description: Apache Lucene is a high-performance, full-featured text search engine library written entirely in Java. It provides indexing and search technology, as well as spellchecking, hit highlighting, faceting, vector similarity search, and advanced analysis and tokenization capabilities. Lucene is the foundation for many popular search applications including Apache Solr.

providers.name: Arc (The Browser Company)
providers.description: Arc is a Chromium-based alternative web browser from The Browser Company, organized around Spaces, Profiles, Split View, Boosts (user-authored CSS/JS overlays), Easels, Notes, and Arc Search on mobile. Arc is primarily a consumer product without a broad public developer REST API. Developer surface area is limited to Developer Mode in the desktop browser, the underlying Chromium extension model, and user-created Boosts. The company has signalled that Arc's active product investment is winding down in favor of the successor product, Dia.

providers.name: Arch Network
providers.description: Arch Network is Bitcoin-native financial infrastructure and a computation environment that lets developers build DeFi and capital-markets applications — lending, yield, trading, and structured products — with settlement kept local to Bitcoin. It executes programmable smart contracts (written in Rust) over Bitcoin UTXOs using a specialized virtual machine and threshold-cryptography (FROST/ROAST) validator security, and exposes a JSON-RPC API with first-party TypeScript and Rust SDKs, a CLI, and an AI agent kit. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Beaconcure
providers.description: Beaconcure is a clinical data technology company whose AI-enabled platform, Verify, automates the statistical analysis and reporting workflow for biometrics teams running clinical trials. Verify converts static Tables, Listings and Figures (TLFs) into machine-readable form and runs format, reference, within-table and cross-table validation checks, tracks quality-control progress in a shared review workspace, and captures every fix in an inspection-ready audit trail across its Essentials, Validate and Generate modules. Beaconcure also documents a customer-scoped Verify REST API that exposes near real-time QC data — deliverables, projects, protocols, users, files, suspected and verified outputs, and discrepancies — as JSON or CSV, though each customer receives a unique API version and endpoint behind an IP allowlist. Founded in Israel with US headquarters in Boston, the company works with top-10 pharmaceutical companies and contract research organizations.

providers.name: BloomThis
providers.description: BloomThis is a Malaysian online florist and gifting brand (backed by 500 Global) offering fresh flower boxes, hand-tied bouquets, and weekly fresh-flower subscriptions, with a free personalised card and photo on every order and free same-day delivery across Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Kedah, Penang, Negeri Sembilan, and Johor Bahru. Its Shopify storefront natively exposes an agent-commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP): a hosted MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp, an OpenID Connect / OAuth Customer Account API, and published /llms.txt and /agents.md instructions that let AI shopping agents search the catalog, build a cart, and run a buyer-approved checkout.

providers.name: BoaConsulta
providers.description: BoaConsulta is a Brazilian digital-health platform, founded in 2012 and part of the Pixeon healthtech group, that connects patients, health professionals, and institutions. It pairs a free B2C marketplace for booking in-person consultations, teleconsultations, exams, and vaccinations with a full B2B/SaaS practice-management system (150+ integrated modules covering smart scheduling, electronic health records, telemedicine, financial management, TISS insurance billing, inventory, and automated reminders). The platform reports more than 58,000 health professionals, 1.7 million registered patients, and over 2 million appointments, with LGPD-compliant end-to-end encryption and daily automated backups. It has no public developer API; this profile is enriched from BoaConsulta's own public surfaces (llms.txt, status page, help center, blog, and legal pages).

providers.name: Briefcase
providers.description: Briefcase is an AI-native accounting and bookkeeping automation platform for UK accounting firms and businesses. Founded in 2024 in London by Reuben Steenkamp and Ján Stehlík, and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, Entrepreneur First and Tiny, Briefcase describes itself as building the world's first AI autopilot for accounting firms. The product uses multimodal AI and agentic workflows to automate the most tedious parts of accounting: extracting data from invoices, receipts and bank statements, categorising transactions against a firm's chart of accounts, handling VAT (with embedded HMRC legislation for standard, reverse-charge and zero-rated VAT), automating prepayments and expense claims, and driving month-end and financial close. It publishes results into Xero and QuickBooks. Briefcase is delivered as a cloud SaaS application (app.briefcase.so); it is a consumer of accounting APIs rather than a public API producer, and at the time of this profile it publishes no developer/API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Brisk Teaching
providers.description: Brisk Teaching is a K-12 education technology company that integrates AI directly into the tools teachers already use. Its platform spans three connected products: the Brisk Extension (which brings AI into Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, and YouTube), Brisk Boost (a safe, teacher-controlled, student-facing AI workspace), and Brisk Next (a web-based planning and instruction hub). Brisk helps educators give feedback, create instructional materials, change reading levels, inspect student writing, and generate presentations, lesson plans, rubrics, quizzes, IEP goals, and math problems. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Brisk publishes an llms.txt for AI representation and a public status page, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks its public surface.

providers.name: Caya
providers.description: Caya (Caya GmbH, Berlin) is a German intelligent document processing (IDP) company whose Document Automation Suite digitizes, classifies, and routes business documents end to end. Its core capabilities are Post Scan (physical mail intake with OCR and automatic classification), Document Extractions (AI-powered structured data extraction), and Document Automations (rule-based routing and distribution into downstream systems). Caya connects to 100+ tools across accounting, ERP, HR, cloud storage, and e-signature, and hosts data in a high-security Frankfurt data center. It is certified and compliant against ISO 27001, GDPR/DSGVO, DORA, GoBD, and German HGB/AO retention rules, with a public Vanta-hosted trust center. Surfaced as an HV Capital portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cents
providers.description: Cents is an all-in-one laundry business management platform for laundromats and dry cleaners. It combines point of sale, self-service machine payment systems, wash-and-fold order management, online ordering, pickup-and-delivery route management, memberships and recurring billing, inventory tracking, team management, marketing tools, customer-facing websites, commercial invoicing, and reporting and financial tools into a single operating system for local laundry businesses. Cents also offers an AI Receptionist team and laundry-first insurance, and has acquired Insight Systems and Laundroworks to extend support for dry cleaners and card-based self-service payment technology.

providers.name: Claroty
providers.description: Claroty is a cybersecurity company that protects cyber-physical systems (CPS) across industrial, healthcare, commercial, and public-sector environments. Its AI-powered platform delivers asset discovery, exposure and vulnerability management, threat detection, and secure remote access for operational technology (OT), IoT, and the extended internet of things (XIoT) that traditional IT security tools cannot adequately protect. Claroty serves more than 1,300 customers across 60+ countries, including 24 of the Fortune 100, and its Team82 research group publishes original vulnerability research and open-source ICS security tooling. This profile was seeded as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Claroty publishes no public product API or developer portal, so enrichment is limited to company identity, GitHub open-source presence, and security/compliance posture.

providers.name: Cocoon
providers.description: Cocoon is next-generation employee leave management software that automates the complexities of compliance, claims, and payroll for every type of employee leave (parental, medical, caregiver, accommodation, bereavement, and personal) across all 50 U.S. states. It factors in state, federal, company, and insurance benefits to calculate eligibility, generate designation notices, and streamline the leave experience for both employees and HR teams. Cocoon connects to 20+ HRIS and payroll platforms (Workday, Rippling, Gusto, BambooHR, ADP, Paylocity, UKG, and more) via API integrations that sync employee data in real time. Founded in 2020 by former Stripe and Square leaders and backed by Index Ventures and First Round Capital, Cocoon was acquired by TriNet in April 2026. Cocoon is a consumer of HRIS/payroll APIs rather than a publisher of a public developer API; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal are published.

providers.name: Complir
providers.description: Complir is the AI infrastructure for product compliance, described by the company as "Vanta for physical products." Its AI agents map product data, analyse compliance risks, generate audit-ready documentation, and track regulatory changes across every market a brand sells in - covering GPSR, ESPR, EPR, REACH, RoHS, PPWR, EUDR, CE/UKCA marking, Digital Product Passports and 100+ other frameworks across 40+ markets. The platform maps each SKU to its regulatory requirements, produces translations, labels, warnings, declarations of conformity and technical files, verifies marketing claims, and offers native Adobe Illustrator/InDesign plugins plus a natural language interface for querying compliance data. Founded in 2024 (Gustav Bang, Marc Kaa Brejner, Tine Kuhnel) and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch, Complir monitors 100,000+ products for international retailers including Flying Tiger Copenhagen, Konges Sloejd, Matas and COOP.

providers.name: Contify
providers.description: Contify is an AI-powered market and competitive intelligence platform that helps businesses track competitor activity, market trends, and industry news. It exposes a REST News API that delivers structured, deduplicated, and enriched business news data on companies, industries, and topics.

providers.name: Devv
providers.description: Devv (devv.ai) is an AI coding agent and instant-backend platform that lets indie builders, small teams, and non-technical creators ship full-stack, AI-powered web applications from natural-language prompts. It began as a developer-focused AI search engine and was rebuilt as Devv 2.0 into a no-code app builder with a three-step workflow. The platform pairs code generation with built-in backend integrations — authentication, database, email, LLM chat, image and audio generation — plus third-party connectors such as OpenRouter, Replicate, and ElevenLabs, alongside web search and web reader tooling. Devv is a product company rather than a public API provider: it publishes docs, a dated changelog, and an llms.txt, but exposes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or hosted MCP server at this time. Backed by DCM Ventures.

providers.name: Donuts
providers.description: Donuts (now operating as Identity Digital, following the 2022 merger of Donuts Inc. and Afilias) runs the world's largest portfolio of new generic top-level domains (gTLDs) — more than 280 extensions such as .email, .guru, .social, .live, and .restaurant. As a wholesale domain registry it provides DNS infrastructure, domain-name security, premium-domain services, and rights-protection tooling to the accredited registrars and resellers who sell domains to end customers. Its programmatic surface is registry-oriented and partner-facing: an EPP (Extensible Provisioning Protocol) interface for domain provisioning, a HTTP Reports API that delivers weekly domain and billing report files (CSV.gz over HTTP basic auth), and a Registrar Portal. There is no public REST/OpenAPI developer surface.

providers.name: Dylibso
providers.description: Dylibso, Inc. is the company behind Extism, the open-source, cross-language framework for building with WebAssembly (Wasm). Its focus is AI-driven application extensibility: giving developers an off-the-shelf, secure-by-default, fully sandboxed plug-in system that is "just a library import away" and runs almost anywhere, with idiomatic Host SDKs for JavaScript, Python, Rust, Ruby, Go, .NET, PHP, Java, C/C++, OCaml, Haskell, Perl, and Zig. Beyond Extism, Dylibso builds Chicory (a native pure-JVM WebAssembly runtime) and Turbo MCP (formerly mcp.run / XTP), a standards-compliant, self-hosted Model Context Protocol gateway and management platform with OIDC identity integration and audit controls. Dylibso is backed by Felicis.

providers.name: Easol
providers.description: Easol is an experience commerce platform for creators of festivals, adventure and travel operators, entertainment venues, and multi-day events. Its all-in-one system combines a branded website builder, booking and ticketing, packages and upsells, global payments and on-site POS, marketing and CRM, operations analytics, AI support agents, and creator capital/funding, letting experience businesses move beyond rigid legacy ticketing systems and sell and scale on their own platform. Plans range from Easol Stride (from $250/month) to a custom-priced Easol Pro tier. Easol does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its public commercial, support, security, and status surfaces, and is backed by Tiger Global.

providers.name: Electric
providers.description: Electric (Electric AI) is an IT and security management platform for small and medium-sized businesses, consolidating device management, application and SaaS management, security posture monitoring with automatic remediation, and employee onboarding/offboarding into a single platform that requires no in-house IT skills and syncs with HR systems. Founded in New York and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Electric bundles partner tooling (JumpCloud MDM/SSO, Keeper, ThreatDown, Harmony Email, Perimeter81 VPN, Drata) behind an AI-powered IT Hub, help desk, and hardware procurement service. It is not a developer-API company: there is no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company and enriched from Electric's public web surface.

providers.name: Fifth Dimension
providers.description: Fifth Dimension AI is a London-based decision intelligence platform for real-assets investors and asset managers. Its AI co-worker, Ellie, automates document-heavy real estate workflows — deal screening, underwriting, due diligence, and lease and investment analysis — by reading email bodies and PDF attachments and returning transparent, sourced, auditable reasoning rather than black-box answers. Founded in 2023 by Johnny Morris and Dr. Kate Jarvis, the platform integrates with existing property management, CRM, data room, and financial systems and preserves each fund's institutional knowledge and investment criteria. The company is backed by HV Capital, Seedcamp, Speedinvest and Anthemis, and raised a $26M Series A in 2026.

providers.name: Firecamp
providers.description: Firecamp is an open-source API development platform for designing, testing, and documenting REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket APIs. It provides multi-protocol playgrounds (REST, GraphQL, WebSocket, SocketIO), team collaboration in shared workspaces, API collection management, a test runner, and CLI/CI-CD integration. Firecamp does not expose a public consumer API; it is a tooling product for working with other APIs.

providers.name: Frame Security
providers.description: Frame Security is an AI-powered human risk management and security awareness platform that defends organizations against human-targeted attacks such as phishing, deepfakes, and social engineering. Frame generates personalized security awareness training in 70+ languages, hyper-realistic email, voice, and video phishing and deepfake simulations built from an organization's own context, employee risk scoring with targeted interventions, automated phishing triage of reported suspicious emails, and cross-platform reporting and integrations. The company is backed by Index Ventures and raised a $50M round in 2026.

providers.name: Glowforge
providers.description: Glowforge is a Seattle-based consumer hardware company that makes desktop 3D laser printers (Glowforge Pro, Plus, Aura, and Spark) which cut and engrave materials such as wood, acrylic, leather, fabric, and paper. The machines are cloud-connected: designs are prepared in the browser-based Glowforge App (app.glowforge.com) and sent to the printer over the internet, with camera-based material placement, autofocus, and an online design catalog and marketplace. Glowforge does not publish a public developer API; its developer-facing footprint is limited to open-source GPL firmware and kernel components on GitHub (published for license compliance) and a public system status page.

providers.name: Helsing
providers.description: Helsing SE is a Munich-based European defense AI company founded in March 2021 by Torsten Reil, Gundbert Scherf, and Niklas Köhler. Helsing builds AI software and autonomous weapons systems for European and allied militaries — reconnaissance-strike software (Altra), electronic-warfare AI (Cirra), an AI fighter pilot (Centaur), loitering-munition strike drones (HF-1 and HX-2), an autonomous combat aircraft (CA-1 Europa), and underwater autonomy (Lura acoustic processing, SG-1 Fathom long-endurance underwater drones). The company is sales-led and government-restricted; there is no public REST API or developer portal. This profile documents the publicly visible product surfaces and partnerships rather than endpoint shapes. Funding totals roughly €1.37B across four rounds, with a $1.2B Series E at an $18B valuation reportedly being finalized as of May 2026. Daniel Ek's Prima Materia is the largest shareholder. Public partnerships include Saab (Gripen E integration of Centaur, including the 2025 Project Beyond combat trial), Airbus, Rheinmetall, the Bundeswehr, and the Eurofighter Typhoon EK programme.

providers.name: HireVue
providers.description: HireVue is an AI-driven hiring platform built around video interviewing, conversational AI, structured assessments, automated scheduling, and an AI Hiring Agent. The platform plugs into the major ATS systems (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle/Taleo, iCIMS, Greenhouse, SmartRecruiters, PageUp, Cornerstone, Avature, Oleeo, BrassRing) and exposes REST APIs and webhooks to customers and certified partners via the HireVue developer portal at developer.hirevue.com. At the time of this profile the public developer portal was not responding to crawl, so APIs are listed at the product/capability level and the developer portal URL is captured as the canonical reference.

providers.name: Hopstack
providers.description: Hopstack is an AI-native, cloud-based warehouse management system (WMS) and fulfillment operations platform that helps warehouses, 3PLs, and e-commerce operators optimize inbound logistics, inventory, order processing, picking, packing, shipping, and returns across channels. Hopstack exposes a documented RESTful API (referenced at apidocs.hopstack.io) for programmatic access to core resources such as orders and consignments, secured with a per-user X-API-Key generated from the Hopstack Dashboard. API access is gated - a customer must contact Hopstack Support to enable API-key generation in the UI - and the full endpoint surface, base URL, and machine-readable specification are published behind that account/partner reference rather than as a fully open catalog.

providers.name: JOLT
providers.description: JOLT is a Sydney-headquartered electric vehicle charging network operator that builds and runs free-to-start kerbside DC fast chargers across Australia, and has since extended the same model into New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States. Its charge points deliver the first 7kWh of each day's charging at no cost — around 45km of range in roughly 15 minutes over CCS2 or CHAdeMO — funded not by the driver but by the digital out-of-home advertising screens mounted on the charger itself, which makes JOLT simultaneously a charge point operator and a media network selling audience reach to advertisers. It sits in the energy value chain as a downstream infrastructure and demand-side player: it buys electricity (claiming 100% GreenPower green-certified wind and solar), owns and operates the charging assets on public and retail land in partnership with governments and hosts such as Transport for NSW, Ausgrid and major grocery retailers, and monetises the dwell time rather than the kilowatt-hour. Its API posture is honestly closed. JOLT publishes no developer programme, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no open data feed; the only public HTTP surfaces on its domains are a marketing WordPress install (whose custom jolt/v1 REST namespace exposes a single VAT form endpoint) and an api.joltcharge.com host that serves a static redirect to the mobile app rather than any API. It is not a designated data holder under the Australian Consumer Data Right for energy — it does not appear in the CDR Register's energy data holder brands — so the CDR energy mandate that compels Australian electricity retailers to expose standardised usage and tariff data does not reach it, and no OCPP, OCPI, ISO 15118 or Green Button/ESPI conformance is published. All customer charging data, session history and audience analytics are reachable only through the JOLT consumer app or a sales conversation.

providers.name: Jules
providers.description: Jules is Google's autonomous, asynchronous AI coding agent, developed inside Google Labs and powered by the Gemini family of models (currently Gemini 2.5 Pro on the free tier and Gemini 3 Pro on paid tiers). Jules connects to a user's GitHub repositories, clones the target repo into a sandboxed Google Cloud VM, generates a multi-step plan, and then executes coding tasks such as bug fixes, refactors, dependency bumps, test authoring, and small feature builds, ultimately opening a pull request for human review. Jules ships three surfaces beyond the web app at jules.google.com: a documented REST API in alpha at jules.googleapis.com/v1alpha (Sources, Sessions, Activities) authenticated via X-Goog-Api-Key, a lightweight CLI called Jules Tools installable via npm, and a Gemini CLI extension that exposes Jules as a /jules slash command. Access is gated to Google account holders and the API is experimental. Jules is sold as part of the Google AI subscription bundles, with a free introductory plan (15 tasks/day, 3 concurrent), Google AI Pro at $19.99/month (100 tasks/day, 15 concurrent, Gemini 3 Pro), and Google AI Ultra at $124.99/month (300 tasks/day, 60 concurrent, priority Gemini 3 Pro access).

providers.name: Latenode
providers.description: Latenode is an enterprise-grade low-code integration and AI automation platform with prebuilt SaaS integrations and native access to top-tier LLMs. It combines the ease of no-code tools with the flexibility of low-code development for building automated workflows. Latenode supports inbound webhooks and JavaScript-based custom logic within scenarios but does not currently publish a public OpenAPI specification for an external REST API.

providers.name: Latent
providers.description: Latent (Latent Health) is an enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform for health systems, built around a clinical agentic engine that reads the chart, reasons over payer policy and drug labels, and acts inside the electronic health record. The platform spans four modules — Identify (care-gap identification, eligibility screening, site-of-care routing), Access (prior authorization, clinical review, appeals generation, benefit routing, payer outreach), Capture (340B eligibility auditing, leakage analytics, financial dashboards), and Engage (patient outreach, queue management, outcomes analytics). Latent is chart-native and EHR agnostic, integrating with Epic, Cerner and others, and is used by more than 45 health systems including Ochsner Health, MetroHealth, Yale New Haven Health, St. Luke's Health System and Henry Ford Health, serving over two million patients annually. Founded by Sriram Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, the company has raised $80M from Spark Capital, Transformation Capital, McKesson Ventures, Conviction, General Catalyst and Y Combinator. Latent publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its integration surface is delivered through EHR-native deployment with health-system customers, and its security posture is published on a Vanta-hosted trust center with HIPAA-compliant data handling.

providers.name: Librato
providers.description: Librato was a hosted metrics, monitoring and analytics service for operational data — time-series measurements, tagged metrics, dashboards ("spaces"), charts, annotations, alerts and notification services — delivered as a developer-first SaaS with a JSON REST API at metrics-api.librato.com/v1. Backed by Cowboy Ventures among others, the San Francisco company was acquired by SolarWinds in 2015 for a reported $40 million, and its metrics platform was folded into SolarWinds AppOptics — released in November 2017 — which has itself since reached end of life. The librato.com domain and every product subdomain (metrics., status., www.) now 301-redirect to the SolarWinds AppOptics end-of-life notice, the metrics-api.librato.com API host no longer resolves in DNS, and the github.com/librato organization was archived on 2024-01-02. This profile is retained as a historical record of a well-regarded developer API: the API reference source, the first-party Ruby, Python, Java and Node client libraries and the collection agents remain publicly archived and are catalogued here. The successor product is SolarWinds Observability SaaS.

providers.name: Lily AI
providers.description: Lily AI, Inc. is a retail product-intelligence company whose platform, Lily Max, enriches e-commerce product catalogs so that products are legible to advertising platforms, search engines, onsite search, and AI shopping agents. Agents identify gaps in a retailer's product data, generate consumer-centric attributes and copy, run controlled tests against a holdout, and deploy the winning enrichments across Google Merchant Center feeds, Meta Commerce Manager catalogs, AI discovery and agentic commerce surfaces, and onsite PDP, search, and faceting. Lily AI sells to enterprise retailers, brands, and agencies and positions itself as a layer over the existing commerce stack rather than a replacement for a PIM or feed manager. The company raised a $25M Series B with participation from Canaan Partners, Conductive Ventures, Sorenson Ventures, and NEA. As of this enrichment pass Lily AI publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or GitHub organization; the platform is delivered as a managed enterprise service with onboarding handled through sales.

providers.name: Mattilda
providers.description: Mattilda is a financial management platform for private educational institutions across Latin America, operating in Mexico, Colombia, and Ecuador. It automates tuition collection and payment processing, offers tuition advances that guarantee schools receive full monthly tuition on the first day regardless of family payment rates, and provides academic operations and admissions tools under its Algebraix product line. Families can pay through multiple channels, including WhatsApp. Mattilda operates under the oversight of Mexico's financial authorities CNBV and CONDUSEF and is backed by QED Investors. Mattilda does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation portal; this profile captures the company's public identity, status page, and Vanta-hosted trust center.

providers.name: MentorCloud
providers.description: MentorCloud is an AI-enabled, enterprise mentoring software platform that helps organizations optimize employee engagement, retention, and career development through structured mentoring programs. It serves HR and Learning & Development teams and enterprise leaders looking to scale human-led learning across engineering, management, higher education, hospitality, and non-profit contexts. The platform covers mentor/mentee matching, program management, sessions, circles, learning, and community, with use cases spanning new-hire onboarding, leadership development, career progression, and Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) initiatives. MentorCloud is delivered as a hosted B2B SaaS product with managed, custom two-way integrations to enterprise CRM, HR, and single sign-on systems rather than a self-serve public developer API. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mihup
providers.description: Mihup is an enterprise Voice AI and speech analytics platform founded in 2016 and headquartered in Kolkata, India. Its full-stack voice AI (ASR, NLU, TTS, analytics) powers four products: Interaction Analytics (MIA) for 100% call auditing, Voice Agent (MVA) for inbound/outbound call automation, Agent Assist (MAA) for real-time live-agent guidance, and Automotive Voice Agent (AVA) for in-car assistants in software-defined vehicles. Proprietary phoneme-based (G2P) recognition supports 120+ languages, accents and dialects including 20+ Indian languages and code-mixed Hinglish. Mihup runs in 1.5M+ cars, processes 5M+ interactions daily, and is trusted by 500+ businesses including Tata Motors, SBI Life and IDFC FIRST Bank. ISO 27001 certified, DPDP Act 2023 and RBI data-localization compliant, hosted in AWS Mumbai. Mihup exposes APIs and SDKs for IVI systems, chipsets, telecom stacks and CRMs, but publishes no public developer portal — access is enterprise/demo-gated.

providers.name: MotherDuck
providers.description: MotherDuck is a serverless cloud data warehouse built on DuckDB. Connectivity is via DuckDB clients (Python, Node.js, Wasm, Go, JDBC) using access tokens or SSO; the service does not publicly document a separate REST management API.

providers.name: Motion
providers.description: Motion is a creative analytics platform for performance marketing and creative teams, headquartered in Toronto and founded in 2021 by Reza Khadjavi, Alexander Sloan, and David Berglas. Motion connects a brand's Meta, TikTok, YouTube, and LinkedIn ad accounts — plus Google Analytics 4 and Northbeam attribution — into a single command center where marketers and agencies identify which creative elements drive performance, run comparative and launch analysis, auto-tag ads with AI across multiple dimensions, and research competitor ads via its Inspo tool. The company also offers Runneth by Motion, an AI layer for marketing. Motion serves 2,100+ teams analyzing over $14B in annual ad spend and is backed by Threshold Ventures, Inovia Capital, Headline, Abstract Ventures, and Sugar Capital. Motion does not currently publish a public developer API; it integrates into ad and attribution platforms as an OAuth data consumer.

providers.name: MyTime
providers.description: MyTime is an all-in-one business management platform for retail service chains and franchises, combining point-of-sale (POS), online appointment scheduling, integrated payments, customer management, inventory, staff and payroll tools, loyalty, reputation management, and marketing automation across single- and multi-location operations. It serves beauty salons, barbershops, pet grooming, wellness spas, and learning services, offering omnichannel booking (web, Google Reserve, Instagram/Facebook, ClassPass) and analytics. MyTime runs a first-party API host (api.mytime.com) that backs its web and native iPhone/Android apps, and offers partner integrations (Stripe, QuickBooks, Shopify, ADP, Zapier), but does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI definition. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Palm HR
providers.description: Palm HR (palm.hr, operating on palmhr.net) is an HR management and payroll platform built specifically for the UAE and broader MENA region, trusted by organizations from startups to enterprises for local labor-law and WPS compliance. The platform spans people management (employee profiles, onboarding and offboarding, document management), attendance and time tracking (mobile check-in/out, timesheets, shift scheduling, project time), payroll automation (WPS-compliant processing, expenses, loans, multi-country and multi-currency), performance management, and recruiting, plus an outsourced-HR service. Palm HR exposes REST APIs with API keys carrying granular permissions so customers can push data to ERPs and external tools, and ships prebuilt integrations with accounting suites (Xero, QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Wafeq, Qoyod, Odoo, Tally), biometric devices (ZKTeco, CAMS), and automation platforms (Zapier, Make, Power Automate). The company is a portfolio company of Speedinvest. This profile was enriched from public web surfaces; no public OpenAPI specification or developer portal was discovered.

providers.name: Pantomath
providers.description: Pantomath is an AI-powered Data Operations Center that monitors, manages, and automatically resolves issues across an organization's entire data analytics ecosystem. The platform combines 24/7 automated data monitoring, cross-platform data lineage and impact analysis, AI-driven incident detection, and autonomous root-cause analysis and remediation to deliver full self-resolution of issues across the data stack. Pantomath integrates with 60+ platforms spanning data warehouses (Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks), orchestration (Airflow, dbt, Astronomer), integration (Fivetran, Informatica, Matillion), BI/reporting (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Sigma), and notification channels (Slack, Teams, PagerDuty). It exposes a first-party API-key-authenticated ingestion API and a published JavaScript SDK for sending custom real-time job and dataset logs. Backed by General Catalyst (Series B, $30M) and Snowflake Ventures.

providers.name: Paradox
providers.description: Paradox builds Olivia, a conversational AI assistant for high-volume hiring. The platform is delivered as a suite of "Conversational" products - ATS, CRM, Career Sites, Apply, Scheduling, and Events - and ships pre-built integrations for Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, and Indeed plus an Open API for custom partner integrations with systems like iCIMS, Greenhouse, and others. Paradox is sales-led; APIs are made available to enterprise customers and certified partners under contract rather than via a public self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Parspec
providers.description: Parspec is an AI-native platform for electrical, lighting, and MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) distributors and manufacturer rep agencies in the construction supply chain. It consolidates fragmented, manual workflows into one system covering quoting for complex projects, automated submittal and O&M document creation, project management (orders, fulfillment, billing), and sales management, with ERP integrations (Epicor Eclipse, Epicor Prophet 21, SAP). Parspec is SOC 2 Type II attested and markets itself to help distributors and rep agencies bid more, win more, and improve profitability. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: PokéAPI GraphQL
providers.description: GraphQL beta endpoint for PokéAPI providing Hasura-powered queries over the complete Pokémon database including species, moves, abilities, items, evolutions, and game version data.

providers.name: RapidFort
providers.description: RapidFort is a software supply chain security platform focused on container hardening and automated CVE remediation. Its platform analyzes container vulnerabilities across build and runtime, profiles what software actually executes, and removes unused components to shrink the attack surface - remediating up to 95% of CVEs without code changes. RapidFort publishes a registry of 9,000+ near-zero-CVE curated container images and malware-scanned open-source libraries, and its CART capability automates compliance validation and remediation reporting for programs such as FedRAMP, cATO, CMMC, NIS2, and SOC 2. The company operates its platform through a hosted web application and a command-line workflow (analyze, profile, harden), with an open-source community-images catalog and the Kimia Kubernetes-native OCI image builder published on GitHub.

providers.name: Rocket Lab
providers.description: Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq RKLB) is an end-to-end space company providing launch services, spacecraft, satellite components, and on-orbit services. Its Electron rocket is the world's most frequently launched orbital small launch vehicle; the medium-lift Neutron rocket is in development. Rocket Lab Space Systems supplies Photon spacecraft, reaction wheels, star trackers, solar arrays, propulsion, separation systems, and composite structures to civil, national security, and commercial customers. Rocket Lab does not currently offer a public developer API.

providers.name: Score
providers.description: Score is an open-source, platform-agnostic workload specification developed under the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox program. It provides a developer-centric YAML specification that enables teams to define application workloads once and deploy them across multiple container platforms including Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and cloud runtimes without environment-specific configuration drift. The score-spec organization provides reference CLI implementations (score-compose and score-k8s) that translate Score YAML into platform-specific manifests, eliminating YAML bloat and reducing cognitive load for platform engineering teams.

providers.name: Sportwey
providers.description: Sportwey is a Mexican SaaS platform that digitizes and automates the operations of sports organizations across multiple segments — tournaments and leagues, training academies, and sports facilities. It provides team management, scheduling, results and statistics, attendance and membership tracking, payments, class scheduling, court and field reservations, and referee coordination. The company reports more than 10,000 organizers and 2.3 million players using the platform, delivered through dedicated player and referee apps and a manager back office. Sportwey is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Structure
providers.description: Structure (Structure Financial Inc.) is a Web3 platform for designing, backtesting, and deploying fully automated, permissionless crypto trading strategies without writing code. Its visual strategy editor and AI-assisted code generation let users build algorithmic strategies that compile to Rust and deploy non-custodially to decentralized exchanges including Hyperliquid, Drift, and Jupiter; strategies receive trading-only permissions so funds never leave the user's vault. The company documents live, paper, and backtest execution paths and references MCP-agent and code-based access alongside its no-code visual interface. Founded by MIT and Jump Trading alumni and backed by the investors behind Coinbase and Solana.

providers.name: Superside
providers.description: Superside is an always-on, AI-powered creative-as-a-service (CaaS) company that helps enterprises and high-growth brands scale their in-house creative teams with top global talent and industry-leading AI workflows. It delivers graphic and brand design, ad creative and digital campaigns, social media creative, presentation design, illustration, web design and Webflow development, video production and motion graphics, AI-enhanced creative, packaging and print, email design, and 3D/AR design. Superside serves 400+ major brands via a subscription and dedicated-team model. The company operates a marketing website and a customer application (app.superside.com) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its public web, legal, and operational-transparency surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sword Health
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital musculoskeletal (MSK) and virtual physical-therapy company that pairs licensed clinicians with an AI Care platform (programs including Thrive for MSK, Bloom for pelvic and women's health, Move, and Mind for mental health, with the Phoenix AI care specialist and the Sword Intelligence division). Founded in Portugal in 2015, it sells to employers, health plans, and governments rather than to individual developers. As of this enrichment pass Sword Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; its digital surface is member/clinician apps and employer client portals. Real public surfaces captured here are its trust center (SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR), legal pages, newsroom, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Table22
providers.description: Table22 is a subscription commerce and growth platform built specifically for food & beverage businesses. It enables restaurants, wine shops, wineries, butchers, bakeries, specialty grocers, and retailers to launch and grow subscriptions, clubs, memberships, pre-orders, and product drops that generate predictable recurring revenue beyond their four walls. The full-service platform combines branded storefronts, an order management system, white-glove fulfillment coordination, automated lifecycle marketing and CRM, five-star consumer support, and AI tools for hospitality. Over 1,000 merchants across 40 U.S. states use Table22, representing $100M+ in revenue impact. Pricing is success-based (15% revenue share, no upfront or setup fees). Table22 is a sales-led SaaS with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, website surface, and machine-readable llms.txt.

providers.name: The Travelers Companies
providers.description: The Travelers Companies, Inc. (NYSE: TRV) is a leading United States property and casualty (P&C) insurance carrier providing auto, home, and business insurance to individuals, agencies, businesses, government units, and associations. Travelers is a component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average, generated approximately $48.83 billion in revenue in 2025, holds roughly $143.7 billion in total assets, and employs approximately 34,000 people plus 15,000 independent agents and brokers across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Republic of Ireland. The company operates through three reportable segments — Business Insurance, Bond & Specialty Insurance, and Personal Insurance — distributing primarily through a network of independent agents and brokers, and through direct-to-consumer channels for segments of its personal lines. Travelers has a developer portal at developer.travelers.com that surfaces APIs intended for appointed agents, agency-management-system (AMS) vendors, and integration partners; the portal is gated (Salesforce Experience Cloud) and individual API specifications, endpoints, and pricing are not publicly published. The company also publishes the IntelliDrive and IntelliDrivePlus telematics mobile apps used to score personal-auto driving behavior for rating credits.

providers.name: Themis
providers.description: Themis (askthemis.com) is a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) SaaS platform positioned as a "compliance collaboration" tool that streamlines partnerships between companies and their vendors, banks, credit unions, and fintechs by accelerating onboarding, due diligence, and risk assessments. The platform bundles modules for policies, procedures, documents, vendor and risk management, risk register, control mapping, issue and change management, complaints, QA testing, training, audit, key risk indicators (KRI), FINRA 4530, and conflicts of interest. Themis serves banking, payments, lending, crypto/DeFi, exchanges, BaaS, and credit-card sectors, and is used through a hosted web application at portal.askthemis.com. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public or developer API surface. Themis is a portfolio company of Felicis.

providers.name: Tink
providers.description: Tink (a Visa company) is a European open-banking platform offering account aggregation, payment initiation, identity, and KYC products across 3,400+ banks. The Tink API exposes Account Check, Account Aggregation, Income Check, Risk Insights, Money Manager, and Payments products under a single OAuth-protected REST surface at api.tink.com.

providers.name: TravelJoy
providers.description: TravelJoy is software for travel advisors and agencies — a client CRM, itinerary and proposal builder, secure payment collection, forms and questionnaires, and automated client communication combined in one platform. Travel professionals use it to manage trips, capture and nurture leads, send branded proposals, gather traveler details, and collect payments. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass TravelJoy publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK program; this profile tracks its identity and public web properties for discovery.

providers.name: Unframe AI
providers.description: Unframe AI is an enterprise AI platform (Unframe AI OS) that assembles production-ready AI solutions from modular building blocks — an Agent Orchestrator, Knowledge Fabric, AI-native Data Store, and Voice Agents — so companies can deploy agentic AI across unstructured data, cross-system workflows, and legacy systems without rebuilding core software. Deployments run in cloud, private VPC, or fully on-premises, are model-agnostic, and are governed with RBAC, SSO, lineage tracking, and audit logs. Founded by Shay Levi, Larissa Schneider, and Adi Azarya, with offices in Cupertino, Tel Aviv, and Berlin; backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and others; acquired Swish AI. Sales-led platform with no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: UnitedMasters
providers.description: UnitedMasters is an independent music distribution platform founded by Steve Stoute in 2017 and backed by Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and Apple. Artists distribute music to 150+ streaming services while keeping full ownership of their master recordings, with real-time royalty payouts, Blueprint AI artist development tools, analytics, and brand and sync licensing partnerships with the NBA, ESPN, TikTok, and other major brands. UnitedMasters does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Vesence
providers.description: Vesence builds agentic AI for professional-services firms that works directly inside Microsoft Office. Its agents operate in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, plus a web app, reviewing emails, documents and projects before they leave the firm and turning Microsoft Word into a purpose-built workspace for high-stakes drafting, quality assurance and knowledge work. Vesence connects to SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, Teams and document-management systems so agents work with a firm's existing files and context, with every edit traceable through tracked changes. Trusted by law firms, banks and investors, Vesence targets transactional legal work such as fund formation, M&A and corporate matters. It is a Y Combinator-backed startup surfaced through the venture portfolios of Creandum and Emergence Capital.

providers.name: Biomodal
providers.description: Biomodal (formerly Cambridge Epigenetix) is a Cambridge, UK genomics and epigenetics company whose duet multiomics solutions capture genetic and epigenetic information from a single low-input DNA sample in one experiment, giving researchers access to the six-base genome (the four canonical bases plus 5-methylcytosine and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine). Its products include the duet multiomics solution evoC and duet +modC library-prep assays, the biomodal CLI and duet post-sequencing pipeline (alignment, methylation quantification, and variant calling), and the modality XPLR analysis software. The technology is applied to cancer and liquid-biopsy research, neurodegenerative disease, aging, precision medicine, and non-invasive prenatal testing. Biomodal is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences provider profile.

providers.name: Bloomfilter
providers.description: Bloomfilter is a process intelligence platform that gives enterprises end-to-end visibility, traceability, and control over how AI agents and humans execute software delivery work. It unifies data across development and design tools such as Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, and Figma into a structured, AI-enabled data stream and builds a connected process graph across the software development lifecycle. Teams use Bloomfilter to govern hybrid human-agent workflows through process mining, compliance monitoring, cycle-time analysis, and performance measurement, so leaders can see how work actually flows and where value is created or lost. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: Concourse
providers.description: Concourse builds AI agents for corporate finance teams. Concourse connects natively to financial and operational systems including QuickBooks, NetSuite, Ramp, Snowflake, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, Brex, Rippling, Gusto, BigQuery, and Databricks, and says it cuts manual finance work by over 75%. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and backed by CRV, raising a $12M Series A alongside general availability. providers.name: easyJet
providers.description: easyJet Airline Company Limited is a British low-cost short-haul carrier registered in England (company number 03034606, registered office Hangar 89, London Luton Airport, Luton, Bedfordshire, LU2 9PF), flying a point-to-point network that its own trade pages describe as connecting more than 155 airports across 35 countries. Its home market is the United Kingdom and its commercial centre of gravity is intra-European leisure and short-haul business traffic, extended by the easyJet holidays package business and by ancillary products (seat selection, hold and large cabin bags, Flex, Pass Extra, Smart+, Inclusive and Inclusive Plus fare bundles). easyJet sits at the direct end of the airline distribution chain. It was built without a GDS dependency and still sells the overwhelming majority of its seats through its own website and app; agency and OTA access exists but is a controlled secondary channel rather than the primary rail. That channel is governed by a published Distribution Charter (version March 2026) which permits a Reseller to access easyJet Data in exactly two ways — "via an easyJet Approved Channel which has entered into an API agreement with easyJet" or "directly via the easyJet API, if the Reseller has a Direct API Agreement with easyJet" — and which explicitly forbids screen scraping and any other automated extraction. easyJet publishes the list of Approved Channels and a per-partner functionality matrix current to the end of May 2026: Amadeus, Anaxys, Bewotec, Duffel, JFA Systems, Kyte, Paxport, Peakwork, Sabre, Travelfusion, Travelport, Traveltek, Viaxoft and Ypsilon. Its API posture, stated honestly, is commercial-agreement-gated and undocumented. There is no developer portal — developer, developers, docs, apis, ndc, partner, partners, trade, agent, sandbox, dev, portal, connect and xml subdomains of easyjet.com all fail to resolve — and no machine-readable contract of any kind is published: no OpenAPI, no Swagger, no AsyncAPI, no GraphQL schema, no security.txt, no llms.txt and no .well-known API catalogue. Two real API hostnames do exist, api.easyjet.com and b2b.easyjet.com, but both sit behind Akamai and return HTTP 403 Access Denied on every path probed. Just as importantly, easyJet is not an NDC carrier: the March 2026 charter never mentions NDC, easyJet does not appear on ndctracker.com's list of 73 airlines with launched or in-development NDC programmes, and its aggregators describe the connection as a direct-connect API rather than an NDC one — Duffel labels it "Direct Connect". A reseller therefore integrates against a bilateral, proprietary, unpublished interface under an English-law contract that easyJet may amend without notice and under which it reserves the right to restrict, suspend or terminate access and to cancel bookings already made. A second enrichment pass on 2026-07-28 did find one live, anonymously reachable easyJet integration surface the first pass missed: the easyWidget / easyDom partner component platform at brand.easyjet.com, a hosted JavaScript widget service that partner and white-label sites embed for easyJet page chrome and for easyJet customer sign-in, registration and visitor recognition. It is undocumented, partner-scoped by a query-string partner identifier and built on legacy jQuery, but it is real and it is the only easyJet interface that answers a stranger with a 200. The REST hostnames stay closed, and this record stays honest about the difference: only what can be verified is catalogued, and an Akamai-gated hostname is still not listed as an API.

providers.name: Essex Open Data
providers.description: Essex Open Data is a local council open-data portal for United Kingdom running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately an open datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Fullseam
providers.description: FullSeam builds AI agents for corporate accounting and finance operations teams, automating the manual work that happens outside traditional accounting software. Its agents handle accounts receivable (following up on payments, generating requested documentation, and entering invoices into customer AP portals), accounts payable (extracting invoices from multiple sources, matching them against purchase orders and contracts, chasing vendors for missing information, and categorizing expenses before posting to the general ledger), cash application, and reconciliation. FullSeam integrates with existing systems including QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Sage, Bill, Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, and PandaDoc rather than requiring a platform migration, flagging exceptions with full context for human review and maintaining audit logs for compliance. Founded by the team behind TaxProper (acquired by Opendoor), FullSeam is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company.

providers.name: Halo Investing
providers.description: Halo Investing is a Chicago-based financial technology company that operates a marketplace for "protective investments" — structured notes, multi-manager structured note SMAs, buffered ETFs, annuities and insurance — connecting financial advisors, RIAs and financial institutions with more than 40 global banking and insurance issuers. Founded in 2015 by Biju Kulathakal and Jason Barsema, the platform lets advisors analyze, customize, price, execute and then monitor outcome-based products from a single dashboard, with tools such as the Aura portfolio simulator and an asset allocation framework for structured notes. Halo reports more than $45.5B in transactions since 2015 and employs 100+ people. Its affiliate Halo Securities LLC is an SEC-registered broker-dealer and a member of FINRA/SIPC, acting as distributor and selling agent for structured note products. The advisor platform at notes.haloinvesting.com is entirely authenticated behind a login. As of this profiling pass Halo Investing publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK, CLI, MCP server or A2A agent card; advisor-side API integration is offered through the third-party Schwab OpenView Gateway rather than a Halo-published API.

providers.name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
providers.description: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem (HUJI) is Israel's leading research university, ranked #272 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates multiple campuses in Jerusalem, Rehovot, and Eilat across the humanities, sciences, medicine, and law. HUJI does not publish a dedicated public developer portal or documented open API program. Its developer-relevant surface is limited to standards-based academic infrastructure: an Ex Libris Primo/Alma library discovery system (whose APIs require institution-issued keys), the OpenScholar profile/CMS platform, Shibboleth/SAML single sign-on (internal/gated), and a number of research-lab open-source GitHub organizations. No public, self-service API endpoints were confirmed.

providers.name: Indian Institute of Technology Madras
providers.description: Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) is a public technical and research university in Chennai, India, ranked #227 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates an institutional website (iitm.ac.in), a central library with electronic databases, a large online BS degree program in Data Science and Applications, and SSO/OAuth2-based identity endpoints. As of this review IIT Madras does not publish a public, documented developer portal or open API program. Its official GitHub organization exists but currently exposes no public repositories. The properties cataloged below reflect only publicly confirmed institutional web properties and identity endpoints, not documented third-party APIs.

providers.name: InvestaX
providers.description: InvestaX is a Singapore-based, MAS-licensed tokenization platform for real-world assets (RWAs), operated by IC SG Pte. Ltd. under a Capital Markets Services license (CMS100635) and a Recognised Market Operator license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The platform provides end-to-end infrastructure for the issuance, distribution, secondary trading, and custody of security tokens and tokenized securities, plus a Tokenization SaaS product for institutional issuers and RWA investment products such as tokenized money market funds and private credit. It supports multiple blockchain protocols including Ethereum, Polygon, BASE, Algorand, Tezos, and Hedera. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Kratix
providers.description: Kratix is an open-source framework for building internal developer platforms using Kubernetes, enabling platform teams to deliver customizable, composable Promises as a Service. Kratix exposes its capabilities through Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions (Promise, Resource, WorkloadGroup, Destination, StateStore) rather than a traditional HTTP API.

providers.name: LAKRIDS BY BÜLOW
providers.description: LAKRIDS BY BÜLOW is a Danish gourmet liquorice maker founded by Johan Bülow, who opened his first shop in Svaneke on the island of Bornholm on 07.07.2007 and built the brand by cooking liquorice on-site so the aroma drew customers in. Trading as Lakrids by Johan Bülow A/S (CVR 33041586) from Sydholmen 5, 2650 Hvidovre, Denmark, the company makes plain and chocolate-coated liquorice — its flagship being "A - THE ORIGINAL", a gluten-free sweet liquorice core coated in milk chocolate — and sells direct to consumers across Europe alongside concept stores, retail partners and a B2B corporate gifting business. The company operates no public developer program: its storefront runs on the BigCommerce Stencil platform, and the only API surface reachable on its own host is platform-provided and documented by BigCommerce.

providers.name: Maersk
providers.description: A. P. Moller-Maersk is a Danish integrated logistics and container shipping company and one of the world's largest container shipping lines. Maersk operates ocean transport (Maersk Line), port and terminal operations (APM Terminals), supply-chain management, air cargo (Maersk Air Cargo), inland services, and customs solutions, connecting ports across more than 130 countries with end-to-end supply chain offerings. Maersk operates a public developer portal at developer.maersk.com that hosts APIs for shipping customers and partners covering tracking, schedules, rates, bookings, and related logistics workflows.

providers.name: Meshcrafts
providers.description: Meshcrafts, operating publicly as CURRENT (Current Eco AS, formerly Meshcrafts AS, of Oslo, Norway), is a charge point management system (CPMS) provider for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. Its cloud platform lets location owners and charge point operators manage EV charging points, handle payment and invoicing, apply smart energy management and load balancing, and offer white-label charging experiences to drivers. The platform is hardware-agnostic and OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) certified for OCPP 1.6 and OCPP 2.0.1, including Advanced Security, and advertises 99% uptime. Current was the first in the Nordics to reach OCPP 2.0.1 CORE and Advanced Security. The company is backed by 500 Global and surfaced in the API Evangelist network through that portfolio.

providers.name: moodytiger
providers.description: moodytiger is a technology-driven, design-led activewear brand for kids, offering leggings, shorts, tees, skirts and outerwear for boys and girls. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, its direct-to-consumer storefront runs on Shopify at moodytiger.com. The store has no bespoke first-party developer API, but it does expose a modern agent-native commerce surface: a published Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, ucp.dev) MCP shopping endpoint, an /agents.md agent-instructions document mirrored at /llms.txt, and Shopify Customer Account OIDC discovery under /.well-known/. This profile captures those verifiable agent and well-known surfaces.

It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 16,907 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.
