It is one of the largest natural gas producers in the United States, with operations focused on the Marcellus and Utica Shale formations.

providers.name: Apache Groovy
providers.description: Apache Groovy is a powerful, optionally typed and dynamic language, with static-typing and static compilation capabilities, for the Java platform aimed at improving developer productivity thanks to a concise, familiar and easy to learn syntax. It integrates smoothly with any Java program, and immediately delivers powerful features to your application.

providers.name: Apache PySpark
providers.description: Python API for Apache Spark - A unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing supporting batch processing, streaming, machine learning, and graph computing.

providers.name: Autofleet
providers.description: Autofleet is a fleet and mobility optimization platform founded in 2018 in Tel Aviv by Kobi Eisenberg and Dor Shay, and since 2024 an independently operated, wholly owned subsidiary of Element Fleet Management Corp. (TSX: EFN). Its AI-driven software plans, dispatches, routes and simulates vehicle-based operations across postal and parcel delivery, last-mile logistics, rental and car sharing, corporate motor pools, microtransit, NEMT and school transport, taxi and rideshare, field service, and autonomous mobility, in more than 20 countries. The platform is sold as an integration hub — Autofleet markets a public API and webhooks for connecting telematics, GPS, keyless access, maintenance, booking, dispatch, CRM and ERP systems — and adds Nova, a fleet-specific generative AI layer for natural-language operational questions. The API gateway is live at api.autofleet.io, but the developer reference at docs.autofleet.io is a password-protected ReadMe hub, so no machine-readable contract is publicly retrievable.

providers.name: Balancer
providers.description: Balancer is a DeFi AMM and programmable liquidity platform supporting weighted, stable, and custom pools (v2 and v3). Balancer publishes a public GraphQL API at api-v3.balancer.fi for pool, swap, and analytics data, plus per-chain subgraph endpoints. Smart-contract entry points (Vault and Router) are the primary write surface; SDKs wrap the SOR (Smart Order Router) for client-side route construction.

providers.name: Breef
providers.description: Breef is an online agency marketplace and payments platform that connects brands with vetted marketing, creative, digital and web agencies. Founded in New York in 2019 as Curated and rebranded to Breef in 2021, the company is now headquartered in Denver. Brands scope a project on the platform, receive curated pitches from hand-picked agencies across 50+ project types in days rather than months, and then run contracts, milestones and payments through Breef — including Breef(Pay), its agency-now-pay-later payment product. The network spans roughly 25,000 vetted agencies across 27 countries. Breef is a hosted end-user SaaS product: it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or webhook surface.

providers.name: Cadence Solutions
providers.description: Cadence Solutions, Inc. — operating as Cadence — is a New York-based clinical AI and remote patient monitoring company founded in 2020 by Chris Altchek. Cadence partners with large health systems and payers to deliver continuous chronic-care management between clinic visits: FDA-cleared connected devices (blood pressure cuffs, glucometers, weight scales) stream daily vitals to a 24/7 clinical care team backed by supervised AI agents that flag out-of-range readings, close care gaps, and escalate to clinicians for medication titration. The platform covers hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure and COPD, is integrated two-way into partner EHRs (Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth), and supports Medicare RPM/CCM and the CMS ACCESS model. Cadence serves more than 100,000 patients across systems including Community Health Systems, LifePoint Health, Providence, Rush, MemorialCare, Corewell Health, Ardent Health and Duke Health. It raised a $100M Series C led by Spark Capital in June 2026 ($241M total, ~$1.23B valuation). Cadence publishes no public developer program or API: EHR interoperability is delivered as bilateral health system integrations, not a self-serve API surface.

providers.name: ChatGPT Atlas
providers.description: ChatGPT Atlas is OpenAI's Chromium-based AI browser, launched October 21, 2025 for macOS, with Windows, iOS, and Android announced as coming soon. It embeds ChatGPT as a sidebar assistant for page summarization, comparison, and cursor-chat text rewriting, plus an Agent Mode (paid Plus/Pro) that can browse and act on the user's behalf to book hotels, create documents, and run multi-step tasks. Consumer browser product with no publicly documented REST API surface.

providers.name: Cicada
providers.description: Cicada Securities, LLC is a financial technology company revolutionizing the bond markets in Emerging Markets. It operates an Alternative Trading System (ATS) focused on local-currency-denominated government bonds in Mexico (M Bonos, UDI Bonos, and Cetes), enhancing liquidity and facilitating all-to-all access in an anonymous trading environment through central limit orderbook and request-for-quote protocols. Cicada Securities, LLC is an SEC-registered broker-dealer and FINRA member, and Cicada SEF, LLC is an applicant for swap execution facility registration with the CFTC. The company offers a trading platform, live pricing data, and a programmatic API for direct access to LatAm local-currency rates market liquidity, backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Graffer
providers.description: Graffer, Inc. (株式会社グラファー) is a Tokyo-based GovTech and generative-AI company founded in 2017 whose mission is to change behavior and society through the power of products. It operates two pillars: the Graffer Platform, a suite of digital-government services for municipalities and national agencies (Smart Application for online applications, Procedure Guide, Window Reservation, and Graffer Call AI voice guidance), adopted by 179+ Japanese municipalities including Fukuoka, Sapporo, Kyoto, and Oita; and Graffer AI Solution, a generative-AI adoption offering for enterprises (consulting, training, and the Graffer AI Studio product). Graffer also runs the citizen-facing お悩みハンドブック benefits-discovery service and the Govtech Trends media. In 2023 it entered a capital and business alliance with Change Holdings. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Hubble Protocol
providers.description: Hubble Protocol is a Solana-based decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that lets users borrow the USDH stablecoin against multiple crypto collateral assets (SOL, mSOL, stSOL, ETH, BTC and more) with interest-free, fixed-fee loans held open for unlimited time. The protocol pairs a Stability Vault, a Peg Stability Module, a hybrid liquidation model, and native yield on deposited collateral. Developers integrate with Hubble on-chain through its Anchor programs (IDLs published on GitHub) and the open-source "@hubbleprotocol/hubble-sdk" TypeScript client, which exposes borrowing market states, HBB staking and USDH stability-pool data, user loans, treasury and circulating-supply metrics, and peg-stability swaps. Hubble published security audits (Arcadia, Kudelski, Smart State, Sec3) and runs a funded bug-bounty program; its core contributors later built Kamino Finance.

providers.name: Logility
providers.description: Logility is an AI-powered supply chain planning platform providing solutions for demand sensing, inventory optimization, supply planning, S&OP process management, and supply chain analytics. Part of Aptean, Logility serves 600+ clients across 80 countries with capabilities for demand planning, inventory optimization, scenario planning, manufacturing execution, and supplier management across 12+ industry verticals.

providers.name: Nori
providers.description: Nori (Nori Robotics) is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) hard-tech company in San Francisco building affordable bimanual humanoid home robots — the NORI L2, a sub-$1,300 wheeled robot with dual Z-axis lift arms that autonomously handles household chores like loading dishes, making beds, food prep, and cleaning, with multiple units able to collaborate on coordinated tasks. Beyond the hardware, Nori publishes a developer surface: the @nori/sdk robot-local teleoperation SDK connects to a robot over WebRTC to stream video and telemetry and drive it from the browser in ~20 lines, with all safety mechanisms (clamping, watchdog, E-STOP, motor torque lifecycle) enforced on the robot's control daemon. The SDK targets the nori-protocol v1 wire format (NDJSON over a WebRTC data channel to the daemon on port 7777), is Apache-2.0 licensed, and is distributed to a small set of collaborating developers as a tarball rather than on public npm.

providers.name: Ntopology
providers.description: nTop (formerly nTopology) is a computational design software platform for engineering teams building complex, high-performance products. Its parametric, field-driven modeling engine combines geometry, simulation data, and manufacturing constraints so engineers can move from requirements to production-ready designs in a fraction of the traditional time. nTop is used across aerospace and defense, automotive, medical, and industrial energy sectors for lightweighting, lattice and implicit modeling, thermal and structural optimization, and additive manufacturing. nTop also ships nTop Core, a first-party developer library (C++, .NET, and Python) for working with implicit bodies exported from nTop. The company is headquartered in New York City and is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and DCVC.

providers.name: OrderCircle
providers.description: OrderCircle is a B2B wholesale order management software platform, founded in 2015 in San Francisco, that gives fast-growing brands one system to automate wholesale orders, track inventory in real time, generate invoices, and run a self-service B2B eCommerce portal for their buyers. It targets wholesale operations in apparel, coffee, jewelry, food and beverage, hemp, vape, and CBD, and connects to existing tools through pre-built integrations with Shopify, WooCommerce, QuickBooks, Xero, ShipStation, Stripe, Square, PayPal PayFlow, and Authorize.Net. OrderCircle does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; its programmatic surface is limited to its packaged third-party integrations. This profile was seeded as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Pango
providers.description: Pango is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-powered operating system for e-commerce post-purchase and logistics operations. The platform positions itself as an "agentic OS" — autonomous AI agents that handle back-office logistics tasks — and consolidates multi-carrier delivery management, checkout delivery options, branded order tracking, and returns processing into a single unified system. Pango advertises multi-carrier orchestration across 100+ shipping providers with AI-powered routing and rate optimization, self-service return portals with automated approvals, warehouse pick-and-pack automation, and AI agents that resolve exceptions and automate workflows. It integrates with major commerce platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Salesforce Commerce, NetSuite) and 100+ carrier, WMS, marketing, and support partners. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass the company markets an "API-first architecture" but publishes no public developer documentation, API reference, OpenAPI spec, or SDK.

providers.name: Razer
providers.description: Razer is a global lifestyle brand for gamers that designs gaming hardware (Blade laptops, mice, keyboards, headsets and other peripherals), software (Synapse, Cortex) and services. For developers Razer operates the WYVRN immersive gaming platform, exposing the Razer Chroma RGB SDK and REST API for controlling 16.8-million-color lighting across devices, the Razer Sensa HD Haptics and THX Spatial Audio SDKs, Razer ID for user sign-in, and the Razer Gold / Razer Silver virtual-currency payment and rewards APIs for in-app monetization across 34,000+ integrated games and apps.

providers.name: RPM International
providers.description: RPM International Inc. is a multinational specialty coatings and sealants company headquartered in Medina, Ohio, with annual revenues of approximately $7.4 billion. RPM operates a portfolio of over 100 leading brands across three segments: Consumer (Rust-Oleum, DAP, Zinsser), Construction (Tremco, Dryvit, Flowcrete), and Performance Coatings (Carboline, Stonhard, Plasite). RPM International does not currently offer a public developer API, but its subsidiaries and brands serve the construction, maintenance, and protective coatings markets globally.

providers.name: ShiftMed
providers.description: ShiftMed is a McLean, Virginia healthcare workforce technology company operating an on-demand clinician marketplace and AI-powered open shift management platform for hospitals, health systems, skilled nursing facilities and post-acute providers. It matches credentialed W-2 CNAs, LPNs and RNs to open shifts, and markets an API that lets a facility tap that clinician network directly from its own scheduling stack. The API surface reaches customers through workforce-management partner integrations — UKG Pro Workforce Management (formerly UKG Dimensions), symplr Smart Square, QGenda, Smartlinx and Attendance on Demand — alongside file-based SFTP feeds. ShiftMed publishes no public developer portal, documentation, specification or SDK; API access is arranged through a workforce consultation.

providers.name: Smile Digital Health
providers.description: Smile Digital Health (formerly Smile CDR) is a Toronto-based health interoperability software company and the commercial steward of the open source HAPI FHIR project (the world's most widely deployed Java implementation of the HL7 FHIR standard). Its flagship product, Smile CDR — marketed under the broader Smile Omni portfolio as the OmniVera Health Data Platform — is a FHIR-native clinical data repository and integration platform that ingests HL7 v2.x, CDA, CSV, JSON, XML, and FHIR payloads, normalizes them into FHIR (R4, R5, STU3, DSTU2), and exposes them through a hardened FHIR REST API, SMART on FHIR / OAuth2 / OIDC security, Bulk Data export, Subscriptions, MDM, Terminology Services, CQL-based Quality Measures, and a JSON Admin API. The platform is deployed on-prem and across AWS, Azure, and GCP, with HITRUST v9.4, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ONC 2015 Edition certifications, and is used by 190+ global customers, including 30+ US payers running CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (CMS-0057-F) workloads on its CMS Suite. Adjacent Smile Omni product families include OmniCompli (regulatory compliance, including CMS Suite and CMS Concierge), OmniQ (digital quality measures / HEDIS, Intelligence Hub), and OmniConcierge (managed and professional services). The primary developer surface is the FHIR REST API, with per-endpoint auto-generated OpenAPI / Swagger UI at `{baseUrl}/swagger-ui/`, plus a separate JSON Admin API for cluster, module, user, audit, batch job, MDM, and OpenID Connect administration.

providers.name: Trovy
providers.description: Trovy (Trovy Technologies, Inc.) is a Kleiner Perkins-backed fintech building "the homeowner platform" -- consumer credit products that turn home equity into a flexible financial tool. Its flagship Trovy HELOC Card is a credit card powered by home equity with variable APRs as low as 5.99%, alongside the Trovy 1Loan home-equity loan, with preapproval in minutes and rewards, balance-transfer, and payment-calculator features. Trovy is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, docs, or SDK surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Twaice
providers.description: TWAICE (TWAICE Technologies GmbH) is a Munich-based battery analytics software company. Its predictive analytics platform turns BMS data from battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric-vehicle fleets into actionable insights for performance management, warranty management, safety monitoring, digital commissioning, and BESS reporting, alongside a battery simulation model library for engineers. Customers include BESS asset owners and operators, IPPs, utilities, automotive and bus/truck OEMs, and battery manufacturers. TWAICE is ISO 27001 certified, holds the automotive TISAX label, and is backed by investors including Creandum and Speedinvest. It publishes no public API or developer program; the platform is a closed SaaS.

providers.name: Upsolver
providers.description: Upsolver is a cloud data ingestion and lakehouse pipeline company whose SQLake platform lets teams build and deploy high-scale streaming data pipelines using familiar SQL, with automatic schema evolution and Apache Iceberg optimization. Upsolver was acquired by Qlik and the product now continues as Qlik Open Lakehouse; the standalone Upsolver (SQLake) product is legacy, with documentation maintained under Qlik's help site and first-party Python SDK, CLI, and dbt tooling still published on PyPI.

providers.name: VuMedi
providers.description: VuMedi (Vumedi, Inc.) operates a video education platform for physicians and other healthcare professionals. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Oakland, California, with offices in Saint Louis Park, Minnesota and Zagreb, Croatia, the platform aggregates a library of long-form educational videos, webinars, conference coverage and case discussions contributed by key opinion leaders and academic medical centers across more than twenty-five clinical specialties. Physicians use it to watch surgical technique videos, follow live and on-demand webinars, discuss cases with peers and presenters, and stay current on clinical evidence. The company monetizes through industry partnerships with pharmaceutical and medical-device brands rather than a subscription paywall. As of August 2026 VuMedi publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs or MCP server; its public surface is the consumer web application, an iOS app, and a set of static marketing and policy pages.

providers.name: Wheel
providers.description: Wheel is a healthcare technology company providing the infrastructure for modern telehealth. Its Wheel Horizon platform is a modular care-enablement system that combines a nationwide clinician network, evidence-based virtual care programs, and integrated clinical operations so digital health companies, health plans, retailers and pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations can launch and scale virtual care. Wheel also operates WheelX, an enterprise AI health exchange, and Connected Services for integration. Wheel exposes a partner API, governed by an API Terms of Use and gated behind an approval process; the platform is HIPAA compliant and maintains SOC 2 controls. Public API reference documentation, SDKs, and a developer portal are not published. Wheel was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV.

providers.name: Accurx
providers.description: Accurx is a United Kingdom clinical communication and workflow company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, whose software is used across NHS primary care, secondary care, and community and mental health services to message patients, run patient triage, batch-message cohorts, book and remind appointments, and (via its Scribe product) draft clinical notes with AI. Accurx integrates around the NHS as an assured IM1 live supplier, using NHS Digital's interoperability standards for primary care and connecting bi-directionally to the GP clinical-system duopoly (EMIS Health, TPP SystmOne) and Vision, plus NHS national services including the Personal Demographics Service (PDS), NHS Single Sign-On, NHS Login, and the NHS App. Accurx is a consumer and integrator of NHS FHIR and IM1 interfaces rather than a publisher of its own public developer API: as of this review it operates no public developer portal, no self-serve REST/FHIR API, and no downloadable OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement. Third-party and trust integrations are arranged through its partnerships and integration teams under partner agreement.

providers.name: Aiwyn
providers.description: Aiwyn is a practice-automation platform built for modern accounting and CPA firms, unifying payments, practice management, client experience, and tax into a single relationship-centered system. Aiwyn Payments automates invoicing, card and ACH collection, and reconciliation; Aiwyn Practice covers time, billing, project management and resource planning; Aiwyn Experience delivers a unified client portal for engagement letters and secure document exchange; and Aiwyn Tax adds AI-assisted tax preparation. The company serves 800+ firms and raised $113M from KKR and Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company; Aiwyn publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time, so enrichment is limited to identity, its published llms.txt, and probed domain security.

providers.name: Albo
providers.description: Albo (albo.com, formerly albo.mx) is a Mexican digital financial services company founded in 2016 and operating since 2022 as an Institución de Fondos de Pago Electrónico (IFPE) authorized by the Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV) and regulated by Banco de México. Albo ships a mobile-first personal account with a Mastercard debit card — SPEI transfers, bill payments, cash deposit and withdrawal at partner locations, and real-time notifications — alongside "albo empresa", a business account for payroll, employee cards, and bulk dispersion of up to 3,000 transactions at a time. Adjacent credit (abea, by Aureo Lab) and crypto (albit, by Indigo DeFi) products are offered by independent partners. Albo publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog, or sandbox was found on any albo.com, albo.mx or albo.live host.

providers.name: Ancient8
providers.description: Ancient8 is a gaming-focused Ethereum Layer 2 blockchain built on the Optimism OP Stack with Celestia for data availability, designed to power Web3 gaming experiences at scale. The network is EVM-equivalent, so developers deploy Solidity smart contracts and dApps using standard tooling (Hardhat, Remix, thirdweb) against a public Ethereum JSON-RPC interface. Ancient8 Mainnet uses chain ID 888888888 with ETH as its gas currency, complemented by a Celestia-backed testnet, native and third-party bridges (Meson, Relay), block explorers (Routescan, Blockscout/A8Scan), a faucet, staking, and a vault. The programmable surface exposed to integrators is the JSON-RPC endpoint over HTTPS and WebSocket. Backed by Pantera Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from its venture portfolio.

providers.name: Angular 14
providers.description: Angular 14 is a major release of the Angular TypeScript framework from Google, released June 2, 2022. Key features include strictly typed reactive forms, standalone components (developer preview), protected component template members, extended template diagnostics, and improved CLI auto-completion. Angular 14 targets TypeScript 4.7 and ES2020.

providers.name: Angular 15
providers.description: Angular 15 is a major release of the Angular TypeScript framework, released November 16, 2022. Key features include stable standalone components and directives, the new directive composition API, stable NgOptimizedImage for improved image load performance, standalone router APIs with up to 11% bundle size reduction, functional HTTP interceptors, and improved esbuild integration for faster build times.

providers.name: Angular 17
providers.description: Angular 17 is a major release of the Angular TypeScript framework, released November 8, 2023. Key features include stable Signals for reactive state management, deferrable views (@defer blocks) for lazy loading, new built-in control flow syntax (@if, @for, @switch) that is ~30% faster than NgIf/NgFor, improved server-side rendering with non-destructive hydration, View Transitions API support, and a new application builder powered by Vite and esbuild.

providers.name: Angular 18
providers.description: Angular 18 is a major release of the Angular TypeScript framework, released May 22, 2024. Key features include experimental zoneless change detection, stable deferrable views and built-in control flow (@if, @for, @switch), stable Material 3 components, functional route redirects, hybrid change detection with signals, improved Signals APIs, and TypeScript 5.4 support.

providers.name: Angular 20
providers.description: Angular 20 is a major release of the Angular TypeScript framework, released May 28, 2025. All fundamental reactivity primitives (signal, effect, linkedSignal, signal-based queries and inputs) graduate to stable. Zoneless change detection matures significantly. Incremental hydration and route-level render mode graduate to stable. The esbuild/Vite-based builder receives further optimization, and Angular Material aligns more closely with Material Design 3.

providers.name: ANNA Money
providers.description: ANNA Money (a trading name of Absolutely No Nonsense Admin Ltd, company number 10149389, Cardiff, a subsidiary of ANNA Holdings Ltd) is a UK digital business account and tax app for freelancers, startups, and small businesses, positioned as a challenger to the high-street banks. ANNA is not a bank but an e-money proposition: its Mastercard and e-money services are issued by PayrNet Limited, authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority for electronic money service activities (FCA FRN 900594), and its Account Information Services are provided under agency of TrueLayer (FCA FRN 901096). Within UK Open Banking, ANNA is a consumer / third-party provider (TPP) rather than an account-holding ASPSP or a CMA9 mandated bank - it uses TrueLayer's Data and Payments APIs for external account aggregation, automatic VAT calculation, and QR-code "pay by bank" collection. ANNA publishes no public developer portal, no Open Data API, and no OBIE Read/Write (AIS/PIS/CBPII) API surface of its own; its public GitHub organisation hosts open-source engineering tooling (asyncio, aiohttp, and Postgres libraries) rather than product APIs.

providers.name: Astral
providers.description: Astral (Astral Software Inc.) builds high-performance developer tools for the Python ecosystem, written in Rust. Its products are uv, an extremely fast Python package and project manager that replaces pip, pip-tools, pipx, poetry, pyenv, twine, and virtualenv; Ruff, an extremely fast Python linter and code formatter; and ty, a fast Python type checker and language server. Founded by Charlie Marsh (creator of Ruff) and backed by Accel, Caffeinated Capital, and angel investor Guillermo Rauch, Astral ships open-source command-line tooling distributed via PyPI, crates.io, npm, and Homebrew. In March 2026 Astral agreed to join OpenAI as part of the Codex team.

providers.name: AtoB
providers.description: AtoB is a fleet payments platform for the trucking and transportation industry, offering fuel cards, spend-management controls, driver payouts, and trip credit to fleets of every size. Its cards work across a nationwide fuel network with truck-stop discounts, granular purchase controls (fuel-only, category/MCC restrictions, per-transaction and daily limits), telematics-aware fraud prevention, and reporting that supports IFTA fuel-tax and expense compliance. AtoB also runs partner programs for factoring companies, freight brokers, and merchants, and exposes a private Partners API used by telematics and fleet-management integrations (for example Fleetio and Oxmaint) to sync cards, drivers, vehicles, and settled fuel transactions. AtoB was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and General Catalyst; this profile has been enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Automatisch
providers.description: Automatisch is an open source business automation tool and self-hosted alternative to Zapier that connects different services to automate workflows without programming knowledge. Built with JavaScript/Node.js, it supports 100+ integrations including Slack, GitHub, Gmail, PostgreSQL, and AI services. Licensed under AGPL-3.0 for the community edition, with an enterprise edition for commercial deployments.

providers.name: Axial Networks
providers.description: Axial Networks operates Axial (axial.net), a private deal network for mergers, acquisitions and capital raising in the North American lower middle market. Founded in 2010 and based in New York, the platform connects business owners, M&A advisors, private equity buyers, strategic acquirers and lenders around live sell-side and buy-side transactions, and publishes a public member directory, the Middle Market Review editorial forum, industry deal-activity dashboards and business valuation calculators. The member product runs at network.axial.net and product help documentation at guide.axial.net. Axial publishes an llms.txt orientation file for language models and a public status page, but ships no public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer program — the platform is delivered as an authenticated end-user application only.

providers.name: Barn2Door
providers.description: Barn2Door is a Seattle-based commerce and business-management platform purpose-built for independent farmers and local food producers. It gives farms an online store, order and subscription management, inventory tracking, delivery and pickup logistics, integrated payments, and built-in marketing and customer-relationship tools, consolidating the systems a farm needs to sell direct-to-consumer and wholesale into a single dashboard. Barn2Door connects to partners including Mailchimp, QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Avalara, Shippo, Routific, Squarespace, and Facebook, but does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal at this time.

providers.name: Behavox
providers.description: Behavox is an AI-native compliance and conduct-surveillance software company serving the world's leading financial institutions and regulated enterprises. Its Unified AI Controls Platform spans directive, preventive, detective, and corrective controls — including Quantum (voice and text communication surveillance across 50+ languages and 150+ channels), Polaris (trade surveillance), Falcon (insider-threat and human-risk detection), Compass (conflicts of interest and personal account dealing), Atlas (control-room enforcement), Pathfinder (regulatory-change-to-policy), Intelligent Archive, Digital Employees, and Mosaic front-office revenue intelligence. Behavox is backed by Index Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company sells directly to enterprise financial-services customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Bippit
providers.description: Bippit is a UK-based financial wellbeing platform that gives every employee access to personal, qualified financial coaching alongside AI-powered guidance available 24/7, planning and budgeting tools, payroll savings, and educational content and webinars. Sold to employers as a workplace benefit, it also provides organisations with aggregate financial-wellbeing insights and analytics. Bippit is FCA-regulated (No. 845814), ICO-registered (No. ZA533579), ISO 27001:2022 certified, and GDPR / UK DPA 2018 compliant, with data stored in the EEA. Backed by Techstars. Bippit publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and compliance surface.

providers.name: Bureau of Land Management
providers.description: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) is a U.S. government agency responsible for managing vast stretches of public lands across the country, primarily focused on activities like outdoor recreation, livestock grazing, mineral development, and energy production, aiming to sustain the health and diversity of these lands for future generations.

providers.name: City National Bank
providers.description: City National Bank is a national bank chartered in the United States and a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) since 2015, headquartered in Los Angeles, California and known historically as "the bank to the stars" for its deep roots in the entertainment industry. With roughly $98 billion in assets, it is an FDIC-insured, super-regional institution offering personal, business, and private banking, wealth management, treasury management, and capital markets services, with industry expertise across entertainment, healthcare, real estate, technology, and law. City National operates as CN Bank in Florida. It runs NO first-party public developer portal or documented public API: developer.cnb.com and developers.cnb.com do not resolve and api.cnb.com returns 404. Consistent with the voluntary, fragmented US open-finance model, consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a direct City National API. As a covered depository institution it falls under the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule, but no City-National-specific 1033 or FDX participation posture is publicly documented. Its Canadian parent RBC runs a separate developer portal (developer.rbc.com) under a different charter that does not expose City National Bank APIs.

providers.name: Code4rena
providers.description: Code4rena (C4) is a competitive smart-contract security auditing platform that connects Web3/DeFi projects (sponsors) with a global community of security researchers (wardens) through time-boxed competitive audits and ongoing bug bounties. Sponsors fund an audit, wardens compete to surface vulnerabilities, and judges rate severity, validity, and quality to distribute awards via a ranked-curve incentive model. Over five years the platform ran 512+ audits, engaged 16,600+ researchers, and surfaced 26,898 findings including 1,607 high-severity vulnerabilities. Code4rena announced it is winding down operations, seeing active competitions and bounties through to completion. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a paradigm portfolio company; the platform is web/app-based with GitBook documentation and does not publish a public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Coinshift
providers.description: Coinshift is a non-custodial, multi-chain onchain treasury management platform for startups, DAOs and crypto-native organisations, founded in 2021 as MultiSafe and built on top of Safe (Gnosis Safe) multisig accounts. The application unifies portfolio tracking across ERC-20 tokens and NFTs, multi-signature proposal and transaction workflows, mass and recurring payouts, contact and label management, CSV transaction export and cash-flow reporting, plus embedded dApp integrations for Aave, CoW Swap, 1inch, LI.FI, ParaSwap, Hedgey, Request Finance and Superfluid money streams, with Slack and Discord signing notifications. Coinshift also issues onchain yield assets — csUSDL, an ERC-4626 vault receipt token for USDL deposited into the Coinshift USDL Morpho Vault, csUSDC, the SHIFT governance token, and the iUSPC institutional credit product. Coinshift publishes no public developer API: the documentation at docs.coinshift.xyz is entirely end-user product and asset guidance, with no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, GraphQL schema or webhook catalog.

providers.name: Collective
providers.description: Collective is an all-in-one financial back-office platform built for self-employed entrepreneurs, solopreneurs, and businesses-of-one. It bundles S Corp formation and election, bookkeeping, payroll (as a Gusto partner), business and personal tax preparation and filing, quarterly tax planning, and a dedicated accounting team into a single membership. Roughly 12,000 members use Collective to optimize self-employment taxes, with members reporting average annual business-tax savings around $10,000. Collective is a private fintech company backed by General Catalyst, Kindred Ventures, and QED Investors. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public web, security, and compliance footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Crash Override
providers.description: Crash Override is a software supply chain security company building a control plane for software development in the agentic era. It monitors code from developers and AI coding agents, inspects builds across CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins), cryptographically tags software artifacts, and tracks them from development through production. The company delivers its capabilities primarily through open-source tools — Chalk (code provenance tagging) and Ocular (Kubernetes-native software asset scanning orchestration) — plus a hosted control plane with enterprise SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM support. Founded by Mark Curphey (founder of OWASP) and John Viega, and backed by GV, Syn Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Blackstone. Philosophy: "Tag. Track. Trust." No public REST API or OpenAPI specification is published at this time; this profile was enriched from the company's public web, GitHub org, and security surface.

providers.name: DayDream Dental
providers.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: DXY
providers.description: DXY (丁香园) is China's leading digital healthcare technology company, founded in 2000 in Harbin and headquartered in Hangzhou. It operates a "D+C" dual strategy: a professional physician community and clinical toolset (drug reference "用药助手", clinical case database, medical education, and the "Insight" pharmaceutical data analytics platform) alongside consumer health services under the "丁香医生" (Dingxiang Doctor) brand. DXY also runs the Biomart / 丁香通 life-sciences supplies marketplace. Its Medical Data Open Platform (open.dxy.cn) exposes standardized healthcare data services — newly-approved drugs, drug SKU and drug search, disease search, and hospital/institution search — as REST/JSON APIs under api.dxy.cn for pharmaceutical, medical, and health-tech partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Ethos
providers.description: Ethos is a US digital life insurance company headquartered in San Francisco, founded in 2016, offering term life, whole life, and indexed universal life policies through an online, mostly no-medical-exam application flow. Ethos operates as a technology-driven insurance agency, distributing policies underwritten by carriers such as Ameritas, Banner Life (Legal & General America), Protective, and TruStage. Coverage is available in 49 states and Washington, D.C., with term policies offered for 10, 15, 20, 30, and 40 year durations and face amounts ranging from $15,000 to $3 million. The company has raised over $400 million from investors including Goldman Sachs, SoftBank, GV, Sequoia, and Accel, and is widely cited as one of the leading insurtech companies modernizing the life insurance buying experience. Ethos exposes a Partnership API that lets approved business partners embed quoting, identity validation, instant underwriting, application capture, billing, and signed policy issuance directly into their own products. The Partnership API uses bearer-token authentication tied to a partner API key and per-applicant session, and consolidates steps such as identity validation and quoting into combined endpoints to enable instant decisioning. There is no public, self-serve OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer signup; access requires a partnership agreement with Ethos. Ethos's only material open-source footprint is the ethos-design-system React component library on GitHub.

providers.name: EverBank
providers.description: EverBank, N.A. is a Jacksonville, Florida based national bank (Member FDIC) focused on high-yield consumer deposits, business and treasury banking, and commercial lending, serving customers nationwide online plus a small network of financial centers in Florida, California and New York. The bank operated as TIAA Bank from 2017 until 2023, when it was acquired by an investor group and reverted to the EverBank brand as an independent institution. Like most US banks, EverBank publishes NO first-party public developer API or developer portal; there is no documented open-banking, FDX, or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API exposed directly. Consumer-permissioned account data is reached only through third-party aggregators (e.g. Plaid, MX, Finicity), which is the honest, non-fabricated posture recorded here.

providers.name: Exaforce
providers.description: Exaforce is a security operations platform that pairs AI agents with a unified data layer to help teams detect, triage, investigate, and respond to threats faster. Its four autonomous "Exabot" agents (Detect, Triage, Investigate, and Respond) automate SOC workflows across 100+ data sources spanning cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and code repositories, and can run as a self-operated platform or as a managed detection and response (MDR) service staffed by expert analysts working alongside the AI 24/7. Exaforce positions itself as an agentic-SOC alternative to traditional SIEM tooling while retaining integration compatibility. The company is backed by Mayfield and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or reference documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, security, and trust surface.

providers.name: Fifteenth
providers.description: Fifteenth is a San Francisco-based fintech company operating an AI-powered personal tax platform for ambitious earners — founders, investors, executives, and technology professionals with complex financial situations such as equity compensation (ISOs, RSOs, RSUs, NSOs), liquidity events (IPOs and acquisitions), partnership income (K-1s), and active stock and crypto trading. The service pairs dedicated human CPAs with AI-driven automation: users link their banking, payroll, and investment accounts via one-click integrations (Workday, Rippling, Robinhood, Wealthfront, Carta, Charles Schwab, AngelList, Coinbase and more), and the platform automatically detects tax-relevant transactions, organizes documents, models scenarios, and delivers proactive quarterly planning plus unlimited year-round advice at flat-fee pricing starting around $1,000 per year. Fifteenth raised $8.25M in seed funding (February 2025) led by A* and General Catalyst. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Govini
providers.description: Govini (rebranded to Air, air.ai, in 2026) is a defense-technology and decision-analytics company whose Ark platform combines proprietary defense acquisition data with AI-enabled applications to close the national-security "Readiness Gap" across supply chain, science and technology, production, sustainment, logistics, and modernization missions. Ark holds FedRAMP High authorization and a DISA Impact Level 5 (IL5) Provisional Authorization plus service-level IL5 ATOs, making it a closed, government-authorized SaaS platform rather than a public developer API. Led by CEO Tara Murphy Dougherty and backed by investors including Accel and Bain Capital. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and has been enriched with the provider's real public identity, security posture, and published compliance authorizations.

providers.name: Habu
providers.description: Habu was a data clean room and data collaboration company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Francisco, that let brands, publishers, and media platforms run privacy-safe joins and analytics on each other's first-party data without moving or exposing raw records. In January 2024 Habu was acquired by LiveRamp, and the product now ships as LiveRamp Clean Room within the LiveRamp data collaboration network. The standalone habu.com domain now 301-redirects to liveramp.com, and Habu's former developer surface (docs.habu.com, developer.habu.com) no longer resolves — the successor developer, security, and compliance surfaces live under liveramp.com. This profile originated as a portfolio-lead stub (backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Wing Venture Capital) and is enriched here to reflect the acquisition and the real, still-live security posture inherited by LiveRamp.

providers.name: Humio
providers.description: Humio is a log management and observability platform built for ingesting, storing, and searching machine data in real time at scale. Backed by Accel and acquired by CrowdStrike in 2021, Humio is now delivered as CrowdStrike Falcon LogScale. It provides high-throughput streaming ingest (including Splunk HEC and Elastic bulk compatible endpoints), a live query language for dashboards and alerts, and index-free retention. Developers integrate through a REST API for ingest and search plus a GraphQL API for administration (repositories, parsers, users, ingest tokens), with official client libraries for Python, Node.js, Go, and JavaScript and the humioctl command-line client.

providers.name: Incredible Health
providers.description: Incredible Health is an AI-native healthcare career marketplace that connects registered nurses, technicians, and technologists with permanent jobs at top hospitals and health systems. It flips traditional recruiting by having employers apply to pre-screened, verified professionals rather than the reverse. The platform serves 1.5 million+ U.S. healthcare workers and 1,500+ employers, including a majority of the nation's top-ranked hospital systems, cutting time-to-hire from a national average of roughly 86 days to under 20. Two purpose-built AI agents power the marketplace: Gale, a career partner for professionals (resume wizard, interview practice), and Lyn, a voice interview agent for employers that integrates with applicant-tracking systems. Founded by Iman Abuzeid, MD, and headquartered in San Francisco, the company is venture-backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Obvious Ventures, and NFX.

providers.name: Jify
providers.description: Jify is an India-based financial wellness platform (part of the Moneyview group) that partners with employers to give employees earned wage access: its On-Demand Salary lets workers draw already-earned pay before payday. Beyond earned wage access it offers salary advances, a rewards and discount marketplace, micro-savings, digital gold investing, credit-score tracking, smart tax tools, and a money manager for budgeting and expense tracking, delivered through Android and iOS apps. Jify is a consumer / B2B2C fintech app and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, domain-security posture, and published compliance claims (ISO 27001, CISA-certified, independently tested by Appknox).

providers.name: Kaniko
providers.description: Kaniko is an open-source tool from Google that builds container images from a Dockerfile inside a container or Kubernetes cluster without requiring a Docker daemon. It executes each command within a Dockerfile in userspace, enabling secure container builds in environments where running a Docker daemon is impractical or insecure. The project was archived on June 3, 2025, and is now read-only.

providers.name: Maywood
providers.description: Maywood is a Y Combinator (W26) artificial-intelligence startup building a finance-compliant, proactive AI platform that automates deal execution for investment banks. The product runs continuously across a banker's network, pipeline, and active M&A processes, generating client-ready CIMs, pitch decks, and financial models, drafting outreach in the banker's voice, and managing due-diligence workflows through a connected data layer that updates automatically. Maywood is built to FINRA and SEC requirements: autonomous within scope, human-approved at every external boundary, and fully reconstructable in between. Founded in 2026 and based in New York City, it is an early-stage SaaS company with no public developer API at this time; this profile tracks its public web, security, and trust surfaces so the network can detect an API program when one appears.

providers.name: Mimic
providers.description: Mimic is an enterprise cybersecurity company building ransomware and AI-threat defense based on "Known-Good Enforcement" at the kernel level. Its SaaS platform models a system's authorized state and blocks unauthorized modifications, detecting ransomware in fractions of a second to deflect attacks before they can encrypt data or damage infrastructure, and providing rapid-recovery technology that restores in seconds-to-minutes rather than days. Product lines include Ransomware Defense, AI Shield (Guard/Patch/Trace) and Agentic AI Governance. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Mimic raised a $27M seed and a $50M Series A led by GV (Google Ventures) and Menlo Ventures, with Ballistic Ventures, Team8, Wing Venture Capital and Shield Capital participating; former Mandiant CEO Kevin Mandia joined its board. The platform is enterprise/government-facing (sold via demo, no public developer API) and is aligned with GDPR, SOC 1 & 2, IL4/IL5 and holds FedRAMP Ready status. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Netflix Zuul
providers.description: Netflix Zuul is an open-source L7 application gateway that provides dynamic routing, monitoring, resiliency, and security for edge services. Originally developed by Netflix, Zuul 2 uses Netty for non-blocking I/O and is commonly used as an API gateway and edge service.

providers.name: Newfront
providers.description: Newfront is a modern business insurance brokerage and technology company headquartered in San Francisco. It combines a traditional insurance brokerage (commercial business insurance, employee benefits, retirement services, and risk management) with a software platform that gives clients transparent data and analytics to understand and lower their total cost of risk. Formed from the merger of Newfront and ABD Insurance, the company serves technology, venture-backed, and enterprise clients across property and casualty, health and benefits, and personal lines. Backed by Index Ventures, Susa Ventures, and SV Angel. As of this enrichment pass Newfront exposes a client-facing web application (app.newfront.com) but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Nowlun Holding Corp.
providers.description: Nowlun is a digital freight-forwarding platform serving the Middle East and North Africa that lets businesses compare instant ocean-freight quotes from 30+ shipping lines, book FCL and bulk sea shipments, arrange inland trucking to and from ports, track cargo through transit, and handle customs clearance. Beyond its shipper-facing web application, Nowlun operates a live, OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://nowlun.com/mcp, secured with RFC 8414 authorization-server and RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery (Authorization Code + PKCE, "mcp" scope). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: NutriSense
providers.description: NutriSense is a metabolic health and wellness company that pairs continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with 1:1 registered-dietitian coaching and a mobile app. Members receive glucose biosensors, real-time and historical glucose analytics, AI-assisted pattern insights, stress-management sessions, and video consults with credentialed, glucose-certified nutritionists to build sustainable nutrition, weight-loss, and metabolic-health habits. Nutrisense runs a consumer product with a member web and mobile app experience; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. It does publish a machine-readable llms.txt at nutrisense.io/llms.txt.

providers.name: Orolabs
providers.description: ORO Labs provides an agentic procurement orchestration platform for enterprise spend management. It coordinates people, processes, systems, and data so employees can get what they need without friction, unifying intake management, supplier onboarding and lifecycle, risk and compliance orchestration, and AI-driven workflow automation. The platform offers a no-code workflow builder, a purpose-built agent builder for custom procurement AI agents, and bring-your-own-LLM flexibility, with secure, semantically rich integrations across the procuretech landscape. ORO Labs is backed by Felicis and Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Papaya Pay
providers.description: Papaya Payments is a Los Angeles based fintech that operates a mobile-first digital billing and bill-pay platform. Businesses in healthcare, government and municipalities, utilities, insurance, field services, and debt collection use Papaya to let their customers pay bills by photographing a paper statement or scanning a QR code and paying over SMS, email, or the Papaya iOS and Android apps, with no account or login required. Papaya advertises a Quickpay embeddable payment widget for paper-statement and portal integrations, and states that more than 2.5 million Americans have used the service. The company markets PCI, HIPAA, and SOC2 compliance. As of this profile Papaya publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or API specification; it is a consumer-facing payments product rather than a developer platform. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Passionfroot
providers.description: Passionfroot is a Berlin-based platform for creator-led go-to-market (GTM), pairing a self-service marketplace where business, productivity, and thought-leadership creators sell sponsorships, ad placements, and brand collaborations with an AI agent ("Zest") that helps brands discover creators, plan campaigns, run outreach, process payments (via its FrootWallet), and measure performance across Twitter/X, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Beehiiv, and Substack. Creators manage storefronts, pricing, bookings, invoicing, and payouts in one place; the company monetizes by taking a commission on completed deals rather than charging a subscription. As of this enrichment pass Passionfroot exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation — it is an end-user SaaS product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Percent
providers.description: Percent is a private credit platform that opens privately negotiated loans and debt financing from non-bank lenders to accredited and institutional investors, specialty-finance borrowers, and debt underwriters. The marketplace lets individual accredited investors access institutional-grade private credit deals (asset-backed securities and corporate loans) with entry points from $500 for direct deals, $5,000 for diversified Blended Notes, and $50,000 for Separately Managed Accounts, alongside a secondary market for eligible positions. Percent Securities, LLC is a U.S. registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA and SIPC; Percent Advisors LLC provides advisory services. Investor, borrower, and manager workflows run through authenticated portals; the public percent.com surface is marketing, education, performance, and regulatory disclosure. Percent has no public developer API — programmatic/deal-level access is not published.

providers.name: Pitch
providers.description: Pitch is a collaborative presentation software company (pitch.com) that builds a fast, web-based tool for teams to create, share, and present decks together in real time, with templates, brand controls, live collaboration, analytics, and in-product integrations. Backed by Index Ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this profile Pitch publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or MCP server; enrichment here captured its published security and identity surface.

providers.name: Siemens Healthineers
providers.description: Siemens Healthineers AG is a German medical technology company (XETRA SHL) covering medical imaging, laboratory diagnostics, point-of-care testing, advanced therapies, and cancer care (following the April 2021 Varian Medical Systems acquisition for USD 16.4 billion). Its digital surface is anchored by the teamplay digital health platform, the Digital Marketplace, syngo.via OpenApps, and the Frontier Development Kit, with developer access offered through a gated teamplay developer portal that exposes APIs for single sign-on, licensing, user roles and permissions, the teamplay receiver plug-in, DICOM image access, customer-specific report submission, and status indicator notifications. No public OpenAPI specifications are published; the API catalog and reference documentation sit behind teamplay developer account authentication.

providers.name: Simulmedia
providers.description: Simulmedia is a technology-driven television advertising company that helps advertisers, agencies, and growth marketers plan, buy, and measure campaigns across linear TV, connected TV (CTV), and games. Its products include the Performance TV media-buying service, the AI-powered TV+ media-buying platform, and Simulmedia Self-Serve. Through PlayerWON, Simulmedia operates an in-game rewarded-video engagement and monetization platform for free-to-play console and PC games, exposed to game developers through the PlayerWON API and a first-party Unity/Unreal SDK. Simulmedia is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's public developer surface and the open-source PlayerWON SDK.

providers.name: Strella
providers.description: Strella is an AI-powered customer research platform that automates qualitative research at scale. It runs AI-moderated interviews with adaptive questioning, auto-generates discussion guides, recruits participants from an 8M+ global panel or a company's own customers, supports 46+ languages, and synthesizes insights and video highlights within hours instead of weeks. Research types span exploratory research, concept testing, usability testing, market research, and customer journey mapping. Strella is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API or SDK surface is currently published; this profile captures the company identity, security posture, and product changelog.

providers.name: Tobii
providers.description: Tobii is the global leader in eye tracking and attention computing, headquartered in Danderyd, Sweden and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Its developer offering centers on the Tobii Pro SDK — Python (tobii-research), .NET, C and Matlab bindings for streaming gaze and eye-tracking data from Tobii's screen-based and wearable eye trackers — together with the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 API (with official g3pylib Python and .NET client SDKs) and XR / consumer game-integration developer kits. Tobii's technology serves scientific and behavioral research, UX, healthcare, XR/VR, automotive driver monitoring and PC gaming markets.

providers.name: Tomorrow Health
providers.description: Tomorrow Health is an AI-powered platform for home-based care that connects providers, payors, and durable medical equipment (DMEPOS) suppliers, using intelligent automation to simplify ordering, routing, and reviewing home healthcare services. Its Horizon Suite includes AI Ordering, AI Fax Intake, and THEA (Tomorrow Health Expert Assistant). Headquartered in New York and backed by a16z, Bond Capital, and Obvious Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is currently published; the customer application is a private authenticated web app.

providers.name: Trudenty
providers.description: Trudenty is a fraud and risk intelligence platform that operates The Trust Network — a distributed, privacy-preserving infrastructure delivering real-time consumer trust and fraud intelligence across the payments ecosystem. It combines behavioural, transactional and network-level signals with machine learning and behavioural science to distinguish trusted consumers from fraudsters and prevent first-party (friendly) fraud, producing an explainable Trust Score across the checkout, claims and dispute lifecycle. Trudenty serves PSPs, acquirers and processors, and merchants, processing data where it lives so that no data leaves a client's organisation. It is a Mastercard Start Path and Techstars-backed startup, ISO 27001 certified and SOC 2 Type II audited.

providers.name: Trust Token
providers.description: TrustToken, founded in San Francisco in 2017 and rebranded as Archblock in November 2022, builds infrastructure for moving institutional funds and real-world assets onto blockchain rails. The company created the TrueUSD (TUSD) stablecoin and the TrueCurrencies family, and launched TrueFi, an on-chain under-collateralized lending protocol governed by the TRU token. Today Archblock operates a marketplace and fund-tokenization platform for institutional capital at app.archblock.com, with smart contracts, audits, and bug bounty programs published through its trusttoken GitHub organization. Backed by a16z, Founders Fund, BlockTower, and Morgan Creek.

providers.name: Tulip Interfaces
providers.description: Tulip is a manufacturing operations platform that enables frontline operations teams to build apps, connect machines and devices, and analyze production data without code. The Tulip REST API provides programmatic access to apps, tables, connectors, stations, automations, and analytics, supporting integration with ERP, MES, and industrial equipment on the shop floor.

providers.name: UNest
providers.description: UNest is a Los Angeles-based fintech app that helps parents and families save and invest for their children's futures through UTMA/UGMA custodial investment accounts, with brand rewards contributions, gifting, financial literacy content, and term life insurance offered through Ladder. UNest Advisers, LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser, with brokerage through UNest Securities, LLC (FINRA/SIPC) and clearing through Apex Clearing. The company is a consumer mobile-app business and publishes no public developer API, though its site ships a real llms.txt. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Unobravo
providers.description: Unobravo is Europe's largest online psychology service, founded in 2019 by psychologist Danila De Stefano. It matches people with one of 9,500+ individually vetted psychologists and psychotherapists for individual, couples, and group therapy delivered online, serving Italy, Spain, and France as well as Italians abroad, with 500,000+ people supported across more than 10 million online sessions, plus a B2B mental-wellbeing offering (Unobravo Business) and an ECM training academy. Backed by Insight Partners and Northzone. Its backend API (api.unobravo.com) is private, with no public developer surface.

providers.name: Wing Cloud
providers.description: Wing Cloud is the company behind Wing (Winglang), an open-source, cloud-oriented programming language created by Elad Ben-Israel, the creator of AWS CDK. Wing unifies infrastructure and application code into a single model: a "preflight" phase compiles to Terraform/CloudFormation while an "inflight" phase compiles to JavaScript for runtime. Developers build and test distributed cloud systems locally with the Wing Simulator and Wing Console, then deploy to any major cloud provider. The project is MIT-licensed, ships the `wing` CLI (npm: winglang) and the standalone Wing SDK (@winglang/sdk, Apache-2.0), and the company is backed by Battery Ventures. Wing is a language and developer-tooling company; it does not publish a public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Zip Security
providers.description: Zip Security is a cloud-based security, IT, and compliance platform that automates identity management, device management (MDM for macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android), and endpoint threat detection for small and mid-sized businesses. It unifies tools such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, and CrowdStrike behind a single dashboard, deploying frameworks, policies, and controls that are continuously enforced to help teams reach SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, CMMC, and PCI readiness, often within two weeks. Zip Security is backed by General Catalyst. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Ampere Computing
providers.description: Ampere Computing is a Santa Clara, California semiconductor company founded in 2018 by Renee James and now part of the SoftBank Group. It designs Arm-based Cloud Native Processors — the Ampere Altra and Altra Max families (up to 128 cores) and the flagship AmpereOne family (up to 192 single-threaded cores) — for cloud, AI inference and edge deployments. Alongside the silicon it ships a software stack: Ampere Optimized AI frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX Runtime, llama.cpp, Ollama) distributed as first-party container images, tuned GCC/glibc/binutils builds, performance and porting tooling, and an arm64 developer community. Ampere publishes no public developer API — its developer program is a hardware, tooling and porting program rather than an API program.

providers.name: Angular
providers.description: Angular is an open-source TypeScript-based web application framework maintained by Google and a community of contributors. It provides a comprehensive platform for building single-page applications with a component-based architecture, reactive Signals, deferrable views, built-in control flow, zoneless change detection, server-side rendering, and the Angular CLI. Angular follows a major release cadence of two versions per year.

providers.name: Anjuna
providers.description: Anjuna Security provides a confidential-computing platform that lets organizations run existing applications inside hardware-based secure enclaves (Trusted Execution Environments) across AWS Nitro, AMD SEV, and Intel SGX without code changes, keeping data encrypted at rest, in transit, and in use. Its Seaglass platform, Policy Manager, Overwatch agentic-AI governance, and Northstar AI data clean room deliver hardware-rooted cryptographic attestation and policy-based access control for sensitive workloads and privacy-preserving AI. Anjuna is delivered as command-line runtime tooling and open-source attestation libraries rather than a public HTTP API.

providers.name: Arconic
providers.description: Arconic Corporation is an aluminum solutions company producing rolled aluminum sheet and plate, extrusions, and architectural building products for the aerospace, automotive, commercial transportation, building & construction, industrial, and packaging markets. Spun off from Alcoa in 2016, separated from Howmet Aerospace in 2020, and acquired by Apollo Global Management in August 2023 for approximately $5.2 billion, Arconic now operates as a private company headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Key brands include Kawneer architectural systems and Reynobond aluminum composite panels.

providers.name: Arf
providers.description: Arf is a Switzerland-regulated liquidity and settlement platform for cross-border payments, providing short-term, receivable-backed, revolving working capital to licensed payment institutions and money-transfer operators. Its core product, Arf Liquidity, lets payment companies settle across any corridor 24/7 without prefunding destination accounts, using regulated real-world-asset-backed digital assets and stablecoins (including USDC) for native on-ramp/off-ramp value transfer and real-time treasury management. Arf is a compliance-first, VQF self-regulatory-organization member serving only licensed financial institutions, and partners with Circle, Stellar, and Visa. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from Arf's public web presence; Arf does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Based
providers.description: Based is a consumer crypto super app built on Hyperliquid that unifies trading, prediction markets, and real-world payments in a single self-custody account. Users trade spot and perpetual futures with sub-second execution and deep liquidity, speculate on prediction markets, and spend crypto from Solana, Arbitrum, and Polygon at 70+ million Visa merchants across 160+ countries via Based debit cards, including the premium Gold+ card. BasedCloud lets partners spin up white-label Hyperliquid trading frontends (web, mobile, desktop, Telegram), and a three-tiered affiliate program amplifies Hyperliquid referral fees. Based is backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Hashed, Ethena, and Spartan Group. It publishes consumer product docs on GitBook and an agent-oriented llms.txt index, but exposes no public developer API of its own — programmatic trading runs on the underlying Hyperliquid API.

providers.name: BestDoc
providers.description: BestDoc is a healthcare patient-relationship-management (PRM) company that helps hospitals improve the patient experience across inpatient and outpatient care. Its platform includes BestDoc Concierge for inpatient experience management (non-clinical requests, room food ordering, discharge management), BestDoc Practice for outpatient patient-request management, BestDoc Survey for omni-channel patient feedback, an AI Reply Assistant for automated review responses, and continued-care engagement tools. BestDoc integrates with hospital information systems (HIS), EMRs, and payment gateways. BestDoc Technology Pvt. Ltd. is an ISO 27001:2013 certified company operating from Kochi, Bangalore, and Dubai. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Binu
providers.description: Datafree Technologies (originally biNu, founded 2008 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia) operates a #datafree reverse-billing connectivity platform that lets enterprises sponsor the mobile data cost of their websites, apps and portals so end users can reach those digital services without spending their own airtime or data - much like a toll-free number, but for the mobile internet. Widely deployed across South African mobile networks, the platform works on any device with no new SIM, top-up or contract, and layers on security controls, allowlist management, time windows, usage caps and audit logging. Products include the Datafree Platform and Datafree Connect. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Caidya
providers.description: Caidya is a full-service, global clinical research organization (CRO) formed from the April 2021 merger of dMed and Clinipace, rebranded to Caidya in October 2022. It runs clinical development programs end to end — pre-IND and regulatory strategy, early phase, Phase II/III delivery, study start-up, trial feasibility, clinical operations, risk-based quality management, medical monitoring, clinical data management, biometrics, medical writing, pharmacovigilance, quality assurance and post-marketing surveillance — across oncology and hematology, cardiovascular-metabolic, rare disease, pediatrics, gastroenterology, nephrology, dermatology, ophthalmology, cell and gene therapy, neurology, immunology and infectious disease. The company took a $165M strategic growth investment from Rubicon Founders and announced a strategic combination with Simbec-Orion. Caidya is a clinical services provider rather than a software vendor: it integrates with sponsor-preferred EDC, eCOA, IRT, CTMS, eTMF and safety platforms rather than publishing a developer program or a public API of its own.

providers.name: Coasts
providers.description: Coasts (Containerized Hosts) is an open-source, MIT-licensed CLI tool that provides localhost service isolation and orchestration for git worktrees. It spawns multiple fully isolated development runtimes for the same project on a single machine, giving each worktree its own ports, databases, and services so parallel AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Conductor, and others) can build and test side by side without clashing. Built on Docker Compose, with a thin CLI client talking to a local coastd daemon over a unix socket plus a bundled React/Vite web observability UI, Coasts is local-first and offline-capable, with optional extension to remote machines over SSH. Backed by Y Combinator (Fall 2025) and founded by Jamie Sunderland and Dan Hyman.

providers.name: Commerce Bank
providers.description: Commerce Bank is the principal banking subsidiary of Commerce Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ CBSH), a Missouri-based regional bank holding company with roughly $32 billion in assets and dual headquarters in Kansas City and St. Louis. Commerce Bank is a Missouri state-chartered bank and Federal Reserve member, founded in 1865, offering personal, business, commercial, and wealth-management services across the U.S. Midwest. Its API posture is corporate/embedded-banking oriented rather than a fully open public program: it runs a registration-gated external developer portal (developers.commercebank.com) and a CommercePayments developer platform, and delivers ERP-embedded banking via Commerce Connections Direct. Consumer-permissioned data sharing is largely intermediated through aggregators such as Plaid and platforms like Modern Treasury rather than a documented first-party, self-serve open-banking API. No public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented, and no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger is publicly available.

providers.name: Coravin
providers.description: Coravin is a consumer beverage-technology company best known for its wine preservation systems, which use a thin needle and inert argon gas to pour wine by the glass without pulling the cork, leaving the remaining wine unoxidized for weeks or months. Its product line spans the Timeless, Pivot, and Sparkling systems plus Pure argon capsules, sold direct-to-consumer and through retail and trade channels. Coravin does not operate a standalone public developer API; its direct storefront runs on Shopify, which exposes a real agent-native commerce surface — a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, a hosted shopping MCP endpoint, and OIDC / OAuth 2.0 authorization-server metadata for Shopify Customer Accounts. Backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Credit Sesame
providers.description: Credit Sesame is a consumer financial health platform that provides free daily credit-score monitoring, credit reports, and personalized recommendations for credit cards, loans, and insurance based on a member's approval likelihood. Members can build credit through everyday debit purchases and upgrade to the Sesame+ premium tier for three-bureau credit reports, advanced credit tools, and identity-theft protection. Credit Sesame operates consumer web and mobile applications and, as of this profile, does not publish a public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile backed by Menlo Ventures.

providers.name: DeepStream Technologies
providers.description: DeepStream Technologies (deep.stream) is a London-based AI-enhanced eSourcing and source-to-contract platform for mid-market procurement teams. It digitalizes buyer-to-supplier sourcing with best-of-breed eRFx, supplier discovery, supplier pre-qualification, eAuctions, contract management, management reporting, and AI-driven RFP generation and conversational analytics, aiming to help procurement teams work faster, reduce risk, and gain visibility while keeping implementation simple. Customers include Walkers Shortbread, BrewDog, Abbott, and Free Now. DeepStream does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation; integrations with ERP and PO systems are delivered as a service. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched with public company and infrastructure signals.

providers.name: Documint
providers.description: Documint is a programmatic document generation platform with a template editor, REST API and integrations with major CRMs and automation tools (HubSpot, Airtable, Zapier, Make). Documents are generated by merging user-supplied JSON data into pre-built templates; data is not stored on Documint servers. The REST API is published on the Platinum plan.

providers.name: Effectful
providers.description: Effectful Technologies is the company behind Effect, an open-source ecosystem of production-grade TypeScript libraries. The flagship `effect` library is a composable standard library and execution engine that unifies error handling, resource management, concurrency, dependency injection, observability, schema, and testability, letting developers focus on what a program should accomplish rather than how. Effect is positioned as "Layer 0" of a broader vision extending into distributed systems — RPC, SQL, clustering, AI integrations, and durable execution. The ecosystem ships as first-party npm packages under the `effect` and `@effect/*` scopes (MIT licensed) from the Effect-TS GitHub organization. Effectful is developer-tooling / library company, not an HTTP API provider, and is backed by Amplify Partners.

providers.name: Ermeo
providers.description: Ermeo (rebranded Causeway Field) is a French connected-operator / field-operations SaaS platform that lets industrial and field teams digitize paper procedures into dynamic, interactive workflows for inspections, maintenance, and interventions. Operators complete pre-built interactive forms on mobile, capture equipment and report data in the field in real time, and operational managers monitor all field work from a central console. Ermeo exposes a REST API secured with OAuth 2.0 so customers can connect their information systems (CMMS, MES, EDM) to import and synchronize equipment, forms, and reports and enrich the data collected in the field.

providers.name: Faro
providers.description: Faro Health is an AI platform for clinical development that helps biopharma and clinical research teams design and execute better studies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Diego, California, Faro provides study design optimization, automated protocol document authoring, and clinical workflow automation, digitizing and structuring trial protocols so teams can accelerate development without compromising scientific rigor, patient safety, or patient-centricity.
