MoBagel exposes Decanter AI programmatically through an official first-party Python SDK (decanter-ai-sdk) that authenticates with an API key and drives data upload, model training, and prediction. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Multus CNI
providers.description: Multus CNI is a container network interface plugin for Kubernetes that enables attaching multiple network interfaces to pods. It acts as a meta-plugin that can call multiple other CNI plugins, allowing pods to have connectivity to multiple networks simultaneously.

providers.name: NeonRain, Inc.
providers.description: NeonRain, Inc. is a 500 Global portfolio company whose public product surface resolves to Playabl (playabl.ai), an AI-powered, no-code platform that lets anyone create web games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Users describe a game idea in plain English and Playabl's generative AI produces a playable prototype instantly, which can be refined conversationally and published to the web. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in the United States, the product targets educators, indie developers, marketers, and hobbyists. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web application with no developer-facing API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: OneScreen AI
providers.description: OneScreen AI is a data-driven out-of-home (OOH) advertising company that makes real-world media — billboards, transit, and place-based advertising — as queryable and buyable as any digital channel. It combines more than 1,500 OOH audience personas, close to one million live inventory listings, and audience-based market and inventory recommendation models. OneScreen exposes this OOH intelligence to AI agents through a public Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (OAuth 2.1, free public beta) that connects to Claude, ChatGPT, or any MCP-compatible client. Products include OneScreen Research (free) and OneScreen Planner (closed beta). The company was originally surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts.

providers.name: Opti
providers.description: Opti is an AI-native identity and access management (IAM) platform for enterprises struggling with access sprawl across human, non-human, and agentic identities. Founded in 2024 by Barak Perelman, Mille Gandelsman, and Ido Trivizki, Opti deploys pre-trained, domain-specific large language models trained on curated identity data to interpret risk, recommend least-privilege access decisions, and orchestrate safe permissions. The platform spans Access Intelligence, Risk Mitigation, Lifecycle Management (joiner/mover/leaver), and Compliance, integrating with 250+ identity solutions, IdPs, IGAs, HRIS, and ITSM systems without rip-and-replace. Opti raised a $20M seed round led by YL Ventures, Mayfield Fund, and Hetz Ventures.

providers.name: ORAS
providers.description: ORAS (OCI Registry As Storage) is a CNCF project that provides a CLI and a set of client libraries for pushing and pulling arbitrary OCI artifacts to and from OCI-compliant registries, allowing container registries to be used as a generic artifact distribution mechanism.

providers.name: Outschool
providers.description: Outschool is an education-technology marketplace for live, small-group online classes for learners ages 3-18. It connects families and independent teachers across 140,000+ subjects — from math and coding to art, music, and hobbies — offered as one-time sessions, ongoing courses, camps, and social clubs delivered over live video. Outschool also serves schools and districts through its for-organizations program. Backed by Bond Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Union Square Ventures, and Y Combinator, the platform is a consumer web application; it exposes no publicly documented developer API. The site is powered by an internal, undocumented GraphQL endpoint (outschool.com/graphql) used only by its own front end and largely blocked to crawlers. This profile is an API Evangelist network company record enriched from the provider's public web surface.

providers.name: Partsimony
providers.description: Partsimony is an intelligent supply chain platform that helps hardware companies turn engineering designs into manufactured products with less time, cost, and friction. Its software analyzes component designs to recommend manufacturing methods, materials, price estimates, and lead times, then matches each part to the optimal manufacturers inside and outside a company's network — batching components for volume leverage across processes like 3D printing, CNC machining, injection molding, castings, electronics, and assemblies. The platform also coordinates RFPs, proposals, orders, messaging, and payment terms between OEMs and their manufacturing partners. Partsimony operates a web application and product documentation but does not currently publish a public developer API. Founded in 2015 and based in Brooklyn, NY; backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Pebblely
providers.description: Pebblely creates AI product photos that help you sell more. No Photoshop skills required. The Pebblely API allows programmatic access to AI-powered product photography generation, background creation, and image styling.

providers.name: Phaidra
providers.description: Phaidra builds AI agents for autonomous data center and industrial operations, using reinforcement learning to control cooling, power, and workloads in mission-critical facilities. Its products include Phaidra Prism, an LLM for data center operations that helps technicians identify, prioritize, and resolve infrastructure issues, and Phaidra Factory, self-learning AI agents that continuously monitor and optimize thermal reliability, energy efficiency, and IT capacity to maximize tokens per watt across AI factories. Phaidra is an enterprise vendor with no public API or developer program; this profile captures its public security, compliance, and web posture. Backed by Index Ventures.

providers.name: Praxis AI (Vortexify)
providers.description: Praxis AI is a Y Combinator (Fall 2024) company that now operates as Vortexify (vortexify.ai). Vortexify is an AI-native platform that generates operational software directly from a company's data: teams connect data sources through 20+ prebuilt connectors (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, BigQuery, Redshift, Snowflake, NetSuite, Oracle, S3, Azure Blob, Google Sheets/Drive, SharePoint and more), describe requirements in plain English, and AI agents plan, code, test and deploy backend logic plus custom frontends with no infrastructure to manage. The platform emphasizes building complete apps on operational data rather than just dashboards, with built-in scheduling, serverless compute execution, role-based access control, audit logs, sandboxed environments, token-based authentication, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Praxis AI was founded by Aditya Tewari (ex-Palantir) and Ransika Liyanage (ex-Tesla, GM, Deloitte), originally focused on manufacturing-specific AI agents for predicting and preventing machine failures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator. Vortexify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: RetailNext
providers.description: RetailNext is an AI-powered in-store retail analytics platform that helps physical retailers understand shopper behavior and optimize store operations. Its product suite spans traffic analytics (real-time foot-traffic counting and benchmarking across locations), shopper journey and zone insights (which layouts convert and where shoppers are lost), asset protection and loss prevention that combines video intelligence with shopper analytics, and Pulse AI, a conversational layer for answering retail questions in plain language. The platform is used by 600+ retailers across 100+ countries, including brands such as Macy's, Sephora, and Calvin Klein. RetailNext is a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source infrastructure tooling and publishes a responsible-disclosure security program, but does not currently expose a publicly documented developer API or portal.

providers.name: Rondo Energy
providers.description: Rondo Energy is an Alameda, California industrial decarbonization company led by CEO John O'Donnell that builds the Rondo Heat Battery (RHB), a thermal energy storage system that converts intermittent wind and solar electricity into heat stored in thousands of tons of refractory brick at temperatures up to 1,500C and returns it as continuous steam, thermal oil, superheated air, or combined heat and power at rated outputs from 2MWth to over 100MWth. The RHB is sold as a drop-in replacement for a fossil-fuel boiler, via capital purchase, lease, or heat purchase agreement, into cement, food and beverage, chemicals, fuels and ethanol, textiles, pulp and paper, mining, pharmaceuticals, and direct air capture. Rondo operates the world's largest industrial heat battery and has announced a 90GWh factory plan with Siam Cement Group, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Catalyst, Energy Impact Partners, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Rio Tinto, SABIC, Aramco Ventures, and the European Investment Bank. Rondo sells hardware and delivered heat, not software: it publishes no developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Runsybil
providers.description: RunSybil is an AI-native autonomous offensive security platform. Sybil — a system of AI agents — continuously penetration tests live applications and infrastructure, finding, exploiting, and validating real vulnerabilities without a human in the loop. It tests live applications black-box by default (no source code required), integrates with GitHub and GitLab to trigger targeted change testing on every code push, and validates every finding through a multi-agent pipeline before it surfaces, aiming to eliminate triage and false positives. RunSybil positions as a replacement for point-in-time penetration testing, legacy DAST/SAST scanners, and bug bounty programs, and also offers white-box testing for deeper codebase exploration. Founded in 2023 by Ari Herbert-Voss (OpenAI's first security hire) and Vlad Ionescu (Offensive Security Tech Lead at Meta), the company raised $40M led by Khosla Ventures and is trusted by security teams at Notion, Cursor, Turbopuffer, Baseten, and Thinking Machines Lab. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface is published at this time.

providers.name: ServiceMax
providers.description: ServiceMax is asset-centric field service management (FSM) software that helps equipment manufacturers and service organizations maximize equipment uptime, optimize technician productivity, and streamline service delivery. Its cloud platform, built natively on the Salesforce platform (ServiceMax Core and Asset 360), spans work order and workflow management, scheduling and dispatch (Service Board), preventive and predictive maintenance, contract and entitlement management, parts and inventory, offline-capable mobile tools (ServiceMax Go), real-time technician collaboration (Zinc), and customer self-service (Engage). Founded in 2007 and acquired by PTC in 2023, ServiceMax integrates with PTC's IoT and PLM portfolio (ThingWorx, Windchill) and exposes its data and workflows through the underlying Salesforce API surface rather than a standalone public developer API.

providers.name: SetSail
providers.description: SetSail is a revenue-operations and sales-AI platform (now part of ZoomInfo) that automatically captures sales activity data from email, calendar, and contacts and syncs it to Salesforce, then layers AI-powered revenue intelligence on top of it, including MEDDIC deal analysis, meeting preparation, deal alerts, and performance coaching. Insights are delivered to sales reps and leaders through Slack, email, the browser, and Salesforce, and activity data can be routed to Snowflake, Databricks, Tableau, and Looker for analytics. SetSail does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Showbie
providers.description: Showbie is a K-12 learning platform for iPad that streamlines teaching workflows across assignments, feedback, grading, and classroom communication for teachers, students, and parents. Backed by Point Nine, it combines a digital classroom, annotation and file-sharing tools, and messaging into a single app used by schools worldwide. Showbie exposes no public developer API, SDK, or docs surface; this profile captures the company's public web, support, compliance, privacy, and terms properties, plus a live domain security probe.

providers.name: Snackpass
providers.description: Snackpass is an all-in-one marketing, point-of-sale (POS), and payments platform built for quick-service and fast-casual restaurants. It unifies front-of-house and back-of-house operations in one system: cloud POS, integrated card and mobile payments, self-serve kiosks, online and QR/table ordering, a consumer mobile app, kitchen display systems, loyalty and rewards, SMS/marketing automation, and commission-free delivery. Snackpass serves thousands of restaurants from independent boba and coffee shops to national franchises and has facilitated tens of millions of guest transactions. The company is privately held and backed by a16z, Craft Ventures, and General Catalyst. Snackpass does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; third-party ordering and delivery integrations (Uber Eats, DoorDash, GrubHub) are brokered through partners such as Deliverect and GetOrder rather than a documented public API surface.

providers.name: Stacks
providers.description: Stacks is an AI-native financial close and accounting platform for controllers, CFOs, and accounting teams. It automates the monthly close across existing ERPs with agentic tooling for account reconciliations and transaction matching, journal-entry posting and review, close-management checklists and approvals, and AI-powered analysis, variance explanation, and reporting. Stacks connects directly to ERP systems (Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite, SAP S/4HANA, Workday), data warehouses (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift), file storage, and spreadsheets, and offers an Excel add-in for manual journals. A developer API for custom reconciliation logic is announced as "coming soon." Stacks is a fintech company backed by EQT Ventures, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Version One Ventures. Profile enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public web surfaces (no public API specification is yet available).

providers.name: Stride
providers.description: Stride is a multichain liquid staking protocol built as a Cosmos SDK appchain (chain-id stride-1) and secured by Cosmos Hub interchain security. Users stake proof-of-stake assets such as ATOM, TIA, DYDX, OSMO, DYM, SAGA, and LUNA and receive liquid staking receipt tokens (stATOM, stTIA, and others) that keep accruing staking rewards while remaining usable across DeFi for trading, lending, collateral, and liquidity provision. Stride is IBC-connected and uses a Hyperlane bridge for cross-chain reach. Its machine-readable surface is the Cosmos SDK gRPC and REST (LCD) query interface plus IBC, wrapped by the official stridejs TypeScript SDK; Stride does not publish a REST OpenAPI. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Sunairio
providers.description: Sunairio is a grid forecasting company that provides integrated weather, climate, and energy insights for power markets. Its flagship platform, Sunairio ONE, generates 1,000-member ensemble forecasts across horizons from hourly to decadal, capturing extreme-weather and grid-stress scenarios that traditional forecasts miss. The company also publishes SHED (Sunairio High-resolution Earth Data), a proprietary historical weather dataset for the Continental US from 1950 to present at roughly 100x the resolution of ERA5, with asset-level wind and solar variability. Customers such as energy traders, grid operators, utility-scale asset developers, and demand-response aggregators access forecasts and data through a web UI, an API, and (on higher tiers) direct Snowflake data delivery. Founded in 2020 by Rob Cirincione, the company has been recognized by the National Science Foundation, American Clean Power, and EPRI.

providers.name: SurePath AI
providers.description: SurePath AI (now part of F5) is an enterprise AI governance and security platform that lets organizations safely adopt generative AI across their workforce. The platform gives security and IT teams visibility into GenAI usage by recording conversations, mitigates risk by detecting and redacting sensitive data in prompts and enforcing role-based access guardrails to public and private models, and increases safe adoption through a branded enterprise GenAI portal that enriches interactions with enterprise data. It is delivered as a SaaS product with an admin console rather than a public developer API, and maintains SOC 2 compliance.

providers.name: The Coca-Cola Company
providers.description: The Coca-Cola Company is the world's largest non-alcoholic beverage company, owning and marketing more than 200 brands across sparkling soft drinks, water, hydration, sports, coffee, tea, juice, dairy, and plant-based drinks. The company sells its products in more than 200 countries through a bottling and distribution partner network. While Coca-Cola does not currently publish a broadly available public REST API, it is a heavy enterprise API consumer running an internal API program on MuleSoft that connects ERP, manufacturing, distribution, retail, marketing, and consumer engagement systems through a Center for Enablement (C4E) model. Historical Coca-Cola Enterprises (CCE) Product and Location APIs at developer.cokecce.com are no longer maintained as a public-facing developer program.

providers.name: TikTok Shop API
providers.description: TikTok Shop is TikTok's integrated e-commerce platform that lets sellers, creators, and partners list products, manage inventory and fulfillment, and sell directly within TikTok's live streams, short videos, and shop tabs. The TikTok Shop Open API (open-api.tiktokglobalshop.com) is a RESTful API that uses OAuth 2.0 authentication and enables developers to programmatically manage products, orders, fulfillment, returns, finance, promotions, and seller authorization across TikTok Shop's global marketplaces.

providers.name: Trust & Will
providers.description: Trust & Will is a digital estate planning platform, headquartered in San Diego, California and founded in 2017, that lets individuals and families create legally valid, state-specific estate planning documents entirely online. Members build will-based or trust-based estate plans and related documents such as guardianship designations, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and the company also offers probate support and nationwide notarization. Trust & Will distributes through direct-to-consumer subscriptions as well as B2B partnerships with financial advisors, wealth managers, and employers offering it as a benefit. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; this enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, but did confirm a live security program and trust posture.

providers.name: Tulyp
providers.description: Tulyp is a SaaS treasury platform from French company SmarTrade SAS that gives CFOs and treasurers of SMEs and mid-caps (10-200M euro revenue) real-time visibility into their foreign-exchange (FX) exposure. The platform aggregates financial data from connected ERPs, accounting software, and banks, calculates net currency exposure by type and timeframe, translates currency movements into impact on revenue, margins, and EBITDA, and alerts when exposure crosses risk-policy thresholds. Backed by Speedinvest. Tulyp publishes no public developer API; it does publish an llms.txt content index for AI systems.

providers.name: Twill
providers.description: Twill is a referral-based recruiting platform with the tagline "talent recommended talent." It makes hiring easier and faster by having a network of more than 50,000 vetted, experienced professionals across engineering, product, sales, and growth recommend their peers and friends for open roles, producing warm introductions to passive candidates instead of recruiter cold outreach. Twill advertises an average 22-day time to hire, a 90-day retention guarantee on placements, flat-fee pricing, and intelligent matching built in partnership with MIT's Generative AI Lab. The company is backed by Bloomberg Beta and does not currently publish a public developer API or API documentation; api.withtwill.com serves its private platform backend.

providers.name: Twisty
providers.description: Twisty, operated by Bright Live Inc. (dba Twisty) of Santa Monica, California, is an AI character creation platform that lets creators generate lifelike AI characters and produce personalized, expressive video messages as an alternative to generic talking-head videos. The product ships as a web app plus iOS and Android apps with a free tier and a paid monthly plan, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Twisty does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Vennre
providers.description: Vennre is a Sharia-compliant private-market investing platform built for HENRYs (High Earners, Not Rich Yet). It curates and vets institutional-grade opportunities across real estate, private equity, venture capital and private credit from leading global managers, lowering entry thresholds so members can start building wealth from as little as $5,000. Delivered through a mobile app and web experience with a smart wallet, portfolio tracking and personalized wealth coaching, the platform is regulated in the UK as an appointed representative of Talbot Capital Ltd (FCA FRN 489839) and operates in Saudi Arabia under the Capital Market Authority (CMA License 19206-20). Vennre is a consumer wealthtech product; no public developer API or developer platform is published at this time.

providers.name: Zuma
providers.description: Zuma (legally Resident Boost Inc., d/b/a Zuma) is an AI platform for the multifamily / apartment industry, best known for "Kelsey," an AI assistant with human back-up that handles renter engagement across the resident lifecycle. Kelsey automates leasing (responding to inquiries, qualifying prospects, and scheduling tours), rent collections (payment reminders, late-resident follow-up, and commitment tracking), move-outs (notices, inspections, and security-deposit handling), and inbound property calls via VoiceAI. Zuma integrates into property-management and CRM systems used by operators — Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, Knock, and Microsoft/Google calendars — to boost NOI and conversion. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). Zuma does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API reference; this profile captures its public web, commercial, and operational surface.

providers.name: Zyla
providers.description: Zyla API Hub is an API marketplace that provides unified access to over 10,000 APIs through a single account, API key, and SDK, simplifying API discovery, integration, and management for developers.

providers.name: 1X Technologies
providers.description: 1X Technologies is a humanoid robotics company headquartered in Palo Alto, California with vertically integrated manufacturing at the NEO Factory in Hayward. Its product line includes EVE (an earlier wheeled-base humanoid used for commercial pilots) and NEO, the company's bipedal consumer humanoid marketed as the "world's first consumer-ready humanoid robot for the home," with NEO Beta and NEO Gamma development variants and a consumer pre-order program. 1X is an OpenAI portfolio company and collaborates with NVIDIA on training-data generation and on-board model execution. The company maintains a public GitHub organization (github.com/1x-technologies) with 24 repositories, most notably 1xgpt — a world-modeling challenge for humanoid robots — alongside Halodi robot URDF models, ROS2 examples for the EVE robot, and robotics infrastructure tools. 1X does not publish a public hosted API or developer SDK; engagement is via product purchase, research challenges, and open-source code.

providers.name: AAZZUR
providers.description: AAZZUR is a Berlin-based embedded finance and Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that lets enterprises, financial institutions, and startups embed financial services into their own products. It provides modular "Smart Finance Blocks" (pre-configured front-end screens, micro-services, and connections to underlying API providers) alongside its own developer-portal APIs and a smart marketplace of BaaS and fintech partners. Customers can consume the APIs directly, drop in AAZZUR's embeddable front-end components, or launch stand-alone apps and web frontends covering banking, payments, cards, lending, wealth management, and insurance without building the underlying financial infrastructure themselves.

providers.name: Acretrader
providers.description: AcreTrader is a farmland investment platform headquartered in Fayetteville, Arkansas that lets accredited investors buy fractional, passive ownership stakes in individual US row-crop, permanent-crop and timberland farms. AcreTrader sources and vets each farm, then handles the legal entity, farm management and administration while investors earn returns from annual cash rent and long-term land appreciation. Securities are offered through North Capital Private Securities Corporation, a FINRA/SIPC member broker-dealer that is not an affiliate of the platform. Since 2018 AcreTrader has enabled investment in over 140 farmland properties spanning roughly 44,000 acres across 20 states, and its investment management arm, AcreTrader Management LLC, reports net IRR of 9.4% to 30.3% on realized deals. Proterra Investment Partners LP acquired AcreTrader in August 2025. AcreTrader publishes no public developer API, no developer portal and no machine-readable specification; contract discovery was run in full against acretrader.com and api.acretrader.com on 2026-08-10 and every discovery path returned 404.

providers.name: Apache MADlib
providers.description: Apache MADlib is an open-source library for scalable in-database analytics. It provides data-parallel implementations of mathematical, statistical, and machine learning methods for structured and unstructured data, executed within PostgreSQL or Greenplum Database. MADlib enables data scientists to run machine learning algorithms directly in the database using SQL.

providers.name: ApplyBoard
providers.description: ApplyBoard is a study-abroad application platform that simplifies the international education journey by connecting students, recruitment partners, and partner schools on a single platform. Students explore and apply to more than 1,500 global universities and colleges across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and Germany, with supporting services spanning financial products, English-language test vouchers, and accommodation. ApplyBoard also operates ApplyProof, a document-verification and trust product. The company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK; its programmatic surface (including ApplyProof) is partner-gated. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Arrived Homes
providers.description: Arrived (Arrived Homes) is an SEC-qualified real estate investing platform that lets anyone buy fractional shares of income-producing single-family rental homes and vacation rentals for as little as $100. Arrived curates and acquires properties nationwide, handles acquisition, financing, property management, tenant placement, maintenance, and financial reporting, and passes rental income to investors as quarterly dividends alongside long-term appreciation. The platform also offers pooled funds including a Single Family Residential Fund and a Real Estate Income (debt) Fund. As of profiling it reports roughly 981K registered investors, $445M invested, and $95M distributed. Backed by Forerunner Ventures, it operates as a consumer fintech / proptech product with a web and mobile app; it publishes no public developer API. This API Evangelist profile is enriched from public company surfaces.

providers.name: Avenue One
providers.description: Avenue One is a New York-based technology service platform and investment marketplace for institutional owners, buyers, sellers, lenders and borrowers of residential rental real estate. Founded in 2020, it connects institutional debt and equity capital to local operating partners and property owners across 21+ U.S. markets, combining proprietary property data, automated valuation, and a vetted partner network to find, finance, buy, renovate, lease, manage and sell single-family rental homes at scale. Its service lines span lending (bridge and SFR portfolio loans), strategy development, acquisitions, renovations, asset management, title and brokerage or dispositions. The company reports $2.2B+ of capital deployed. Its software runs as a private, login-gated product suite ("AvenueOS") for internal, builder, investor and partner users; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Beyond Limits
providers.description: Beyond Limits (trading as BeyondAI) is an enterprise and industrial artificial intelligence company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Glendale, California, built on cognitive and neuro-symbolic AI technology licensed from Caltech and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Its Hybrid AI Platform combines machine learning, generative AI and rule-based symbolic reasoning so that industrial operators get explainable, auditable recommendations instead of black-box predictions. Products include the Hybrid AI Platform (with Data, ML Ops/PRE, KB Ops and a low-code API available under a development license), Operations Advisor, Beyond Search generative AI, AI in a Box on-premises infrastructure, and DocLink document process automation from its Altec subsidiary. The company sells into energy and LNG, oil and gas, refining, petrochemicals, utilities, mining, manufacturing, aerospace and critical infrastructure. Beyond Limits publishes no public developer portal, API reference or self-service sign-up; platform API access is granted to licensed customers, so there is no publicly discoverable machine-readable contract for this provider.

providers.name: Boardable
providers.description: Boardable is board management software for nonprofits, associations, foundations, and other mission-driven organizations, covering meeting scheduling, agenda building, a document center, minutes and AI-generated meeting summaries, e-voting, task assignments, groups/committees, member directories, and built-in video conferencing. As of this review Boardable does NOT publish a documented public developer API: there is no developer portal, no published API reference, no OpenAPI, no self-serve API keys, and no documented webhooks. A private, authentication-gated backend API exists at https://api.boardable.com (for example, GET https://api.boardable.com/accounts returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized) that powers the Boardable web and mobile apps, but it is undocumented and not offered as a public/partner integration surface. Third-party listings occasionally describe Boardable as having an "open API," but Boardable provides no public developer documentation to substantiate that. Integrations are delivered through pre-built connectors (Salesforce, Microsoft 365 / Teams / Outlook / SharePoint / OneDrive, Google Drive & Calendar, Zoom, Dropbox, LinkedIn) rather than a documented API. This entry is therefore an honest stub: no APIs are listed because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Boatsetter
providers.description: Boatsetter is a Fort Lauderdale, Florida founded and Miami headquartered peer-to-peer boat rental marketplace that connects boat owners with renters and with United States Coast Guard licensed captains. Founded in 2012, the platform lists more than 50,000 boats across 600 to 700 locations worldwide and 20,000 makes and models, spanning fishing boats, pontoons, sailboats, party boats, watersports vessels and luxury yacht charters, bookable either bareboat or with a captain. Boatsetter layers identity verification, an insurance program underwritten through its Buoy partnership, payments, messaging, calendar and pricing tools for owners, and trust and safety on top of owner supplied inventory, and takes a marketplace commission on each booking. The company also operates a separate Boatsetter Owner application for hosts, and in December 2025 announced a merger with Getmyboat to form a combined boat rental marketplace expected to process roughly 500 million dollars in bookings across 50 countries, with both platforms and apps continuing to operate. Boatsetter does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, developer portal, or partner API documentation; its only public GitHub presence is a single archived fork of a jQuery form serialization plugin, and its third party surface is limited to consumer facing partnerships (Airbnb) and an affiliate marketing program.

providers.name: Booster Fuels
providers.description: Booster (Booster Fuels, Inc.) is a mobile energy delivery company that brings gasoline, diesel, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF), and renewable fuel alternatives directly to vehicles, fleets, and on-site fuel tanks using a fleet of Smart Tankers, removing the need for drivers to visit gas stations. The company serves enterprise fleets and local businesses across the United States, pairing on-demand fueling with a proprietary technology platform (BoosterOS / the Fleet dashboard at fleet.trybooster.com) for real-time fleet management, fuel-usage reporting, invoicing automation, fraud prevention, and emissions reduction. Booster offers custom enterprise integrations (ERP, CRM, and telematics such as Geotab and Samsara) but does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. This profile is a company/lead entry in the API Evangelist network; no public API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Brain
providers.description: Brain Co. builds agent-native operating systems for institutions across the public and private sectors. Its Atlas platform powers GovOS — permitting, licensing, claims, and casework for government agencies at national scale — and InsuranceOS for underwriting, claims, authorization, and insurance operations, with an emphasis on sovereign-grade security and vendor neutrality. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the company was cofounded by Elad Gil, Jared Kushner, and Luis Videgaray, with a team drawn from Google, DeepMind, NVIDIA, Palantir, and Tesla. Brain Co. does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definitions; this profile tracks its public web surface (news, trust center, privacy and terms) pending any future developer program.

providers.name: BWX Technologies
providers.description: BWX Technologies is a manufacturer of nuclear components and provider of nuclear services to the U.S. government and commercial customers worldwide. The company delivers innovative nuclear solutions across naval propulsion, small modular reactors, nuclear fuel, medical isotopes, and complex site operations.

providers.name: Campflare
providers.description: Campflare provides real-time campground availability data and cancellation alerts as a public API. The platform tracks campsites across every major public reservation system in North America and notifies users (via webhook) the moment a site matching their criteria becomes available. Campflare's data and services are open to the public programmatically — individuals and non-profits get free access to all APIs, while commercial use requires a paid license. Campflare also powers partner products such as Hipcamp Alerts. Current API access is invite-only; requests go to contact@campflare.com and are typically granted within 24–48 hours.

providers.name: CloudLock
providers.description: CloudLock is a cloud-native Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) that protects data, users, and applications across SaaS, IaaS, PaaS, and IDaaS environments. Founded in 2011 and acquired by Cisco in 2016, it is now delivered as Cisco Cloudlock within Cisco Umbrella / Cisco Security Cloud. The platform uses an API-driven model to discover sensitive content, detect policy violations, flag anomalous user behavior, and manage cloud application (OAuth) risk. Developers integrate through the Cisco Cloudlock API (v2), a Bearer-token REST API exposing activities, incidents, incident entities, incident aggregates, policies, apps, entities, IP libraries, and anomalies. Originally a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, CloudLock's developer surface is documented on Cisco DevNet and the Cisco Umbrella documentation hub.

providers.name: Cogoport
providers.description: Cogoport is a global logistics and supply chain platform offering freight booking, customs, trade finance, and supply chain visibility for businesses across ocean, air, and inland transport. It provides ocean (FCL and LCL) and air freight booking with real-time rate discovery, customs clearance and compliance support, trade finance including invoice financing and pay-later solutions, end-to-end shipment tracking, and logistics tools such as an HS Code Finder, container trackers, and shipping cost calculators. Cogoport is backed by Accel and headquartered in India, serving importers and exporters worldwide.

providers.name: Corduro
providers.description: Corduro is a payments-as-a-service company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Southlake, Texas, offering a mobile, online, and point-of-sale payment platform for small businesses, enterprises, and organizations. Its platform enables merchants to accept credit-card and electronic-check payments, bill pay, recurring billing, text giving, and event and donation payments through a single intelligent payment gateway that is advertised to reduce processing fees by 20% or more. Corduro bundles eCommerce, Engage, Events, Text Giving, and Developer Tools products, provides embeddable iFrame and API-based payment integrations, and markets PCI compliance as a managed capability. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and enriched from the company's public web presence; Corduro publishes no public OpenAPI, developer portal, or API reference, gating developer/API access behind sales contact.

providers.name: Corebridge Financial
providers.description: Corebridge Financial (formerly AIG Life and Retirement) is one of the largest and most established retirement and insurance solutions providers in the United States. Spun off from AIG in September 2022 in the largest IPO of that year, Corebridge provides retirement solutions, life insurance, fixed and variable annuities, and institutional products. The company is a leading retirement plan provider for K-12 schools, healthcare, government, higher education, and other not-for-profit institutions. Corebridge Financial does not currently publish a public developer API; participant and plan sponsor access is provided through dedicated portals.

providers.name: Cortico
providers.description: Cortico (Cortico Health Technologies) is a Vancouver, British Columbia based healthcare connection platform, founded in 2019, that links patients, medical clinics, and health records across Canada and the United States. Its patient-engagement suite layers online booking, automated appointment reminders, secure two-way patient messaging, digital intake forms, telemedicine, specialist e-referrals, payments, and AI-driven administrative automation on top of the electronic medical records (EMRs) clinics already run — most notably a supported two-way integration with OSCAR EMR through that system's REST/SOAP web services, plus SMART on FHIR contextual launch and robotic process automation (RPA). Cortico is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and compliant with HIPAA, PIPEDA, and PHIPA. Cortico consumes EMR and FHIR interfaces rather than publishing its own public developer API: as of this review there is no public developer portal, API reference, or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and integration is delivered through a partnership and onboarding model rather than self-serve API access.

providers.name: COUNTRY Financial
providers.description: COUNTRY Financial is the marketing name for an Illinois-headquartered family of affiliated insurance and financial services companies that includes COUNTRY Life Insurance Company, COUNTRY Mutual Insurance Company, COUNTRY Casualty Insurance Company, COUNTRY Preferred Insurance Company, and related subsidiaries based in Bloomington, IL. Founded in 1925 by Illinois Agricultural Association members, COUNTRY today offers auto, home, life, farm, crop, and commercial insurance along with investment, retirement planning, and trust services through a captive agent network in 19 U.S. states. COUNTRY does not publish a public developer API; partner and agency integrations occur through internal agency systems.

providers.name: CVS Health
providers.description: CVS Health is a Fortune 50 healthcare services and retail pharmacy company. Its core operating units include CVS Pharmacy (retail pharmacy and mail-order), CVS Caremark (pharmacy benefit management / PBM), Aetna (health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, dental and vision), MinuteClinic (walk-in clinics), Oak Street Health (primary care for Medicare patients), and Signify Health (in-home health evaluations). CVS Health does not currently operate a public developer portal or generally available REST API. Programmatic integrations with CVS Pharmacy, Caremark, and Aetna are typically established through business partnership agreements, EDI / NCPDP pharmacy networks, and HIPAA-aligned interoperability channels (e.g., FHIR endpoints exposed to qualifying healthcare partners under regulatory mandates such as the CMS Interoperability Rule). Developer-facing artifacts in this index are limited to public marketing, corporate, and digital health references.

providers.name: Deep Rooted
providers.description: Deep Rooted.Co is a direct-to-consumer fresh produce brand operated by Clover Ventures Pvt. Ltd, a Bengaluru-based agritech company founded in 2018 that launched the Deep Rooted consumer brand in 2020. The company works with a network of small-scale farmers using greenhouse and hydroponic techniques within roughly 150km of Bengaluru and Hyderabad, providing agronomy support from seed to harvest and delivering fruits, vegetables, Indian staples and greens, exotic produce and an easy-cook range direct to households the morning after ordering. Deep Rooted is backed by Accel. It sells through a consumer web storefront and mobile apps; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification, so this profile captures company identity and web properties only.

providers.name: Defense Information System for Security
providers.description: The Defense Information System for Security (DISS) is the enterprise-wide Department of Defense system of record for personnel security, suitability, and credentialing management for military, civilian, and contractor personnel. Operated by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), DISS replaced the Joint Personnel Adjudication System (JPAS) as the system of record on March 31, 2021. DISS is restricted to authorized DoD and federal users and contractor security officers; it does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: doinstruct
providers.description: doinstruct is an AI-powered frontline training and compliance platform for deskless and shift-based workforces. Founded in Osnabrück, Germany in 2021 and now headquartered in Brooklyn, New York with an office in Berlin, it turns internal SOPs, documents, and expert knowledge into mobile-first courses delivered in 35+ languages. Its Genius AI authoring tool, a 400+ lesson training library, a manager dashboard for assigning and documenting training, and a mobile learner experience serve 400+ frontline teams across food & beverage, logistics, manufacturing, construction, and general compliance, with audit-ready reporting for standards such as HACCP, GFSI, and ISO 27001. Backed by Creandum and HV Capital.

providers.name: EverTrue
providers.description: EverTrue is a donor experience and fundraising platform for nonprofit, higher-education, and healthcare advancement teams, serving more than 13,000 teams. Its product suite spans AI-driven prospect identification and research (Signal, DonorSearch), donor outreach and stewardship (ThankView personalized video, Pledgemine direct mail), and endowment reporting (Balance, Impact, ODDER). EverTrue integrates with advancement CRMs such as Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT via an automated data sync. EverTrue operates as a closed B2B SaaS: it runs internal REST APIs behind its iOS, Android, and single-page web applications but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API program. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Techstars.

providers.name: exein
providers.description: Exein is a Physical AI and embedded/IoT cybersecurity company (Italy) that secures connected devices, firmware, and Linux/RTOS embedded systems. Its platform pairs on-device runtime threat detection (Exein Runtime) with AI-powered firmware analysis and SBOM ingestion (Exein Analyzer), mapping findings to standards including the EU Cyber Resilience Act, ETSI EN 303-645, IEC 62443, RED 3.3, and the US Cyber Trust Mark. Exein does not publish a hosted public REST API; its developer surface is open-source security tooling in the exein-io GitHub organization — notably Pulsar (an eBPF-powered runtime security agent) and Kepler (a NIST-based CVE lookup store and API). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital, hv-capital, and partech.

providers.name: Freedom Robotics
providers.description: Freedom Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics infrastructure company founded in 2017 that builds mission-critical software to help robotics companies build, operate, support, and scale heterogeneous robot fleets. Its cloud platform — sometimes referred to as Mission Control — provides device and fleet management, remote teleoperation (Pilot), live data streaming, smart alerts and notifications, fleet maps and heatmaps, deployment and service management, remote development, and analytics across cobots, industrial robots, AMRs, drones, and custom hardware. The platform is robot- and OS-agnostic, installs on a device in seconds via a single-line Freedom Agent installer, and integrates with ROS, ROS 2, Python, microcontrollers, Protobuf, Docker, and the cloud offerings of AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Freedom exposes a public REST API at api.freedomrobotics.ai covering accounts, devices, alerts, statistics, uploads, tokens, users, user groups, and zones, plus a Python SDK (freedomrobotics.link) with Link, MicroLink, message, log, image, and command-callback primitives for programmatic control and telemetry of large numbers of robots. The company has raised approximately $17M in venture funding and operates on a per-robot subscription model (publicly cited at roughly $300 per robot per month) with custom enterprise plans negotiated through sales.

providers.name: Gireve
providers.description: Gireve is a B2B digital platform for electric-vehicle charging and new-mobility services, connecting charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs), and EV drivers across Europe. Its interoperability hub powers EV charging roaming, clearing and transaction settlement, Plug & Charge, smart charging, and mobility data services, spanning 680,000+ connected charging points and roughly one million monthly roaming transactions across 13,000+ signed agreements. Technical integration is delivered to connected operators over an OCPI-based hub through the Connect Place B2B platform; Gireve does not publish a public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Go To-U
providers.description: GO TO-U is an operating system for electric-vehicle charging management, built for Charge Point Operators (CPOs) and businesses that run charging infrastructure. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating with 50+ charger manufacturers (ABB, Wallbox, Siemens, EVBox and others), and bundles charge-point management, AI-powered analytics and load optimization, a driver-facing mobile app (iOS and Android), roaming, white-label options, and integrated payment processing. Its Advanced Reservation Technology (ART) lets drivers book charging slots in advance to reduce wait times. GO TO-U is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from the company's public website; no public developer/API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications were discoverable at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Goldbelly
providers.description: Goldbelly is a curated online marketplace for gourmet food and mail-order culinary gifts, shipping iconic meals, desserts, regional specialties, and artisanal products from renowned restaurants, bakeries, and celebrity chefs across the United States directly to consumers' doors. The platform partners with thousands of local and legendary food makers to make hard-to-get regional foods available nationwide, and operates a merchant program ("Sell on Goldbelly") plus corporate and subscription gifting. Goldbelly is a consumer e-commerce brand with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, merchant, and corporate identity. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Habitat Lab
providers.description: Habitat Lab is Meta AI Research's embodied AI simulation platform. It provides documentation, quickstart code, and tools for training and evaluating AI agents in photorealistic 3D environments, with Habitat 2.0 focusing on household rearrangement tasks. Habitat Lab is delivered as a Python research library; it does not currently expose a public HTTP API.

providers.name: Heartland Payment Systems
providers.description: Heartland Payment Systems is a payment processing company offering payroll, customer engagement, point-of-sale, and other business solutions to merchants across the United States. Heartland is now a brand of Global Payments, and developer resources for Heartland integrations are published through the Global Payments developer portal. The platform supports online and in-person payments, bill pay, IoT/connected device payments, gift and loyalty, payroll, and PCI-validated point-to-point encryption.

providers.name: Hrmony
providers.description: Hrmony is a Berlin-based employee-benefits platform that lets German employers offer modern, tax-advantaged perks to their staff — meal allowances (Essenszuschuss), the 50 euro monthly non-cash benefit (Sachbezug) and benefit card, mobility and public-transit budgets, health and recreation benefits, internet-cost subsidies and digital gifts — all managed through an admin portal and employee app with built-in payroll and tax compliance. Its Hrmony Embedded product exposes this benefits infrastructure as a white-label RESTful API so software platforms and SaaS providers can integrate multiple benefit modules without building the tax-compliance, operations or regulatory layer in-house. Hrmony is backed by Techstars. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; no public developer documentation or OpenAPI is currently published (Embedded onboarding is partner-gated).

providers.name: Insuretech Connect
providers.description: InsureTech Connect (ITC) is the world's largest insurance innovation event series, produced by Clarion Events. Its flagship, ITC Vegas, brings together 9,000+ insurance carriers, insurtech startups, brokers, reinsurers, and investors for three days of content, networking, and dealmaking, with regional editions in Europe and Asia. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qed-investors and added to the API Evangelist network. ITC is an events and media brand; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or event webhooks, so this entry carries company identity and probed domain-security signals only.

providers.name: JMock
providers.description: JMock is a library that supports test-driven development of Java code with mock objects. It provides an expressive API for defining expectations and mock behavior in unit tests, integrating with popular testing frameworks including JUnit. The most recent stable release is jMock 2.13.1.

providers.name: Kotlin
providers.description: Kotlin is a modern, concise, and safe programming language for the JVM, Android, and multiplatform development. It is developed by JetBrains and provides full interoperability with Java. Kotlin's standard library and ecosystem offer rich APIs for building applications across all platforms.

providers.name: LabDoor
providers.description: Labdoor is an independent San Francisco-based supplement testing company that buys top-selling vitamins, supplements, protein powders and energy drinks off retail shelves and online stores and sends samples to FDA-registered analytical laboratories for chemical analysis of active ingredients and potential contaminants. It grades every product on Label Accuracy, Product Purity, Nutritional Value, Ingredient Safety and Projected Efficacy, then publishes the resulting rankings, scores and expert reports for free so consumers can compare products, and it funds that testing through retail sales and through Labdoor Enterprise certification and custom-testing services sold to manufacturers. Labdoor publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or API documentation as of July 2026.

providers.name: LaborUp
providers.description: LaborUp is an AI-powered recruiting platform for American manufacturing, connecting skilled industrial workers — machinists, CNC programmers, welders, and maintenance technicians — with manufacturing employers. The platform combines voice-first AI screening, skills verification, and constraint-aware matching with dedicated recruiter support, and claims 5-10x faster hiring, more than 50% lower cost than traditional staffing agencies, 3x better post-hire retention, and a proprietary network of 25,000+ vetted workers. Founded by Simba Jonga, LaborUp raised $7.74M ($1.935M pre-seed plus a $5.8M seed announced in August 2025) led by NVP with Torch Capital, Threshold, Heartland VC, Daybreak, Westbound, Marketplace Capital, and Market Square Ventures. Early traction is concentrated in the Knoxville, Tennessee manufacturing corridor and in aerospace, shipbuilding, and critical infrastructure. As of July 2026 LaborUp publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification; the product is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application.

providers.name: Liftoff
providers.description: Liftoff (onliftoff.com, formerly liftoff.xyz) is a B2B network-based hiring and networking platform for startup leaders and hiring managers. Rather than cold applications or job-board sourcing, companies create a job search, attach a self-set "Match Incentive" referral bonus, and share the search link with their own network or with Liftoff's curated "Top Connectors" — senior leaders who refer pre-vetted candidates from their professional circles. Candidates surface through 2nd- and 3rd-degree trusted connections, and companies pay on a success-only basis, with fees due after a new hire completes 90 days. Liftoff targets seed-to-Series-B technology companies, primarily in the New York City and San Francisco ecosystems, and positions itself between LinkedIn recruiting and traditional retained search. Backed by Forerunner Ventures. Liftoff publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; it does publish an llms.txt for AI agent grounding. Not to be confused with Liftoff Mobile (liftoff.io, ad tech) or useLiftoff (useliftoff.com, job-seeker interview practice).

providers.name: Linas Matkasse
providers.description: Linas Matkasse is a Swedish meal-kit subscription service that delivers pre-portioned ingredients and nutritionally calculated recipes to customers' homes each week. Customers pick from more than 150 weekly recipes across concepts such as Chef's Choice, Family Favorites, Quick & Easy, Calorie-Smart, Vegetarian, Gluten-Free and Lactose-Free, and can change their selection until Tuesday night before a Saturday-to-Monday delivery. The brand is operated by Cheffelo, a Scandinavian meal-kit group listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market that also runs Godtlevert in Norway and RetNemt in Denmark and delivers roughly 17 million meals a year. Linas Matkasse runs a consumer subscription e-commerce storefront and a "Mina Sidor" customer account area; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Listia
providers.description: Listia is a peer-to-peer marketplace where members give away and acquire secondhand goods using an internal virtual currency ("Points") rather than cash. Launched in 2009 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, the service lets members list unwanted items in auction-style listings, earn Points when an item sells, and spend those Points to claim items from other members — a closed-loop credit-and-reputation economy layered on a classic online-auction flow. The site reports over 10 million members, operates iOS and Android apps alongside the web marketplace, and runs adjacent programs including Listia Rewards (redeeming Points for gift cards and retail goods) and Listia Assurance (buyer and seller protection). Listia publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, and no first-party SDKs on npm, PyPI, RubyGems or Packagist. The api.listia.com host serves the same Rails application as the website and acts as the private backend for the mobile apps, not a documented public API.

providers.name: Luko
providers.description: Luko is an online home, travel, and auto insurance provider founded in France in 2016 and now operating as Luko by Allianz Direct after its acquisition by the Allianz group. It sells rental, owner-occupied, non-occupant-owner (PNO), student, and co-housing home policies from around EUR 5 per month, plus travel and Eurofil-partnered auto cover, with sub-two-minute online subscription, instant attestations, digital claims declaration through a customer account portal, and 24/7 emergency support. Originally a VC-backed insurtech (Accel, Speedinvest), Luko today runs as a consumer insurance brand with no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable security and identity footprint.

providers.name: Milkman
providers.description: Milkman is an open-source, JavaFx-based, plugin-driven request/response workbench and desktop alternative to Postman and Insomnia. It supports multiple protocols including HTTP/REST, GraphQL, gRPC (with server reflection and streaming), WebSocket, Socket.IO, JDBC/SQL, Cassandra CQL, and Model Context Protocol (MCP).

providers.name: Motional
providers.description: Motional is a Boston-headquartered autonomous-vehicle company formed as a joint venture between Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv. Its core product is an all-electric IONIQ 5 robotaxi built on a Hyundai E-GMP platform with Motional's full Level 4 autonomous driving stack and a sensor suite including lidar, radar, and cameras. Motional operates commercial robotaxi service in Las Vegas in partnership with Uber, Uber Eats, and Lyft, with additional operations in Boston, Pittsburgh, Santa Monica, Singapore, and Seoul. The company's most influential developer artifact is nuScenes, the open large-scale multimodal autonomous-driving dataset originally released by nuTonomy (a Motional predecessor), now a de facto benchmark for 3D perception research. Motional also publishes the nuscenes-devkit Python library and AVCDL cybersecurity development lifecycle materials on GitHub. Motional does not publish a traditional public developer API; the developer surface is research-dataset access plus open-source devkits.

providers.name: Nova Benefits
providers.description: Nova Benefits is an India-based employee health and benefits platform that provides group health insurance, super top-up plans, and COVID-19 cover alongside wellness services such as telehealth consultations, mental-wellness support, fitness programs, maternity benefits, and annual health, dental and vision checkups. It gives HR teams an employer dashboard for administering benefits and managing claims, and gives employees web and mobile (iOS/Android) apps to view coverage, book consultations, and file and track claims. The company reports serving 500+ companies covering 200,000+ employees, is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 Type II compliant, and operates as an IRDAI-regulated insurance broker. Nova Benefits publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: NumPy
providers.description: The fundamental package for scientific computing with Python. NumPy provides multi-dimensional array objects, various derived objects, and an assortment of routines for fast operations on arrays, including mathematical, logical, shape manipulation, sorting, selecting, I/O, FFT, and random number generation.

providers.name: Octane Lending
providers.description: Octane (Octane Lending, Inc.) is a New York City fintech founded in 2014 that makes powersports, outdoor power equipment and recreational-vehicle financing as simple as paying cash. It runs an end-to-end digital lending platform — instant soft-pull prequalification for consumers, real-time credit decisioning and eContracting through its in-house lender Roadrunner Financial, Inc., and loan servicing — connecting more than 4,000 dealer partners and 30-plus OEMs with prime through non-prime buyers. Its Dealer Portal 2.0 and dealer-management-system integrations (AppOne, Ekho and similar DMS platforms) submit credit applications and return decisions over a partner API whose credentials are coordinated privately by Octane account managers; Octane publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: OpenEBS
providers.description: OpenEBS is a popular and widely deployed open source Container Native Storage platform for stateful persistent applications on Kubernetes. It provides dynamic provisioning of storage resources using containerized storage controllers, making it highly flexible and cloud-native.

providers.name: Ottonova
providers.description: Ottonova is a Munich-based digital private health insurance provider (private Krankenversicherung) founded in 2015, positioned as "the insurance for the mobile age." It sells private full health insurance and supplementary dental and hospital coverage to consumers in Germany, delivering onboarding, claims, a concierge medical service and digital health records through its mobile app rather than through a public developer API. Ottonova is backed by venture investors including Earlybird and HV Capital and operates in the insurtech sector. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio-lead stub and has been through one enrichment pass: probing confirmed a consumer web presence with a published RFC 9116 security.txt but no public API surface (no developer portal, OpenAPI, OAuth/OpenID metadata, or API catalog).

providers.name: Outverse
providers.description: Outverse is an enterprise "service AI operating system" from Outverse Limited, a UK company backed by Seedcamp and Wing Venture Capital. Its platform lets support and operations teams deploy governed AI agents across complex customer-service workflows — email, chat, voice, and API-driven actions — from a single control center. Teams define logic, policies, and human handoffs in natural language SOPs rather than rigid workflow builders, and get observability over every agent decision, tool call, workflow path, and escalation. Outverse integrates with existing CCaaS and CRM stacks (Salesforce, Freshdesk, Genesys, Twilio, Talkdesk) and offers voice agents that verify identity, retrieve data, apply policy, and resolve calls end to end. The company advertises SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification and does not expose a public developer API at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Plans
providers.description: Plans (plans.app, formerly lun.energy) is a climate-technology company focused on decarbonising the built world. It removes the friction that stands in the way of transitioning homes to low-carbon energy faster, letting professionals capture building data on a mobile device, analyze it, and produce retrofit / energy plans — "capture, analyze, plan, all in your pocket." A web platform (platform.plans.app) and a Chrome extension support the workflow, and the product is offered across English, Danish, and French markets. Plans is backed by Partech. No public developer API has been identified during enrichment; the platform is a login-gated single-page application and the site exposes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or developer portal.

providers.name: PraxisPro AI
providers.description: PraxisPro AI is an AI-powered training platform built to modernize pharmaceutical and medical device sales training for life sciences organizations. Its modules include PraxisPlay (AI roleplay simulations with realistic healthcare-provider agents), PraxisCertify (certification tracking and knowledge-gap identification), PraxisCoach (performance coaching and feedback), and PraxisIntelligence (analytics and insights for management). The platform serves sales reps, trainers, managers, MSLs, compliance, and marketing teams with personalized, AI-driven scenarios, immediate feedback, and performance tracking. Backed by Techstars. Delivered as a SaaS product; no public developer API surface is published at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Raymond James Bank
providers.description: Raymond James Bank is a Florida-chartered state member bank headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Raymond James Financial, Inc. (NYSE: RJF), a diversified financial services holding company founded in 1962. Supervised by the Federal Reserve and the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, the bank provides securities-based lending, residential mortgages, commercial and industrial and commercial real estate loans, tax-exempt loans, and deposit products (including its Enhanced Savings Program) primarily to Raymond James wealth-management and institutional clients. On open finance, the bank runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators such as Plaid. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented for this institution as of this record.

providers.name: Regrello
providers.description: Regrello is an AI operating system for manufacturing and supply chain operations, giving teams that are stuck in email and stifled by decades-old ERPs an agentic AI platform to accelerate innovation and productivity. Its product, Agentforce Operations, orchestrates enterprise manufacturing and supply chain workflows with generative AI. Regrello was acquired by Salesforce and is backed by a16z and Bloomberg Beta. This profile currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network for its identity, security posture, and published compliance program.

providers.name: Replenysh
providers.description: Replenysh is an enterprise circularity platform that runs circular supply chains for brands and recovery facilities. It routes, recovers, verifies, and optimizes material recovery flows across a network of 5,000+ partners, giving enterprises a single control layer for reverse logistics with audit-ready chain-of-custody, pricing, settlement, and compliance documentation. Customers include PepsiCo, Disney, Marriott, and Live Nation. Backed by Kindred Ventures and M13. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Schaeffler
providers.description: Schaeffler Group is a German global Tier 1 automotive and industrial supplier headquartered in Herzogenaurach. Schaeffler designs and manufactures precision bearings, powertrain components, chassis applications, and e-mobility systems for the automotive and industrial sectors.

providers.name: Sphero
providers.description: Sphero designs programmable robots and STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and math) learning tools for K-12 education. Its product line spans indi, Mini, Snap, BOLT+, littleBits, RVR+ and Blueprint robots, paired with standards-aligned curriculum (NGSS, CSTA, ISTE) delivered through Sphero Central. For developers and educators, Sphero publishes a public robot-control SDK (sdk.sphero.com) that programs Sphero RVR+ / RVR robots from development boards — Raspberry Pi, micro:bit and Arduino — using Python, Node.js/TypeScript and C++. Sphero exposes robot-control SDKs and a locally-run Node.js RESTful interface rather than a hosted public web API. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist as part of the APIs.io network.

providers.name: Standard Practice
providers.description: Standard Practice builds voice AI for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) teams. Its AI agents place and handle outbound phone calls to insurance payers to automate administrative work — claim status follow-up, benefits verification, prior authorization, and EDI enrollment — so billing teams can scale collections and get paid more, faster. The platform is delivered as a private, login-gated web application. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Wing Venture Capital and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Tabnine
providers.description: Tabnine provides AI code completion, chat, and agentic workflows across IDEs and CLI, with strong support for SaaS, VPC, and air-gapped on-prem deployments. The Enterprise Context Engine indexes a customer's codebase, dependencies, and architecture. Tabnine's consumer surface is via IDE plugins (VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse) and the Tabnine CLI; there is no general-purpose public REST inference API for end-developers.

providers.name: Tennr
providers.description: Tennr is a New York City-based healthcare technology company (founded 2021) building agentic patient-orchestration software that automates referral-based care operations for providers and health systems. Its proprietary vision-language model, RaeLM, is trained on over 100 million anonymized medical documents to read faxes, referrals, and unstructured records, then automates document classification, data extraction, patient qualification, insurance eligibility verification, and prior-authorization submission by integrating directly with existing EHR systems. Tennr processes over 10 million documents monthly and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant. It raised a $101M Series C at a $605M valuation led by IVP, with a16z, Lightspeed, GV, ICONIQ, and Foundation Capital participating. Tennr does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or specification; integrations are delivered through EHR connections and professional services.

providers.name: Terra
providers.description: Terra Security operates an agentic-AI-powered continuous offensive security (penetration testing) platform. Founded in 2024 and based in Tel Aviv, Terra runs a swarm of AI agents with a human-on-the-loop workflow that continuously validates every attack surface — web and internal applications, external and internal networks, and AI systems such as LLMs, copilots, MCP servers, and autonomous agents (AI red teaming). The platform compresses multi-week legacy pentests into hours, produces verified (low-noise) findings, and generates audit-ready evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA programs. Terra raised a $30M Series A led by Felicis in 2025. Terra publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web surface and security posture.

providers.name: TherapyNotes
providers.description: TherapyNotes is a HIPAA-compliant practice management and electronic health record (EHR) platform built specifically for behavioral health - therapists, psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers, and group practices. It provides interactive note templates and clinical documentation, scheduling with appointment reminders, a client portal, telehealth, electronic insurance claims and ERA, credit card processing, and TherapyFuel AI tooling. As of this writing TherapyNotes does NOT expose a public or partner developer API, webhooks, or documented programmatic interface; access to client, appointment, clinical-note, and billing data is through the browser application and manual exports only. This entry documents TherapyNotes as an API-relevant provider and honestly models the capability areas a behavioral-health EHR API would cover; the API surfaces below are modeled, not published, and no endpoints are fabricated.

providers.name: Tia
providers.description: Tia is a women's healthcare company that operates in-person clinics and a virtual care platform, bringing primary care, gynecology, mental health, and wellness services into one connected care experience. Founded in 2017 and backed by Canaan Partners, Tia runs clinics in New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix, offers virtual visits across multiple states, and partners with health systems. Tia is a consumer healthcare provider and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Tillpoint
providers.description: Tillpoint is a modular, cloud-based EPOS (electronic point of sale) and business management platform for retail, hospitality, and services. A single subscription bundles 25+ modules - Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers/CRM, Staff, Accounting, Purchase Orders, Reporting, and more - across one terminal or thousands of locations. As of this review Tillpoint does not publish a documented public or partner developer API - there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no OpenAPI. Connectivity is delivered through pre-built integrations (QuickBooks Online, Xero, WooCommerce, PayPal, Worldpay, Mailchimp). The API surfaces catalogued here (Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers, Accounting) are logical capability areas of the platform and are honestly marked as endpointsModeled - no endpoints are fabricated. Direct/programmatic access requires contacting Tillpoint.

providers.name: TOCA Football
providers.description: TOCA Football, Inc. is a technology-enabled soccer experience and entertainment company headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, founded on the training methodology of former US international and Premier League player Eddie Lewis. It operates two businesses: TOCA Soccer, a network of indoor soccer training centers across the United States, Canada and Mexico offering private training, classes, clinics, camps, youth and adult leagues, tournaments and pickup play; and TOCA Social, a soccer-themed dining and entertainment venue brand. Its training centers pair a proprietary ball-delivery machine and digitalized smart targets with the MyTOCA player app, which tracks session performance, player cards, leaderboards and progress. TOCA is the official soccer training partner of Major League Soccer. TOCA publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer program: its software ships only as end-user consumer apps and in-venue systems.

providers.name: TradeDepot
providers.description: TradeDepot is a Lagos-based B2B commerce and distribution platform that connects consumer-goods brands and distributors with neighborhood retailers across Africa. Its ShopTopUp platform lets small retailers order and pay for inventory, and its first-party developer surface is a set of ShopTopUp "Agent/Shop Checkout" mobile SDKs (Android, React Native, Cordova) published under github.com/tradedepot and npm, initialized with partner API keys. TradeDepot publishes no public REST API, developer portal, or API documentation. Backed by Partech.

providers.name: University Startups
providers.description: University Startups is an AI-powered transition planning management platform built for special education teams. The platform helps teachers create IDEA-compliant IEP transition plans in under 10 minutes, audits plans against 11 IDEA Indicator 13 criteria in under 90 seconds, generates SMART-format IEP goals, and engages students with disabilities in building their own transition plans, alongside a college and career readiness curriculum and internship simulator. A Techstars portfolio company serving United States school districts including NYC Public Schools; no public developer API surface is published.

providers.name: Upwave
providers.description: Upwave (formerly Survata) is the Brand Outcomes Measurement Platform — it brings science to top-of-funnel advertising by measuring Brand Lift, validating Brand Reach, and surfacing optimization insights for brand campaigns across CTV, digital, linear TV, audio, and social channels. Advertisers, agencies, and media platforms use Upwave dashboards and its Bayes AI layer to quantify how campaigns move awareness, favorability, consideration, and intent. Upwave is delivered as a SaaS application with a managed partner ecosystem of ad servers and DSPs, and does not publish a public developer portal or API documentation. It is a portfolio company of Y Combinator, Uncork Capital, and Initialized Capital.

providers.name: Valeo
providers.description: Valeo is a French global Tier 1 automotive supplier headquartered in Paris. Valeo designs and manufactures comfort and driving assistance, powertrain, thermal, and visibility systems for the automotive industry, with a strong focus on electrification and ADAS.

providers.name: Vector.ai
providers.description: Vector.ai, now operating as Raft (raft.ai), is an AI-powered logistics automation platform for freight forwarders, customs brokers, and trade finance teams. The Raft Intelligence Engine layers organization data, contextual LLMs, orchestration, and specialized governed agents to automate document processing, invoice matching, data extraction, and exception handling across supply chain operations, reporting 20M+ tasks completed by AI agents and 5M+ shipments processed annually. Raft publishes no public developer API; the platform is an enterprise application that integrates with customers' TMS and ERP systems.

providers.name: Voya Financial
providers.description: Voya Financial (NYSE: VOYA) is a leading health, wealth, and investment company serving approximately 14.7 million individual, workplace, and institutional clients. Voya specializes in retirement plans, group employee benefits, health savings accounts (HSAs), and investment management.
