providers.description: tvScientific is a connected-TV (CTV) advertising platform for performance marketers, pairing premium streaming-TV inventory with AI-powered bidding and optimization and outcome-based measurement so brands can run television campaigns against measurable goals like sales, app installs, and site traffic. It positions itself on "premium inventory, AI-powered optimization, and radical transparency," and offers a self-serve buying platform plus an academy and reporting resources for advertisers and agencies. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners, its own web properties now brand it "tvScientific by Pinterest." No public developer/API surface, OpenAPI, or documentation portal was found during enrichment; the company publishes a trust center, blog, and legal pages.

providers.name: United States European Command
providers.description: United States European Command (EUCOM) is one of the eleven unified combatant commands of the U.S. Department of Defense. EUCOM is responsible for U.S. military operations and security cooperation in Europe, as well as parts of North Africa and the Middle East. The command works to support NATO allies, deter aggression, and ensure regional stability through military exercises, humanitarian operations, and partnership activities. EUCOM does not expose public-facing REST APIs; access to EUCOM data systems requires DoD Common Access Card (CAC) authentication through restricted portals including the EUCOM intranet portal and milSuite collaboration platform.

providers.name: Utilidata
providers.description: Utilidata is an Ann Arbor, Michigan software company building Karman, a distributed AI platform that runs on a custom NVIDIA system-on-module embedded directly into electrical infrastructure — smart meters and grid-edge devices on the utility side, PDUs and power trays inside AI data centers. Karman processes high-resolution AC metrology locally (single-cycle waveform statistics at 1+ MS/s sample rates) to produce "data products" such as Power Quality Analytics, enabling millisecond-level power control, GPU/PSU failure prediction, phase balancing and power-aware scheduling. Utilidata publishes the Karman Power Aware Module as Apache-2.0 open source: a Rust reference implementation that serializes Karman data products as Protocol Buffers (package utilidata.karman.bibimbap.v1), transports them over ZeroMQ, and exposes them to Prometheus and TimescaleDB through a Helm-packaged Kubernetes stack. The company has raised a $100M Series C and counts NVIDIA, Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, American Electric Power and Renown Capital Partners among its backers.

providers.name: Xpedeon
providers.description: Xpedeon is a construction-specific ERP platform from Algorithms Software Pvt Ltd (30+ years in construction software), serving general contractors, specialist contractors, housebuilders and developers, engineer-to-order manufacturers, and off-site manufacturers across the UK, India, the GCC, and the US. The cloud platform covers construction finance and accounting, job costing and CVR, contract and subcontractor management, procurement, inventory and supply chain, plant and equipment, warehouse management, HR and payroll, CRM, and a mobile app for site teams, and is ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 and SOC 2 certified. Xpedeon publishes no public API, developer portal, or integration documentation, but does publish an llms.txt. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Xpeng
providers.description: XPENG (Xiaopeng Motors) is a Chinese smart electric-vehicle company headquartered in Guangzhou that designs and manufactures smart EVs (G6, G7, G9, P7/P7+, X9, MONA M03) with in-house advanced driver-assistance and in-car software, listed on the NYSE (XPEV) and HKEX (9868). Surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and idg-capital. XPENG publishes no public developer API: its open platform (open.xiaopeng.com) is geo-restricted and account-gated, and no public API docs, specs, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Abacum
providers.description: Abacum is an AI-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform built for CFOs and finance teams to connect financial data, automate planning and reporting, and align cross-functional teams. It unifies budgeting and forecasting, headcount and revenue planning, scenario modeling, investor and board reporting, and P&L / balance-sheet / cash-flow roll-ups, with 700+ prebuilt integrations across ERP and accounting systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Xero, Dynamics 365), HRIS and payroll (Workday, Rippling, BambooHR, Gusto, Deel), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), billing (Stripe, Chargebee, Maxio), and data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks). An Excel connector and embedded workflows keep planning models and actuals in sync. Abacum surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum and Scale Venture Partners.

providers.name: Acturis
providers.description: Acturis is a United Kingdom insurance software company founded in 2000 by David McDonald and Theo Duchen, operating the UK's leading multi-tenant SaaS platform for general insurance brokers, insurers and MGAs. The Acturis system covers commercial and personal lines broking, e-trade and digital distribution, policy administration, claims, document management, premium finance and accounting, and it builds and runs eight of the top ten UK insurer extranets. Acturis Group extends the platform into Germany, France and Canada (through the acquisitions of Power Broker and Brovada) and reports over 100,000 users across more than 40 countries. Its API posture is partner-gated and honestly not developer-facing: acturis.com markets an "API-enabled platform" and "API capabilities" but publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no self-serve onboarding. developer.acturis.com, developers.acturis.com, docs.acturis.com and api.acturis.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer and /integrations all return 404. Real integration happens through commercial agreements — insurer extranet and e-trade connections, the Polaris imarket digital-trading standards Acturis has traded on since 2005, and named bilateral work such as the Aviva claims Broker API launched in December 2024, which brokers enable through an Aviva Claims Service Manager or an Acturis Account Manager rather than through any public signup.

providers.name: AdReady (CPXi)
providers.description: AdReady is a digital advertising execution brand now operated by Digital Remedy (formerly CPX Interactive / CPXi). Digital Remedy runs an omnichannel advertising platform (AdReady+) for agencies, brands and media companies, covering campaign planning, programmatic/CTV/DOOH execution, measurement and attribution, with a RemyAI assistant and 100+ martech API integrations. AdReady originated as a Seattle self-serve ad-building tool and was acquired by CPXi in 2013; the brand and platform are today part of Digital Remedy. This company profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Digital Remedy publishes no public developer API or documentation portal, but does operate a SOC 2 trust center.

providers.name: Aeva
providers.description: Aeva Technologies is a Mountain View, California sensing and perception company that builds 4D LiDAR based on proprietary Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) technology, measuring instant velocity in addition to 3D position for every point in a scene. Its product line spans Atlas and Atlas Ultra long-range automotive-grade sensors, the Omni wide-view short-range sensor, and Eve 1 precision laser speed sensors for factory automation, serving autonomous vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, security, and physical-AI markets. Aeva is a hardware and perception-software provider rather than a web-API company: its developer surface is open-source software on the aevainc GitHub org (the AevaScenes Python SDK and Doppler ICP), the AevaScenes dataset, and product SDK/EULA-gated software delivered with its sensors. No public REST or web API is published.

providers.name: Akur8
providers.description: Akur8 is a cloud-based actuarial AI platform for P&C and life insurers, covering pricing (Data, Risk, Demand, Rate, Rate Repo, Optim, Discover), reserving, and production deployment of rating models. There is no self-serve public developer API or public API reference published on akur8.com; the platform is sold and onboarded as enterprise SaaS through a sales-led, typically two-week free pilot. The one confirmed API capability is Akur8 Deploy - once a pricing model built in Akur8 Rate is finalized, Deploy auto-generates a private, tenant-specific real-time REST rating/scoring endpoint that a customer's own policy admin or quoting system calls at quote time to return a price in milliseconds. Access to that generated endpoint is provisioned per customer within a paid contract, not published for anonymous developer signup; rating tables can also be exported in CSV, JSON, PMML, and POJO formats for offline integration.

providers.name: Amperos Health
providers.description: Amperos Health (Amperos) is an AI-native insurance revenue recovery platform for healthcare providers. It uses agentic AI together with experienced revenue cycle management (RCM) specialists to run the full insurance collections process, from claim submission through denial resolution to payment. The platform automates first-touch routine tasks, works complex denials with specialist oversight, and adapts configurable workflows to each organization's procedures across specialties including orthopedics, cardiology, behavioral health, DME/HME, ophthalmology, anesthesiology, dermatology, urology, dental, and oncology. Amperos reports outcomes such as higher claim recovery, reduced accounts receivable backlogs, and lower cost to collect for the healthcare providers it serves. The company is backed by Uncork Capital and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company. Amperos currently exposes a marketing and demo-request surface rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public web properties and security posture.

providers.name: Apiable
providers.description: Apiable is an API portal platform that enables businesses to create single-tenant, white-label developer portals with custom domains, branding, and API product management. It supports API monetization, developer self-service onboarding, usage metrics, subscription lifecycle management, and integrates with API gateways including Amazon API Gateway and Kong.

providers.name: Beautylish
providers.description: Beautylish is a San Francisco based online beauty retailer and community, founded in 2010 by Nils Johnson, Vu Nguyen and Sameer Iyengar. It began as a community where beauty enthusiasts shared tutorials, reviews and product knowledge, and launched its own e-commerce storefront in 2012. Beautylish curates makeup, skincare, hair, fragrance, nails, bath and body, wellness and tool brands from around the world, pairs them with editorial content and makeup-artist guidance, and operates its own fulfillment, rewards (Beautylish Rewards), flexible payments and Zero Day Delivery programs. The company runs a first-party storefront rather than a developer platform: as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no SDKs. Its public partner surface is a ShareASale/Awin affiliate program rather than an API.

providers.name: Brainly
providers.description: Brainly is an education technology company founded in 2009 in Krakow, Poland (originally Zadane.pl) and now headquartered in New York City. It operates the world's largest online learning and homework-help community, a gamified, crowdsourced social-learning network where students, parents, and teachers ask and answer academic questions with verified answers from peers, educators, and Brainly's proprietary AI. As of 2025 the platform serves over 350 million monthly users across roughly 35 countries and has evolved from a community Q&A product into an agentic AI Learning Companion spanning homework help, AI tutoring, test prep, and classroom participation. Brainly is a consumer subscription business (Brainly Plus); it publishes no official public developer API — this profile captures its public web, security, and policy surface.

providers.name: Comstruct
providers.description: Comstruct is a Munich-based construction technology company that provides AI-powered agents to automate the procurement of construction materials. Its platform runs the full procurement workflow from the bill of materials (Leistungsverzeichnis) through supplier inquiry, offer comparison, contract negotiation, digital delivery notes, AI-based invoice verification, and sustainability reporting. Customers include HOCHTIEF, Implenia, Marti, and Leonhard Weiss. Comstruct is backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of enrichment the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network from its public web presence.

providers.name: Concirrus
providers.description: Concirrus Ltd is a London-headquartered insurtech founded in 2012 that builds AI-driven underwriting software for the specialty and commercial insurance market — marine (hull, cargo, P&I), aviation, construction, property, and political violence and terrorism. Its platform (Quest, Marine One, the Underwriting Workbench, Exposure Management, Loss Run Intelligence, and an "Enterprise Model" universal submission-ingestion layer) ingests broker submissions, structures the risk data, scores behavioural risk, and returns rating and exposure decisions to carriers, MGAs and brokers — much of it aimed at the Lloyd's and London subscription market. Concirrus is a vendor to insurers rather than an insurer itself, so it touches quote and rating rather than bind, issue or FNOL. Its API posture is partner-gated: marketing describes "a modular, API first platform" and "seamless integration with London Market platforms", but as of 2026-07-25 there is no public developer portal, no published API reference, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, no Postman collection, and no public GraphQL or webhook catalog. Every developer and docs hostname probed (developer./developers./docs./api. on both concirrus.com and concirrus.ai) does not resolve, and every on-site developer path returns 404. Integration is obtained through a commercial engagement or the partner ecosystem programme, not self-serve signup. No ACORD, AL3, NGDS or ACORD XML reference appears anywhere on the public site. Concirrus does publish a real compliance posture: in August 2025 it announced ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management), ISO/IEC 27001 (information security) and SOC 2 certification, claiming to be the first insurtech to hold all three — though no trust center or downloadable report accompanies the announcement.

providers.name: Continental AG
providers.description: Continental AG is a German multinational automotive supplier and tire manufacturer headquartered in Hanover. As a global Tier 1 automotive supplier, Continental designs and manufactures tires, automotive electronics, brake systems, powertrain components, ADAS, and interior solutions for vehicle manufacturers worldwide.

providers.name: Defense Intelligence Agency
providers.description: The Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) is the U.S. Department of Defense combat support agency that produces, analyzes, and disseminates military intelligence on foreign militaries and operating environments to support warfighters, defense planners, and national-security policymakers. As an intelligence agency, DIA does not publish a general-purpose public API; its developer-facing surface is largely internal or restricted to the Intelligence Community. Public touchpoints include the GAMECHANGER policy analytics initiative, the DIA FOIA reading room, public news and article feeds, and procurement and recruiting portals.

providers.name: Fannie Mae
providers.description: Fannie Mae, officially known as the Federal National Mortgage Association, is a government-sponsored enterprise that plays a critical role in the American housing market. Established in 1938, Fannie Mae operates as a secondary mortgage lender, purchasing mortgages from banks and other financial institutions. By buying these loans, Fannie Mae helps to provide liquidity to the mortgage market, enabling banks to lend more money to homebuyers. Fannie Mae operates a developer portal that hosts API integrations for mortgage industry partners; access typically requires authenticated business relationships.

providers.name: Frec
providers.description: Frec is a San Francisco fintech offering tax-aware, automated direct indexing for retail investors. Its products — Classic Direct Indexing, Long Short Direct Indexing, Diversify, Trade, Treasury cash management, and a Portfolio Line of Credit — replicate market indices with individual stocks while running automated tax-loss harvesting to minimize capital gains taxes at fees starting around 0.09%. Frec is an SEC-registered investment adviser and SIPC member managing over $1.25B in assets, founded by Mo Al Adham and backed by Greylock. The company ships a consumer investing app and website but does not currently expose a public developer API, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.

providers.name: Getsafe
providers.description: Getsafe (Getsafe Digital GmbH) is a Heidelberg, Germany-based digital insurance company (insurtech) that lets consumers buy, manage, and file claims for insurance entirely through a mobile app. Getsafe operates as a licensed insurance carrier and offers 15+ products across liability and legal protection, health (public, private, dental, and travel), living (contents and drone), pet (pet health and dog liability), and protection and finance (income protection, term life, private pension, and children's savings). It serves 500k+ customers in Germany and Austria with English-language, app-based support. In 2018 Getsafe launched an early-access P&C and health insurance API and embeddable widget for partner distribution; that partner API is no longer offered as a public self-service developer program, so this profile is maintained as a company record. Backed by earlybird and partech.

providers.name: Goose Insurance
providers.description: Goose Insurance Services Inc. is a Vancouver, British Columbia based digital insurance distributor — an app-first licensed agency and MGA rather than a carrier — that sells travel medical, Visitors to Canada, term life, whole life, final expense, critical illness, accidental death and dismemberment, hospital cash, kids and renters coverage through the Goose mobile "insurance super app". Founded in 2017 and licensed in British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec (AMF firm registration 603913), New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, Goose underwrites nothing itself: every policy is placed with a partner carrier including AIG Canada, iA Financial Group, TuGo, IMG, MSH, American-Amicable, Teachers Life, Lloyd's of London and Sutton National. Its home market is Canada, with a US launch in 2020, and it sits in the thin digital-broker layer beneath the Big-Few Canadian oligopoly alongside Zensurance and APOLLO. Goose's API posture is closed: as of the 2026-07-25 review there is no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger, and no published ACORD, AL3 or agency-management-system integration. The only host that answers on the api. subdomain is a private Heroku-backed mobile-app backend that returns 404 at every probed path, and the only partner surfaces the company publishes are a marketing affiliate/referral program and a carrier-relationships page — quote, bind, issue and FNOL are all consumer-facing inside the app only.

providers.name: HAAS Alert
providers.description: HAAS Alert operates Safety Cloud, a connected-vehicle safety platform that delivers real-time digital alerts to nearby motorists about active emergency responses, roadside hazards, work zones, stopped vehicles, and slow-moving equipment. Using vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and cellular messaging, Safety Cloud gives drivers up to roughly 30 seconds of advance warning to help reduce collisions with first responders, tow operators, and roadway workers. HAAS Alert integrates with telematics platforms, fleet manufacturers, OEM vehicles, in-car navigation (including Waze), and roadway infrastructure to form a large connected-vehicle alerting ecosystem. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. This profile was enriched from HAAS Alert's public web surface; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs were found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: IBM Db2
providers.description: IBM Db2 is a family of data management products from IBM that includes relational and hybrid database servers running on cloud, distributed, and z/OS platforms, supporting transactional, analytical, and AI workloads. Db2 exposes RESTful services that let applications create, discover, execute, and manage user-defined services natively against the database, and IBM Db2 as a Service on IBM Cloud provides a managed REST API for administering and querying cloud-hosted Db2 databases. Authentication is performed via HTTP basic auth, client certificates, or IBM Cloud IAM Bearer tokens depending on the deployment.

providers.name: Kallyope
providers.description: Kallyope, Inc. is a New York City clinical-stage biotechnology company, founded in 2015 by Columbia University scientists Charles Zuker, Tom Maniatis and Richard Axel, that translates the biology of the gut-brain axis into medicines. It launched with a $44M Series A and has since raised a $66M Series B, a $112M Series C and a $236M Series D co-led by Mubadala Investment Company and The Column Group, with backers including Bill Gates, Lux Capital, Polaris Partners, Casdin Capital and Alexandria Real Estate Equities. Its proprietary Klarity platform integrates single-cell sequencing, pathway circuit mapping, optogenetics and chemogenetics, proprietary human genetics, mouse and human organoid systems, and small-molecule and peptide chemistry to map the neural circuits underlying migraine and metabolism; lead candidate elismetrep, a TRPM8 blocker, is in Phase 3 development for acute migraine. Kallyope publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, CLI, status page or public GitHub organization, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A agent-card surface was found on any host. Enrichment probing did find one real, anonymous, read-only REST surface: kallyope.com runs WordPress and exposes the WordPress REST API publicly at https://kallyope.com/wp-json, carrying the company news feed, site pages, media library and a first-party "document" content type of scientific posters, presentations and publications classified by the custom program, event, content-type and document-type taxonomies.

providers.name: Komprise
providers.description: Komprise is an unstructured data management company whose Intelligent Data Management platform analyzes, tiers, migrates and governs file and object data across NAS, cloud and object storage. The platform spans Komprise Analysis, Elastic Data Migration, Transparent Move Technology, Smart Data Workflows, the Global Metadatabase Service, KAPPA Data Services and Transparent File Tables, giving enterprises a single metadata layer for discovery, classification, sensitive-data detection, ransomware-attack-surface reduction, intelligent tiering and AI data preparation. Komprise publishes an llms.txt bot-access and content policy at www.komprise.com/llms.txt, but its product documentation portal at docs.komprise.com is authentication-gated and no public REST API reference, OpenAPI description, SDK or package was found on any public registry as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Lightship
providers.description: Lightship is an American manufacturer of all-electric travel trailers, co-founded by former Tesla leaders Toby Kraus and Ben Parker, with design and manufacturing in Colorado and offices in San Francisco. Its flagship product, the AE.1, is marketed as the first mass-produced all-electric travel trailer, offering up to 77 kWh of battery capacity, 1.8 kW of integrated solar, and named technologies including TrekDrive self-propulsion, CampQuiet silent operation, and Aero-Electric Design. Owners control the trailer through an onboard Atlas tablet and companion mobile app. Lightship sells direct to consumer and states that more than 85% of its supply chain is in the United States. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API listing.

providers.name: MyBuilder
providers.description: MyBuilder is a UK online marketplace that connects homeowners with local, reviewed tradespeople for home improvement, repair and maintenance work. Founded in 2004 by stonemason Ryan Notz and headquartered in London, the platform lets homeowners post a job for free, review interested tradespeople by their profiles, work history and customer feedback, and shortlist the ones they want to hire. Tradespeople browse leads for free and pay a fee only when a customer shortlists them. MyBuilder was acquired by IAC's HomeAdvisor in 2017 and now operates as part of the Instapro Group of European home-services marketplaces. MyBuilder is a consumer-facing web platform and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, security and domain posture.

providers.name: NewCore
providers.description: NewCore is an enterprise identity-security company building an identity platform that governs both human and AI-agent identities across the enterprise. Its three pillars are Identity Discovery (continuously discovering and mapping every identity across directories, PAM, shadow systems, and AI infrastructure), Identity Security (breach prevention through phishing-resistant authentication and device-bound sessions that cannot be stolen or replayed), and Human + AI Agent Governance (minimum-access provisioning, full lifecycle management, and support for ephemeral agentic workloads). NewCore is backed by Index Ventures. It sells to enterprises via demo request and publishes a trust center (SOC 2 Type II, CSA STAR Level 1, GDPR, CCPA) but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Onlia
providers.description: Onlia is a Canadian digital insurance brokerage, operating as the registered business name of Onlia Agency Inc. and backed by Southampton Financial Inc. (the Southampton group of companies). It sells personal lines direct to consumers online and by phone — auto (car, motorcycle, ATV, snowmobile, trailer, motorhome), property (home, condo, tenant, landlord, second home, mobile home) and lifestyle lines (boat, pet, life, travel, seasonal) — plus group and bundle programs. Onlia does not underwrite; it places business with a panel of Canadian carriers disclosed publicly on its broker-disclosure page, including Aviva, Gore Mutual, Economical/Definity, Pembridge, Pafco, Echelon, Wawanesa, Unica, Forward, Premier, Facility Association (Intact) and APOLLO. Its home market is Canada, concentrated in Ontario, where market conduct sits with FSRA while OSFI supervises the federally-regulated carriers behind the policies. API posture, recorded honestly: Onlia publishes NO public developer portal and NO self-serve API. developer., developers., docs. and api. under onlia.ca do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer and /integrations on the marketing site all return 404. The only quote/bind/issue/FNOL surface is app.onlia.ca, a consumer-facing Angular single-page app running on a white-labelled Ignite Insurance policy administration platform whose backend is private to the app. The one "partner" page is a B2B marketing page inviting affinity discount partnerships by email, with no technical onboarding. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference appears anywhere on the public site. The app's own bundle shows the private backend runs on MuleSoft Anypoint CloudHub ESB services (auto and home policy, authentication, documents, VIN/MVR, claims) plus an Ignite Insurance authentication service — real REST plumbing behind the SPA, but undocumented, uncredentialed and not offered to third parties, so no API entry is claimed here.

providers.name: Openprise
providers.description: Free your RevOps teams from the complexities of bad data and give them data they can trust, take action on, and make better decisions with. A simple way to achieve the highest data quality across your marketing, sales, and RevOps processes with the Openprise RevOps Data Automation (RDA) Cloud.

providers.name: Plumerai
providers.description: Plumerai builds AI software for intelligent cameras that pairs tiny on-device edge AI models with cloud Vision Language Models (VLMs). Its Video Intelligence products cover detection of people, vehicles, animals and packages, Familiar Face Identification, cross-camera Re-Identification, noise-robust motion detection, VLM-based video search, and custom AI notifications. The Plumerai Inference Engine is a deep-learning model compiler and runtime optimized for CPU inference on Arm Cortex-M / Cortex-A, RISC-V and x86_64. Plumerai integrates via SDKs (C++, C, Python, Rust, Java) rather than a hosted REST API, with the same unified API running from microcontrollers to servers. Plumerai also maintains the open-source Larq ecosystem for training and running Binarized Neural Networks.

providers.name: Propseller
providers.description: Propseller is a Singapore-based, technology-powered real estate brokerage founded in 2018 by Adrien Jorge. It helps property owners sell, buy, and rent residential real estate — HDB flats, condominiums, and landed homes — pairing top-performing human property agents with data and technology to deliver an end-to-end transaction experience at a transparent commission starting from 1%. Backed by Vertex Ventures and Partech, Propseller operates a consumer-facing real estate service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Raven
providers.description: Raven is a runtime security platform that protects applications from the inside, detecting and preventing malicious code execution as it happens rather than relying only on perimeter defenses. Its capabilities span Runtime Prevention (blocking exploit execution regardless of CVE availability), Runtime ADR (application-level attack detection and response with forensics), Runtime AI-Agents (discovering and monitoring AI agents in an environment), Runtime SCA (prioritizing vulnerable dependencies by actual execution), and Runtime Gatekeeper (keeping risky applications out of production). The platform is self-hosted on Kubernetes, deployed via Helm/OCI charts and a sensor operator across AWS, Azure, and GCP, and is positioned as an application-level alternative to WAF, EDR, RASP, SCA, and ASPM tools. Raven is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: rekord
providers.description: Rekord is a Dublin-based fintech platform that helps banks and fintechs automate credit underwriting and customer onboarding. Its AI-native decisioning platform unifies data from many sources into a single view, orchestrates decision workflows, runs a natural-language policy engine, and provides AI-assisted case management so credit and risk teams can make defensible, transparent decisions at scale. Rekord surfaces the signal buried in large volumes of applicant and transaction data to speed underwriting and onboarding while enforcing identity verification and compliance. It is a portfolio company of point-nine. Rekord does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine discovery surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SolveBio
providers.description: SolveBio is a platform for biomedical and genomic datasets that lets developers query, harmonize, and automate bioinformatics workflows over curated reference data through a REST API and first-party client libraries (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and R). SolveBio has been rebranded to QuartzBio, a Precision for Medicine company: the solvebio.com website now redirects to quartz.bio, the legacy API is served as the QuartzBio EDP REST API on per-customer instance hosts, and the SolveBio SDKs are being deprecated in favor of the quartzbio packages (Python client end of maintenance 2026-03-31). Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched from its public GitHub organization and package registries.

providers.name: Swept
providers.description: Swept (sweptworks.com) is workforce management software for commercial cleaning and janitorial businesses - scheduling, GPS-verified time tracking and payroll reporting, mobile crew messaging, quality inspections, supply requests, client portals, and one-time work order management. As of this catalog entry, Swept does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key or OAuth signup, published OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or webhook documentation on sweptworks.com or in the Swept Support Center knowledge base. The only documented outbound data path is a one-way, manually-activated QuickBooks Online payroll sync set up per account by a Swept Customer Success Manager - not a self-serve developer integration. Swept's public GitHub organization contains only take-home coding-challenge repositories used for hiring, not a first-party API client, SDK, or spec. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: TE Connectivity
providers.description: TE Connectivity is a global manufacturer of connectors and sensors headquartered in Galway, Ireland with operational headquarters in Berwyn, Pennsylvania. TE provides electrical connectivity and sensor solutions for transportation, industrial, and communications markets, with strong automotive Tier 1 supply relationships.

providers.name: Telepresence
providers.description: Telepresence is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox open source tool that enables fast local development for Kubernetes and OpenShift microservices. It creates a bidirectional network bridge between a developer's local machine and a remote Kubernetes cluster, allowing services to run locally while connecting to remote dependencies. Originally created by Ambassador Labs, Telepresence lets developers intercept traffic destined for specific cluster workloads and route it to their local environment for testing and debugging.

providers.name: Universal Robots
providers.description: Universal Robots is a Danish collaborative-robot (cobot) manufacturer headquartered in Odense, Denmark, founded in 2005 by Esben Østergaard, Kasper Støy, and Kristian Kassow, and acquired by Teradyne in 2015 for USD 285 million. Universal Robots is the market leader in cobots, with more than 100,000 units sold worldwide and a 40–50% share of the global collaborative-robot market. The company ships two product generations — the e-Series (UR3e, UR7e, UR12e, UR16e) and the newer high-payload UR series (UR8 Long, UR15, UR18, UR20, UR30) — running the PolyScope 5 teach-pendant software stack and the next-generation PolyScope X platform. Universal Robots is unusual among industrial-robot vendors in publishing an extensive open developer surface: the C++ Universal_Robots_Client_Library, the Universal_Robots_ROS_Driver and Universal_Robots_ROS2_Driver, the RTDE Python Client Library, the Universal_Robots_Isaac_Driver for NVIDIA Isaac, the URCap SDK (PolyScope 5 Java) and PolyScopeX URCap SDK (TypeScript/HTML), and the URScript language. The wire-level protocols — Real-Time Data Exchange (RTDE), Dashboard Server, Primary/Secondary Client Interface, Reverse/Trajectory interfaces, XML-RPC, and the Tool Communication forwarder — are all documented and externally addressable over TCP, making UR cobots first-class citizens in third-party automation stacks, ROS/ROS 2, MoveIt, Isaac Sim, and the UR+ ecosystem (500+ certified end-effectors, vision systems, and URCap software extensions on universal-robots.com/plus). Universal Robots does not publish a public HTTP/REST API or OpenAPI specification — all programmatic access is via the documented socket protocols and SDKs.

providers.name: Uplevel
providers.description: Uplevel is an engineering intelligence platform for enterprises — an operating system for engineering transformation that helps leaders see team performance clearly, solve root causes, and sustain improvement in the AI era. The platform pulls data from existing tools and uses machine learning to produce engineering metrics and actionable insights: DORA metrics, time allocation and ML issue classification, deep-work and interruption measurement, developer-experience metrics, and AI-impact analysis, framed by the company's WAVE framework of engineering KPIs. Founded in 2018 and led by CEO Joe Levy, Uplevel is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Madrona Ventures, and Voyager Capital. Uplevel serves enterprise customers such as Xactly, Accolade, Braze, Avalara, and Qualtrics; it operates an internal API behind the product (api.uplevelteam.com, AWS API Gateway) but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: UXD Protocol
providers.description: UXD Protocol is a decentralized stablecoin protocol built on Solana, operated by Soteria FZCO, whose UXD token is backed 100% by an Asset Liability Management Module that deploys collateral into delta-neutral positions, on-chain lending, and real-world assets. The protocol is governed by the UXP token, is documented on GitBook, publishes six third-party security audits and a self-run bug bounty, and ships an open-source Solana program with a TypeScript client on npm and a Rust CPI client on crates.io. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Vinyl Equity
providers.description: Vinyl Equity is a modern transfer agency providing equity, cap-table, and shareholder-management software for private and public companies. Its platform covers registrar services, proxy and AGM (annual general meeting) management, and shareholder security, replacing legacy transfer-agent workflows with a modern web application. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface is documented at this time; the profile currently captures the company's security and compliance posture.

providers.name: Activ Surgical
providers.description: Activ Surgical is a Boston, Massachusetts digital surgery company building intraoperative surgical intelligence for the operating room. Its flagship product, the ActivSight Intelligent Light imaging module, attaches to existing laparoscopic and robotic surgical systems and renders augmented-reality overlays on a standard monitor, letting surgeons see physiology the naked eye cannot. ActivPerfusion delivers dye-free, real-time blood-perfusion imaging using laser speckle contrast imaging, while ActivICG supports conventional indocyanine green visualization of structures such as bile ducts. The module is powered by the ActivEdge platform, a hardware-agnostic computer-vision, AI and machine-learning stack the company is building to turn intraoperative data into real-time surgical guidance. Activ Surgical performed the first autonomous robotic soft-tissue surgery in 2018, received FDA 510(k) clearance for ActivSight in April 2021 and CE Mark approval in December 2022, and sells on a subscription model with no capital-equipment purchase. The company publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract as of this profiling pass; its public technical surface is regulatory (EU MDR declarations of conformity, ISO 13485:2016) and clinical (peer-reviewed studies and white papers).

providers.name: Aily Labs
providers.description: Aily Labs is a Munich-based enterprise AI company that builds an AI Decision Intelligence Suite — a platform that connects siloed internal and external data to deliver real-time, explainable predictions and recommendations across Finance, R&D, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Go-To-Market, Procurement, and People functions. The suite ships with 300+ validated predictive models and an iOS app, and is deployed across Healthcare & Life Sciences, Consumer Goods, Luxury & Fashion, Media & Tech, Retail, and Services (clients include Sanofi). Aily Labs is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Alem Health
providers.description: AlemHealth is an AI-powered teleradiology and medical imaging platform that unifies image acquisition, diagnostic reading, reporting, and analytics into a single cloud system used by 500+ radiologists across 20+ countries. Its product suite includes Connect PACS (cloud image archiving with an FDA-approved diagnostic viewer), FrontDesk RIS scheduling, a referring-physician Referral Portal, a patient QR-access app, and the AlemBox gateway and AlemHub reporting-server hardware. AI features cover automated report drafting, quality-assurance scoring, laterality-mismatch detection, and ICD-10 tagging, metered via an AI-tokens model. For providers, AlemHealth supports bi-directional HL7, FHIR, and API integrations plus standard DICOM connectivity to sync orders, patient demographics, and finalized reports with existing EMR/EHR and PACS systems.

providers.name: BabyCenter
providers.description: BabyCenter is an online pregnancy and parenting media company founded in 1997 and operated today by Everyday Health Group, a division of Ziff Davis. It provides medically reviewed information and interactive tools covering conception, pregnancy, birth, and early childhood development, and publishes the widely used "My Pregnancy & Baby Today" mobile app for iOS and Android used by hundreds of millions of expecting and new parents worldwide. BabyCenter operates as a content and community destination rather than an API platform: it does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or hosted API, and its verified GitHub organization contains only forked iOS libraries. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public operational surface — domain security posture, a live RFC 9116 security.txt with a Ziff Davis Bugcrowd vulnerability disclosure program, and its editorial/legal properties.

providers.name: Bioniq
providers.description: Bioniq is a personalized nutrition and supplement company founded in London in 2019 that combines individual biomarker and blood-test data with a proprietary algorithm to formulate customized vitamin and mineral blends delivered as Swiss-made granules. Its consumer product line spans Bioniq GO (wellness-assessment based), Bioniq PRO (blood-test driven), and Bioniq Essential, supported by iOS and Android apps for tracking health and supplement routines. Bioniq is a portfolio company of HV Capital and now operates within Herbalife. It exposes consumer web, mobile, and partner/affiliate surfaces but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Blaize
providers.description: Blaize (NASDAQ: BZAI) is an edge AI company headquartered in El Dorado Hills, California that builds a programmable inference platform uniting silicon and software. Its Graph Streaming Processor (GSP) powers the Pathfinder and Xplorer accelerator families — SoM, M.2, EDSFF and PCIe form factors plus the DST developer station and Blaize Inference Server — and its software layer pairs the Picasso SDK (C++, Python, OpenVX, with TensorFlow/PyTorch/ONNX import via NetDeploy) with AI Studio, a code-free environment spanning the full edge AI DataOps/DevOps/MLOps lifecycle. In April 2026 Blaize announced a planned Blaize AI Services platform that packages multimodal inference, business logic and orchestration as modular application-level APIs across vision, video, document, speech and moderation workloads. The developer surface — SDK downloads, repositories and reference material — is served from a self-hosted GitLab at software.blaize.com and requires an account, so no public machine-readable API contract is published.

providers.name: Blink Health
providers.description: Blink Health is a healthcare technology company that operates BlinkRx, a digital pharmacy platform connecting patients, prescribers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers to simplify prescription access, fulfillment, and affordability. The platform streamlines the path from a provider writing a prescription to a patient receiving medication at a transparent price, with copay support, home delivery, and manufacturer-sponsored programs. Backed by 8vc, Blink Health runs consumer-facing prescription-savings tools and a provider/pharma-facing BlinkRx offering. No public developer API program or documentation was found during enrichment; a live undocumented API host exists at api.blinkhealth.com.

providers.name: C-Infinity
providers.description: C-Infinity is a Mountain View, California company founded in 2023 that builds foundational AI for mechanical design and manufacturing — AI that reasons about geometry, motion, spatial constraints, and production logic. Its platform, AutoAssembler, connects directly to existing CAD and PLM environments to automate assembly process planning, accelerate engineering change order (ECO) reviews, and generate production-ready assembly work instructions, compressing work that historically took weeks into minutes. The product is described by the company as API-first, with an integration layer that connects upstream to engineering systems and downstream to production, but as of July 2026 C-Infinity publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition — the AutoAssembler application is gated behind a request-a-demo flow and integration is arranged directly with the company. C-Infinity raised a $16M round in April 2026 led by Canaan Partners, with participation from Inventus Capital, Bee Partners, and Radius Capital, and reports deployments across Global Fortune 100 manufacturers as well as small and mid-sized enterprises.

providers.name: Casana
providers.description: Casana (Casana Care) is a Rochester, New York digital-health company building passive, in-home remote patient monitoring hardware. Its flagship Smart Seat (formerly the Heart Seat) is a toilet-seat replacement that captures vital signs — heart rate, heart-rate variability, blood-oxygen (SpO2), respiration rate, blood-pressure insights, and sit-to-stand power — during normal bathroom use, with no wearables, no daily charging, and explicitly no camera or microphone. Readings sync to companion iOS, Android, and web apps for patients, families, and caregivers. The company operates in the digital health, remote patient monitoring, and connected medical-device space and is backed by General Catalyst and Kaiser Permanente. As of this profile Casana publishes a consumer product, companion apps, and legal/privacy pages, but no public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cloudgenix
providers.description: CloudGenix was a cloud-native SD-WAN (software-defined wide area network) company founded in 2013 and backed by Mayfield. Its AppFabric platform let enterprises build application-defined, policy-driven WANs managed from a cloud controller, with a full REST API (the CloudGenix Cloud Controller / AppFabric API) and first-party SDKs in Python, C#, Java, and JavaScript plus a CI-capable configuration CLI. Palo Alto Networks acquired CloudGenix in April 2020 for more than $420M and rebranded the product as Prisma SD-WAN, now part of the Prisma SASE portfolio. The public developer tooling remains published under the official CloudGenix GitHub organization.

providers.name: Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States
providers.description: The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) is an inter-agency committee chaired by the U.S. Department of the Treasury that reviews certain foreign investment transactions for national security implications. CFIUS reviews are governed by the Defense Production Act and Section 721, and were significantly strengthened by the Foreign Investment Risk Review Modernization Act of 2018 (FIRRMA). On September 15, 2022, President Biden issued Executive Order 14083 directing CFIUS to focus on emerging national security risks. CFIUS work is largely confidential, and the public-facing surface is limited to regulations, annual reports to Congress, FAQs, declarations and notices guidance, and case studies.

providers.name: CRS Credit API
providers.description: CRS Credit API delivers credit data-as-a-service for fast, compliant financial decisioning. The platform aggregates consumer and business credit, identity, fraud, and public records data from major bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, LexisNexis, CIC, PitchPoint) through a single contract and developer interface.

providers.name: DoorFeed
providers.description: DoorFeed is a technology-led residential real estate investment platform, founded in 2021 and headquartered in Paris, that helps institutional investors, funds, and family offices source and manage single-family rental portfolios at scale across the UK and France. The platform ingests roughly 150,000 new property listings and over 1,000,000 property images every day, structuring market data, comparable transactions, valuation signals, and energy-performance data into a single acquisition and asset-management workflow that takes investors from market screening to investment decision in minutes. DoorFeed is backed by HV Capital, Seedcamp, and Motive Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline; DoorFeed publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Duna
providers.description: Duna is an AI-native business identity platform for KYB (Know Your Business), KYC (Know Your Customer), AML (Anti-Money Laundering), and lifecycle compliance. It accelerates enterprise business onboarding by turning compliance policy into auditable code via a policy engine, using AI agents for document verification and periodic reviews, with deep localization across 210+ business registries and 7+ languages. Duna serves fintechs, banks, and platforms including Plaid, Moss, and Bol, and is backed by Index Ventures. Note: docs.duna.com is password-protected, so no public API reference, OpenAPI, or developer portal was available at enrichment time.

providers.name: Dune Security
providers.description: Dune Security is a cybersecurity company whose User Adaptive Risk Management platform uses AI-driven behavioral analysis to quantify and reduce user-layer cyber risk. It runs omni-channel attack simulations (email/spear phishing, smishing, vishing, deepfakes, and encrypted-app lures) tailored to each employee's role and behavior, generates a live User Risk Score from five inputs (business impact, simulations, training activity, external security integrations, and historical data), and automatically adapts micro-training and security controls in real time. The platform integrates with IAM, EDR, SEG, DLP, and HRIS systems to escalate or restrict access for high-risk users, and ships an in-house training library (Security Awareness, Compliance, and Functional-Specific Training) covering NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, ISO 27001, FFIEC, GLBA, and GDPR. Dune Security is backed by Craft Ventures.

providers.name: Ecovadis
providers.description: Ecovadis is a global leader in providing sustainability ratings and performance improvement tools for companies looking to assess and improve their environmental and social practices. Their platform helps organizations evaluate the sustainability performance of their suppliers, partners, and vendors, enabling them to make more informed decisions when it comes to selecting business partners.

providers.name: Extensity
providers.description: ExtensityAI is an AI research company building trustworthy, verifiable AI for enterprise environments through a neurosymbolic architecture that combines large language models with symbolic validation and knowledge-graph reasoning. Its flagship open-source framework, SymbolicAI, treats LLMs as programmable, differentiable primitives (Symbol objects) governed by Design-by-Contract validation, giving developers source-traceable, contract-enforced AI they can run on-premise with sovereign data control. The company also ships developer tooling including the ontoloom MCP server for building and exploring OWL 2 ontologies with AI agents. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: First Hawaiian Bank
providers.description: First Hawaiian Bank is Hawaii's oldest and largest financial institution, founded in 1858 and headquartered at First Hawaiian Center in Honolulu. It is a Hawaii state-chartered commercial bank and member FDIC, operating as the principal subsidiary of First Hawaiian, Inc. (NASDAQ ticker FHB), a publicly traded bank holding company. The bank serves consumer and commercial customers through roughly 57 branches in Hawaii plus locations in Guam and Saipan, offering deposit accounts, lending, wealth management, treasury/cash management, and merchant services. On the open-finance front, First Hawaiian operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; probes of developer.fhb.com, api.fhb.com, and fhb.com/en/developers returned no host or HTTP 404. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a direct bank API. No documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participation or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found as of this record. Its commercial online banking product (FHB Commercial Online, formerly OBC) is a traditional web application rather than a developer-facing API surface.

providers.name: Flecto
providers.description: Flecto is a SaaS platform for rental businesses, providing tools to manage bookings, inventory, payments, and customer verification across both online and in-store channels. Backed by Techstars, the company offers "The Flecto Link" for flexible checkout, ID and face-scan verification, item protection and insurance, a hosted online store builder, and the Flecto Market marketplace. It supports payment methods including MB Way, PayPal, Mastercard, and Apple Pay. Flecto does not currently publish a public API or developer platform; this profile tracks its public web and business surface.

providers.name: FYLD
providers.description: FYLD is an AI-native frontline intelligence platform for the global critical-infrastructure sector, turning field-operations data into real-time, structured intelligence for utilities, energy, and heavy-civils operators. Its products include the FYLD Platform for work execution, FYLD Control Room for remote supervision, and FYLD ShowMe for customer self-service reporting, serving managers, fieldworkers, contractors, and civil engineers via web and mobile (iOS and Android) apps. FYLD is a Partech portfolio company. As of this profile FYLD publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; integration is delivered through partnerships such as Procore, and this record captures its public identity, security, and trust surface.

providers.name: Greenwork
providers.description: Greenwork builds software for the HVAC (heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) industry and is backed by GV (Google Ventures). Its flagship product, Onsite Pro, is a digital pricebook and proposal platform for HVAC distributors and their dealers: it replaces Excel and PDF catalogs with searchable product data, automated AHRI equipment matchups, incentive and rebate application, and one-click proposal generation, while giving distributors visibility into dealer catalog performance, win rates, and share of wallet. Greenwork does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures the company identity and its public web and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: iBasis
providers.description: iBasis is a global communications solutions provider serving mobile operators, MVNOs, over-the-top players, and IoT device companies worldwide. Its portfolio spans international and managed voice, 5G data roaming and roaming hub/breakout, A2P and RCS messaging monetization, and IoT connectivity built on eSIM technology, the Simfony connectivity-management platform, MVNO-as-a-Service, and fixed wireless access. iBasis also offers signaling and fraud security (FraudLock iQ360, Security iQ360, Signaling Vulnerability Scanner) and business intelligence for carriers. Customer and partner operations run through the eCare portal behind single sign-on; iBasis does not currently publish a public developer program, OpenAPI specifications, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and enriched from the public iBasis web presence and live domain probes.

providers.name: Ipid
providers.description: iPiD (International Payments Identity) is a fintech providing real-time Know Your Payee (KYP) verification for cross-border and domestic payments. Its single, payment-rail-agnostic API lets banks, PSPs, and corporates validate bank account ownership and match payee names before funds move, reducing authorized push payment (APP) fraud, business email compromise losses, and failed transactions. Products include iPiD Validate (global payee / bank account verification with name-matching), iPiD Node (a scheme-compliance layer for EU Verification of Payee, UK Confirmation of Payee, FATF Recommendation 16, and US Nacha), and a Payment Agent agentic verification layer. Founded in 2021, iPiD is backed by QED Investors, Monk's Hill Ventures, Quona Capital, Jungle Ventures, Saison Capital, and others. Public API access is gated behind a sales/demo process; no machine-readable specification is published publicly.

providers.name: Joko
providers.description: Joko is a French fintech company operating a consumer cashback, rewards, and savings application that connects shoppers with more than 3,500 partner brands online and in physical stores. Users earn cashback and automatically apply promo codes through the Joko iOS and Android apps and browser extensions (Chrome, Firefox, Safari), while also managing budgets, loyalty cards, gift cards, and split (3x installment) payments. Joko also runs a business solution offering brand partnerships and consumer market research. Backed by Partech, Joko is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Karat.io
providers.description: Karat (trykarat.com) is a fintech platform providing integrated business banking and financial tools built for entrepreneurs, content creators, agencies, and small businesses managing irregular income. Its product suite spans FDIC-insured business checking accounts with high APY, the Karat Card and Karat Max charge/credit cards with rewards and no annual fees, mass and international contractor payments, AI-powered bookkeeping with automatic transaction categorization, invoicing, and multi-entity team management. Surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Karat publishes a consumer web and mobile app but no public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Karate
providers.description: Karate is an open source API test automation framework combining API testing, mocks, and performance testing in a single tool using BDD syntax.

providers.name: Kasheesh
providers.description: Kasheesh is a consumer fintech platform that lets people split a single purchase across up to five credit and debit cards in one transaction. Instead of a traditional buy-now-pay-later loan, Kasheesh combines the funds and credit a customer already holds into a single digital Kasheesh Card that works at any Mastercard-accepting merchant online or in-store via tap-to-pay. The service charges a flat service fee, returns card rewards on spend, and requires no sign-up fee or credit check. Kasheesh is offered through iOS and Android apps and a web app, targeting everyday shopping, bill payment, and rent. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Anthemis; it does not currently publish a public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Kestrl: Muslim Money App
providers.description: Kestrl is a UK-based, FCA-regulated ethical fintech offering a values-aligned money app for Muslim and ethically-minded consumers. In partnership with Maybank Islamic, it provides interest-free (Sharia-compliant) banking, a Mastercard debit card with values filtering, goal-based sub-accounts, interest purification and Zakat calculation, transaction monitoring that alerts users to payments toward ethically questionable companies, and security features such as card freezing and biometric authentication. Kestrl is a consumer mobile application on iOS and Android; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: KitchenMate
providers.description: KitchenMate is a Toronto-based autonomous retail and workplace food-service company that operates 24/7 unattended micro-markets built around two pieces of proprietary hardware, a checkout-free Smart Fridge that uses vision sensors to detect what a customer removes and bill them automatically, and induction-based Smart Cookers that heat chef-prepared entrees in seven to ten minutes. The kiosks are installed in workplaces, condominiums, schools, hospitals and other commercial locations, require roughly seven square feet plus standard electrical and network connectivity, and accept Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Apple Pay and Google Pay at the unit. A companion iOS and Android app carries loyalty rewards, dietary filters and meal feedback. The company has since rebranded its platform business as Micromart, which markets the same autonomous smart-store technology under the tagline "Be anywhere. Sell anything." across a stated 2,000+ locations in North America. KitchenMate publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and probed security posture only.

providers.name: KoRo
providers.description: KoRo (KoRo Handels GmbH) is a Berlin-based direct-to-consumer food retailer that sells nuts, dried fruit, nut butters, snacks, protein products, baking ingredients and drugstore goods in bulk packaging at wholesale-style prices, shipping across Europe from country storefronts in Germany (korodrogerie.de), Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy and the Benelux/EU shop at koro.com. Founded in 2014 and backed by HV Capital and Partech, KoRo runs a headless commerce stack — a Shopware 6 backend fronted by a Nuxt storefront deployed on Vercel — and publishes its engineering work as open source through the KoRoHandelsGmbH GitHub organization, including a Nitro-based Shopware Store-API proxy and several Shopware 6 build-tooling packages on npm under the @korodrogerie scope. KoRo publishes no public developer portal, no documented partner or commerce API, and no API specifications; its Store-API surface is internal and gated behind per-sales-channel access keys.

providers.name: Levit
providers.description: Levit Inc. (레브잇) is a software company headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, best known for Alwayz (올웨이즈) — a mobile-first team-purchase commerce app launched in July 2021 that lets shoppers group together with other buyers to unlock prices below normal retail. Levit describes itself as building "a service that everybody uses everyday," and previously launched Ping in March 2021. The company runs the Alwayz Seller Center for merchants selling on the platform and publishes a seller-focused commerce blog. As of this profile Levit publishes no public developer API program, no API documentation or reference, no developer portal, and no SDKs — the enrichment pipeline probed the company and product domains and found no developer surface.

providers.name: Liftopia
providers.description: Liftopia is a consumer marketplace for advance-purchase ski and snowboard lift tickets, letting travelers browse and buy discounted day tickets and multi-day passes at hundreds of ski areas across the United States, Canada, Europe, South America, Japan, Australia and New Zealand. The site is organized by region, state and destination with dated availability and 1-8 day ticket search, and carries an affiliate program for partners. Liftopia's engineering organization operates on GitHub as Catalate Commerce, Inc., and the site footer points to Spotlio. As of this profile Liftopia publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition or client SDKs.

providers.name: Margo
providers.description: Margo is a Linux Foundation open standard initiative for interoperability at the edge of industrial automation ecosystems. Founded by ABB, Capgemini, Microsoft, Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric, and Siemens, it defines mechanisms for interoperability between edge applications, devices, and orchestration software.

providers.name: Matcherino
providers.description: Matcherino is an esports crowdfunding and tournament-management platform that provides monetization infrastructure for competitive gaming events of every scale, from college clubs to stadium finals. Its stack covers prize-pool crowdfunding, brackets, player signups, ticketing and entry fees, streaming overlays, sponsor activation, and a publisher dashboard for distributing cash and in-game prizes. Matcherino handles global payouts to organizers and winners across 120+ countries with tax-form collection, and surfaces real-time analytics for organizers, sponsors, and publishers. The company reports having paid out more than $5.2M across 14,000+ tournaments. Matcherino is a Techstars-backed company; it does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Medeloop
providers.description: Medeloop is an AI platform for the clinical research lifecycle, describing itself as an operating system for clinical research that spans grant discovery and funding, real-world evidence generation from patient data, and delivering actionable intelligence at the point of care. Its products include Medeloop Analytics (AI agents that analyze EHR, claims, and registry data without requiring users to code), EvidenceKit (analytics paired with all-payer claims data), Medeloop Grants (AI-assisted grant discovery and proposal writing), and Medeloop Care (population health and care management). The platform is federated (compute moves to the data, which stays in the customer's infrastructure), CDM-agnostic (Epic, Cerner, Meditech, OMOP, i2b2, or custom schemas), and model-agnostic (routing tasks across OpenAI, Anthropic, or DeepSeek), with multi-cloud deployment across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premise. It serves pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies, health systems, and clinical researchers. As of this enrichment pass Medeloop publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; its documentation host (docs.medeloop.ai) is gated behind Okta authentication and its analytics application is a private client login.

providers.name: MedHOK (Hearst Communications)
providers.description: MHK (formerly MedHOK), part of Hearst Health, is a healthcare technology company providing a unified SaaS platform for health plans and payers. Its CareProminence suite spans utilization management, care management, complaints/appeals and grievances, pharmacy management, population health and quality management, and interoperability (the MHK Interop Suite), while its MarketProminence suite covers enrollment and member maintenance, premium billing, financial reconciliation, and member web portals. MHK helps Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial health plans streamline operations, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the member experience. The MHK Interop Suite supports FHIR, SMART on FHIR, Da Vinci, and CMS-0057 interoperability requirements. MHK publishes HITRUST and ISO 27001 certification and NCQA prevalidation. The company operates a public marketing and resource site but does not publish a public developer portal or API program.

providers.name: Mercanto
providers.description: Mercanto (mercanto.mx) is a Mexican B2B wholesale marketplace that supplies restaurants, cafeterias, and food-service businesses with ingredients, groceries, cleaning supplies, and packaging bought at wholesale from vetted suppliers, with negotiated pricing and next-day delivery. Buyers order across categories including produce, groceries and pantry, dairy and eggs, proteins and cold cuts, bakery and desserts, beverages, frozen foods, and non-food items, while Mercanto handles supplier selection, negotiation, and fulfillment. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures. Its customer-facing storefront runs on a private backend (api.mercanto.mx) that is not publicly documented for third-party developers, so there is no public API product, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Nfinite
providers.description: Nfinite (formerly Hubstairs) is a visual intelligence platform for the digital shelf. It helps consumer brands and retailers automatically analyze, generate, and monitor compliant product visuals — detecting visual compliance gaps across every retailer and brand and fixing them at scale using AI-generated 3D and synthetic product imagery. The product is delivered as a web application (my.nfinite.app) rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, developer portal, or published documentation exists at the time of enrichment. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Nowports
providers.description: Nowports is a digital freight forwarder for Latin America, offering technology-enabled international logistics across ocean, air, and ground freight. Its Centraliza platform centralizes shipment tracking, document management, and alerts, while adjacent services cover cargo insurance and GPS tracking (Protege) and inventory financing and factoring (Financia). Backed by Partech and Y Combinator, Nowports serves importers and exporters on major trade routes through its authenticated web app at app.nowports.com. As of this profile Nowports exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; access is via its authenticated web platform.

providers.name: Periphery
providers.description: Periphery is a cybersecurity company providing embedded, device-level threat management for critical industrial and defence platforms. Its lightweight, architecture-agnostic agent secures, fingerprints, and continuously monitors devices, detecting unauthorized changes and hardening what is risky even in constrained, offline, or air-gapped environments. The platform spans three products: Insights (point-in-time security evaluation with agent-based pen-testing and SBOM risk analysis), Vantage (on-prem intelligence that establishes a known-good baseline, detects change, and restores devices), and Outpost (real-time on-device threat detection and prevention for air-gapped deployments). Periphery targets regulatory compliance across NDAA, EU CRA, NIS2, UN R155, UN R156, and IEC 62443. It is a Techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: Ploy
providers.description: Ploy is an AI-powered marketing platform that turns a company's website into its growth engine. Founded in 2025 by former Webflow CTO Bryant Chou and backed by Y Combinator, Ploy deploys AI agents that build and optimize web pages, write copy, run technical SEO fixes, identify and enrich site visitors, launch ad campaigns, and track attribution across three product surfaces (Web, Grow, and Ads). Users activate pre-built marketing strategies called PloyBooks or author custom strategies that agents execute. Ploy is a SaaS product with a credit-based pricing model; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or developer portal — only a product help center and native integrations (Google, GitHub sync, CRM, and ad platforms).

providers.name: Prudentia Sciences
providers.description: Prudentia Sciences provides a scientific intelligence layer powering life-sciences dealmaking. The platform unifies fragmented pharmaceutical and biotech data sources, applies expert-developed evaluation frameworks, and applies AI trained on drug development so that pharma companies, biotech firms, investors, and deal teams can assess pharmaceutical assets faster and with more confidence during M&A and licensing transactions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; the company operates as a single-tenant, SOC 2-aligned SaaS platform.

providers.name: Robert Half International
providers.description: Robert Half International is the world's first and largest specialized staffing and talent solutions firm. Founded in 1948, it provides contract, temporary, and permanent placement solutions across finance and accounting, technology, marketing, legal, and administrative fields. The company is the parent of Protiviti, a global consulting firm. Robert Half does not publicly expose a developer API; integration is available through partner programs and ATS ecosystem connectors. Listed in the Fortune 500.

providers.name: SkyWest Airlines
providers.description: SkyWest Airlines is the largest regional airline in North America, headquartered in St. George, Utah. Operating under partnership agreements with United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, and Alaska Airlines, SkyWest serves over 256 destinations across the United States, Canada, and Mexico with a fleet of 500+ Bombardier regional jets (CRJ200, CRJ550, CRJ900). Founded in 1972, SkyWest carries over 46 million passengers annually operating as United Express, Delta Connection, American Eagle, and Alaska SkyWest. The company does not offer a public developer API; flight data is accessible through third-party aviation data providers.

providers.name: Soundboks
providers.description: Soundboks is a Danish consumer-electronics company that designs and manufactures loud, durable, battery-powered Bluetooth party speakers (Soundboks 4, Soundboks Mix) plus companion products such as Lightboks party lights. Products are sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify-powered storefront and controlled with a companion iOS/Android app that supports wireless playback and multi-speaker pairing (TeamUp). Soundboks does not publish a first-party developer API or SDK; its only programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account API (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect) exposed on its own store domain via the standard Shopify discovery documents, which is what this enrichment pass captured.

providers.name: Spectora
providers.description: Spectora is home inspection software used by more than 10,000 inspectors to build inspection reports, schedule jobs, manage clients and agents, run a website, take payments, and automate follow-up. Spectora does NOT publish a public, self-serve developer REST API and there is no developer portal, API reference, or API keys for third-party programmatic access as of this writing. Integration with outside systems is instead delivered three ways: (1) a Zapier integration (requires the paid Spectora Advanced add-on) that fires triggers when agent or client contacts are created or updated; (2) outbound webhooks configured through Advanced Actions that POST event data to a URL you supply (e.g. Zapier, Make, or your own endpoint); and (3) a fixed set of named, vendor-built partner integrations (QuickBooks Online, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Mailchimp, HomeBinder, RecallChek, Repair Pricer, Blipp Reviews, InterNACHI BuyBack, and call-center partners). All of these are configuration-time connectors and one-way (outbound) event flows rather than a documented request/response API you can call.

providers.name: Tasso
providers.description: Tasso, Inc. designs painless, needle-free blood collection devices and an end-to-end logistics platform for decentralized and at-home blood sampling. Its product line includes Tasso+ for capillary whole-blood collection, the Tasso-M20/Mini for dried blood microsampling, and the tile-T20 for liquid serum and plasma, enabling remote specimen collection for clinical trials, patient screening, diagnostics, and research. Tasso pairs the hardware with kitting, shipping, and sample-return logistics and is cited in over 100 peer-reviewed publications. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Textsidekick
providers.description: Textsidekick (Sidekick) is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) workforce communication and knowledge-management platform built for frontline workers who do not have a desk. Workers text a question or report an issue over plain SMS with no app to install and no login; Sidekick triages the message, answers from company knowledge, converts issues into work orders, routes them to the right person, and captures every fix as searchable organizational knowledge. It also AI-generates safety procedures, handbooks, and FAQs, schedules preventive maintenance, and delivers text-based onboarding and training. Founded to serve the roughly 80% of American workers without a desk, it is live across 20+ plants serving 600+ frontline workers. No public developer API, SDK, or API reference is published at this time.

providers.name: Tourlane
providers.description: Tourlane (Tourlane GmbH) is a travel planning company that creates personalized, custom multi-day trip packages. Travelers are paired with English-speaking, native-European destination travel experts for one-on-one consultations, free initial trip planning, complete booking management, and dedicated support throughout their trip, across destinations such as Italy, Greece, Ireland, Spain, Scotland, and France. Tourlane is a portfolio company of HV Capital. Sector: consumer travel. Tourlane publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Trim
providers.description: Trim is a consumer fintech company founded in 2015 that built an automated personal finance assistant which finds and cancels unwanted subscriptions, negotiates bills such as cable and internet, and automates savings for its users. Trim was backed by Version One Ventures and was acquired by OneMain Financial; its former asktrim.com home now redirects to OneMain MyMoney (onemainmymoney.com), where the product lives on as a personalized money insights and expense tracking app. Trim/MyMoney is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Uniko
