CCC defines, advances, and standardizes hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) that protect data and code while in use, complementing existing protections for data at rest and in transit. The consortium governs open source projects and specifications spanning attestation, trustworthy workload identity, and TEE runtimes.

providers.name: Context.ai *
providers.description: Context (context.ai) is a unified enterprise AI platform for building, deploying, and improving AI agents at scale. The product is organized into modular components: a Workspace for authoring agent workflows in plain English, an Engine with 800+ connectors and IdP-brokered identity, Unify as a knowledge/institutional-context repository, and Evals for rubric-based quality scoring. It is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, or open weights) and offers hosted, VPC, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment. The company originated as a GV (Google Ventures) and Theory Ventures backed product-analytics-for-LLMs startup and now operates as an enterprise agent platform used by teams including Qualcomm, Stripe, and Palantir. This repo carries no public developer/API surface: the provider publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation, so most machine-readable artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Curve Dental
providers.description: Curve Dental is a cloud-based, all-in-one dental practice management software company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia. Its flagship platform, Curve Hero, serves more than 80,000 dental professionals across the United States and Canada, unifying scheduling, clinical and perio charting, imaging, billing, insurance, smart forms, reporting, patient engagement, and business analytics in a single browser-based system. Curve is privately held and backed by Battery Ventures, and connects to a growing ecosystem of integration partners (including DentalXChange, DentalHQ, Pearl AI, Bola AI, and Mango Voice) rather than exposing a public self-serve developer API. This profile was seeded from Battery Ventures' portfolio and enriched from Curve Dental's public web surface; no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: DELLI
providers.description: DELLI is a UK online marketplace for independent food and drink makers, founded in 2022 by Depop founder Simon Beckerman with co-founder Marie Petrovicka. Often described as "the Depop for food," DELLI curates niche and small-batch products — snacks, sauces and condiments, pantry staples, drinks, alcohol, sweets and lifestyle goods — from micro-bakers, picklers, olive-oil producers and drink makers, and sells them to consumers, in part through a drop-style release model. The platform has since evolved into an AI-powered companion for makers and retailers, adding tools that cut the operational overhead of running a small food business. DELLI is backed by Balderton Capital and HV Capital, the original investors in Depop. The storefront runs on Shopify; DELLI publishes no first-party developer API at this time.

providers.name: Diagon
providers.description: Diagon is a California-based industrial equipment sourcing company building Albus, an equipment intelligence platform for manufacturing buyers and sellers. Buyers search across millions of industrial equipment listings, compare models, specifications, pricing and availability, and connect directly with sellers; sellers publish AI-powered catalogs, reach qualified buyer demand, and see live equipment searches in real time. Diagon indexes manufacturing equipment products, suppliers and service providers, bringing hardware, services and financing into a consolidated procurement experience. Founded by a team out of Tesla, Bright Machines, Rivian and Snackpass, and backed by Anthemis under its data, tech and infrastructure thesis. Diagon publishes no public developer API today; its /api surface is an authenticated first-party application API (Clerk-based session auth) and is disallowed in robots.txt.

providers.name: Diagon Technologies
providers.description: Diagon Technologies operates Albus, an industrial equipment intelligence and procurement platform for North American manufacturing. Albus aggregates millions of industrial equipment listings so buyers can search by make, model, or specification, compare equipment specs, pricing, and availability side by side, and connect directly with sellers to request quotes. Sellers publish AI-powered catalogs, reach qualified buyer demand, and see live equipment searches in real time across categories such as subtractive manufacturing, forming, joining, surface treatment, and polymer processing, and OEMs including DMG Mori, Trumpf, Okuma, FANUC, and Mazak. Diagon is a Techstars portfolio company; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DiversyFund
providers.description: DiversyFund is a San Diego based private-markets investment platform that packages institutional-style fixed income and multifamily real estate offerings for individual accredited investors. Formed in 2016 and qualified under SEC Regulation A+, the firm acts as sponsor, developer and manager of its own funds rather than as a broker, and reports having acquired more than $300 million across 20+ multifamily properties for a base of 28,000+ investors. Its current offering, the Distressed Income Fund, is a Reg D 506(c) preferred-equity vehicle sold to accredited investors with a target allocation of $100K to $1M. Investing is transacted through a private, authenticated investor portal at portal.diversyfund.com (WorkOS AuthKit); DiversyFund publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Doctronic
providers.description: Doctronic is a consumer telemedicine platform that pairs an AI doctor with licensed physicians for anonymous, low-cost health care. Users describe their symptoms to an AI assistant that performs a free symptom assessment and health consultation, then can escalate to a real doctor for a video visit ($39/visit), prescription refills, lab orders, and follow-up care. Positioned as "Free. Anonymous. Built by doctors," the product is direct-to-consumer web and mobile rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation. The only public machine-readable surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure policy. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Egab
providers.description: Egab is a journalism platform founded in late 2020 and headquartered in Cairo, Egypt, that connects local journalists across the Global South — the Middle East, Africa, and beyond (60+ countries) — with international media outlets. It specializes in solutions journalism, offering journalists mentoring, editorial support, skills development, and fair compensation from pitch to publication, while giving newsrooms cost-efficient access to authentic, exclusive stories and diverse local contributors without flying in reporters.

providers.name: Emeritus
providers.description: Emeritus is a global online education company that partners with more than 80 premier universities — including Wharton, MIT, Columbia, Harvard, Kellogg, and UC Berkeley — to deliver outcome-based executive education, professional certificates, and skill-development programs to over 500,000 learners worldwide. It operates across individual learners, enterprise/corporate training, and university-branded partnership programs, spanning topics such as AI and machine learning, data science, finance, leadership, and digital transformation through instructor-led online and blended formats. Emeritus is backed by Accel and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Emeritus publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Epsor
providers.description: Epsor is a French fintech, founded in 2017, that manages employee savings and retirement plans (épargne salariale et retraite) for companies and helps them turn that benefit into an HR lever. A certified B Corp and mission-driven company, Epsor ranks among the top 10 employee-savings and retirement providers in France and serves more than 2,500 corporate clients. It targets HR, Compensation & Benefits, and Finance teams at mid-size and large French firms, combining a pedagogical, personalized saver experience, an open-architecture fund range (40+ funds from 15+ asset managers, with a strong ESG/SRI focus), and year-round support to run and promote the plan. Epsor is neither an asset manager nor a bank: it is the single point of contact for companies and their employees, and delegates account-keeping to Société Générale Securities Services (SGSS). Products span PEE, PER Collectif (PERECO), PER Obligatoire, intéressement, participation, abondement, and employee share ownership. Epsor exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ernesta
providers.description: Ernesta is a direct-to-consumer, custom-sized rug company that lets homeowners and interior-design professionals order high-design rugs made to measure down to the inch. Founded by three Peloton co-founders (John Foley, Hisao Kushi, and Yony Feng) and backed by True Ventures, Addition, and Platform Capital, Ernesta sells online through a Shopify storefront and a growing set of showrooms, and runs a dedicated Trade Program and Trade Portal for designers. Ernesta publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile catalogs the company's consumer and trade web properties plus the discovery, security, and identity signals observable on its public hosts.

providers.name: Fab.com
providers.description: Fab.com is a digital content marketplace operated by Epic Games, where creators buy and sell 3D models, materials, environments, VFX, audio, and game-ready assets. Launched in October 2024, Fab consolidated four of Epic's prior storefronts — the Unreal Engine Marketplace, the Sketchfab Store, Quixel, and the ArtStation Marketplace — into a single catalog with unified licensing, and integrates into Unreal Engine, UEFN, and the Epic Games Launcher. The fabcom entry was originally added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead for the earlier, unrelated Fab.com flash-sale design-commerce company (2011–2015), which wound down before the domain passed to Epic Games; see x-identity-note. Fab publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification as of this pass — the surface captured here is its documentation, support, and security-disclosure posture.

providers.name: Fertifa
providers.description: Fertifa is Europe's reproductive healthcare benefits provider for employers, giving companies a way to offer fertility, family-forming, women's health, maternity, menopause, men's reproductive health, and neurodiversity support to their employees. The platform pairs an in-house clinical team with education and training, diagnostics and testing, prescriptions and medication delivery, and financing/reimbursement, delivered to staff through a mobile app and to HR teams through enterprise and SME plans. Fertifa is London-based, backed by Speedinvest, and works with employers including Lululemon, Meta, Bain Capital, and Virgin. No public developer API or OpenAPI surface is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, and support properties.

providers.name: FITCO
providers.description: Fitco is the leading management software for boutique fitness studios and gyms in Latin America. It lets centers administer reservations, memberships, payments, online classes and check-in, and provides a custom website and mobile app for each studio's members. It specializes in pilates, barre, indoor cycling, yoga, functional training, strength, sports academies and wellness centers. Fitco operates in Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Chile, Argentina and the United States; as of May 2026 more than 1,400 fitness centers use it. It integrates online payments via Stripe and Mercado Pago and customer acquisition via Wellhub and TotalPass.

providers.name: Flatiron Health
providers.description: Flatiron Health is a healthcare technology company focused on oncology, combining real-world data from millions of cancer patients with software and AI to support life sciences research and clinical care. Its platforms include OncoEMR and OncoCloud for oncology practices, Flatiron Vessel (clinical research EDC, formerly Protocol First) and Clinical Pipe for clinical trials, and real-world evidence products for life sciences. Flatiron data has informed thousands of peer-reviewed publications and regulatory submissions. The company is part of Roche.

providers.name: Freterium
providers.description: Freterium is a cloud-native AI Transport Management System (TMS) and unified logistics operating system that connects shippers, carriers, and fleets on a single intelligent layer. It spans first-mile, middle-mile, and last-mile operations across eight integrated modules — order management, AI-powered route planning, collaborative shipper and carrier portals, real-time GPS tracking with predictive ETAs, fleet management, freight billing and costing, intelligent document control, and analytics and reporting — and exposes a documented REST API for ERP/WMS integration alongside 50+ off-the-shelf telematics and hardware integrations. Surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Partech portfolio company.

providers.name: Funding Societies
providers.description: Funding Societies (known as Modalku in Indonesia) is Southeast Asia's largest unified SME digital finance platform, founded in 2015 and operating across Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. It provides small and medium-sized enterprises with business financing — term loans, micro loans, revolving credit lines, invoice and trade financing — and offers retail and institutional investors the ability to fund those loans for a return. The group is licensed and regulated in its markets and is backed by investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Sequoia, and SoftBank Ventures Asia. Funding Societies does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK program; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web properties and security posture. It will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is published.

providers.name: Gatling
providers.description: Gatling is an open source load and performance testing framework for web applications and APIs with a Scala-based DSL and detailed HTML reports. The Gatling Enterprise Edition exposes a public REST API for triggering runs and fetching run results and metrics.

providers.name: Gigster
providers.description: Gigster is an enterprise software-development services company that connects businesses with top-tier global talent for custom software development, AI solutions, and digital transformation. Through a network of 50,000+ vetted developers, designers, and product experts, Gigster delivers work under three engagement models: Fully Managed (Gigster owns scoping through delivery), Dedicated Teams (skilled teams that scale with a client's goals), and Talent On Demand (specialists who blend into an existing team). Specialized practices cover AI development, innovation/design/UX, applications and platforms, and system modernization. Gigster reports 1,000+ enterprise engagements, a 95% on-time/on-budget delivery rate, and average staffing under 10 days, and is backed by a16z, Bloomberg Beta, and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio company profile.

providers.name: Gravel AI
providers.description: Gravel AI is a beauty and personal care market intelligence platform that turns alternative data into early trend, ingredient, brand, and product signals for the global cosmetics industry. It offers a suite of analysis tools — application and ingredient trends, brand and market deep dives, consumer review analysis, new brand and product launch monitoring, ingredient supplier and OEM mapping, and product analyzers — alongside curated datasets, market reports, and an enterprise data/API service that delivers licensed beauty data into customer pipelines (API, Snowflake, S3). Backed by Techstars, Gravel AI serves beauty brands, ingredient and contract manufacturers, and enterprise insights, R&D, procurement, and data teams. Its flagship Gravel Early Trends product positions against incumbents such as Euromonitor, Mintel, NielsenIQ, Circana, WGSN, and Spate.

providers.name: Greenplaces
providers.description: Greenplaces is a sustainability and ESG reporting platform that pairs software with expert consulting to help companies — especially suppliers responding to enterprise requirements — measure their carbon footprint under the GHG Protocol and complete sustainability framework submissions including CDP, EcoVadis, SBTi, GRI, SASB/ISSB and GRESB. The managed-service platform also supports B Corp certification, CSRD readiness, SOC 2 and AI-governance compliance, and tracking of regulations such as California SB 253 and SB 261. Greenplaces is venture-backed by Felicis and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio data; the company publishes a managed product (app.greenplaces.com) but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Greyparrot
providers.description: Greyparrot is a London-based AI waste analytics company that turns materials recovery facilities (MRFs) into data-driven operations. Its Greyparrot Analyzer uses computer-vision cameras mounted over waste conveyor belts to identify, count, and measure the composition of waste streams in real time, giving recyclers continuous visibility into what flows through their plant. The Greyparrot Sync product routes that analytics stream into existing operational control systems, ERP platforms, Power BI dashboards, and OEM sortation hardware (robotic arms, air-jet systems, balers, belt control), while Deepnest turns real-world recovery data into design feedback for packaging brands. Backed by Speedinvest, Greyparrot serves recyclers, equipment manufacturers, and consumer-goods companies working to raise recycling rates and automate compliance reporting. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web, product, and content surface.

providers.name: Heyo
providers.description: Heyo is a social marketing platform for building and running online promotions such as sweepstakes, contests, giveaways, quizzes, and coupons. Businesses use Heyo's drag-and-drop campaign builder and landing pages to create interactive campaign apps that publish to the web, mobile, and social networks including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. It is used to grow email marketing lists, generate sales leads, acquire new customers, reward existing customers, and increase social followers, with templated promotion apps and a free trial. Heyo is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: HiGuest
providers.description: HiGuests (Hi Guests Vacation Homes Rental LLC, License 765614) is a Dubai-based short-term rental property management company. It offers full-service management for vacation homes and furnished apartments, listing owners' properties across 20+ booking channels (Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia, and others), and handling profile creation, dynamic pricing, booking and guest communications, 24/7 guest support, check-in/check-out, housekeeping, and maintenance, alongside transparent owner reporting. HiGuests markets a zero-commission subscription plan for landlords and operates a guest-facing booking site. It is a hospitality services business, not an API/developer platform; no public API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hipcamp
providers.description: Hipcamp is the #1 app to find and book campsites globally, with real-time availability across more than 500,000 sites in the United States, Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom. Campers search national parks, state parks, RV resorts, and private land stays (farms, ranches, vineyards) in one app, with filters, Pro map layers (BLM/USFS land, cell coverage, dark skies), road-trip search, and free availability alerts. Hosts list and manage campsites, sync calendars, and take weekly payouts. Hipcamp integrates with campground reservation systems (ResNexus, Cloudbeds, Newbook, RMS, Bedful) but publishes no public developer API — /api and /graphql are internal-only. Surfaced as an a16z / Bond Capital / Slow Ventures portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Horizon Quantum Computing
providers.description: Horizon Quantum Computing is a Singapore-based quantum software company founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons. It builds software infrastructure for quantum applications, centered on Triple Alpha, an integrated development environment that lets developers write hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction and deploy them to quantum processors. Triple Alpha's final workflow step packages a program and deploys it as an API so developers can invoke quantum backends from Python scripts, web pages, and other technologies. Horizon operates its own quantum computing testbed at its Singapore headquarters and supports a range of external quantum processors, aiming to bridge the gap between today's quantum hardware and real-world applications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or client SDK; API-based program deployment is offered to early-access users of the Triple Alpha platform.

providers.name: Housewhisper
providers.description: HouseWhisper (legal name Real Estate Productivity, Inc.) is a Seattle-based AI platform for real estate teams and brokerages, founded by former Zillow executives. It acts as a 24/7 AI teammate that automates the full lead lifecycle through personalized voice and text conversations: a Lead Engine that re-engages and revives cold database contacts, a Rules Engine that routes leads to the right agent with fallback escalations, and an AI Teammate that handles CRM updates, follow-ups, scheduling, reminders, and administrative busywork by call or text. It connects to real estate CRM, dialer, and calendar systems via API keys with no data migration, integrating with Follow Up Boss, Sierra Interactive, kvCORE, MoxiWorks, Salesforce, Lofty, HubSpot, and others. Pricing is outcome-based (a small monthly platform fee plus referral fees on closed deals). HouseWhisper has raised roughly $10M in seed funding led by Mayfield. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Huginn
providers.description: Huginn is an open-source system for building agents that perform automated tasks online. Self-hosted agents can monitor the web, send and receive events, and trigger workflows. Each Huginn instance exposes a JSON-based HTTP interface (the Web Requests API) that lets external systems trigger scenarios and post events into the platform.

providers.name: Hurl
providers.description: Hurl is an open source command-line tool for running HTTP requests defined in a simple plain text format with built-in assertions for API testing.

providers.name: iMotorbike
providers.description: iMotorbike is a Southeast Asian online marketplace and service platform for buying, selling, and servicing pre-owned motorcycles, operating across Malaysia and Vietnam. Sellers submit their bike details, book a free inspection, receive a quotation, and get paid fast, while iMotorbike handles loan settlement and JPJ ownership transfer on their behalf. Buyers shop iM Certified motorcycles backed by a 170-point inspection, a 12-month warranty, and a 6-day return policy, and can book test rides, inspections, and roadside assistance (iM Rescue) through the platform. Founded in 2017 and backed by 500 Global, Headline, Gobi Partners, and Endeavor Catalyst, iMotorbike closed a US$10M Series A in 2025 to expand across the region. The company runs a consumer-facing web marketplace and an internal admin platform; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Incluyeme
providers.description: Incluyeme.com is a Latin American social enterprise, founded in 2013 by Gabriel Marcolongo, working toward the social and labor inclusion of people with disabilities. Its online platform connects candidates with disabilities to inclusive employers, offering job listings, virtual training courses, scholarships, and mentorship for individuals, alongside inclusive-hiring consulting, talent sourcing, staff training, and physical/web accessibility evaluation for companies. Operating across roughly a dozen countries in Latin America (Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, Uruguay, Paraguay and more), it has registered hundreds of thousands of people with disabilities and placed thousands into roles with 100+ corporate clients. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Instaread
providers.description: Instaread is a media and audio technology company with two products. Its consumer app delivers ~15-minute audio and text summaries of bestselling books across business, self-help, history, health, politics, and fiction on mobile, tablet, and desktop. Its publisher product, Instaread Player, is a free embeddable audio widget that uses AI text-to-speech (including custom voice cloning) to convert website articles, blogs, and newsletters into natural-sounding audio, monetized for publishers through programmatic audio advertising. The Player is used by 200+ brands, ships ADA/WCAG accessibility support, an analytics dashboard, podcast distribution, and a WordPress plugin, and works on Squarespace, Wix, Webflow, and custom sites via a single embed code. Instaread does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Jeeng
providers.description: Jeeng (formerly PowerInbox) is a multichannel monetization and audience-engagement platform for digital publishers. It helps publishers grow first-party, opt-in audiences and generate advertising revenue across email newsletters, websites, push notifications, and newsreader apps, reaching more than 150M opt-in subscribers. Its products — AdFill, AdServe, AdMarket, and Renderer — fill vacant ad inventory with monetized content, extend direct ad campaigns into email through existing ad servers, connect advertisers to opt-in audiences, and streamline Google Ad Manager ad-ops workflows. Publisher integration is handled through merge tags, per-newsletter ad tags, and cs_email tracking parameters plus direct Google Ad Manager integration; campaigns and reporting are managed through the PowerInbox Portal at manage.jeeng.com. Jeeng publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Jome
providers.description: Jome is a real estate technology marketplace for buying new construction homes, describing itself as the most joyful way to buy a new home in the age of AI. Buyers can search and compare thousands of new-construction homes and communities from multiple builders, view pricing and builder incentives, instantly book and confirm home tours, and receive AI-powered personalized recommendations, with new-home experts guiding them from contract to closing. Jome operates as a licensed real estate brokerage across 18+ U.S. metros, primarily in Texas, Florida, North Carolina, Arizona, Georgia, Colorado, South Carolina, and Tennessee, and runs dedicated portals for builders and agents. Backed by Techstars. Jome publishes no public API or developer program; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity and public web presence.

providers.name: KITRO
providers.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

providers.name: KupiVIP
providers.description: KupiVIP (kupivip.ru) is a Russian online outlet retailer for luxury and premium fashion, selling women's and men's apparel, footwear, bags, accessories and home goods from more than 250 international designer brands at discounts of up to 90% on previous-season collections. The 1C-Bitrix storefront ships across Russia, publishes a 100% authenticity guarantee backed by expert verification, offers free delivery on orders over 30,000 RUB, and runs telephone, email, WhatsApp and Telegram customer support. The company was originally surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio company. As of the 2026-07-19 enrichment probe KupiVIP publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: LawTrades
providers.description: LawTrades is a legal talent marketplace, founded in 2016, that matches companies with vetted independent attorneys, paralegals, and legal operations professionals on flexible, on-demand terms rather than through traditional law firms or ALSPs. The platform covers eleven practice areas — commercial contracts, corporate law, data privacy and cyber security, intellectual property, labor and employment, legal operations, litigation, M&A, product counsel, real estate, and regulatory compliance — and handles matching, work-log management, invoicing, payments, and real-time spend analytics in-product. A human-in-the-loop AI layer drafts documents and flags risk for lawyer review. LawTrades raised a $6M Series A backed by 500 Global, Draper Associates, Social Capital, and AngelList. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Leta
providers.description: Leta is a pan-African logistics technology company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Westlands, Nairobi, Kenya, with operations across Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. Leta builds an AI-driven delivery management platform that helps businesses move goods cheaper and faster while minimising climate impact: route optimization, automated dispatch and broadcast, live GPS track-and-trace, payment on delivery, fleet management, and delivery analytics. The platform is delivered as logistics SaaS plus on-demand and dedicated rider services, including an M-PESA business mini-app, and serves e-commerce, third-party logistics and courier, food and beverage, retail and consumer goods, and pharmacy and healthcare delivery operators. Leta is backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Linguatrip
providers.description: Linguatrip is a language-education and language-travel company founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global. It operates two connected businesses: a booking marketplace for accredited language schools abroad — covering course selection, accommodation, airport transfers and visa support across countries including the United Kingdom, Malta and the United Arab Emirates — and its own online English school offering 25+ self-paced courses, one-to-one tutoring, speaking clubs and exam preparation for IELTS, TOEFL, GMAT, GRE and SAT. It also provides higher-education placement consulting for US, UK and Canadian universities. Linguatrip publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; its surfaces are consumer web properties in four languages with pricing in 18 currencies.

providers.name: Livsn Designs
providers.description: Livsn Designs is a Techstars-backed outdoor apparel brand that makes durable, minimalist technical clothing (its Flex Canvas pants and multi-use travel and hiking apparel) sold direct-to-consumer from a Shopify storefront at livsndesigns.com. It publishes no first-party developer API or documentation portal. Its only programmatic surface is the agent-commerce layer Shopify serves on the merchant's own domain: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) shopping MCP endpoint for agent-driven checkout, a Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth2 authorization server, and an llms.txt / agents.md agent-instructions document. This profile captures that real agent surface; there is no bespoke API to catalog.

providers.name: Manifest Law
providers.description: Manifest Law operates ManifestOS, a communication and case management platform for the legal industry, and is backed by Menlo Ventures. The platform exposes a standards-based OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization server at app.manifestlaw.com, with an `api` scope for programmatic access and dynamic OAuth client management (`oauth_clients:manage`). This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Manifest Law's public discovery documents; no OpenAPI specification was published at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: McGrath
providers.description: McGrath is one of Australia's largest residential real estate brokerage networks, founded in Sydney in 1988 by John McGrath and operating a mixed company-owned and franchise network of roughly 118 offices across New South Wales, Queensland, the ACT, Victoria and Tasmania. Its business lines span residential sales, property management and rentals, projects and new-development marketing, rural and livestock, an Asia Desk for offshore buyers, and mortgage broking through Oxygen Home Loans. Listed on the ASX in 2015 as McGrath Limited (ASX:MEA), it was acquired in June 2024 by a consortium of Knight Frank Australia and New Zealand's Bayleys for A$95.5m and delisted from the ASX on 28 June 2024. McGrath sits on the demand side of the Australian property value chain: it is a brokerage that publishes listings into the REA Group (realestate.com.au) and Domain portal duopoly, settles transactions over the PEXA electronic conveyancing network, and consumes valuation data from PropTrack and CoreLogic rather than producing any of those rails itself. Its API posture is honestly nil. No developer portal exists — developer., developers., api., docs., feeds., data. and portal. subdomains of mcgrath.com.au all fail to resolve (NXDOMAIN), and /developers, /api, /docs, /api-docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /$metadata and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return HTTP 404. RESO — the only genuinely mandated machine-readable real estate contract anywhere in this study — is a North American standard driven by NAR and MLS membership; it has no Australian counterpart and McGrath has no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData surface, and no Universal Property Identifier usage. The only interoperability standards McGrath demonstrably implements are robots.txt and twelve XML sitemaps; every /.well-known/ document probed — security.txt, openid-configuration, oauth-authorization-server, api-catalog, ai-plugin.json — and /llms.txt return 404. Its robots.txt enumerates twenty crawler groups including GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot and Bytespider, but under RFC 9309 group-matching rules those named AI agents are disallowed only from Google Maps JS/RPC paths — the /properties/ and /search/ disallow lands solely on User-agent: *, so the listing corpus is nominally open to the named AI crawlers and closed to generic ones, while the properties-buy/sold/rent/leased sitemaps advertise those same URLs. Reachability is the harder gate: www.mcgrath.com.au sits behind a Vercel Security Checkpoint that answers scripted clients with HTTP 429 and a browser challenge on every path, so no unattended agent can read the site regardless of robots.txt. The listing inventory is a marketing asset routed to portals under commercial agreements, not a developer surface.

providers.name: Natural Cycles
providers.description: Natural Cycles is a Swedish women's-health company behind the first birth-control application cleared by the US FDA (2018) and CE-marked in Europe as a Class IIb medical device. Its subscription app uses a proprietary temperature-based algorithm to identify fertile and non-fertile days from a user's daily basal body temperature, supporting both preventing and planning pregnancy as well as cycle, ovulation, and perimenopause tracking. Temperature is captured with a paired Bluetooth basal thermometer or through consumer wearables the app integrates with — Apple Watch, Oura Ring, and the NC B1 band. Natural Cycles publishes clinical research, an educational content library (CycleMatters), an e-commerce shop for thermometers and tests, and a public bug-bounty / responsible-disclosure program, but it does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. Backed by EQT Ventures.

providers.name: NetSuite Accounting
providers.description: NetSuite Accounting is the cloud financial management module of Oracle NetSuite that delivers general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, cash management, tax management, fixed assets, and real-time financial reporting and consolidation for growing businesses. NetSuite exposes its accounting records (invoices, bills, journal entries, payments, accounts, customers, vendors, and ledgers) through SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL queries, and RESTlets, secured with OAuth 2.0 and token-based authentication for ERP and finance integrations.

providers.name: Novidea
providers.description: Novidea is a cloud-native insurance management platform built on Salesforce that helps insurance brokers, MGAs (managing general agents), coverholders, and carriers digitize the full insurance distribution lifecycle across front, middle, and back office operations. The platform unifies quoting, underwriting, binding, policy administration, claims, and accounting with real-time data and analytics, workflow automation, document generation, and customer portals. It markets a "truly open API framework" and an "API a la carte" offering for extending and integrating the platform, but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs; its API surface is delivered to customers on top of the Salesforce platform. Novidea is backed by Battery Ventures and serves insurance distribution businesses globally.

providers.name: NuORDER
providers.description: NuORDER by Lightspeed is a global B2B commerce platform for wholesale buying and selling between brands and retailers. It combines a fully-branded wholesale eCommerce storefront with account-specific pricing and discounts, an Assortments planning tool for data-driven buying and reduced markdowns, and a Marketplace that connects buyers to 3,000+ brands across fashion, footwear, and apparel. NuORDER exposes a partner-gated REST API at api.nuorder.com for syncing products, orders, catalogs, and customer data with ERP, PIM, and other commerce systems. Acquired by Lightspeed in 2021, it is used by brands including Arc'teryx, Kendra Scott, TOMS, Barbour, and Canada Goose.

providers.name: OakNorth
providers.description: OakNorth is a UK-based commercial bank and business-lending institution founded in 2015, providing debt financing to mid-market and lower-mid-market businesses in the UK and, through its New York team, the United States. Its products span business loans (from roughly GBP 1m to tens of millions), commercial real estate lending, commercial & industrial cash-flow financing, fund finance, and business and personal savings accounts. OakNorth is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. It publicly exposes no developer API, open-banking API, or developer portal; its public technical surface is limited to a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program and standard web/legal properties. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Our Place
providers.description: Our Place is a direct-to-consumer kitchenware and cookware brand, best known for the multi-purpose Always Pan, selling cookware, bakeware, appliances, tableware, and kitchen tools at fromourplace.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc, its digital storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a native agentic-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) shopping endpoint, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect authentication, and an agent-facing llms.txt / agents.md. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's live public agent surface.

providers.name: Paro
providers.description: Paro is an AI-powered professional services marketplace that connects businesses and accounting firms with vetted, on-demand finance and accounting experts. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Chicago, Paro uses proprietary AI matching to pair clients with the top 2% of finance professionals across 60+ industries and 250+ skill sets — spanning bookkeeping, fractional CFO and controller services, financial planning and analysis, tax and compliance, and full-time recruiting. For accounting firms it provides staff augmentation, busy-season support, and service-expansion consulting. Paro operates a talent platform (app.paro.io) but does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, content, and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Peer39
providers.description: Peer39 is a contextual advertising and intelligence company that provides pre-bid controls and post-buy analytics built on verified contextual data for programmatic media buyers. Its platform delivers contextual targeting, brand safety and suitability, and contextual analytics across web, mobile, and connected TV (CTV) and video environments, helping advertisers and platforms make privacy-forward, cookieless media decisions. Peer39 was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Peer39 exposes no public API or developer portal — access is via an authenticated customer application (app.peer39.com) and platform integrations rather than a documented, self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: Pharmeasy
providers.description: PharmEasy is one of India's largest digital healthcare platforms, operating a consumer online pharmacy and health marketplace at pharmeasy.in. It lets users order prescription and over-the-counter medicines (with prescription upload and verification), buy health and wellness products, book diagnostic lab tests and health checkup packages, and consult doctors via telemedicine, plus a PLUS subscription for recurring savings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Prosus Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. PharmEasy runs an internal API at api.pharmeasy.in but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it does operate a responsible-disclosure security program (infosec@pharmeasy.in). Sector: healthcare / e-pharmacy.

providers.name: PLOS
providers.description: These examples use the search API to search the PLOS corpus of scientific articles. These examples are not intended to be a full explanation on the use of Solr. A full Solr query language explanation can be found here and a tutorial here. The construction of PLOS search queries deviates from the standard Solr query URL by using search instead of select when making request to the end point. The primary endpoint is http://api.plos.org/search and supports parameters such as q, fl, wt, start, and rows for querying the PLOS Solr index.

providers.name: Purely B
providers.description: PurelyB is a natural superfood and wellness brand founded by Raja Jesrina Arshad, rooted in ancestral Asian health traditions and selling halal-certified, vegan, gluten-free herbal supplements (Pegaga, Tiger Milk Mushroom, Manjakani, Super Immune-C and a SuperKids line) direct to consumers across Malaysia and Singapore. The storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a standards-based agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping server, Shopify Customer Account OAuth/OIDC, and a published llms.txt for AI shopping agents. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its public developer/agent surface.

providers.name: PyTorch
providers.description: APIs and resources for PyTorch, an open source machine learning framework for tensor computation and deep learning developed by Meta.

providers.name: Quanta
providers.description: Quanta is a San Francisco-based accounting services company built for SaaS businesses, pairing expert human accountants with proprietary software that "shows its work." The platform delivers continuous accounting and reconciliation, explainable financial reporting through its agentic reporting layer (Prism), SaaS revenue and accounts-receivable insights, and real-time visibility into cash, burn, and runway alongside department-level spend tracking. Quanta is a managed-services and software product for finance teams rather than a developer-facing API provider; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Homebrew and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: rebtel
providers.description: Rebtel is a Swedish international communications company (Rebtel Networks AB, registered 556680-3622, headquartered in Stockholm) serving the world's roughly two billion international migrants with low-cost international calling, mobile top-up / airtime recharge, and calling cards delivered through its iOS and Android apps. It routes calls over optimized local phone lines to keep prices low. Backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. Rebtel exposes no public developer API or SDK program; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, support, and security.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Red Points
providers.description: Red Points operates an AI-powered brand protection and anti-counterfeiting platform used by businesses to detect and remove counterfeits, unauthorized sellers, fake websites, social media impersonation, and digital piracy across more than 5,000 marketplaces, social networks, and app stores. Its software combines automated detection with enforcement and takedown workflows, domain monitoring, gray-market and unauthorized-seller blocking, ad-fraud detection, and revenue-recovery and litigation services. Red Points was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it does not expose a public developer API or documented API surface as of this enrichment pass, so this profile captures the company's public web, legal, security, and llms.txt footprint rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Rilla
providers.description: Rilla is an AI conversation-intelligence and coaching platform built for in-person and outside sales teams. Reps record their face-to-face customer conversations, and Rilla transcribes and analyzes them so managers can run virtual "ridealongs" and deliver targeted, data-driven coaching at scale. The platform surfaces talk patterns, objection handling, and outcome analytics across thousands of field conversations to help teams raise close rates, increase ticket size, and speed up rep ramp. Rilla is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the AI sector. As of this profile Rilla exposes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs; this record captures its public web identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: RippleMatch
providers.description: RippleMatch is an AI-powered early-career recruiting platform that matches college students and recent graduates with internships and entry-level jobs based on their background, skills, and career goals rather than mass applications. For employers it offers "Campus OS", an all-in-one recruiting operating system for sourcing, skills validation, and campus event management, and it transfers matched candidates into most major applicant tracking systems (Greenhouse, Workday, Lever, SmartRecruiters, BambooHR). RippleMatch was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook/event surface; its integrations are one-way ATS data transfers rather than an openly documented API.

providers.name: Saffron
providers.description: Saffron (trysaffron.ai) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI-native technical assessment platform for engineering hiring. Candidates build real features on a company's actual codebase using AI coding tools such as Claude Code inside a sandboxed environment, while Saffron captures every keystroke and AI interaction to score submissions against custom rubrics. It provides line-by-line attribution distinguishing human-written, AI-generated, and AI-modified code, and replaces traditional phone screens, take-homes, and on-site interview loops with a single AI-integrated assessment.

providers.name: Scalable CFO
providers.description: The Scalable CFO is an Abu Dhabi (ADGM) based financial-operations platform for small and medium-sized enterprises. Its MADI software delivers real-time cash-flow forecasting, "what-if" scenario simulation, bill-payment planning and invoice-collection tracking, syncing with accounting systems such as Xero and QuickBooks. Alongside the software it runs a marketplace connecting businesses to 6,300+ pre-vetted fractional CFOs and accountants for accounts cleanup, tax compliance, margin optimization and fundraising readiness. The Scalable CFO is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: Selency
providers.description: Selency is the leading European online marketplace for vintage furniture and second-hand home decor. Founded in Paris in 2014 (formerly Brocante Lab), it connects individual sellers and professional antique dealers with buyers around a curated catalog of more than 300,000 unique pieces: Scandinavian, art deco, mid-century, 20th-century and contemporary design, lighting, mirrors, rugs and decorative objects. Selency acts as a trusted third party, editorially validating each listing and arranging specialized furniture delivery across Europe. It is a B Corp certified consumer marketplace with French, UK and Netherlands storefronts. No public developer API is offered.

providers.name: Smalls
providers.description: Smalls is a New York City based direct-to-consumer pet food company founded in 2017 by Matt Michaelson and Calvin Bohn, selling gently cooked human-grade fresh cat food, freeze-dried raw and treats on a personalized monthly subscription that customers build through an onboarding quiz at smalls.com, shipped nationwide and, since 2023, also sold into brick-and-mortar retail and wholesale. The company had raised roughly $34 million as of March 2023 — including a $9M Series A round announced in 2020 and a $19M Series B closed in mid-2022 — from investors including Left Lane Capital, Founder Collective, Digitalis Ventures and R/GA Ventures, and its shares trade on the Forge Global secondary market. Smalls runs its own Remix storefront on Netlify backed by a Contentful CMS rather than a hosted commerce platform, and publishes no first-party developer program: contract discovery in August 2026 found no OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL endpoint, MCP server, A2A agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known documents on any smalls.com host, and no GitHub organization or public client library.

providers.name: Speechly
providers.description: Speechly was a real-time spoken language understanding (SLU) and streaming speech recognition platform from a Finnish startup, offering low-latency voice transcription, intent/entity parsing, written language understanding (WLU), batch audio processing, and audio/text moderation through a gRPC API with browser, React, iOS, Unity/.NET, Python and Go client SDKs and a command-line interface. Speechly was acquired by Roblox; the standalone product and hosted API have since been discontinued — speechly.com now redirects to roblox.com, the api.speechly.com and docs.speechly.com hosts no longer resolve, and the github.com/speechly organization was archived on 2025-01-07. Its open-source client SDKs and protobuf/gRPC API definitions remain publicly available and are cataloged here by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Spoiler Alert
providers.description: Spoiler Alert is a Boston-based software company (a Techstars portfolio company) that helps consumer packaged goods (CPG) manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers manage and sell excess, short-dated, and obsolete inventory. Its purpose-built platform digitizes discounting and liquidation processes, matching surplus inventory with the right buyers at the right price through a secondary marketplace, with automated listing generation, dynamic pricing optimization, freight cost management, and performance analytics to recover margin and reduce food and product waste. The platform is delivered as a closed SaaS application (app.spoileralert.com); no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Start Playing
providers.description: StartPlaying (startplaying.games) is the largest online marketplace connecting tabletop roleplaying game (TTRPG) players with professional Game Masters for systems including Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, Starfinder, Warhammer, and many more. Players discover, book, and join online sessions filtered by system, platform, genre, playstyle, and GM reviews, while Game Masters build careers by hosting paid games across virtual tabletops. The platform also offers gift cards, learn-to-play one-shots for beginners, kids' games, and corporate team-building events. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a consumer web product with no public developer API.

providers.name: Tealet
providers.description: Tealet is a wholesale tea marketplace that connects independent tea growers and family farms directly with retailers and businesses. Buyers browse, trace, and order specialty teas sourced from family farms and cooperatives across 8 countries and 15 growing regions, with grower profiles, farm videos, subscription ordering, and a wholesale request flow that emphasize transparency and direct trade from source to cup. Tealet originated in Hawaii and is backed by 500 Startups and Blue Startups. The company operates a consumer/B2B web storefront with account sign-up, newsletter, and blog; it does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or an MCP server.

providers.name: The Meta
providers.description: The Meta is the gaming-performance company behind KovaaK's Aim Trainer (formerly "Kovaak 2.0: The Meta"), a PC esports training platform distributed on Steam that pairs guided, skill-specific training modules with Kovaak's Sandbox aim trainer and its library of 2,600+ user-generated scenarios. The platform lets FPS players measure, diagnose, and improve their mechanical aim and in-game habits, feeding back insights on weaknesses so players can target their practice. Founded by Duncan Haberly, Jay Brown, and Chris Olson and backed by Canaan (Beta Fund), Village Global, Courtside VC, betaworks, GFR, and Akatsuki Entertainment Technology (AET Fund). The Meta operates a consumer game product, a community wiki, and a Discord community; it does not currently publish a public first-party developer API.

providers.name: Tigerconnect
providers.description: TigerConnect is a healthcare clinical communication and collaboration (CC&C) platform used by 7,000+ healthcare organizations to unify secure messaging, clinical collaboration, alarm management, physician and nurse scheduling, patient engagement, nurse call, and pre-hospital care-team coordination on one activation layer. It integrates with 200+ medical devices and EHR systems and adds an AI orchestration engine (CareConduit) that routes alerts and workflows to the right clinical role at the right time. TigerConnect is recognized as a leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Clinical Communications and Collaboration. The company publishes end-user product release notes, an SLA, and legal terms, but exposes no public developer API portal or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Topia
providers.description: Topia is a global mobility platform for distributed workforces, used by HR, Finance and Legal teams at mid-market and enterprise companies to manage international assignments, relocations, business travel, remote work and cross-border compliance across 190+ countries in a single system. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in the United States, with additional offices in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Estonia, Topia spans global talent mobility, a tax and compliance engine, cost estimation and tracking, global workforce planning, cost and immigration risk management, and business travel. In April 2026 Topia launched Horizon, an agentic AI workspace for mobility teams that the company describes as built natively into MCP (Model Context Protocol) environments. Topia integrates with HRIS, payroll, travel and expense systems including Workday (a Workday Approved Integration), SAP, ADP, Oracle, Ceridian, SAP Concur and BCD Travel. Topia publishes an llms.txt at its marketing host, but no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; the support center sits behind a customer login.

providers.name: Trelora
providers.description: Trelora is a technology-driven, full-service discount real estate brokerage founded in Denver, Colorado and now operating as part of HomeSmart. It lets people buy and sell homes for a low, transparent fee instead of the traditional percentage-based commission, helping sellers save thousands of dollars and offering buyers cash-back rebates of up to several thousand dollars at closing. Trelora pairs salaried, non-commissioned real estate agents with an online platform and IDX-powered property search across markets including Colorado, Washington, and other U.S. states, and publishes a real estate blog, glossary, and city-level market reports. Originally a Techstars-backed startup, Trelora is consumer-facing and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Tripitaca, Inc.
providers.description: Tripitaca is a Kenya-based travel and hospitality booking marketplace where travelers get the best deals when they travel and where property owners list their properties. The platform lets travelers receive offers from hosts and hotels, while hosts create curated packages and special offers, see travelers interested in their area, and make them offers. Coverage spans destinations including Nairobi, Mombasa, Nakuru, Kisumu, and Maasai Mara safari experiences. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Truemeds
providers.description: Truemeds is an India-based online pharmacy and digital healthcare platform operated by Intellihealth Solutions that lets consumers order branded and generic prescription and over-the-counter medicines for home delivery across India, typically positioned around savings on genuine medicines, free teleconsultation with doctors, and substitute-medicine recommendations. It runs a consumer web and mobile app experience (order medicines, upload prescriptions, health blog, help center) rather than a public developer API program; no public API documentation, developer portal, OpenAPI, or partner API surface was found during enrichment. Backed by Accel and other investors, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Tungee
providers.description: Tungee (Guangzhou Tungee Technology Co., Ltd., 探迹科技) is a Chinese AI sales-intelligence company backed by Qiming Venture Partners. Its Tungee AI Sales Cloud covers the full B2B sales cycle -- AI prospecting over a 300M+ company knowledge graph, inbound capture, outreach via call center, SMS, and email, and an AI CRM -- plus a Sales GPT agent line, a mobile app, and a DingTalk edition. The group also operates Futern, an international B2B leads product, and reports 50,000+ customers. Tungee publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Twelve
providers.description: Twelve is a carbon transformation company that converts CO2, water, and renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals that serve as drop-in replacements for petroleum-based products. Its proprietary eManufacturing technology powers AirPlant One in Moses Lake, Washington, which produces E-Jet sustainable aviation fuel and E-Naphtha, while its eMade program partners with consumer brands on CO2-made materials. Investors include TPG, DCVC, Microsoft, Carbon Direct, Breakout Ventures, and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Twelve publishes no public developer API, but its Wix-hosted site exposes an llms.txt and a live site MCP endpoint for agentic access.

providers.name: Uhnder
providers.description: Uhnder is an Austin, Texas fabless semiconductor company founded in 2015 that designs the S80 and S81 77 GHz 4D digital imaging Radar-on-Chip (RoC) for automotive ADAS and automated mobility. Its Digital Code Modulation (DCM) approach on a 28nm RF CMOS process replaces analog FMCW radar with a software-defined sensor, and each RoC ships with an ASPICE-qualified Software Development Kit carrying ready-to-integrate software APIs, on-chip user algorithm support and system tools for Tier-1 and OEM radar stacks. Uhnder is a chip supplier rather than a web-API provider: the SDK and its APIs are embedded interfaces delivered under a commercial customer relationship, and the company publishes no public developer portal, documentation host or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Umrahme
providers.description: Umrahme is a consumer online travel platform from the Traveazy Group focused on the Umrah pilgrimage, letting pilgrims across the GCC, UK, US, Europe, and Egypt book complete Umrah packages as well as individual hotels in Makkah and Madinah, Haramain high-speed train tickets, ground transfers, holiday add-ons, and travel eSIMs. The company is an Accel portfolio company and operates a companion B2B portal for travel agents, mobile apps on iOS and Android, and a travel-guide blog, but publishes no public developer or API program.

providers.name: Urbia
providers.description: Urbia is a German online community and content platform for parents and families, covering fertility, pregnancy, birth, babies, and family life through expert-written magazine articles, active discussion forums, and planning tools. Founded in Cologne in 1998 and backed early by Earlybird Venture Capital, urbia.de is today part of the ELTERN family of parenting brands, operated by Funke Women, People & Family GmbH in Hamburg. Urbia does not publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: User1st
providers.description: User1st is a web and mobile digital accessibility company whose U1 Suite gives organizations an efficient path to WCAG, ADA, and European Accessibility Act (EAA) compliance. It provides accessibility toolkits and remediation across web frameworks (JavaScript/TypeScript, React, Angular, Vue, WordPress, Shopify) and mobile platforms (iOS Native, Android Native, React Native, Flutter), plus a free accessibility scanner and GenAI-assisted code-fixing and image-description tooling. Trusted by organizations including Amtrak, Fannie Mae, IKEA, iRobot, T-Mobile, Santander, Mount Sinai, and the City of New York. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the product backend is an internal SaaS API with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Varagesale
providers.description: VarageSale is a community-based online marketplace for buying and selling used items locally, founded in 2012 by Montreal teacher Tami Zuckerman and programmer Carl Mercier and headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Members join a local community, verify their identity, and buy and sell with verified neighbors through native iOS and Android apps and the web, with communities across North America and beyond. Backed by Sequoia Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners, VarageSale was acquired by VerticalScope in 2017, with online auction company MaxSold assuming operational control in early 2026. It is a direct-to-consumer marketplace and does not publish a public developer API, so this record captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: VOO (now SideUp)
providers.description: VOO was an Egyptian logistics marketplace that rebranded as SideUp in December 2022, relocating its headquarters to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. SideUp is a fully integrated courier marketplace that lets e-commerce businesses ship locally and globally from one dashboard, connecting merchants with multiple courier services alongside payment gateways, shipping API integration, warehousing, and fulfillment, with plugins for Shopify, Salla, and OpenCart. Backed by 500 Global, Launch Africa VC, Riyadh Angels, and Alex Angels ($1.2M seed). No public developer portal or API documentation is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: Vymo
providers.description: Vymo is a sales-engagement and distribution-management platform for financial institutions — banks, insurers, and asset managers — helping field sales and collections teams manage leads, allocate and prioritize activities, and capture engagement in a mobile-first app. It layers AI-driven nudges, activity capture, and analytics on top of CRM and core systems, and integrates with existing enterprise ecosystems. Vymo does not publish a self-serve public developer API or documentation portal; its integrations are delivered through enterprise/partner connections. Backed by Emergence Capital and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

providers.name: Wallet Studio
providers.description: Wallet Studio, built by Miss Moneypenny Technologies GmbH, is a no-code SaaS platform for creating, deploying, and managing Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes. Aimed primarily at insurance carriers, it turns policy administration, claims, and CRM systems into wallet-based customer engagement channels reaching the four billion people who already carry a digital wallet, without replacing existing backend infrastructure. The platform offers visual pass editors with one-click publishing, prebuilt insurance templates, integrated automation, a REST API and webhooks for connecting to third-party systems, and authenticated links to portals and value-added services. Hosting is GDPR-compliant and the company describes the platform as certified for enterprise security standards. Backed by Earlybird, the company raised roughly EUR 7 million in 2025. There is no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; the REST API is provisioned per customer.

providers.name: Weee
providers.description: Weee! is America's largest online Asian grocery store and delivery platform, operating as a direct-to-consumer online supermarket serving major metropolitan areas across the United States. It curates and fulfills inventory through regional distribution centers and cold-chain logistics, bringing together products and ingredients commonly found in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai, Filipino, and Indian supermarkets. The storefront spans fresh produce, frozen meats, seafood, pantry staples, snacks, sauces, hot pot ingredients, beverages, and household essentials, accepts EBT/SNAP in eligible cities, and runs a multilingual experience (English, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese, Thai). Weee is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this profile Weee publishes no public developer API; this record captures its public web identity and AI-indexing (llms.txt) surface.

providers.name: Xh
providers.description: xh is a friendly and fast command-line HTTP client written in Rust, designed as a modern, high-performance alternative to HTTPie. It reimplements HTTPie's request-item syntax and design with improved startup speed, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support, and availability as a single statically-linked binary. xh supports JSON and form data serialization, session management, authentication (basic, bearer, digest), SSL/TLS customization, multipart uploads, proxy configuration, and built-in curl command translation. Installable via Homebrew, Cargo, apt, pacman, and other package managers.

providers.name: XP Health
providers.description: XP Health is an AI-powered vision benefits platform that modernizes employer vision programs with full-replacement and dual-option plans designed to reduce employee out-of-pocket eyewear costs. The platform serves more than 6,300 organizations, offering in-app prescription renewals, virtual try-on across 5,000+ eyewear styles, and a provider network reaching 90% of the U.S. population, with members saving an average of 69% on eyewear claims. Backed by QED Investors. XP Health does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: 10% Happier
providers.description: 10% Happier (now branded Happier Meditation) is a consumer meditation and mindfulness app founded on the best-selling book "10% Happier" by ABC News anchor Dan Harris. The service delivers personalized, science-backed guided meditations, courses, and sleep content from well-known teachers through native iOS and Android apps and a web player, aimed at helping skeptics and busy people build a sustainable mindfulness practice for stress, sleep, focus, and relationships. It operates on a subscription model. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; 10% Happier is a direct-to-consumer app and does not publish a public developer API, so this record captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: 82 Labs
providers.description: 82 Labs, Inc. (doing business as More Labs) is a Los Angeles-based, science-backed wellness beverage company founded in 2016 by former Tesla engineer Sisun Lee. More Labs makes functional drink supplements sold direct-to-consumer, including Morning Recovery (hydration and post-alcohol recovery with electrolytes and DHM), Liquid Focus (a nootropic caffeine energy shot), and Dream Well (a melatonin and lemon-balm sleep aid). It is a consumer packaged goods (CPG) and e-commerce business with no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; it was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Enrichment on 2026-07-17 confirmed no API surface exists to harvest.

providers.name: Aaptiv
providers.description: Aaptiv is a digital fitness and wellness platform offering 10,000+ on-demand audio and video workout classes, AI-powered coaching, access to a network of gyms and studios, and wellness resources such as meditation and mindfulness. It is sold to employers as an employee benefit, to health plans, and to individuals seeking personalized fitness. Backed by Insight Partners. Aaptiv publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, support, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: ACV Auctions
providers.description: ACV Auctions is a digital wholesale marketplace for the automotive industry, operating the leading online platform for dealer-to-dealer used-vehicle auctions across the United States. Franchise and independent dealers source and sell inventory through daily online auctions backed by third-party vehicle inspections, detailed condition reports, and the company's data and analytics products. ACV also offers complementary services including vehicle transportation, dealer floor-plan financing through ACV Capital, and inventory-management and pricing tools. The company is publicly traded and headquartered in Buffalo, New York. It does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Agebold
providers.description: Agebold, which operates as Bold, is a digital healthy-aging platform for adults 65 and older, delivered as a covered benefit through Medicare Advantage plans and other Medicare organizations. Bold offers personalized, science-backed exercise programs shown to reduce fall risk, ease musculoskeletal pain, and increase physical activity, alongside nutrition and weight-loss support (including GLP-1 care), live classes, expert talks, and virtual access to doctors, therapists, and nurse practitioners in select states. The company partners with health plans to improve quality measures, Star Ratings, HOS performance, and total cost of care. Agebold is a Khosla Ventures portfolio company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Air Doctor
providers.description: Air Doctor is a digital health platform that connects travelers and people living abroad with a global network of vetted private doctors and specialists, offering in-person clinic visits, home visits, and telemedicine appointments in multiple languages across more than 75 countries. Users search for and book local doctors through the Air Doctor mobile app and web app, and the company operates a large B2B business embedding its provider network into travel insurance, assistance, and health-plan partners (including brands such as Allianz Global Assistance, ERGO, World Nomads, and Charles Taylor). Air Doctor is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, partner, and web surface; Air Doctor does not publish a public API or developer portal at this time, so this profile is maintained as an identity and web-property record.

providers.name: Albert
providers.description: Albert Invent (Albert Invent Corp.) builds an AI-native operating system for chemistry and materials R&D, giving scientists a unified platform for electronic lab notebooks, chemical drawing, experiment and formulation management, and machine-learning models trained on millions of molecular structures. The platform centralizes fragmented R&D data and workflows for teams inventing new materials across adhesives, coatings, batteries, and life sciences, with role-based access control and regulatory compliance coverage across hundreds of thousands of chemical substances. Albert Invent does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation (its docs surface is password-protected); this profile captures the company's public web, product, legal, and domain-security surface as a lead awaiting a public API. Headquartered in Oakland, California.

providers.name: Aletiq
providers.description: Aletiq is a French software company building a next-generation, AI-powered Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Product Data Management (PDM) platform for regulated manufacturers. The platform centralizes technical data (CAD files, drawings, bills of materials, configurations, and work instructions), enforces traceability and regulatory compliance, and automates business processes such as approvals, engineering change management, and project milestones. Aletiq emphasizes rapid deployment and high adoption across operational teams, and integrates with major CAD tools (SolidWorks, CATIA, Autodesk Inventor, Siemens NX, Creo) and ERP systems (SAP, Sage, Cegid, Infor, Odoo) via connectors and a custom-integration API. It serves aerospace and defense, medical devices, energy, electronics, automotive, and luxury-goods industries. Aletiq is backed by Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile.

providers.name: AmplifyMD
providers.description: AmplifyMD is a virtual care platform for hospitals and health systems, providing a nationwide network of remote specialists across more than 15 essential fields. It powers telemedicine across emergent, inpatient, asynchronous, SNF/LTAC, virtual clinic, and direct-to-patient care models, and integrates with major EHR systems including Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, TruBridge, and MedHost to help organizations build sustainable clinical staffing models. Backed by Forerunner Ventures.

providers.name: Andela
providers.description: Andela is a global talent platform and AI services provider founded in 2014 by Jeremy Johnson, connecting enterprises with vetted, remote technologists and AI engineers across 135+ countries. It grew into a unicorn (valued at $1.5B in 2021) serving 650+ clients, with a network of 200,000+ trained technologists. Its services span hiring AI engineers for application building, systems integration, and platform engineering; building enterprise AI solutions from data readiness to production deployment; and upskilling teams through AI curricula developed with partners such as NVIDIA and Google. Andela operates a fully remote model and is backed by GV, SoftBank Vision Fund, and Susa Ventures. It publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: appearhere
providers.description: Appear Here is the leading online marketplace for short-term retail space, connecting property owners with brands, designers, and entrepreneurs who want to rent shops, pop-up stores, market stalls, showrooms, and event venues on a flexible, short-term basis. Founded in London in 2014 and backed by Balderton Capital, the two-sided marketplace lets tenants search available space by city and date, book securely online with standardized legal agreements, and message landlords directly, while landlords list and monetize idle retail units. Appear Here operates across the UK, US, and France and has facilitated the opening of more than 10,000 stores for over 250,000 brands and creative entrepreneurs. Appear Here does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its public web, brand, and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Applied Compute
providers.description: Applied Compute is a San Francisco AI company founded in 2025 by former OpenAI researchers, building "Specific Intelligence" for the enterprise. It operates a cloud platform for training, inference, and continuous improvement of custom, open AI models and long-horizon, tool-using agents grounded in a company's own proprietary data. Rather than selling a generic model, Applied Compute embeds engineers with customer teams to fine-tune models, mine production data, run online/reinforcement learning, and deploy autonomous agents that operate inside the customer's environment with observability over rollouts.
