Its software surface (the Revivn App at app.revivn.com) lets IT and asset-management teams schedule retrievals, track chain-of-custody, generate compliance and sustainability reporting, and — per Revivn's marketing — integrate Revivn's API with their IT software stack for customized workflows. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK is published; the integration API appears to be a private, enterprise-only surface. Revivn is a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Rezilient Health
providers.description: Rezilient Health is an employer-sponsored primary and specialty care provider that combines physical CloudClinics with telehealth to deliver unlimited, zero-cost care to employees on behalf of employers, health plans, health systems, and brokers. Its hybrid CloudClinic model pairs on-site medical staff with remote physicians and connected diagnostic equipment so members can access in-person and virtual visits, with the goal of lowering total healthcare spend and improving clinical outcomes. Rezilient offers patient-facing web and mobile apps for scheduling and care, but publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that Rezilient operates a consumer/enterprise healthcare service rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: RockFi
providers.description: RockFi is a French private wealth management firm positioning itself as a modern family office, pairing experienced private-banking advisors with technology to serve high-net-worth entrepreneurs, executives, athletes, and independent professionals. Its fixed-fee model offers life insurance (France and Luxembourg), structured funds, private equity, SCPI real estate, PEA and securities accounts, customized investment mandates, and consolidated real-time portfolio monitoring, tax optimization, and wealth-transmission planning. Registered with ORIAS (23004556) under ACPR and AMF oversight. Backed by Partech. No public developer API is currently published; this profile has been enriched from the public site.

providers.name: roli
providers.description: ROLI (Luminary ROLI Ltd.) is a British music-technology company known for expressive electronic instruments — the Seaboard, LUMI Keys keyboards, and the modular BLOCKS system — together with companion software such as ROLI Dashboard, ROLI Connect, Equator, and ROLI Learn. Its instruments pioneer MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression) for per-note pitch, timbre, and dynamics control. For developers, ROLI publishes first-party SDKs under the github.com/weareroli organization — the C++ BLOCKS-SDK and roli_blocks_basics for building applications that talk to BLOCKS hardware, and the archived mpejs library for MPE MIDI in the browser. ROLI is backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with real developer, SDK, and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: SafelyYou
providers.description: SafelyYou is an ambient-AI platform for senior living communities that reduces falls, reveals resident risk, and surfaces operational and staffing insights without requiring residents to wear devices. Its computer-vision system detects and reviews fall incidents, and the broader product suite spans Safety AI for fall detection, Staffing AI for labor allocation and care tracking, Wellness AI for resident well-being, the Halo next-generation eCall system, and Guardian hardware sensors. SafelyYou reports serving over 1,000 communities and 50,000 residents, with outcomes including roughly 45% fall reduction and longer length of stay. The company integrates with senior-living EHR and eCall systems (Yardi, ALIS, PointClickCare and others) and offers SSO, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Salvo Health
providers.description: Salvo Health is a virtual care company delivering continuous gastrointestinal and metabolic care through integrated, tech-enabled clinical teams. Its platform pairs registered dietitians, licensed nurses, and behavioral health specialists with a patient mobile app and remote patient monitoring to manage conditions including IBS, obesity, GLP-1/anti-obesity therapy, and fatty liver disease (MASH/MASLD). Adherence data and monthly patient reports are integrated directly into provider EHR systems. Salvo Health is a portfolio company of Threshold Ventures. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Season Health
providers.description: Season Health is a food-as-medicine platform that helps people living with chronic conditions eat well and live well. It connects patients with registered dietitians, personalized nutrition and meal plans, and medically-tailored groceries and meals, and works with health plans and care providers to deliver nutrition care as a covered benefit. The consumer and provider experiences run through app.seasonhealth.com; the company is a HIPAA-covered digital health service. Season Health is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs — api.seasonhealth.com is a private application backend — so this profile captures the company's real public web properties rather than an API program.

providers.name: Sira Medical
providers.description: Sira Medical develops augmented reality software that transforms 3D radiological imaging into patient-specific holographic models projected onto real-world backgrounds. Delivered through head-mounted AR devices (such as Microsoft HoloLens) and mobile platforms, the technology helps surgeons perform preoperative planning with greater confidence, clinicians educate patients with understandable visualizations, medical schools train students on patient-specific anatomy, and medical-device makers design and validate implants. The company is backed by 500 Global, Eileses Capital, UCSF Innovation Ventures, and Microsoft for Startups. Sira Medical operates as a clinical AR software vendor and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Solace Health
providers.description: Solace Health (solace.health) is a US healthcare navigation and patient-advocacy platform that matches patients and family caregivers with dedicated advocates, many covered by insurance, to handle administrative tasks, coordinate care and referrals, and fight for approvals and treatments. Advocates support members by video, phone, text, and email nationwide across a range of insurance plans, with a member app at app.solace.health. The company is venture-backed (IVP among its investors). As of this enrichment pass, Solace publishes a patient-facing service only and exposes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Spredfast
providers.description: Spredfast was an Austin-based social media marketing and management platform providing social publishing, engagement, listening, and analytics for enterprise brands and agencies. Backed by Battery Ventures, Spredfast merged with Lithium Technologies in 2018; the combined company rebranded as Khoros in 2019, and the Spredfast product line is now delivered as Khoros Marketing. Its developer API surface — the Conversations API, Publishing API, Analytics Reporting API, Notification API, and CRM API — is documented today under the Khoros developer center at developer.khoros.com, secured with OAuth 2.0. The legacy api.spredfast.com host still resolves, while the original devcenter.spredfast.com developer portal is no longer maintained.

providers.name: Sunnyside
providers.description: Sunnyside is a digital health platform for alcohol moderation, founded in 2020, that helps members cut back on or quit drinking through personalized weekly plans, drink tracking and analytics, human text-based coaching, habit-building exercises, and a supportive community. Its separate Sunnyside Med telehealth service connects members with licensed providers who can prescribe compounded naltrexone. Sunnyside is a consumer mobile app and telehealth service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Synapticure
providers.description: Synapticure is a virtual-first telehealth company delivering comprehensive, specialist neurology care for people living with neurodegenerative and complex neurological conditions, including ALS/PLS, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, dementia, Huntington's, and multiple sclerosis. Founded in 2021 by ALS patient Brian Wallach and caregiver Sandra Abrevaya, the company integrates 24/7 access to neurologists, behavioral health (psychiatry and therapy), care coordination, genetic testing, clinical-trial navigation, and insurance support into a single virtual care experience available in all 50 states and covered by most insurance. It is accredited by The Joint Commission and maintains AICPA SOC 2 compliance. Synapticure operates as a healthcare provider and does not publish a public developer program or API; this profile was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and enriched with real, published identity and security signals.

providers.name: TandemAI
providers.description: TandemAI is an integrated drug discovery contract research organization (CRO) that combines proprietary AI and physics-based computational methods with in-house high-performance computing and extensive wet-lab operations to accelerate pharmaceutical research. Its cloud-enabled, data-centric, browser-based platform, TandemViz, spans hit finding, hit-to-lead and lead optimization, digital assays and workflows, medicinal chemistry and synthesis, biological assays, and a peptide platform. TandemAI is offered as an FTE-based service model that bundles wet-lab services with complimentary access to its AI and computational tools, or as a stand-alone SaaS software license. The company merged with Perpetual Medicines and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Tangerine
providers.description: Tangerine is a Canadian direct (branchless) bank headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and a federally regulated Schedule I bank chartered as Tangerine Bank (institution number 614). Founded in 1997 as ING Direct Canada, it was acquired by Scotiabank in 2012 and rebranded as Tangerine in 2014; it remains a separate legal entity operating as Scotiabank's digital-banking arm, serving roughly two million clients with no-fee chequing and savings accounts, GICs, mortgages, mutual funds, and a cash-back Mastercard delivered entirely through mobile and web. On API and open-finance posture, Tangerine publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; Canada has no operational consumer-driven-banking mandate yet (the federal framework is legislated but not live), so third-party access to Tangerine account and transaction data today is aggregator-based via Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard) rather than through a documented first-party API.

providers.name: Tend
providers.description: Tend (Tend Dental) is a consumer dental-care company offering modern, judgment-free dentistry through a network of design-forward "studios" across New York City, Boston, Atlanta, Washington DC, Nashville and Connecticut. The brand pairs a soothing in-person studio experience and top-rated dentists with a fully online booking and patient-intake flow at hellotend.com. Services span preventive hygiene, family dental care, cosmetic dentistry, veneers, Invisalign and clear aligners, orthodontics, dental implants, endodontics, sedation and emergency care. Backed by GV and Redpoint Ventures. This is a consumer web/ booking business with no public developer API surface; the profile is enriched with identity, security-posture and discovery-probe artifacts only.

providers.name: Thruster
providers.description: Thruster was a yield-first decentralized exchange (DEX) built natively on the Blast Ethereum Layer 2, offering Uniswap-style v2 and v3 concentrated liquidity AMMs, a stableswap AMM, and a token launchpad. Backed by Pantera Capital, the protocol shut down on July 29, 2025 after completing THRUST holder redemptions; its thruster.finance website is offline, while the GitBook documentation and the ThrusterX GitHub organization (Solidity contracts and audit reports) remain the surviving public record. No REST/HTTP API was published; the developer surface was on-chain smart contracts on Blast.

providers.name: Tutor Intelligence
providers.description: Tutor Intelligence builds AI-powered robotic workers for industrial and logistics operations, delivered as robots-as-a-service. Its flagship Cassie palletizing robot handles material-handling tasks — palletizing, depalletizing, and case picking — in warehouses and factories without facility retrofits, and a humanoid robot, Sonny, is slated for late 2026. The company pairs on-robot autonomy with a human-in-the-loop teleoperation and data model, priced per robot-hour with no long-term contracts, and is backed by Union Square Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is published as of this profiling; the company's public GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and open-source forks rather than a first-party product API.

providers.name: Verisian
providers.description: Verisian is an AI infrastructure platform for clinical trials, giving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs the information infrastructure required to deploy AI across their experts and processes. The platform provides full study traceability and automates statistical programming workflows: automating the validation of SDTM and ADaM analysis datasets (turning time-consuming QC double-programming into value-generating QA oversight), and generating complete define-XML files and draft reviewer's guides that are guaranteed consistent with the underlying analysis, so teams are submission-ready in hours. Verisian is cloud native, compatible with any statistical computing environment (SCE), storage, or compute, and integrates through simple file transfer with no complex API integration required. It serves statistical programmers, statisticians, data managers, medical writers, clinicians, and regulatory teams across in-house and CRO-outsourced operating models; Bayer is a named customer. There is no public developer API surface — the product is an enterprise application (app.verisian.com) accessed after sales onboarding.

providers.name: VetSource
providers.description: VetSource is a veterinary technology and pharmacy company founded in 2008 that delivers a suite of pharmacy, technology, and business services for the pet health industry. Its offerings span home-delivery prescription management (an online pharmacy and prescription workflow that lets veterinary practices prescribe and fulfill medications with compliance and revenue tools), the Vet2Pet client-engagement platform (a custom-branded app connecting practices with pet owners for communication, reminders, loyalty, and telehealth), and data/analytics services that provide industry benchmarking and practice performance insights. VetSource serves veterinary practices and pet owners across North America. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: WeiMai
providers.description: WeiMai (微脉) is a Chinese healthcare technology company operated by Choice Technology Inc. and headquartered in Hangzhou. It runs an internet-based medical services marketplace and licensed internet hospitals (including Hainan WeiMai Internet Hospital) that connect patients with doctors for online consultation, pharmaceutical products, medical devices, and health-management service packages, delivered primarily through the WeiMai consumer mobile app. WeiMai also operates a partner-facing Open Platform (微脉开发平台) at openapi.myweimai.com that exposes a Swagger 2.0 API surface for approved integrators; the public specification is a minimal stub with no operations exposed without partner credentials. The company is backed by IDG Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company.

providers.name: Xamarin
providers.description: Xamarin was the San Francisco company behind the Mono-based cross-platform mobile development framework, letting developers build native iOS, Android, and Mac apps from a single C#/.NET codebase. Backed by investors including Insight Partners, it was acquired by Microsoft in 2016. Microsoft retired the Xamarin SDKs on May 1, 2024, with Xamarin.Forms succeeded by .NET MAUI. Xamarin shipped developer tooling and SDK packages rather than a public web API; its NuGet packages, docs, and GitHub organization remain its primary artifacts.

providers.name: Yoona.ai
providers.description: Yoona.ai is an enterprise agentic-AI platform for product innovation, originally built for the fashion industry. It creates an adaptive "Enterprise Twin" of a brand by connecting PLM, ERP, e-commerce and market data into a single intelligence layer, then uses AI agents to autonomously generate product designs, optimize assortments and validate sell-through. Capabilities include text-to-image and sketch-to-design generation, trend and data analysis, and a Sales Confidence Algorithm. Integration with a customer's stack (Shopify to SAP) is offered via a flexible REST/GraphQL API, but that API is delivered as an Enterprise-tier custom integration — there is no public self-serve API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification published as of this enrichment pass. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Zehitomo
providers.description: Zehitomo is a Tokyo-based online marketplace that matches consumers in Japan with local professionals across hundreds of service categories — including photographers, personal trainers, house cleaners, graphic and web designers, videographers, tax accountants, interpreters, construction and repair trades, and business consultants. Clients describe the job they need done and receive quotes and proposals from vetted local pros, while professionals pay to respond to matched leads. Founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, Zehitomo runs a consumer-facing web and mobile product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: ZOE
providers.description: ZOE (joinzoe.com, canonically zoe.com) is a personalized nutrition and health science company founded on data from one of the largest nutrition research studies in the world. Its membership program pairs at-home testing (gut health, blood sugar, and blood fat responses) with an AI-powered app that scores meals, tracks personal food responses, and delivers science-backed dietary guidance. ZOE also sells consumer products including the Daily30+ whole-food supplement and Gut Health products, and publishes the ZOE Science & Nutrition podcast. The company operates as a direct-to-consumer health brand rather than an API provider, and is tracked here as a Balderton Capital portfolio company; it currently exposes no public developer platform, API, or developer portal.

providers.name: AirPR
providers.description: AirPR is a public relations analytics and media measurement company whose software helped communications teams quantify the business impact of earned media, tie coverage to web traffic and conversions, and benchmark share of voice against competitors. AirPR is now part of Onclusive, the media intelligence platform that monitors and enriches conversations across 3M+ online sources, 70K+ print outlets, 6K+ broadcast channels, and 25+ social platforms for PR, communications, and marketing professionals. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Altara
providers.description: Altara is a deep-tech AI company (seed-stage, $7M, backed by Greylock and Jeff Dean) building an agentic scientific intelligence platform for the physical sciences. Its AI agents reason across fragmented technical data — sensor and instrument time series, wafer maps, inspection images, and experimental records — to accelerate R&D-through-manufacturing workflows such as experimental design, yield analysis, anomaly detection, and failure analysis. Altara unifies siloed data in place without migrations, giving agents full operational context across numerical, text, and image sources for semiconductors, advanced materials, batteries, medical devices, specialty chemicals, and industrials. The platform is SOC 2 Type II compliant with encryption, RBAC, SSO, and self-hosted (VPC) or dedicated single-tenant cloud deployment. Altara does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity and security posture as a lead for future enrichment.

providers.name: Archer Aviation
providers.description: Archer Aviation is a U.S. eVTOL aircraft company developing Midnight, a piloted four-passenger all-electric aircraft designed for rapid back-to-back urban flights of roughly 20-50 miles with a ~10 minute charge between trips. Archer is pursuing FAA Type Certification and operates through commercial and defense business lines. Key partnerships include Stellantis (contract manufacturing at Archer's Covington, Georgia facility), United Airlines (launch routes including the Manhattan-Newark corridor), and a Launch Edition program in the United Arab Emirates with Abu Dhabi Aviation. Archer also has a dedicated defense division (Archer Defense) developing hybrid VTOL platforms with Anduril and supporting U.S. government missions. The company trades on the NYSE under ACHR.

providers.name: BabyList
providers.description: Babylist is the leading universal baby registry and a baby-focused commerce and content company for growing families. Because the registry is universal, parents can add any product from any store — including Amazon, Target, and Etsy — to a single list. Babylist has grown into a full ecosystem spanning the Babylist registry, the Babylist Shop, Babylist Health (insurance-covered breast pumps), Babylist Money (family financial planning), expert product guides, and a flagship Los Angeles showroom. More than 10 million people shop with Babylist every year. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network; Babylist runs no public developer API, but it does publish an llms.txt agent surface and an OpenID Connect discovery document.

providers.name: Bariendo Inc.
providers.description: Bariendo Inc. (now operating as Everself) is a science-forward digital health company pioneering non-surgical, endoscopic weight-loss care. Founded in 2023 by Harvard Medical School physicians Dr. Christopher C. Thompson (the inventor of Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty) and Dr. Pichamol Jirapinyo, the company delivers minimally invasive procedures — ESG Stomach Tightening, gastric balloon, and revision of prior bariatric surgery — alongside weight-loss medication and a 12-month concierge care program. Its consumer platform streamlines access to these interventions across a dozen-plus U.S. locations, with financing, telehealth consultations, and ongoing weight tracking. Bariendo/Everself is a consumer and clinical health service; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Beazer Homes USA
providers.description: Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (NYSE: BZH) is an Atlanta, Georgia-headquartered national homebuilder founded in 1985 and publicly listed since 1994. The company designs, sells, and builds single-family and multi-family homes across approximately thirteen U.S. states under brand differentiators such as Choice Plans (customizable floorplans), Mortgage Choice (competitive lender program), Style Choice (interior personalization), and Livable Features (accessibility options). Beazer markets itself as "America's #1 Energy-Efficient Homebuilder," citing homes that are 44% more efficient than the average HERS-rated new home and shipping whole-house ERV ventilation in 100% of homes. As of the most recent public data point (FY2016 10-K), Beazer reported revenue of $1.822B, delivered 5,419 homes, operated 161 active communities, and employed approximately 1,100 people. The company has no public developer program or external APIs; its digital surface is a consumer-facing marketing/community-finder website plus an investor relations portal.

providers.name: Better Life Partners
providers.description: Better Life Partners is a Hanover, New Hampshire healthcare provider founded in 2018 that delivers same-day, whole-person treatment for opioid and alcohol use disorder across New Hampshire, Maine, Massachusetts, Vermont and North Carolina. It combines FDA-approved medication for addiction treatment (buprenorphine/Suboxone, naltrexone) with group counseling, peer recovery coaching and mental health care, delivered both virtually and in person, on a non-punitive harm-reduction model. The company contracts directly with Medicaid, Medicare and commercial health plans — MaineCare, NH Healthy Families, Anthem, Cigna, Harvard Pilgrim, Tufts, Humana and UnitedHealthcare — and markets value-based arrangements "from bundles to full risk" to payers and community partners. It is a clinical services organization rather than a software vendor: it references "purpose-built technology" internally but publishes no developer program, API, specification, SDK or integration documentation of any kind.

providers.name: Bit.bio
providers.description: bit.bio is a Cambridge, UK synthetic biology company founded in 2016 by stem cell biologist and neurosurgeon Mark Kotter, headquartered at the Babraham Research Campus with a second site in San Francisco and a discovery subsidiary (bit.bio discovery GmbH) in Vienna. Its proprietary opti-ox cell coding technology uses a dual genomic safe harbour approach to deterministically reprogram human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) into defined, consistent human cell types at industrial scale. The company sells these as ioCells — ioWild Type Cells, ioDisease Model Cells and CRISPR-Ready ioCells covering neurons, microglia, hepatocytes, glial and muscle lineages — plus custom iPSC-derived cell development and expert-led CRISPR functional genomics screening services for research, drug discovery and cell therapy. Products are sold as physical cell vials through a web storefront and a distributor network; bit.bio publishes no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
providers.description: ATF is a law enforcement agency in the United States Department of Justice that protects communities from violent criminals, criminal organizations, the illegal use and trafficking of firearms, the illegal use and storage of explosives, acts of arson and bombings, acts of terrorism, and the illegal diversion of alcohol and tobacco products. ATF publishes firearms trace data, crime statistics, and regulatory information.

providers.name: City Block
providers.description: Cityblock Health is a value-based healthcare provider delivering integrated primary care, behavioral health, and social-services support to Medicaid and lower-income (dual-eligible) Medicare populations across multiple U.S. markets. Cityblock pairs community-based care teams with a proprietary care-delivery technology platform to coordinate wraparound care for historically underserved communities. The company is backed by 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio profile; it operates as a care provider and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: coachhub
providers.description: CoachHub is a global digital coaching platform (headquartered in Berlin) that lets enterprises deliver scalable, measurable one-to-one coaching to their entire workforce through web and mobile apps. Its network spans 3,500+ certified business coaches across 90+ countries with sessions in 80+ languages, matched to learners via AI, and it ships an AI coaching companion (AIMY). CoachHub serves 1,000+ enterprise clients and is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Sofina, HV Capital, Partech and Speedinvest. It offers an account-managed integration approach (SSO, automated provisioning and data sync) with HR/LMS systems such as Workday, SAP, Oracle, Ceridian and Microsoft Teams, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs or GitHub repositories. The platform is ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2 Type II, TISAX and PCI DSS Level 1 certified and GDPR/CCPA compliant.

providers.name: Cogent
providers.description: Cogent Security is an AI-driven vulnerability management platform whose AI agents discover, assess, remediate, and report on software vulnerabilities at machine speed, before attackers can exploit them. The platform spans the CTEM (Continuous Threat Exposure Management) lifecycle: Discover identifies vulnerable software quickly after disclosures, Assess risk-scores and prioritizes remediation, Remediate applies automated and assisted fixes, and Report produces evidence-backed documentation of risk reduction. It is powered by the Cogent AI Engine and Cogent Research with published safety guardrails and defined autonomy levels. Cogent is a venture-backed security company (Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock). Cogent publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its public web, security, and trust surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Compstak
providers.description: CompStak is a commercial real estate (CRE) data platform, founded in 2012, that crowdsources and verifies lease comps, sale comps, loan data, and property data from a network of tens of thousands of brokers and appraisers across US markets. Its products include CompStak One (an all-in-one CRE data platform), CompStak Exchange, CompStak AI, and a contact-sales Data API offering Market Insights, Property Insights, Space Insights, and Property Standardization. CompStak was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Its developer surface is enterprise/contact-sales only — there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or API reference.

providers.name: Convey
providers.description: Convey is an enterprise AI platform for building and running autonomous "digital teammates" — AI workers that non-technical operators train by describing a workflow or sharing their screen, after which the teammate runs business processes end to end across existing enterprise systems (Salesforce, NetSuite, ad operations, reporting) with role-based access, isolated agent identities, dedicated credentials, audit logs, and escalation to a human on high-stakes decisions. Founded by former DoorDash and project44 engineers, Convey raised a $38M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in June 2026 (with Khosla Ventures and Pear VC) and reports 1.1M+ hours of work completed for customers including NBCUniversal, TelevisaUnivision, Unity, and Samsara. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. Convey is an enterprise, contact-sales product with no public developer API or documentation surface as of this profile.

providers.name: DecisionLink
providers.description: DecisionLink pioneered enterprise Customer Value Management (CVM), giving B2B sales, marketing, and customer-success teams a platform to quantify, present, and defend the economic value their products deliver to buyers. The company has since rebranded and relaunched as Xfactor.io, a revenue-operations AI platform that builds a "digital twin" of a company's go-to-market system: it unifies CRM, pipeline, usage, and finance signals into Xfactor Central, surfaces cross-source risk through Xfactor OpenInsights with plain-English alerts, and lets teams simulate growth scenarios before committing with Xfactor Simulation and Growth AI. Backed by Accel, the company sells to revenue and go-to-market leaders. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; security posture is published via a SecureFrame trust center (SOC 2 Type II).

providers.name: EdSights
providers.description: EdSights is a student voice and engagement platform for higher education. It pairs an AI-powered SMS chatbot with real-time analytics to collect continuous feedback from students, surface persistence and well-being risk, and flag individuals who need staff intervention. Its Student Voice Score (SVS) benchmarks student satisfaction the way NPS benchmarks customers, and institutional dashboards help retention, advising, and student-success teams act on that feedback throughout the academic journey. EdSights serves 290+ colleges and universities and connects to campus systems — Banner SIS, Slate, Salesforce, Starfish, EAB Navigate360, and Pharos — via SFTP data feeds. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this profile EdSights exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhooks; integration is data-file (SFTP) based, so most API-artifact enrichment is not applicable.

providers.name: eGifter
providers.description: eGifter is a digital gift card platform that allows people to easily send and receive gift cards for a wide variety of retailers and brands. Users can choose from hundreds of options including popular stores, restaurants, and entertainment venues. Whether it's for a birthday, holiday, or just to show appreciation, eGifter makes it simple to find the perfect gift for any occasion.

providers.name: Electric Car Scheme
providers.description: The Electric Car Scheme is a UK B Corp providing electric vehicle salary sacrifice as an employee benefit. Employees lease any electric car of their choice with the monthly cost deducted from gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance, saving 20-50% versus a personal lease, while employers save on Class 1A National Insurance. Packages are all-inclusive (lease, insurance, maintenance, servicing and breakdown) with Complete Protection covering employees who leave partway through a lease term. The company integrates with employer payroll systems via API or SFTP and offers Single Sign-On for employees, plus an included Charge Scheme for charging access.

providers.name: EXIGER
providers.description: Exiger is an AI-native supply chain, third-party, and software supply chain risk and compliance company. Its 1Exiger platform unifies supplier, product, part, component, and risk data into a single system to help organizations map and orchestrate compliant, resilient physical and software supply chains. Product areas span supply chain visibility and optimization, trade and third-party risk and compliance, due diligence intelligence (DDIQ), and software supply chain security (SBOM analysis, from its Ion Channel acquisition). Exiger serves government and commercial customers and is FedRAMP authorized. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and enriched from Exiger's public corporate, trust, and legal surfaces; Exiger does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Express
providers.description: Express is a fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for Node.js, providing a robust set of features for building web and mobile applications and APIs. Maintained under the OpenJS Foundation, Express is one of the most widely used HTTP server frameworks in the JavaScript ecosystem.

providers.name: Fintor
providers.description: Fintor is an enterprise software company that provides an agentic AI workforce for mortgage lending operations. Its purpose-built, autonomous AI agents execute mortgage workflows end to end - from application through closing - with human-in-the-loop oversight, integrating with existing loan origination systems (LOS), CRMs, and contact centers rather than replacing them. Product modules include a Loan Officer Assistant (document intake, borrower communication, gap analysis), a Processor Assistant (third-party orders, condition tracking, disclosures), Predictive Conditioning, a Closing Agent, and a Manager Assistant for forecasting and reporting. Fintor ships pre-built connectors for Encompass, Salesforce, Five9, Polly, and Blend, exposes documented API integrations, and is SOC 2 Type II certified with encryption, RBAC, approval chains, and audit logging.

providers.name: Finverse
providers.description: Finverse is a unified open finance API platform providing aggregated access to banking data, payments, and financial services across Asia-Pacific. Often described as the Plaid for Asia, it connects to over 40 banks across Hong Kong, Singapore, Philippines, Vietnam, and other Southeast Asian markets.

providers.name: First Tech Federal Credit Union
providers.description: First Tech Federal Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in San Jose, California, and one of the largest credit unions in the United States. It was founded to serve employees of the technology industry and their families, and its membership is drawn heavily from workers at major technology employers. As an NCUA-insured credit union, First Tech offers consumer and business deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, credit cards, and wealth services delivered primarily through its website and mobile apps. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, First Tech publishes no first-party public developer portal or documented open API; consumer-permissioned financial data sharing is handled through third-party data aggregators (such as Plaid, MX, Finicity, and Akoya) rather than a directly documented first-party API surface. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented — the Financial Data Exchange (FDX) standard and the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule are still emerging — and no first-party FDX-conformant data-access API or published Section 1033 posture was found for First Tech during this review.

providers.name: Geneoscopy
providers.description: Geneoscopy is a commercial-stage molecular diagnostics company headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, focused on gastrointestinal health. Its platform analyzes stool-derived eukaryotic RNA (seRNA) biomarkers, a proprietary approach the company applies to colorectal cancer screening, inflammatory bowel disease and other gastrointestinal conditions. Its lead product, ColoSense, is a noninvasive multi-target stool RNA (mt-sRNA) colorectal cancer screening test approved by the FDA in May 2024 for adults aged 45 and older at average risk; it evaluates eight colorectal neoplasia-associated RNA markers together with occult hemoglobin, and has since been added to the American Cancer Society and NCCN colorectal cancer screening guidelines. Geneoscopy operates a CLIA-certified (26D2253457) and CAP-accredited clinical laboratory with permits in New York, California, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island and the District of Columbia, and partners with biopharma and research organizations on stool-biomarker diagnostics and prognostics. Geneoscopy is a diagnostics and clinical-laboratory company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: GoodShip
providers.description: GoodShip is a freight orchestration and procurement platform for shippers, brokers, and asset-based carriers. It unifies TMS tender, contract-award, and location data, enriches it with real-time market rates, and layers AI-assisted bid analysis (via its Laney AI transportation analyst), lane- and carrier-level performance analytics, carrier scorecards, and in-app collaboration on top. Teams run mini-bids and full-network RFPs, benchmark spend against the market, and take corrective action without dedicated developer resources. Plug-and-play with major transportation management systems; backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and serving US and Canadian operations.

providers.name: Goodwin
providers.description: Goodwin (Goodwin Company, teamgoodwin.com) is a B2B charter aviation technology company founded in 2023 and headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, backed by Canaan Partners at Series A. Its API-first platform serves the private-jet charter broker-operator ecosystem with aircraft sourcing across an 11,000+ aircraft database, automated proposal generation, modern payment processing beyond wire transfers, real-time market-adaptive pricing, and post-sale trip management. The white-labeled software integrates with operators' existing scheduling systems and is offered to emerging, growing, and enterprise brokers as well as charter operators. Goodwin operates purely B2B and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Got
providers.description: Got is a human-friendly and powerful HTTP request library for Node.js with support for streams, retries, and pagination.

providers.name: Grade
providers.description: Grade is the API for performance-based payroll, letting companies pay workers, creators, contractors, and AI agents based on results rather than hours worked. Companies push performance signals into Grade via webhooks or direct API calls (task completed, milestone hit, content published, views tracked, invoice processed), and Grade runs them against configurable payout rules — flat fees, tiered commissions, threshold bonuses, or blended structures — handling the math, de-duplication, and approval workflows automatically. Grade tracks every post across platforms, approves and distributes bulk payouts in one click, and handles compliance end to end: KYC verification, tax-form collection, DAC7 reporting, worker classification, and merchant-of-record services. Payouts reach 190+ countries via local bank transfers, PayPal, Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, Airtm, and USDT, with no separate creator account required. Grade (YC W26) is based in San Francisco and has paid out $10M+ to date.

providers.name: Homebound
providers.description: Homebound is a tech-enabled, personalized homebuilder that pairs a proprietary software platform with a managed network of trade partners to build homes on a customer's lot, sell finished and in-progress inventory homes, and run disaster rebuild programs — most notably wildfire recovery in California. Homeowners track budget, schedule, documents, and construction progress through a Homeowner Portal. Backed by Fifth Wall, Forerunner Ventures, and GV, Homebound operates in the construction-tech sector. Homebound does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its public engineering footprint is the homebound-team GitHub organization and the first-party open-source packages it publishes to the @homebound npm scope (the Beam design system, form-state, and truss). This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched from public company surfaces.

providers.name: HomeToGo
providers.description: HomeToGo is the world's largest marketplace and search engine for vacation rentals, aggregating roughly 20 million offers from thousands of providers worldwide across cabins, condos, houses, and apartments. Its B2B segment, HomeToGo_PRO, powers the supply side of travel with SaaS and tech-enabled services for individual hosts, property managers, and agencies. Through its Doppelgänger program HomeToGo offers partners multiple integration surfaces — API, White Label, Travel Agency Hub, ad placement, and pop-under — to embed its vacation-rental inventory. HomeToGo is a publicly listed company (Frankfurt Stock Exchange) and a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It does not publish a public, self-serve API specification; API access is arranged through its partner and supply programs.

providers.name: IATA
providers.description: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) is the global trade association representing and serving the airline industry. IATA sets standards for the aviation industry, promotes cooperation among airlines, and operates an Open API Hub providing access to airline-published APIs for flight status, destinations, baggage, ticket validation, cargo, digital identity, and related aviation data services.

providers.name: IBM App Connect
providers.description: IBM App Connect is an integration platform that enables organizations to connect applications, data, and services across cloud and on-premises environments. It provides low-code integration capabilities with pre-built connectors and a flow editor for building integration flows.

providers.name: Incentivio
providers.description: Incentivio is a Boston-based digital guest engagement platform for multi-unit restaurant brands, unifying online ordering, loyalty, marketing automation, and guest analytics into a single system. Its Incentivio Connect product is an AI-powered, API-first restaurant data platform that ingests data from POS, loyalty, mobile apps, web, and marketplaces, resolves it into a single persistent Guest ID, and scores guests for lifetime value, churn risk, visit frequency, journey stage, propensity-to-purchase, and offer sensitivity. The platform is BigQuery-native with a Star Schema data model, SOC 2 aligned with encryption at rest and in transit and RBAC, and pairs an API-first surface with reverse ETL to sync unified guest records back to existing CRM and ad platforms. Incentivio is built on modern APIs and offers deep partner integrations with POS, payments, delivery, and marketing systems such as Toast, Oracle Simphony, Square, SpotOn, and PAR Brink. Public, self-service developer API documentation does not appear to be available; integration and API access are handled through partnerships and enterprise onboarding (the Connect Enterprise tier markets dedicated API SLAs).

providers.name: Inductive
providers.description: Inductive Bio is a New York-based AI drug discovery company building a virtual lab for small molecule optimization. It pairs medicinal chemists with AI to run millions of in silico ADMET experiments before synthesis. Its Beacon-1 models — trained on a pre-competitive, anonymized data consortium spanning thousands of drug programs — won consecutive first-place finishes in the 2025 Polaris/ASAP and 2026 OpenADMET blind ADMET prediction competitions, beating 370+ submissions including entries from Merck and NVIDIA. Products include the Compass software platform (accessible via API), the Indy AI chemistry assistant, the ADME-One high-throughput profiling service, and Embedded Experts. Founded in 2023 by Josh Haimson and Ben Birnbaum (both formerly Flatiron Health); SOC 2 compliant; backed by Obvious Ventures, a16z Bio+Health, Lux Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Character, and S32.

providers.name: Inductive Bio
providers.description: Inductive Bio is an AI-powered virtual lab for small molecule drug discovery, based in New York and founded in 2022 by Josh Haimson and Ben Birnbaum (both formerly of Flatiron Health). The company pairs medicinal chemists with machine learning to run millions of in silico ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) experiments, surface the strongest compound hypotheses, and accelerate the path to development candidates. Its Beacon-1 models took first place in both the 2025 Polaris/ASAP and 2026 OpenADMET/ExpansionRx blind ADMET competitions, and are delivered through the Compass software platform (with the Indy AI chemistry assistant) and an Embedded Experts services offering. Inductive Bio operates a pre-competitive ADMET data consortium, is SOC 2 compliant, and is backed by a16z, Lux Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Obvious Ventures, Character, and S32. Compass is enterprise/partner software; it exposes an API to partner teams but publishes no public, self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK.

providers.name: Instructions.md
providers.description: File-scoped custom instruction files for GitHub Copilot and VS Code, using applyTo patterns to target specific file types or tasks with tailored AI guidance. These markdown-based instruction files allow developers to provide context-specific guidance for AI coding assistants.

providers.name: Joby Aviation
providers.description: Joby Aviation is a California-based aerospace company developing an all-electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft intended to operate as part of a fast, quiet, and convenient air taxi service. Joby's piloted four-passenger S4 aircraft is designed for a top speed of 200 mph and zero operating emissions, and the company is pursuing FAA Type Certification under Part 23. Joby has strategic relationships with Toyota for manufacturing, Delta Air Lines, Virgin Atlantic and ANA for distribution, Uber for ground integration, the U.S. Department of Defense (Agility Prime), and operates a vertically integrated program covering aircraft, batteries (JoeBen cell technology via Joby's battery group), software, and pilot training. Joby acquired Uber Elevate and is co-located with manufacturing facilities in Marina and Santa Cruz, California, with plans for early commercial passenger service in Dubai and U.S. cities.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: Karmada
providers.description: Karmada is a CNCF incubating Kubernetes management system that enables running applications across multiple Kubernetes clusters and clouds. It provides a unified control plane for multi-cluster scheduling, failover, and traffic management. Karmada uses Kubernetes-native APIs and supports propagation policies, override policies, and federated resource management.

providers.name: KubeEdge
providers.description: KubeEdge is a CNCF graduated project that extends Kubernetes to edge computing. It provides infrastructure support for networking, application deployment, and metadata synchronization between cloud and edge. KubeEdge enables containerized application orchestration at the edge with offline autonomy, ensuring edge nodes continue functioning when disconnected from the cloud.

providers.name: KubeVela
providers.description: KubeVela is a CNCF incubating application delivery and management platform that makes deploying and operating applications across hybrid and multi-cloud environments easier. Built on the Open Application Model (OAM), it provides a higher-level abstraction for defining applications with components, traits, and policies. KubeVela supports workflow-based delivery pipelines and multi-cluster deployment.

providers.name: Layer3
providers.description: Layer3 is a consumer crypto platform that bills itself as a gateway to the onchain economy, combining a gasless smart wallet with curated protocol "Activations" where users complete onchain tasks to earn CUBE rewards and the L3 token. It spans 40+ chains and 500+ applications, adds trading, staking, competitions, perks, and social features, and offers a Builder product that lets protocols launch incentivized activations, set up a Space, and distribute token rewards. It is backed by Electric Capital. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface was found during enrichment; the docs at docs.layer3.xyz cover the end-user Platform and no-code Builder products only.

providers.name: Leapfin
providers.description: Leapfin is an AI-powered financial data platform for record-to-report and automated revenue recognition. It ingests transactional data from billing systems, payment processors, and data warehouses, standardizes it into a unified Financial Records schema, applies templated GAAP, SOX, IFRS, and ASC 606 revenue rules, and produces audit-ready journal entries and revenue reports that post to ERPs such as NetSuite. Programmatic data ingestion is available through the Leap Connect API (released March 2024); the platform also offers Luca, a native AI agent for exploring and reporting on revenue data. Leapfin is enterprise SaaS - the developer reference is on a partner/login-gated documentation portal, so the API surface below is modeled from Leapfin's public product and help-center material rather than fully reproduced endpoint-by-endpoint.

providers.name: Leflair
providers.description: Leflair is a Vietnamese online retail brand selling discounted authentic international brands across fashion and accessories, beauty and health, home and lifestyle, and children's products. Its own terms of service describe it as Vietnam's first members-only flash-sale platform, running daily promotional events on branded goods. The live storefront at leflair.com is operated by Cong ty TNHH Sopa Technology of Ho Chi Minh City on the Haravan commerce platform, and is supported by a Vietnamese-language editorial blog, an account/sign-in surface, and published terms, privacy, payment-security, shipping, and tax policy pages. Leflair is a consumer retail brand: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API definition, and its historical leflair.vn domain no longer serves the storefront. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Legion Security
providers.description: Legion Security is a browser-native AI SOC analyst that learns a security team's real workflows from inside the browser and then helps execute and automate them in phases: Learning Mode captures and maps how analysts actually work, Guided Mode runs those workflows with a human in the loop, and Autonomous Mode takes over the steps the team has signed off on. The platform targets alert triage, investigation, and evidence gathering in the security operations center, positioning agentic AI as a dependable teammate rather than a black box, with every captured insight visible and every action explainable. Legion Security operates a SafeBase trust center and publishes SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA, and CSA STAR Level 1 compliance documentation. The company is seed-stage and backed by Accel; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Linux
providers.description: Linux is an open-source Unix-like operating system kernel originally created by Linus Torvalds. This index catalogs the userspace and kernel programming interfaces exposed by Linux, including system calls, eBPF, ioctl, netlink, procfs, sysfs, GPIO, and security interfaces such as Seccomp, Landlock, and Linux Security Modules. It also covers ecosystem APIs for systemd and PAM.

providers.name: Metal3
providers.description: Metal3 (Metal Kubed) is a CNCF incubating project that provides bare metal host provisioning for Kubernetes. It leverages Ironic for hardware management and integrates with the Cluster API to enable Kubernetes-native lifecycle management of bare metal infrastructure. Metal3 automates server discovery, inspection, provisioning, and deprovisioning using Kubernetes custom resources.

providers.name: OpenYurt
providers.description: OpenYurt is a CNCF incubating project that extends Kubernetes for edge and cloud-edge collaboration scenarios. It provides node autonomy for edge nodes to continue operating during cloud-edge network disconnections, seamless node conversion between cloud and edge modes, and unified management of edge resources through NodePool and YurtAppSet abstractions.

providers.name: Pendulum
providers.description: Pendulum (Pendulum Therapeutics, pendulumlife.com) is a microbiome-management and metabolic-health company that develops clinically validated probiotic supplements built on novel, patented anaerobic microbial strains such as Akkermansia muciniphila. Its consumer products - including Glucose Control, Metabolic Daily, Akkermansia, and a GLP-1 probiotic - are formulated to fuel and maintain the gut lining, support immunity, relieve gas and bloating, and help keep blood glucose in a healthy range, differentiated by double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials rather than off-the-shelf probiotic blends. Pendulum is a direct-to-consumer health and supplement brand and is a portfolio company of DCVC; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Pentera
providers.description: Pentera is an AI-driven automated security validation (exposure validation) platform that lets organizations continuously test their security defenses through automated penetration testing, red teaming, and adversarial validation across internal networks, external attack surface, credentials, and cloud environments. The platform safely emulates real attacker techniques at scale to surface exploitable exposures, validate remediation, and prioritize risk. Pentera is enterprise/on-prem software consumed via its own console and a broad set of product integrations (SIEM/SOAR, ticketing, cloud, EDR, vulnerability management); it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal. Pentera is backed by Insight Partners. Sector: cybersecurity.

providers.name: Pindrop
providers.description: Pindrop is a voice and audio security company providing a continuous identity verification and deepfake-detection platform for enterprises. Its technology authenticates callers and video-meeting participants, detects synthetic (AI-generated) speech and fraudulent activity, and protects contact centers, virtual meetings, and connected devices. Pindrop's products span call-center fraud detection, passive voice authentication, and liveness/deepfake defense, and are delivered largely through partner platforms (Amazon Connect, Zoom, Webex, and others) rather than a public self-service developer API. The company is backed by Felicis, GV, and IVP and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Pinokio
providers.description: Pinokio is an open-source desktop application — self-described as an "AI Browser" — that acts as a 1-click launcher for any open-source AI project. Built by independent developer Cocktail Peanut (cocktailpeanut), Pinokio packages a terminal, package managers (Conda, Homebrew, Pip, NPM), and a graphical UI into a single MIT-licensed desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux with NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon GPU support. Users install AI apps with one click from a curated "Discover" directory of 160+ vetted scripts spanning image generation, video generation, text-to-speech and voice cloning, large language models, 3D generation, music and audio generation, and face swap. Pinokio is driven by a JSON-based scripting language designed to be both human and machine readable, with primitives like shell.run, fs, input, log, jump, hf (Hugging Face), notify, browser, and json that let publishers describe install and launch flows declaratively. Each script is sandboxed under ~/pinokio with isolated paths and Python virtual environments, and featured scripts must transfer ownership to the Pinokio Factory GitHub organization for admin review. Pinokio is purely client-side open source — there is no public REST API, no hosted commercial offering, and no developer SDK beyond the local script syntax and the desktop app itself.

providers.name: PlotBox
providers.description: PlotBox is a deathcare management platform for cemeteries, crematories, and funeral homes. Founded in Northern Ireland, its cloud SaaS combines records management, interactive digital cemetery mapping, financial and trust-fund management, work orders, scheduling, and family-facing records portals to help deathcare providers run compliant, efficient operations. PlotBox serves over 2,000 facilities globally, is hosted on Microsoft Azure, and holds ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certifications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Porsche
providers.description: Porsche is a luxury car manufacturer known for producing high-performance sports cars, sedans, and SUVs. Founded in 1931 by Ferdinand Porsche, the brand has a long history of engineering excellence and precision craftsmanship. Porsche vehicles are renowned for their sleek design, exceptional handling, and powerful engines, making them a favorite among driving enthusiasts around the world.

providers.name: Qognitive
providers.description: Qognitive, Inc. is an AI company that develops QCML (Quantum Cognition Machine Learning), an analytical AI architecture positioned as an alternative to classical statistical modeling. Its product, Hone, targets high-dimensional, multi-modal, and noisy structured data — claiming near-linear scaling with feature count and accuracy improvements over industry-standard models, with peer-reviewed backing in Nature Scientific Reports and Risk.net. Hone is distributed as first-party Python packages (hone-io community edition and hone-io-enterprise) exposing scikit-learn-compatible regression and classification wrappers. The company was surfaced as a Ribbit Capital portfolio company. There is no public REST/HTTP API surface; integration is via the Python SDK.

providers.name: Quantexa
providers.description: Quantexa provides decision intelligence solutions using entity resolution and network analytics to help organizations connect disparate data and make better decisions across financial crime, risk, customer intelligence, and public sector use cases.

providers.name: React
providers.description: A JavaScript library for building user interfaces, maintained by Meta and the open source community.

providers.name: React Native
providers.description: A framework for building native apps using React, enabling cross-platform mobile development for iOS and Android.

providers.name: ReadyAPI
providers.description: ReadyAPI is SmartBear's enterprise-grade automated API testing platform. It unifies functional, security, performance, and virtualization testing for REST, SOAP, GraphQL, Kafka, JDBC, and JMS APIs. ReadyAPI is delivered as a desktop and CI/CD tool rather than as a public REST API, integrating with Jenkins, Azure DevOps, Git, and other automation platforms via TestEngine.

providers.name: Roborock
providers.description: Roborock is a global consumer robotics company best known for its robot vacuum and mop cleaners, wet/dry wash-and-fill floor washers, and connected home-cleaning appliances controlled through the Roborock mobile app. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Beijing, the company was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. Roborock operates a private cloud that backs its consumer mobile app but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program. It does operate a public Trust Center documenting the security and privacy design of its IoT products, including TÜV Rheinland EN 303 645 and UL Diamond IoT Security certifications.

providers.name: Sallie Mae Bank
providers.description: Sallie Mae Bank is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank (industrial loan company) founded on November 28, 2005 and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, operating as the FDIC-insured banking subsidiary (FDIC cert #58177) of SLM Corporation (NASDAQ SLM), the publicly traded, S&P 400 consumer-finance company best known as the largest originator of private student loans in the United States. Beyond student and education lending, the bank offers retail deposit products including high-yield savings accounts, money market accounts, and certificates of deposit through salliemae.com. Sallie Mae Bank does not operate a first-party public developer program - there is no developer.salliemae.com portal, no api.salliemae.com host, and no published OpenAPI/Swagger definitions. Consumer account and transaction data is reachable only on a permissioned basis through third-party data aggregators (historically Plaid), and no first-party FDX data-access API or published CFPB Section 1033 data-rights posture could be confirmed. This is an identity-only, aggregator-access record reflecting the honest reality that this institution exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: Spring Health
providers.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

providers.name: SteadyMD
providers.description: SteadyMD is a telehealth infrastructure and clinical-workforce company (a DocGo company) backed by Lux Capital. It supplies board-certified physicians and nurse practitioners, clinical operations, and 50-state licensing and credentialing, plus technology and telehealth APIs that let healthcare and digital-health partners launch branded, fully managed virtual care. Its APIs cover patient data submission, synchronous and asynchronous consult requests, two-way patient-clinician messaging, intake forms, clinician availability, real-time status updates, document attachments, scheduling, and reporting/SLA retrieval, offered as either a Limited (partner-EMR) or Complete (SteadyMD-EMR) integration. API documentation is provided under a business agreement via a request form; there is no public developer portal or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: StorSimple
providers.description: StorSimple was a Santa Clara, California hybrid cloud storage company founded in 2009 by Ursheet Parikh and Guru Pangal. Its appliances combined primary storage, tiered cloud archiving, deduplication, compression, and encryption behind iSCSI/SMB interfaces, backed by $31.5M from Index Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Ignition Partners, and Mayfield Fund. Microsoft acquired StorSimple in November 2012 and folded it into Azure as Azure StorSimple (8000 series physical and virtual arrays, plus the StorSimple Data Manager). The product is managed through Azure Resource Manager under the Microsoft.StorSimple resource provider and its REST API. Azure StorSimple reached end-of-life in December 2022 and is out of support; Microsoft directs customers to Azure File Sync and Azure Files.

providers.name: Straiker
providers.description: Straiker is an AI-native security company for agentic AI, founded by security veterans from Palo Alto Networks. It protects every layer of AI agent deployments from prompts to infrastructure with a closed-loop system that pairs autonomous adversarial testing with sub-second runtime defense. Its products are Ascend AI (autonomous AI threat detection that integrates into CI/CD to test agents for prompt injection, tool manipulation, goal hijacking and data leakage), Defend AI (agentic runtime security that blocks identity abuse, memory poisoning, data exfiltration and malicious MCP connections in real time using proprietary LLM judges), and Discover AI (agent/MCP discovery and posture management). Straiker is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its developer documentation and API/SDK integration surface are gated behind an enterprise access code; there is no public API reference.

providers.name: Svastia
providers.description: Svastia (Svastia Genetics Inc.) is a precision-genomics and oncology data company that bundles clinical research products with cutting-edge bioinformatics to accelerate precision cancer therapy. It offers DNA/RNA sequencing, exome and gene-panel assays, immune (B/T-cell) repertoire sequencing, cell-based drug-efficacy screening, therapeutic-antibody development toolkits, and siRNA design, together with biomarker analytics (Tumor Mutational Burden, Microsatellite Instability) and clinical reporting based on ACMG/ASCO guidelines. Svastia serves hospitals, diagnostics labs, researchers, and CROs, and runs a bespoke clinical/genetic data-collection service across a hospital network, with HL7-FHIR data exchange between EHR and Clinical Trial Management Systems. Products are delivered through a login-gated web portal; the company does not publish a public developer API. Backed by 500 Global; offices in San Francisco (USA) and Cambridge (UK).

providers.name: TourHero
providers.description: TourHero is a social travel platform and end-to-end group trip operations partner that lets creators, coaches, and community leaders host fully customized group trips in 50+ countries, with itinerary design, vetted local operators, payments, and on-the-ground logistics handled by TourHero. Travelers can browse and book public trips on its Explore page, and hosts plan for free while TourHero earns commission from local suppliers. Backed by 500 Global and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it is a consumer platform with no publicly documented developer API surface at this time, though it publishes an llms.txt profile for AI agents.

providers.name: Tuniu
providers.description: Tuniu (途牛旅游网) is a leading online leisure travel company in China, headquartered in Nanjing and listed on NASDAQ under ticker TOUR. It offers packaged tours, self-guided tours, and a broad range of travel-related services and products including hotels, flights, train tickets, cruises, visas, and local activities. For partners, Tuniu runs an Open Platform (途牛开放平台) at developer.tuniu.com that exposes supplier and retail-partner integration APIs behind developer registration, letting suppliers publish inventory and retail partners distribute Tuniu travel products. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: WalkMe
providers.description: WalkMe is a Digital Adoption Platform delivering in-app guidance, walkthroughs, and analytics that help users navigate and adopt enterprise applications.

providers.name: XebiaLabs
providers.description: XebiaLabs was an enterprise DevOps software company behind XL Deploy (deployment automation), XL Release (release orchestration), and XL Impact (DevOps analytics), backed by Accel and Susquehanna Growth Equity. In February 2020 XebiaLabs merged with CollabNet VersionOne to form Digital.ai; xebialabs.com now redirects to digital.ai and the products continue as Digital.ai Deploy and Digital.ai Release. The XebiaLabs GitHub organizations, Maven/PyPI/Docker Hub packages, and the dist.xebialabs.com distribution site remain live, still shipping the xl CLI on the current Digital.ai version train. No public hosted API is served under the XebiaLabs brand — the product REST APIs are customer-hosted and documented at docs.digital.ai.

providers.name: Xsight Labs
providers.description: Xsight Labs is a fabless semiconductor company redefining AI and cloud connectivity with end-to-end, software-defined silicon for hyperscale data centers. Its X-Series programmable Ethernet switch silicon (X1, X2) delivers 3.2-12.8 Tbps with sub-700ns latency and is programmable through XISA, the first fully open, documented switch instruction set architecture, published under MPLv2. Its E-Series is billed as the industry's first fully software-defined 800G DPU family, placing 64 Arm Neoverse N2 cores directly in the data path and programmable with standard Linux tooling (XDP, DPDK, SPDK) with no proprietary SDK. Xsight Labs contributes SONiC platform code and a SAI implementation through its public GitHub organization. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors. The company publishes technical documentation, XISA specifications, and programming examples rather than a hosted web API; no public OpenAPI, REST endpoints, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Yaak
providers.description: Yaak is an open-source desktop API client for organizing and executing REST, GraphQL, WebSockets, Server Sent Events, and gRPC requests. Built with Tauri, Rust, and React, it is a privacy-first, fast desktop client with no telemetry and no cloud lock-in.

providers.name: Zipcar
providers.description: Zipcar is a Boston, Massachusetts-based car sharing service operating in more than 500 cities across North America and Europe, including major US metros (Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York, Philadelphia, Portland, San Francisco, Seattle, Washington DC) and Canadian cities (Toronto, Hamilton, the Golden Horseshoe). Members reserve vehicles by the hour or day through the Zipcar mobile app, unlock cars with their phone, and pay per usage with gas, EV charging, standard damage protection insurance, and professional maintenance included. Zipcar serves consumer members, universities (Zipcar for Universities), and businesses (Zipcar for Business) with weekday fleet programs. Zipcar is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Avis Budget Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: CAR), which acquired the company in March 2013 for approximately $500 million. Zipcar exposes a REST-based Partner API at api.zipcar.com/partner-api, documented at owa.zipcar.com/documentation, that returns JSON for Location List and Location Detail resources (vehicles available at a lat/long); access is gated and granted on request via developerportal@zipcar.com — there is no public OpenAPI spec, SDK, or self-service developer signup. Zipcar also operates a public GitHub organization (github.com/Zipcar) hosting internal DevOps tooling (Concourse resources, Ansible helpers, BOSH helpers, monitoring agents) rather than client-facing API artifacts.

providers.name: Zolo
providers.description: Zolo is one of Canada's largest national residential real estate marketplaces and a licensed brokerage, operating as Zolo Ventures Ltd. with provincial brokerage subsidiaries — Zolo Realty (Ontario), (Alberta), (British Columbia), (Saskatchewan), (Manitoba) and (Quebec) Inc. — plus Zolo Mortgages Ltd. and Zolo Mortgages (Alberta) Ltd., all owned by Questrade Financial Group Inc. Founded in 2012 as a digital-first brokerage and headquartered at 1900-5700 Yonge Street in Toronto, Zolo reports over 10 million monthly visitors, 750+ active REALTORS®, and $1.5B+ in annual transaction volume across British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan and Ontario. It sits in the Canadian challenger layer alongside HouseSigma, Wahi and Properly, below CREA — the single national cooperative that operates REALTOR.ca and the Data Distribution Facility (DDF) that syndicates member boards' listings — competing on listing speed, sold-price visibility and home-value tooling over data the boards and CREA control. Its API posture is closed. There is no developer portal, no API program page, no partner or data-licensing page, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind — no OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI or MCP surface. The subdomains api., developer., developers., docs., data. and partners.zolo.ca do not resolve in DNS and have never appeared in Certificate Transparency, and every conventional contract path on www.zolo.ca is answered by a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403, cf-mitigated: challenge) rather than a specification. What Zolo does publish is syndication, not integration: an unauthenticated RSS 2.0 new-listings feed at /rss_new_listings.php, a family of sitemaps.org XML documents, and a site-wide schema.org JSON-LD block carrying organization identity only. Behind the edge it operates an undocumented JSON endpoint at /gallery_map_json.php and two first-party mobile apps (com.ols.zolo) on a private backend. Zolo's own robots.txt declares that RSS feed as a sitemap and a CREA terms-acceptance route at /crea_accept.php, and Section 23 of its Terms of Use is a Virtual Office Website (VOW) clause requiring registration, a bona fide interest in buying or selling, personal non-commercial use only, and an express prohibition on "scraping" (including "screen scraping" and "database scraping"), data mining, redistribution or sublicensing — enforceable directly by CREA, TRREB, ITSO, REBGV, Pillar9 and OREB. Access is licensed, not open. RESO is absent: Zolo is not among the nineteen Canadian organizations RESO lists as members, and no Web API or Data Dictionary certification, OData $metadata document, or Universal Property Identifier (UPI) usage was found. No open, unlicensed dataset is published.

providers.name: 7 Cups
providers.description: 7 Cups is an online emotional support and mental health platform founded in July 2013 by psychologist Glen Moriarty (Y Combinator S13) and based in Palo Alto, California. It connects people seeking help with trained volunteer "listeners" for free, anonymous, 24/7 one-to-one active-listening chat, and also offers community forums, group support chat rooms, self-help growth paths, and affordable online therapy with licensed therapists via messaging. The service reports reaching tens of millions of people across roughly 190 countries, supported by hundreds of thousands of trained volunteer listeners, and sells organizational solutions for schools, employers, and health plans. 7 Cups does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Appalachian Regional Commission
providers.description: The Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) is a federal-state partnership that invests in Appalachia's economic future by funding projects that promote economic development, infrastructure improvement, workforce training, and community development across 423 counties in 13 states. ARC provides research data, county-level economic reports, and maps via its Data Report Tool at data.arc.gov.
