Its products include Care Concierge human guidance, an Aging-in-Place Marketplace for OTC products and nonmedical services (home care, safety modifications, meals, transportation), the Helpful benefits card, digital invoicing and claims processing for home and facility care, and digital nurse eligibility assessments for long-term care insurance. The company runs one of the nation's largest networks of vetted in-home care agencies and sells to Long-Term Care Insurance, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid plan administrators. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The Helper Bees publishes member and provider applications (the api.thehelperbees.com app host, the myhomealign.com provider portal, and mobile apps) but does not currently expose a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: TJX Companies
providers.description: The TJX Companies, Inc. is an American multinational off-price department store corporation headquartered in Framingham, Massachusetts, ranked No. 80 on the 2024 Fortune 500 list. Operating over 4,800 stores across nine countries and three continents under brands including T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods, Sierra, HomeSense (US), and Winners, HomeSense, Marshalls (Canada), TJX provides supplier and vendor integration through EDI and web-based portal platforms. Supplier connectivity is handled via Oracle iSupplier, SupplierOne, and the DiCentral ASN Vendor Portal, supporting purchase orders, advanced shipping notices, invoicing, and payment tracking.

providers.name: Tuli
providers.description: Tuli Health operates a UK-wide network of over 300 high-street pharmacies as local diagnostic hubs, making clinical services - primarily blood testing and phlebotomy - accessible in every neighbourhood so people can get care close to home. It offers healthcare providers three models - One Network (white-label phlebotomy), One Solution (end-to-end test kits, draws and lab analysis), and an Enterprise tier with custom integration. Tuli exposes an API and web portal for booking and managing tests, though public developer documentation is not yet published.

providers.name: Vastrm
providers.description: Vastrm is a custom-tailored menswear e-commerce company selling made-to-fit polo shirts with 24 different fits and sizes plus additional free adjustments, an online design-your-own configurator, corporate solutions for businesses, and a retail partners program. Vastrm is a Y Combinator and a16z-backed company tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer storefront at vastrm.com and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Vedanta Biosciences
providers.description: Vedanta Biosciences is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 19 Blackstone Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded by PureTech Health together with a group of scientific co-founders who pioneered the modern understanding of cross-talk between the human microbiome and the immune system. The company develops a potential new category of oral Live Biotherapeutic Products built from rationally defined consortia of human commensal bacteria grown from pure clonal cell banks rather than donor-derived stool, and it maintains technical expertise in the manufacture of live organisms. Its lead program, VE303, is an eight-strain defined bacterial consortium in the global Phase 3 RESTORATiVE303 registrational study for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, following Phase 2 results showing a greater than 80% reduction in the odds of CDI recurrence versus placebo; VE202 is in development for inflammatory bowel disease and VE707 for prevention of multidrug-resistant organism infections. Vedanta has raised a $68 million Series D and a $106.5 million financing, and its programs are supported by non-dilutive awards from BARDA and CARB-X. Vedanta is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it runs a WordPress marketing and corporate site, publishes no developer portal, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract, and an August 2026 probe of vedantabio.com found no OpenAPI, no /llms.txt, no MCP endpoint, no A2A agent card and an empty /.well-known/ discovery surface.

providers.name: Vela Labs
providers.description: Vela Labs, Inc. (Vela, formerly Hive) is a San Francisco company founded in 2018 by Justin Killian and Jason Abaluck that provides an AI-driven platform helping eCommerce sellers manage, optimize, and grow their businesses across multiple channels from a single account. Vela supports Etsy, Shopify, eBay, and Faire, offering bulk listing editing, AI-assisted listing creation and optimization, photo editing, and multi-channel publishing for tens of thousands of sellers. A 500 Global portfolio company that has raised $5.5M. Vela consumes the official APIs of the marketplaces it supports but publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface of its own.

providers.name: Velvet
providers.description: Velvet is a multimodal AI model R&D company (the "multimodal data lab") based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch. It partners with frontier AI labs and enterprises to build state-of-the-art video datasets and evaluation frameworks that improve models' spatial reasoning and interactive, low-latency capabilities. Velvet operates an invite-only platform for sourcing and contributing multimodal training data, with contributor payouts via Stripe and Wise. It was founded by Lucas Mantovani (CEO, formerly video data at Meta FAIR) and Lucas Tucker (CTO, formerly Adobe). As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK.

providers.name: Visby Medical
providers.description: Visby Medical is a molecular diagnostics company that has miniaturized the gold-standard PCR laboratory onto a single-use, palm-sized point-of-care device, delivering lab-quality results in about 30 minutes without any instrument, sample transport, or lab infrastructure. Its consumer offering (sold direct at visby.com) is an FDA-authorized at-home women's sexual health test that detects Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, and Trichomoniasis, paired with same-day telehealth consultation on a positive result. Visby also builds point-of-care PCR platforms for clinical and respiratory pathogen testing. The company is backed by venture investors including Amplify Partners. This API Evangelist profile tracks Visby Medical as a company; the business is a hardware diagnostics and direct-to-consumer commerce operation and does not publish a first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Weekend Health (Found)
providers.description: Weekend Health, Inc. (operating as Found / Found Health) is a consumer telehealth company offering personalized, science-based weight-loss care, including GLP-1 and other obesity medications, clinician oversight, coaching, and habit-change support delivered direct-to-consumer and through employer and health-plan channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal is published as of this enrichment pass; the profile carries the company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Worq
providers.description: WORQ is Malaysia's largest community-centric coworking space operator, backed by 500 Global, offering private offices, dedicated desks, hot desks, virtual offices, meeting rooms, event spaces, and day passes across twelve locations in Greater Kuala Lumpur and Selangor. WORQ publishes no public developer portal or API as of July 2026.

providers.name: Zeroqode
providers.description: Zeroqode is a leading no-code development platform and Bubble agency that provides app templates, plugins, courses, and automation tools for building scalable applications without coding. It offers 800+ plugins for Bubble.io, the Air Native mobile app conversion service, and Framer plugins. Zeroqode helps founders and developers build apps 10x faster using no-code and AI tooling.

providers.name: Adient
providers.description: Adient is a global automotive seating supplier headquartered in Plymouth, Michigan. Spun off from Johnson Controls in 2016, Adient designs and manufactures seating systems for global automakers across passenger and commercial vehicles.

providers.name: Anker Innovations
providers.description: Anker Innovations is a global consumer-electronics company headquartered in Shenzhen, China, known for its Anker charging and power products, Soundcore audio, eufy smart-home and security devices, Nebula projectors, and Anker SOLIX portable power and solar storage. Through the Anker Open Platform (developer.anker.com) the company exposes a developer surface that lets partners integrate and control Anker devices from their own applications via API and SDK, gated behind an Open Platform login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and is being enriched with the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Applied Intuition
providers.description: Applied Intuition builds physical AI software and systems for intelligent machines, helping customers develop, test, validate, deploy, and operate autonomy and vehicle intelligence across automotive, defense, trucking, mining, construction, and agriculture. Its product lines include a Self-Driving System (a unified autonomy stack for land, air, and sea), Vehicle OS (an operating system for intelligent machines), and Tools for Vehicle Intelligence covering simulation, validation, data, training, and evaluation workflows. The company operates as a private enterprise vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API or self-service portal; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and machine-readable llms.txt.

providers.name: Autoura
providers.description: Autoura is a digital experience platform for real-world tourism and travel experiences. They develop software and APIs that enable travel companies, destination management organizations, and developers to access and integrate tourism content including destination information, tour itineraries, cuisine guides, activities, and interactive local experience recommendations.

providers.name: AXA
providers.description: AXA is a French multinational insurance firm and one of the world's largest providers of life, health, property & casualty, and asset management services. AXA does not publish a single global developer portal; technology integration is delivered through country-specific broker and partner portals, AXA Partners B2B2C distribution channels, AXA XL specialty insurance APIs for commercial brokers, and ACORD / EDI standards used across the insurance industry.

providers.name: Axiom Space
providers.description: Axiom Space, Inc. is a privately funded American space infrastructure developer headquartered in Houston, Texas, founded in 2016 by Kam Ghaffarian and former NASA International Space Station Program Manager Michael Suffredini. The company is building Axiom Station, the world's first commercial space station and planned successor to the ISS, and has flown private astronaut missions to the ISS (Ax-1 through Ax-4). Axiom Space also develops the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit for NASA's return to the lunar surface, and sells human spaceflight, microgravity research, in-space manufacturing, and Orbital Data Center services (in-orbit cloud compute, with the ODC T1 node built alongside Kepler Communications and Skyloom Global). As of this enrichment pass Axiom Space publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract — every offering is transacted through direct enterprise, agency, and government engagement, and its only public code presence is a two-repository GitHub organization holding forks of NASA simulation software (Trick and GUNNS).

providers.name: Bayer
providers.description: Bayer is a German multinational pharmaceutical and life sciences company operating across pharmaceuticals, consumer health, and crop science. Bayer does not publish a single corporate-level public developer portal; integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, the Bayer Crop Science Climate FieldView ecosystem (partner-gated APIs and certified-partner integrations), pharmacovigilance and clinical-trial data exchange, and EDI / x12 channels with distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: Capi Money
providers.description: Capi Money is a cross-border payments fintech that lets businesses pay their suppliers in more than 30 currencies, targeting importers in Africa and other emerging markets who have historically faced high fees and multi-week settlement times on international invoices. Founded in 2023 by Mitch Riley and Scott Liddle and headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, the company offers instant FX rate quotes, settlement within 24 hours, real-time payment tracking, and holds customer funds with licensed financial institutions. Capi is a Y Combinator company backed by Creandum, Firstminute Capital, and Raba, having raised roughly EUR 17.2 million in Series A funding. The product is delivered through a web application (app.capimoney.com) and an FX Partner Program; there is no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal published at this time.

providers.name: CBRE Australia
providers.description: CBRE Australia is the Australian arm of CBRE Group, the global commercial real estate services and investment firm, trading locally as CBRE (Gwsla) Pty Ltd (AU09949) and operating across the Pacific from cbre.com.au. It sits on the advisory and management side of the Australian property value chain rather than the data-infrastructure side: capital markets and investment sales, leasing and occupier advisory, valuation and advisory services, property and asset management, and project and design-and-build delivery across office, retail, industrial and logistics, build-to-rent, and alternative asset classes. Its API posture is closed. As of 26 July 2026 no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable contract, or self-serve onboarding exists for CBRE Australia: developer.cbre.com.au, developers.cbre.com.au, api.cbre.com.au, and docs.cbre.com.au do not resolve, and the global developer.cbre.com host is NXDOMAIN as well. CBRE does run API infrastructure — api.cbre.com sits behind an Imperva WAF that returns 403 to every anonymous request, api-dev.cbre.com serves a default WSO2 API Manager landing page, and eipportal.cbre.com is a login-gated "Integration Platform" SPA — but none of it is published, catalogued, or reachable by an outside developer. Commercial listings are distributed through the cbre.com.au property search and Australia's portal duopoly, and CBRE's terms of use explicitly prohibit scraping property listings from the site. RESO is absent entirely, which is the honest answer for Australia: there is no MLS here, no RESO-certified Australian organization, and the country's mandated machine-readable property rail is PEXA's electronic conveyancing network, not a RESO Web API. Access to CBRE data in Australia is a client or partner relationship, not a developer signup.

providers.name: CNCF
providers.description: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) is part of the Linux Foundation and hosts critical components of the global cloud-native technology infrastructure - including Kubernetes, Prometheus, Envoy, etcd, OpenTelemetry, CloudEvents, gRPC, and CNI. CNCF stewards open-source project governance and publishes the Cloud Native Interactive Landscape, a community-curated dataset (landscape.yml) of cloud-native projects and products with metadata such as GitHub stars, contributor counts, funding, and headquarters location.

providers.name: Comet
providers.description: Comet is Perplexity's AI-native browser built on Chromium (Blink), integrating Perplexity Search and an agentic assistant that can summarize pages, draft emails, and complete tasks. Launched July 9, 2025 on Windows and macOS, with Android (Nov 2025), iOS (Mar 2026), and visionOS support added later. Initially gated behind a paid Perplexity subscription, opened free to everyone in October 2025. This is a consumer browser product with no publicly documented REST API surface.

providers.name: Creditas
providers.description: Creditas is a Brazilian digital lending fintech founded in 2012 and headquartered in Sao Paulo, operating in Brazil and Mexico. It provides secured consumer credit - loans backed by real estate (home equity) and vehicles, plus private payroll (consignado privado) loans - alongside auto insurance, multi-bank real estate and vehicle financing, and a corporate benefits platform (salary advance, flexible-benefits cards, and financial education). Regulated by the Banco Central do Brasil, Creditas has originated over R$12 billion in credit. It is backed by QED Investors and the SoftBank Vision Fund. No public developer API program or OpenAPI has been identified; this profile captures the company public identity, its published llms.txt, and its domain security posture.

providers.name: CRU Kafe
providers.description: CRU Kafe is a London-founded organic coffee brand selling Fairtrade, ethically sourced coffee - including award-winning Nespresso-compatible pods from 33p per pod, plus ground coffee and beans - direct to consumers through its Shopify storefront at crukafe.com. Backed by Seedcamp, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. CRU Kafe publishes no first-party developer API; its machine-readable surface is the Shopify / Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-commerce layer served on its own domain: a hosted UCP MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search and buyer-approved checkout, an llms.txt / agents.md for AI shopping assistants, and Shopify Customer Account OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect identity.

providers.name: CSC Generation
providers.description: CSC Generation is an AI-native retail holding company that acquires overlooked store- and catalogue-based retailers and rebuilds them on Genesis, its agent-orchestrated operating platform. Genesis combines a Data Fabric — a Data Management Platform that ingests and normalizes data across every brand without replatforming, and a Data Intelligence Platform that turns it into decision-ready signals for operators and AI agents — with an automation engine, proprietary retail AI tools, and centralized shared services covering customer experience, supply chain, technology and compliance. The company powers 13 brands and more than $1B in revenue, including Backcountry, Competitive Cyclist, Steep & Cheap, MotoSport, BikeTiresDirect, Level Nine Sports, Sur La Table, One Kings Lane, Seattle Coffee Gear and Home Consignment Center, and operates from Chicago, Austin, Los Angeles, Toronto, Seattle and Salt Lake City. CSC Generation publishes no corporate developer API; its machine-readable surface is per-brand — portfolio storefronts advertise Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profiles at /.well-known/ucp that point agents at MCP endpoints for catalog search, cart and checkout.

providers.name: Cypherium
providers.description: Cypherium is a permissionless Layer-1 blockchain built to bridge centralized (CeFi) and decentralized (DeFi) finance and bring real-world assets on-chain at scale. It runs CypherBFT, a hybrid consensus that pairs GPU proof-of-work committee election with HotStuff Byzantine Fault Tolerance for near-instant finality, and is EVM/Solidity compatible (EVM chain ID 16166). Products include CypherLink (cross-ledger notary), Cypherium Connect (bank integration plugin, marketed as ISO 20022 compliant), the Cypherium Validator, and Cypherium ID (decentralized identity). Developers integrate through an Ethereum-style JSON-RPC node API (eth/web3/net/ personal/miner/txpool/admin namespaces over HTTP, WS and IPC) and a Coinbase Rosetta API implementation for exchange and wallet integration. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Drillster
providers.description: Drillster is a digital learning platform that uses adaptive, repetition-based technology to help users acquire and retain knowledge and skills through personalized drills, quizzes, and learning modules.

providers.name: Economic Research Service
providers.description: The Economic Research Service (ERS) is a division of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) that conducts economic research and analysis related to agriculture, food, and rural development. ERS provides policymakers, stakeholders, and the public with valuable information and data to help inform decision-making and policy development.

providers.name: Fleetmatics
providers.description: Fleetmatics was a fleet management, telematics, and GPS vehicle tracking SaaS company whose Reveal platform tracked commercial vehicles, drivers, and mobile assets for small and mid-sized fleets. Founded in Dublin and later headquartered in Massachusetts, Fleetmatics IPO'd on the NYSE in 2012 and was acquired by Verizon in 2016 for about USD 2.4 billion, becoming the core of Verizon Connect. Its Reveal platform exposes a documented REST API and webhook suite - the Fleetmatics Integration Manager (FIM) / Reveal Integration Services APIs - covering vehicles, drivers, GPS positions and history, trips and segments, driver status and safety, hours-of-service logbooks, geofences (places), groups, and non-powered asset tracking. The API gateway still runs on Fleetmatics-branded hosts (fim.api.us.fleetmatics.com); access is gated to Reveal customers and approved integration partners who request Integration Manager and Reveal REST credentials before calling the documented endpoints. The Fleetmatics brand now redirects to Verizon Connect.

providers.name: Galileo
providers.description: Galileo (galileo.io, formerly reached at galileohealth.com) is a value-based, digitally enabled healthcare delivery company founded by Tom X. Lee (previously Epocrates and One Medical). It delivers 24/7 primary and multi-specialty care through a mobile app, in-home visits, mobile clinics, and virtual care, combining a proprietary clinical technology platform, a recruited network of primary-care and specialist clinicians, and hospitality-style member support. Galileo operates a fully bilingual (English/Spanish) platform and serves individuals and families, employers, small businesses, and health plans through membership and population- health partnerships. It is a care-delivery business, not an API platform: as of this profile Galileo publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Geocomply
providers.description: GeoComply is a geolocation compliance, digital identity, and fraud-prevention company that provides the location-verification and anti-fraud intelligence layer behind many of the world's most regulated digital platforms. Its product suite spans GeoComply Core (location-based fraud detection and geolocation compliance), IDComply (KYC and AML identity verification), GeoGuard (VPN and proxy/spoofing detection), PinPoint (on-property geofencing), the Chargeback Integrator (GCI), and the OneComply licensing-management platform, serving the iGaming, financial services, media/entertainment, and cryptocurrency industries. GeoComply's integrations are enterprise, sales-led engagements rather than a public self-serve developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company and has been enriched from GeoComply's public security, trust, and discovery surface.

providers.name: Hidrate
providers.description: HidrateSpark is the world's smartest water bottle brand, tracking daily water intake with a Bluetooth-connected sensor puck that glows to remind you to drink and syncs to the HidrateSpark hydration app, Fitbit, and Apple Watch. The company (originally Hidrate, Inc., a Techstars-backed startup) sells its smart bottles and accessories through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at hidratespark.com. It does not publish a first-party developer or product API; the only machine-facing surface is the Shopify platform layer — OIDC/OAuth customer accounts and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-commerce endpoints that let buyer-approved AI shopping agents browse and check out.

providers.name: Highway 9 Networks
providers.description: Highway 9 Networks delivers AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service, providing secure private mobile networks and deterministic 5G connectivity for enterprise AI workloads. Its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), distributed edge running a 5G core and AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device and robot fleets (Mobile Zones) to give autonomous robots, cameras, and edge devices ultra-reliable, ultra-low-latency connectivity across manufacturing, warehousing, higher education, and energy environments. Highway 9 exposes Mobile Center streaming APIs for orchestration, telemetry, device management, alerting, and analytics, though the full specification is available only through its partner portal for signed partners. The company is backed by Mayfield and was added to the API Evangelist network as an enriched provider profile.

providers.name: Iontra
providers.description: Iontra Inc. is a Denver, Colorado battery technology company that develops proprietary Charge-Control technology for rechargeable lithium batteries. Founded in 2013 and publicly launched in 2022, Iontra applies electrodynamic sensing and signal processing during charging to suppress lithium plating, dendrite growth and SEI-layer expansion, claiming up to 4x cycle life, 2x faster charging, improved cold-weather charging and better safety without changing cell chemistry. The technology is chemistry agnostic across Li-ion, Li-metal, Li-S, solid-state and Na-ion cells, and is delivered to OEMs as custom charging algorithm "recipes" flashed onto an application-specific microcontroller, or as a software-only library. Iontra closed a $45M Series C led by Volta Energy Technologies to launch an integrated RISC-V charge-control and fuel-gauge MCU. Iontra is an embedded/silicon company: it publishes no public web API, no OpenAPI, and no public SDK packages — its SDK is firmware delivered to OEM customers through a login-gated Document Portal under commercial engagement.

providers.name: ivymark
providers.description: ivymark was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found that the repo domain ivymark.com 301-redirects in full to www.ivy.co — Ivy, a business-management platform for interior designers (product sourcing, proposals, invoices, client mood boards, project and time tracking, online payments, and reporting), now operated as part of Houzz Pro. No public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery surface was found on either ivymark.com or ivy.co, so no API artifacts could be produced this round; only the identity, verified marketing links, and a live domain-security probe are recorded.

providers.name: Knoetic
providers.description: Knoetic is an HR technology company that operates CPOHQ, a platform built for Chief People Officers and senior people-function executives. The product combines three surfaces: a private, invite-only community of 3,000+ Chief People Officers (one member per company) who exchange confidential playbooks and benchmarks; an AI "Chief of Staff" that delivers personalized morning briefings and monitors market and talent trends; and a suite of workflow-specific AI agents for people analytics, performance insight, and peer benchmarking across the people function. The company was founded as Knoetic around a people-analytics product and has since consolidated its public brand on CPOHQ — knoetic.com now redirects to cpohq.com, while the customer application remains at app.knoetic.com. Knoetic has raised $50M+ from Accel, EQT Ventures, Menlo Ventures and angel investors. As of this enrichment pass Knoetic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; the platform is a closed B2B SaaS offering sold to enterprise people teams. It does publish a Vanta-hosted trust center and displays a SOC 2 Type II attestation.

providers.name: Kuraseru
providers.description: KURASERU, INC. (株式会社KURASERU) is a Kobe-based Japanese technology company building digital-transformation software for the elderly-care industry. Founded in October 2017 by Taiki Kawahara, a former care worker and hospital medical social worker, the company describes its business as DX promotion for care-related services and system development. Its stated mission is to use technology to lift the administrative burden off care work so that caregivers can spend more of their time with the people they care for, addressing Japan's super-aging society, chronic caregiver shortages, and high turnover. KURASERU is ISO/IEC 27001 certified (IS 716039) and is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this is a company profile rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Lagou
providers.description: Lagou (拉勾招聘) is a Chinese online recruitment platform operated by Beijing Lagou Network Technology Co., Ltd., focused on hiring for the internet and technology sector. It matches software engineers, product managers, designers and other digital-economy professionals with employers across major Chinese cities, publishing verified job listings alongside a browseable directory of hiring companies. Around the core job board it runs Lagou Enterprise (easy.lagou.com) for employer-side recruiting, Lagou Campus (xiaoyuan.lagou.com) for graduate hiring, and Lagou Education (kaiwu.lagou.com) for professional-skills courses. Lagou was surfaced through the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. It publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation — open.lagou.com carries a "Lagou Open Platform" title but serves only a stub page — so this profile captures the company's public web and security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Liquid AI
providers.description: Liquid AI is an MIT spinoff developing Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) - a new class of generative models based on liquid neural networks. Offers LFM2 (2.6B / 8B-A1B / 24B-A2B) and LFM2.5 (350M / 1.2B variants) with text, vision, audio, and thinking modes. The LEAP platform enables LFM customization and on-device deployment.

providers.name: Markt Pilot (aka MP)
providers.description: MARKT-PILOT GmbH is a German software company (registered in Beilstein, business address Stuttgart, with a US office in Chicago) that provides a unified pricing performance platform for industrial manufacturers. Its flagship product, MP ONE, combines an Intelligence Engine (real-time competitor and market data with AI-powered cross-reference part matching), a Decision Engine (cost-plus, market-based, and attribute-based pricing workflows), and a Performance Engine (portfolio, revenue, and margin analysis with executive dashboards). MARKT-PILOT serves 200+ manufacturers across agriculture, construction and mining, machine tooling, packaging, and industrial equipment, helping them move from static annual spare-parts pricing to dynamic, data-driven pricing. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company operates a marketing site, blog, and a hosted (Better Stack) status page, but publishes no public developer/API surface: no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, well-known discovery endpoints, or client SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Mia
providers.description: Mia (Mia Labs, Inc.) is an AI-powered phone agent platform built specifically for automotive dealerships. Its conversational voice AI answers calls 24/7 across sales, service, reception, and outbound operations, handling appointment scheduling, service booking, lead capture, and recall/follow-up outreach over phone, SMS, and voice with automatic multi-language detection. Mia integrates with major dealership platforms and DMS/CRM systems including Tekion, CDK, Reynolds & Reynolds, and Dealertrack, and reports use across 350+ dealerships. The company raised a $20M Series A (roughly $29M total) backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Permanent Capital Ventures. This profile currently covers the company identity; no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Min Doktor
providers.description: Min Doktor is a Swedish digital healthcare provider (operated by MD International AB) offering online primary care through its mobile app and web service. Founded in 2013 as one of Sweden's first digital-first care providers, it connects patients with doctors, psychologists and nurses for consultations, prescriptions, referrals and vaccinations, and also runs white-label care services for partners such as Skandia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of EQT Ventures. Min Doktor operates as a consumer/patient-facing service and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable public security, identity and compliance footprint.

providers.name: Mundi
providers.description: Mundi is a digital cross-border trade finance platform for exporters, primarily connecting Mexican exporters with US importers. It provides non-recourse international factoring (invoice advances up to $10M USD / $200M MXN with rates from 0.9% per month), foreign-exchange spot and hedging across 100+ currencies, purchase-order and revolving-line financing, multi-currency virtual US accounts and international payments/collections, and digital cargo insurance. Backed by Speedinvest and Union Square Ventures, Mundi operates a customer web application but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Nile
providers.description: Nile is a San Jose, California enterprise networking company delivering an AI-native Secure Network as a Service (NaaS). Founded in 2018 by former Cisco executives Pankaj Patel and John Chambers (chairman), Nile replaces traditional campus and branch LAN/Wi-Fi hardware-and-license procurement with a subscription-based, outcome-guaranteed wired and wireless network stack delivered as a service. The Nile Access Service combines its purpose-built Zero Trust Fabric (switches, access points, gateways, and sensors) with cloud-based autonomous operations, the Nile Services Cloud, Nile AI, Nile Nav, and Nile Digital Twin to plan, deploy, monitor, and self-heal enterprise networks. The platform emphasizes built-in Zero Trust segmentation, continuous performance guarantees (coverage, capacity, availability), and consumption-based pricing — marketed against 60%+ breach reduction, 99%+ ticket reduction, ~3x faster change management, and ~40% TCO savings versus traditional enterprise networking. Nile does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or Terraform provider; its programmable surface is limited to a closed admin/portal API and outbound webhooks used for documented integrations with ServiceNow (ticket and alert webhooks), Splunk HEC, CrowdStrike, Zscaler ZIA, Microsoft Entra (SCIM), Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Global Secure Access, Palo Alto Networks, Forescout (device inventory API), SecureW2, Aruba ClearPass, VeloCloud, Graphiant, Hamina, and Ekahau. Nile is available through the AWS Marketplace as a SaaS subscription.

providers.name: Onafriq
providers.description: Onafriq (formerly MFS Africa) is a pan-African digital payments network headquartered in London with operating entities across Mauritius, Ghana, Nigeria, Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda, the DRC, and the UK. Founded by CEO Dare Okoudjou, Onafriq operates what it calls "Africa's largest digital payments gateway" — a network of networks connecting roughly one billion mobile money wallets and 500 million bank accounts across 40+ African countries through 2,000+ cross-border corridors. The platform exposes a REST API surface for partners including Money Transfer Organizations (MTOs), Mobile Network Operators (MNOs), banks, NGOs, governments, and enterprises. Core developer products include Async Payouts (the recommended path for MTOs and bulk disbursement partners, with webhook-based status updates), Sync Payouts (custom-built for MNOs requiring synchronous responses), Sync Bank Transfers, Collections APIs (Payins) for receiving funds from cards, cash agents, and mobile wallets, a Contacts API for managing payer/payee records, a Get Rates API for daily foreign exchange rates, and Async Webhooks for Instant Payment Notifications. Two distinct portal endpoints serve domestic (api.mfsafrica.com/api) and cross-border (mfsafrica.beyonicpartners.com/api) workloads. Beyond cross-border remittance and disbursement, Onafriq operates Baxi — a Nigerian agent banking network of 460,000+ agents across all 36 states with its own Virtual Account, Fingerprint, and Account Debit APIs — plus card issuance and processing for physical/virtual prepaid programs and multi-currency treasury services. Onafriq has raised $200M+ in Series C funding from Vitruvian Partners, AXA Investment Managers, and Goodwell, and holds 16 payment licenses including FSC (Mauritius) and FCA (UK) authorization. The legacy MFS Africa developer hub (developer.mfsafrica.com) remains the canonical reference documentation, with a newer developers.onafriq.com portal reflecting the post-rebrand identity.

providers.name: Operator Framework
providers.description: The Operator Framework is a CNCF incubating toolkit for building and managing Kubernetes Operators. It includes the Operator SDK for scaffolding and building operators using Go, Ansible, or Helm, the Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) for installing and managing operators on clusters, and OperatorHub for discovering and sharing operators. The framework codifies operational knowledge into software.

providers.name: Pathai
providers.description: PathAI is a healthcare artificial-intelligence company transforming pathology through machine learning. Its AISight Image Management System (IMS) and the AISight Link open API deliver AI-assisted disease detection, biomarker quantification, fields-of-interest and AI Impressions, and laboratory workflow integration for pathologists, hospital and reference labs, and biopharma research partners. AISight Link is an enterprise interoperability surface that connects AISight with third-party AI algorithms and Laboratory Information Systems (LIS/LIMS) over REST and HL7; PathAI does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. The company is ISO 27001 certified and operates a vulnerability disclosure program. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc.

providers.name: PC Financial
providers.description: PC Financial (President's Choice Financial) is the financial-services brand of Canadian grocery giant Loblaw Companies Limited. Its personal banking and Mastercard credit-card products are issued by President's Choice Bank, a federally chartered Schedule I bank and CDIC member, while insurance is offered through PC Financial Insurance. The digital-first, branchless brand centers on the no-fee PC Money Account (a Mastercard-network everyday spending account launched September 2020), a line of PC Financial and PC World Elite Mastercard credit cards, and deep integration with the PC Optimum loyalty program across Loblaw's grocery, pharmacy, and retail banners. Consumer banking (chequing, savings, mortgages) was transferred to CIBC's Simplii Financial in 2017, so PC Financial today is a rewards-linked digital banking arm rather than a full-service bank. In December 2025 Equitable Bank (EQB) agreed to acquire PC Financial from Loblaw for roughly $800 million. On open finance, PC Financial runs NO public first-party developer portal or API; Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer account access today is aggregator/screen-scraping-based via providers such as Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard). The bank supports Interac e-Transfer on the PC Money Account as shared payments-rail participation.

providers.name: Plural Finance
providers.description: Plural Finance is a financial operating system for infrastructure — a programmable execution layer that automates ownership, payments, compliance, and reporting across the lifecycle of infrastructure and energy assets. Its AssetOS platform tokenizes infrastructure assets such as distributed renewables, data centers, public-private partnerships, and electricity sales contracts, so institutional and individual investors can underwrite, monitor, and trade projects, with smart-contract execution of capital contributions and distributions and embedded regulatory controls. The company holds broker-dealer licensing and is backed by Paradigm. Plural currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is through its institutional web application.

providers.name: Precision Neuroscience
providers.description: Precision Neuroscience is a New York City brain-computer interface company founded in 2021 by Benjamin Rapoport, Michael Mager, Demetrios Papageorgiou and Mark Hettick, with additional sites in Santa Clara, California and Addison, Texas. Its product is the Layer 7 Cortical Interface, a thin-film microelectrode array that lies on the surface of the cortex rather than penetrating brain tissue, and is designed to be removable and upgradable. The array received FDA 510(k) clearance for recording, monitoring and stimulating on the brain surface for implantation durations of up to 30 days, and the company reports 95+ clinical study participants across 15+ hospital partnerships — Mount Sinai, Penn Medicine, Johns Hopkins, Mass General Brigham, Northwestern, Emory, Barrow Neurological Institute and others — plus a strategic partnership with Medtronic. Precision sells a regulated medical device, not software services. It runs no developer program: no public API, SDK, webhooks, developer portal or machine-readable specification is published anywhere on its domain. Its only public engineering surface is a verified GitHub organization whose single public repository is an Apache-2.0 research notebook accompanying a 2025 neural-decoding result.

providers.name: Presto
providers.description: Presto Charging (Presto) is an electric-vehicle charging platform that aggregates access to 180,000+ public chargers across 20+ North American networks — including EVgo, ChargePoint, Blink, BP Pulse, and Flo — behind a single mobile app, payment method, and account. For drivers it offers price comparison, real-time charger availability, and a unified charging experience on iOS and Android. For fleets and enterprises it delivers charge management, granular usage data, and white-label products so operators can "manage charging like they manage fuel." For charging networks it drives utilization and station profitability. Presto exposes OCPI-compliant, mobile-first APIs and SDKs so fleet-solution and mobility partners can embed public charging — including Plug and Charge and Autocharge — under their own brand. Backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Quip
providers.description: Quip is a Salesforce-owned collaborative productivity platform that combines documents, spreadsheets, chat, and tasks into a single workspace tightly integrated with the Salesforce CRM. It enables teams to embed live data, collaborate in real time, and automate workflows across deal collaboration, account planning, and sales operations. The Quip Automation API is a REST interface for creating and managing threads, documents, messages, folders, and users with OAuth 2.0 Bearer token authentication.

providers.name: QXO Building Products
providers.description: QXO is a publicly traded company focused on building a tech-forward leader in the building products distribution industry through acquisitions and operational improvements. QXO offers a suite of customer-facing APIs for ordering, pricing, account management, product catalog, delivery tracking, and invoicing.

providers.name: Rephrase.ai
providers.description: Rephrase.ai is a Bengaluru-based generative-AI startup whose text-to-video platform, Rephrase Studio, turns plain text scripts into videos of digital human avatars ("actors") that speak the script with lip-synced, natural voices. It exposed a Rephrase Studio API for programmatic video generation (list actors and voices, create and export videos, poll video status) secured with OAuth2 bearer tokens. Backed by Techstars, Rephrase.ai was acquired by Adobe in November 2023 and its technology folded into Adobe's video and generative-AI offerings; the standalone product hosts have since been decommissioned, though the legacy API reference remains hosted on ReadMe. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist for historical and enrichment purposes.

providers.name: Rover
providers.description: Rover is the world's largest online marketplace for pet care, connecting pet parents with sitters and dog walkers for boarding, house sitting, drop-in visits, doggy daycare, and dog walking. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Seattle, Rover was a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: ROVR) until Blackstone completed its acquisition of Rover Group for approximately $2.3 billion on February 27, 2024, taking the company private and delisting its stock. As of this catalog entry, Rover does NOT publish a public, documented developer API or a developer portal. Its platform is a closed consumer/provider marketplace; the only outward-facing integration program is a marketing affiliate program offered through third-party affiliate networks (Impact, CJ, Rakuten, Skimlinks, ShareASale, etc.), not a data/booking API. Programmatic access to Rover data today is only available via unofficial third-party web scrapers (e.g. Apify), which are outside Rover's supported surface. This entry is an honest stub documenting the absence of a public API; it should be revisited if Rover launches a partner or developer API.

providers.name: Sanlo
providers.description: Sanlo is a multi-platform payments and monetization platform built specifically for game developers and studios. Its products let studios run live ops and accept payments outside the walled gardens of the major app stores to reduce platform commission fees: Webshop Builder (a full-stack direct-to-consumer web shop), Web Checkout (accept payments on any website, web shop, or web game), and Unity Checkout (native iOS/Android in-game checkout for Unity titles via a first-party SDK and API, with one-click checkout, fully customizable UI, and creator-code support). Card and payment collection is powered by Adyen underneath. Sanlo also offers game funding to help studios finance user acquisition and growth. The company is backed by Index Ventures and other gaming-focused investors.

providers.name: Slice
providers.description: Slice is an Indian consumer fintech and small finance bank, founded in 2016 as SlicePay by Rajan Bajaj and headquartered between Bengaluru (corporate) and Guwahati (registered). The company originally built a buy-now-pay-later product and a prepaid-card-plus-credit-line offering aimed at students and young professionals — pitched as a credit-card alternative for India's Gen Z — and at its peak was reportedly issuing over 300,000 prepaid cards per month before RBI's 2022 restrictions on credit-linked PPI products forced a pivot. In October 2023 Slice announced a merger with the regulated North East Small Finance Bank (NESFB), the first fintech-into-bank merger in India; the merger received RBI approval in October 2023, CCI approval in March 2024 and NCLT (Guwahati) approval in August 2024, completed on October 27, 2024, and the combined entity was rebranded as Slice Small Finance Bank in May 2025. Today Slice operates a consumer mobile-first neobank — savings accounts, fixed deposits, UPI, a Slice credit card and rewards — alongside a merchant-facing payments stack exposed through a Merchant API (api.nebank.com) covering bank-account validation, payouts, pay-in/collect, refunds, virtual accounts, balance, transactions and webhook notifications. As of late 2024 the company had raised approximately $387M from investors including Tiger Global, Insight Partners and Blume Ventures.

providers.name: Splice
providers.description: Splice is a New York-based music creation platform serving producers, songwriters, and audio creators. Its core offerings are Splice Sounds, a catalog of millions of 100% royalty-free samples, one-shots, loops, MIDI patterns, and presets sold through a credit-based subscription; Splice INSTRUMENT, a creator-first virtual instrument with monthly free drops and unlimited premium presets via subscription; and a Rent-to-Own Plugins marketplace offering pay-as-you-go full-license access to 130+ professional VST/AU/AAX plugins from third-party vendors such as Xfer (Serum 2), Arturia (V Collection 11 Pro), Spitfire Audio (Abbey Road Two), and XLN Audio (RC-20). Splice ships a desktop app, a mobile app, the Splice Sounds Plugin (beta) for in-DAW browsing, and native integrations for Ableton Live 12.3+, Studio One Pro 7, Studio Pro 8+, and Pro Tools 2025.6+. The revenue model is consumer subscriptions (Sounds+ $12.99/mo, Creator $19.99/mo with 200 credits, Creator+ $39.99/mo with 500 credits, INSTRUMENT $12.99/mo) plus rent-to-own plugin payments. Splice does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or partner program; its GitHub organization at github.com/splice contains internal tooling, GitHub Actions, audio engineering exercises, and forks rather than externally consumable APIs.

providers.name: Terminal Logistics
providers.description: Terminal Industries (Terminal Logistics) is the company behind the Terminal Yard Operating System (YOS), an AI-native, fully-integrated platform for yard operations across logistics and supply chain. It unifies gate management, carrier risk assessment and driver ID, dispatch and spotter orchestration, yard visibility, load verification, carrier appointments, and end-to-end yard security from the gate to the dock, using computer vision and agentic AI. It serves third-party logistics, retail and grocery, consumer packaged goods, refrigerated warehousing, contract carriers, manufacturing facilities, and drop lots. Backed by 8vc. No public developer API is currently published; this profile captures the company's public web, security, and status surface.

providers.name: Tienda Pago
providers.description: Tienda Pago is a fintech lender providing working capital and short-term inventory financing to small retailers - bodegas, convenience stores, bars and restaurants - across Mexico and Peru. Operating as a non-regulated financial entity (SOFOM E.N.R.), it offers three core products: LanaYa instant cash deposits, buy-now-pay-later 7-day terms for buying inventory from distributors, and no-upfront-cash mobile phone top-up (recargas). The platform reports serving over 80,000 businesses and more than 18 million families through mobile apps and a web onboarding portal. It is backed by QED Investors. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface has been identified.

providers.name: UL Solutions
providers.description: UL Solutions is a global leader in applied safety science, providing testing, inspection, certification, advisory, and software solutions to help customers innovate safely, demonstrate compliance, and bring trusted products to market. The company offers software products such as ULTRUS and ComplianceWire, customer portals (myUL, Product iQ), and the Marks and Labels Hub. UL Solutions does not currently expose a public developer-facing API portal with open documentation.

providers.name: Vectren (CenterPoint Energy)
providers.description: Vectren Corporation was a Fortune 1000 energy holding company headquartered in Evansville (Newburgh), Indiana providing regulated natural gas and electric distribution services to customers in Indiana and Ohio, along with non-regulated infrastructure services and energy efficiency programs. Vectren merged with CenterPoint Energy on February 1, 2019 in a $6 billion transaction, becoming part of the combined company which serves over 7 million metered customers across Arkansas, Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Ohio, Oklahoma, and Texas. Vectren customer-facing portals continue to operate at vectren.com redirecting to CenterPoint Energy services.

providers.name: Vinted
providers.description: Vinted is a European consumer-to-consumer (C2C) online marketplace for buying and selling secondhand clothes, shoes, accessories, and other lifestyle items, operating across web and mobile apps in dozens of markets. Founded in Vilnius, Lithuania, it is one of Europe's largest secondhand fashion platforms and is backed by Accel, Insight Partners, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Vinted does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public identity, legal, and security (security.txt / domain-security) surfaces.

providers.name: Wexler
providers.description: Wexler AI operates a Fact Intelligence Platform built for legal disputes and investigations. Its AI system, including an assistant named Kim, extracts, structures, and verifies facts across large document sets with source attribution, surfaces inconsistencies and contradictions in evidence, builds chronological case timelines, and produces confidence-scored, testable facts grounded in source materials. It is used by enterprise and AmLaw100 law firms for early case assessment. Wexler currently exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Wisq
providers.description: Wisq is an AI platform for human resources that automates HR service management, HR operations, and employee relations. Its conversational AI HR agent, Harper, answers employee requests across chat, email, Slack, Teams, SMS, and mobile, while its proprietary HR Language Model (HRLM) provides HR-specific reasoning, aiming to resolve the majority of routine HR cases without a human in the loop. Founded by Jim Barnett and Chih-Po Wen (formerly of Glint), Wisq is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Shasta Ventures, and True Ventures. Wisq operates a private, login-gated product and publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Womaness
providers.description: Womaness is a women-founded midlife wellness brand created to modernize aging for women and to help them navigate the phases their bodies move through around menopause. The direct-to-consumer company sells clean, estrogen-free, doctor-approved and clinically tested skincare, supplements, sexual-health and menopause-support products (including Let's Neck serum, Melt for You inserts and Daily V Soothe) through a Shopify-hosted online store and select retail partners. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a consumer e-commerce brand with no first-party public developer API surface.

providers.name: Yardi Propware
providers.description: Yardi Propware was the original flagship property management software by Yardi Systems, first released in 1984. It was an early desktop-based real estate management platform for residential and commercial property accounting, leasing, and management. Yardi has since evolved its platform into cloud-based offerings including Yardi Voyager and Yardi Breeze. No publicly accessible developer portal or documented REST API has been confirmed for Yardi Propware specifically; Yardi's modern integrations are managed through the Yardi Interface Partnership Program.

providers.name: Zeta
providers.description: Zeta is a next-generation banking and payment card processing platform for banks and financial institutions, offering a cloud-native omnistack to launch and manage credit, debit, prepaid, BNPL, and fleet card programs alongside loans and deposits. Its product suite spans Tachyon (core processing and real-time APIs and events), Neutrino (digital app experiences), Elena (conversational AI), Saturn (servicing and back-office operations), Luminos (engagement and rewards), and Zeus (data and analytics). Founded by Bhavin Turakhia and Ramki Gaddipati and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Zeta processes 25+ million cards across seven countries for institutions including HDFC Bank, Pluxee, and Sparrow. Zeta's platform is delivered to enterprise banking partners; its APIs are partner-gated rather than published on a public developer portal.

providers.name: Zoetis
providers.description: Zoetis is the world's leading animal health company, dedicated to discovering, developing, manufacturing, and commercializing medicines, vaccines, diagnostics, and technologies for animals. The company operates in over 100 countries and provides digital connectivity solutions that integrate veterinary diagnostics, reference laboratory services, and practice management systems through the Vetscan platform, enabling bidirectional communication between point-of-care analyzers and veterinary practice information management systems (PIMS).

providers.name: Zomma
providers.description: Zomma (Zomma Labs) is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building AI agents that automate repetitive back-office operations for investment firms — hedge funds, asset managers, and fintech companies. Rather than integrating through traditional APIs, its computer-use agents perceive and operate existing portals, desktop applications, and PDFs the way a human would (clicking, reading, typing) to handle reconciliation, client onboarding, KYC, and investor reporting, with human approval required before any submission. Zomma also markets a developer-facing computer-use API ("plug Hermes, Claude, or your own agent into our API") that is currently waitlist / pre-general availability with no public specification, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: AMERCO
providers.description: AMERCO, operating as U-Haul Holding Company, is America's largest do-it-yourself moving and storage company. The company provides truck and trailer rentals, self-storage facilities, moving supplies, and portable moving and storage containers through its U-Haul brand. AMERCO operates the Moving Help marketplace connecting consumers to moving service providers, the U-Haul Self-Storage Affiliate Network, and WebSelfStorage management software for independent storage facilities. It also operates AMERITAS Life Insurance and Oxford Life Insurance subsidiaries.

providers.name: Biostate AI
providers.description: Biostate AI is a Houston-based precision-health biotechnology company combining proprietary wet-lab chemistry with generative AI to make RNA and DNA sequencing dramatically cheaper and more accessible. Its BIRT (Barcode-Integrated Reverse Transcription) plus PERD (Probes for Excess RNA Depletion) platform delivers Total RNA sequencing from around $60 per sample, and its N-Act and RNAstate AI models turn omics data into clinical insights for autoimmune, cardiovascular, and cancer diagnostics. The company operates a cloud data lake for AI-ready omics data and runs research partnerships across the U.S., India, and China. As of this profile Biostate publishes a marketing and publications site plus open research model repositories on GitHub, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK client library, or developer portal.

providers.name: Cactos
providers.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.

providers.name: Chief Human Capital Officers Council
providers.description: The Chief Human Capital Officers (CHCO) Council is the principal interagency forum to advise and coordinate the activities of members on matters of modernization of human resources (HR) systems, improved quality of human resources information, and legislation affecting human resources operations and organizations across the U.S. federal government. Established under the Chief Human Capital Officers Act of 2002 (5 U.S.C. 1401-1402), the Council is chaired by the Director of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) with the Deputy Director for Management at OMB serving as Vice Chair. The CHCO Council coordinates federal human capital management strategy, supports the Federal HR workforce, advances workforce planning and talent acquisition, and oversees performance management, employee engagement, learning and development, and HR policy implementation across departments and agencies.

providers.name: Chief Information Officers Council
providers.description: The Chief Information Officers Council (CIOC) is the principal interagency forum for improving agency practices related to the design, acquisition, development, modernization, use, sharing, and performance of federal information resources. Established by Executive Order 13011 in 1996 and codified in the E-Government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. 3603), the Council is comprised of the Chief Information Officers and Deputy CIOs of executive branch agencies, the Federal CIO at OMB (who serves as Chair), the Federal Chief Information Security Officer, and the Administrator for Electronic Government. The CIOC develops recommendations for OMB IT policy, identifies opportunities to improve federal IT performance, coordinates multi-agency IT initiatives such as cybersecurity and cloud adoption, supports federal IT workforce development, and disseminates effective IT management practices across the federal government. The Council publishes guidance, playbooks, and resources through cio.gov and councils.gov.

providers.name: CIBC
providers.description: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) is a Schedule I domestic chartered bank and one of Canada's Big Six, formed in 1961 through the merger of the Canadian Bank of Commerce and the Imperial Bank of Canada and headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Serving roughly eleven million personal, business, commercial, wealth, and capital-markets clients across Personal & Business Banking, Wealth Management, and Capital Markets, CIBC is a participant in the shared Canadian rails, including Interac e-Transfer and Payments Canada settlement systems. Canada has no operational open-banking mandate today: the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement, overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), is not yet live, so access remains voluntary and fragmented. CIBC runs no first-party public developer portal (developer.cibc.com does not resolve) and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger specifications. Consumer-permissioned data access is aggregator-mediated: CIBC signed a tokenized data-access agreement with U.S. aggregator MX (announced August 2022, MX's first in Canada) to let clients share financial data with third-party apps without exposing banking credentials, and its accounts are also reachable through Plaid (Assets, Auth, Balance). Corporate connectivity is offered through CIBC SWIFT Corporate Access (SCA) file exchange rather than a public REST API, so CIBC's honest public API surface today is aggregator-mediated only, pending the coming Consumer-Driven Banking regime.

providers.name: Datalot
providers.description: Datalot (now operating under parent company Centerfield Insurance Services) is an analytics-driven digital customer-acquisition and live lead/call marketplace platform for the insurance industry, spanning auto, home, life, health, Medicare, and commercial lines. It runs digital demand-generation campaigns, qualifies consumers in a real-time marketplace, and routes them by data to carriers and agents, adding agent-presence and telephony management, TCPA/regulatory compliance tooling, and secondary-market handling for unmatched consumers. Named carrier clients include Liberty Mutual, Allstate, Farmers, Progressive, Travelers, Aetna, and Humana. The company is SOC 2 certified. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners; the customer-facing surface is an authenticated carrier/agent portal at app.datalot.com with no public API, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Defense Contract Audit Agency
providers.description: The Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA), under the authority, direction, and control of the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller), provides audit and financial advisory services to Department of Defense and other federal entities responsible for acquisition and contract administration. DCAA publishes guidance, audit programs, and reports through its website but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Defense Contract Management Agency
providers.description: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) is the Department of Defense component that works directly with defense suppliers to help ensure that DoD, federal, and allied government supplies and services are delivered on time, at projected cost, and meet performance requirements. DCMA performs contract administration, quality assurance, and earned value management oversight, but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Defense Finance and Accounting Service
providers.description: The Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) is the agency within the Department of Defense responsible for paying members of the U.S. military, DoD civilian employees, contractors, and annuitants, as well as providing finance and accounting services to DoD components and other federal agencies. DFAS exposes member-facing self-service portals such as myPay but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Dominion Dynamics
providers.description: Dominion Dynamics Inc. is a Canadian defence-technology company (Kanata/Ottawa, Ontario) building the autonomy stack for the Arctic and other extreme, infrastructure-constrained operating environments. It develops integrated autonomy, edge sensing, communications, and command-and-control systems for defence, security, and critical infrastructure. Its AuraNet platform is a peer-to-peer sensor mesh that fuses EO/IR/SAR imagery, SIGINT/EW/RF signals, telemetry, and structured reporting into a unified local intelligence stream that interoperates with existing allied C2 architectures, and its Aurion product is an open-source government procurement intelligence platform built on Canadian federal open data. Founded by Anduril alum Eliot Pence, the company raised a $139M CAD Series A (2026) led by Georgian. This profile currently has no public developer/API surface; the entry captures the company identity, security.txt, and llms.txt the company publishes.

providers.name: Earnix
providers.description: Earnix provides an AI orchestration system (Earnix AIOS) purpose-built for insurance and banking decisioning. The platform unifies pricing, an enterprise rating engine, automated underwriting, and real-time customer engagement so insurers and financial institutions can price smarter, underwrite faster, and engage customers better. Earnix serves 100+ leading insurers worldwide, processing billions of transactions annually and compressing rate creation from months to days. Earnix is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Earnix is an enterprise B2B vendor with no public self-serve developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Efflux Systems
providers.description: Efflux (Efflux Systems, Inc.) is a Baltimore, Maryland cybersecurity company founded in 2014 that operates a near real-time asset intelligence and attack-surface platform. Efflux delivers fresh intelligence about the assets of organizations, networks, and services — offered as a one-time Asset Map, scheduled monitoring, or on-demand custom scanning. Its differentiator is radical transparency: rather than opaque risk scores and surface-level abstractions, Efflux records and exposes every scan it runs, every asset it discovers, and every attribution it makes, so teams can see what was found, how it was discovered, and why it matters — raw information and formatted insights side by side. Data is accessible via export, download, share, and a programmatic API. The company is backed by 500 Global, Granite Hill Capital Partners, TEDCO, and Three Tree Ventures, and is currently in early access with a public waitlist.

providers.name: Emidat
providers.description: Emidat GmbH is a Munich-based climate technology company building product intelligence infrastructure for the construction industry. Its SaaS platform lets construction material manufacturers create verified Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), run Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs), and produce Digital Product Passports (DPPs) at scale. Emidat ingests plant, ERP, and energy-management data through integrations, performs intelligent data matching, and generates ISO-compliant, verified EPDs in as little as a day rather than the typical six to twelve months. The platform also surfaces environmental-impact hotspots so manufacturers can find emission-reduction opportunities and turn sustainability data into business value. Related tools include the public EPD Database and Emidat Atlas.

providers.name: Eton Solutions
providers.description: Eton Solutions, L.P. is a Morrisville, North Carolina wealth-technology company that builds AtlasFive, a purpose-built ERP platform for single-family offices, multi-family offices, private funds and the ultra-high-net-worth families they serve. AtlasFive consolidates general ledger and partnership/fund/trust accounting, investment management and performance, bill pay and transaction processing, tax workflow, CRM and document management onto one data core, and aggregates positions and transactions from more than 1,500 banks and custodians via direct electronic feeds, portal scrapes, PDF statement extraction and partner aggregators. The EtonAI product line layers a knowledge graph and generative-AI assistants over that core. Integration is delivered through customer-scoped Reporting APIs and a Power BI connector rather than a public developer program: Eton Solutions publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK or sandbox as of August 2026. The company does publish a substantial compliance posture — ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management), ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II, with GDPR and CCPA alignment — and the platform is hosted on Microsoft Azure. Founded out of the multi-family office Eton Advisors and led by CEO Robert Mallernee with Executive Chairman Satyen Patel, with additional offices in Dubai and Bengaluru.

providers.name: Experiment
providers.description: Experiment is an online crowdfunding platform for scientific research that connects scientists directly with backers who fund individual studies. Researchers across biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, computer science, paleontology, economics, engineering, and neuroscience post projects with goals and budgets; the public pledges funds, follows lab notes, and shares in the discoveries. Experiment (formerly Microryza) also supports university institutions and dedicated funding programs, and publishes results and updates back to funders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, slow-ventures, and y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a live consumer website but no public developer API, docs, or well-known surface.

providers.name: Federal Trade Commission
providers.description: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is a U.S. federal agency that enforces antitrust and consumer protection laws affecting virtually every area of commerce. The FTC publishes developer-facing data products and APIs through ftc.gov/developer and partner platforms, including the National Do Not Call Registry telemarketer access program and the Consumer Sentinel Network of consumer complaint data shared with law enforcement.

providers.name: Formic
providers.description: Formic is a Chicago, Illinois-based Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) company founded in 2020 by Saman Farid that delivers full-service industrial automation to American manufacturers on a pay-per-hour, fixed monthly subscription model with no capital expenditure. Formic specializes in end-of-line manufacturing operations — palletizing, case packing, and robotic pallet wrapping — and pairs deployed robots with a 24/7 remote monitoring, support, and field-service operation. The company's software stack includes Formic Core, an embedded operating system that abstracts motion, vision, sensing, and real-time coordination across heterogeneous industrial robot hardware (Fanuc, ABB, Kuka, Doosan) behind unified control interfaces; Formic Cortex; the Colony 2.0 fleet dashboard; FAST configuration tools; and Formic Production Intelligence (FPI), a manufacturer-facing analytics surface. Formic has raised more than $86M across rounds led by Lux Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and other investors, and works through a network of 100+ system-integrator partners with 500+ systems deployed. Formic's revenue model is the RaaS subscription itself; there is no public developer API, no published SDKs, and no public customer-portal API documentation. Formic Core's "unified APIs" are internal abstractions used by Formic engineers and integrator partners to drive robot hardware — they are not exposed to manufacturers or third-party developers.

providers.name: Labcorp
providers.description: Labcorp helps patients, providers, organizations, and biopharma companies guide vital healthcare decisions every day. Labcorp supports HL7 / FHIR-based integration for laboratory orders and results exchange with electronic health record (EHR) systems, but does not publish a fully open public developer portal; access is granted through health-system and biopharma integration agreements.

providers.name: Meadow
providers.description: Meadow is a financial technology company delivering modern student financial services to colleges and universities. Its platform spans the full student financial lifecycle — Meadow Price (a mobile, SAI-compliant net price calculator), Meadow Pay (student billing and payments with automated workflows), Meadow Pre (pre-collections for recovering unpaid tuition), and Meadow Checkout (campus-wide collection of non-tuition fees). Meadow helps institutions improve enrollment, retention, and payment outcomes from application through graduation. Backed by Matrix Partners and Y Combinator. No public API or developer platform is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Monitaur
providers.description: Monitaur is an enterprise AI governance platform that helps regulated organizations manage machine learning and AI responsibly across the full model lifecycle. Its software lets teams define enterprise-wide AI governance policies, manage and monitor model performance for drift and bias, and automate model validation, risk assessment, stress testing, and vendor governance at scale. Monitaur is built for regulated industries such as insurance and financial services, delivering audit-ready documentation and compliance reporting. A Techstars-backed company, Monitaur has been recognized as a Gartner Magic Quadrant Visionary and is SOC 2 Type II certified. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Mooncard
providers.description: Mooncard is a French corporate expense-management platform that pairs a smart payment card, a mobile app, and accounting-automation software so finance teams can handle business spending end to end without manual data entry. It automates expense reports, VAT recovery, and mileage and per-diem calculations, then syncs transactions into accounting systems such as Sage, Cegid, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, Exact Online, and Agicap. Mooncard also runs a developer program that offers API access plus a sandbox environment, though the API reference and OpenAPI are gated behind a developer-portal login and are not publicly discoverable.

providers.name: Nava
providers.description: Nava (Nava Benefits) is a modern employee benefits brokerage that pairs benefits advisors with AI-powered technology to cut administrative work, simplify renewals, and support employees around the clock. Its HQ platform helps HR teams manage benefits and renewals while an employee app acts as a 24/7 digital benefits concierge for workers and their families, integrating with BenAdmin and carrier systems. Backed by Homebrew, Nava positions itself as an alternative to traditional brokers focused on cost savings and administrative relief. No public developer program, API, or OpenAPI surface is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Office Luv
providers.description: OfficeLuv is office management and purchasing software that centralizes all of a workplace's ordering into a single platform. It aggregates dozens of vendors and thousands of products (supplies, snacks, cleaning supplies, groceries, and more) into one unified marketplace with consolidated invoicing, spend analytics and reporting, multi-user approval workflows, employee stipends for remote and in-office staff, and optional on-site service for program design, pricing negotiation, and restocking. Customers include Wayfair, Braze, Glassdoor, Hulu, and Upwork. Office Luv was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The product is delivered as a private SaaS web application (app.officeluv.com); no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published at this time.

providers.name: On the Beach
providers.description: On the Beach Group plc (LSE: OTB) is a Manchester-headquartered online travel agent and the United Kingdom's largest online short-haul beach package holiday specialist, founded in 2004 by Simon Cooper and registered at Aeroworks, 5 Adair Street, Manchester M1 2NQ. It sits on the demand side of the travel distribution chain: an asset-light dynamic packager that buys real-time seats from 42 airlines and hotel inventory from bedbanks and direct hotel contracts, combines them into ATOL-protected packages, and sells them direct to UK and Republic of Ireland consumers through onthebeach.co.uk, sunshine.co.uk and its mobile app. FY25 total transaction value was GBP 1.25bn across 1.7 million customers.
