Fleek operates a consumer/reseller storefront (built on Shopify) and a separate vendor onboarding flow for suppliers; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced from the HV Capital portfolio and enriched from Fleek's public web surface.

providers.name: FoodA
providers.description: Fooda is a Chicago-based workplace food-service marketplace that brings meals from local, independent restaurants directly to corporate offices, hospitals, universities, retail locations, and distribution centers. Its technology-enabled platform runs restaurant popup dining events, employer-paid meal programs, contactless lunch delivery, event catering and boxed lunches, coffee, pantry, and micro-market services, plus full cafeteria replacement under the Orange by Fooda brand. Fooda works with 2,000+ restaurant partners and serves upwards of ten million meals per year, using AI predictive modeling and machine learning to match restaurants to locations and schedule thousands of events. Sibling brands include Foodsby and Fooda for Restaurants. Fooda is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API or partner developer portal; this profile captures its public web presence and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Foresight
providers.description: Foresight is a predictive project-delivery platform for complex construction and infrastructure megaprojects, with a particular focus on data centers, government, and critical infrastructure. Founded by Dr. Atif Ansar and Igor Shifrin (Oxford) and headquartered in London, it layers on top of existing scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project and Excel to turn raw schedule data into forecasts, risk assessment, delay prediction, and portfolio-wide project assurance. The company reports managing $100B+ in mission-critical projects and is backed by Creandum and Macquarie Capital. Foresight is delivered as a SaaS web application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Freckle Education
providers.description: Freckle is an adaptive learning platform from Renaissance that delivers differentiated, standards-aligned math and English Language Arts (ELA) practice for K-12 students. Teachers assign work and monitor progress while students practice at their own level, with the platform adapting question difficulty to each learner across 70,000+ math questions and 1,000+ ELA passages. Administrators manage rosters and dashboards at the school and district level. Freckle is a school- and classroom-facing application acquired by Renaissance Learning; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal, so this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Freeport Markets
providers.description: Freeport Markets is a Y Combinator-backed fintech and crypto trading platform offering 24/7 self-custody access to stocks, crypto, commodities, forex, rates, perpetual futures and pre-IPO shares, with leverage and AI analysts that turn social and financial media into a real-time feed of market-moving news and actionable trade ideas. The consumer product is delivered primarily through iOS and Android apps and emphasizes self-custody, "smart money" signal tracking (insiders, politicians, hedge funds and social media), and unified DeFi opportunities in a single interface. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Freeport Markets does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Freshket
providers.description: Freshket is a Thai agri-food supply chain technology company that operates a B2B online marketplace connecting farmers and food producers directly with restaurants, hotels, catering operations, and food manufacturers. The platform uses technology to manage the fresh-produce and ingredient supply chain more efficiently and transparently, giving buyers quality ingredients at fair prices with reliable next-day delivery while giving growers better market access and pricing. Founded in Bangkok and backed by 500 Global, Freshket covers ordering, sourcing, cold-chain logistics, and account management for foodservice businesses across Thailand. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as of this enrichment pass Freshket publishes a customer-facing web and mobile ordering platform but no public developer API, SDKs, or documented API surface.

providers.name: Funding Societies | Modalku
providers.description: Funding Societies (known as Modalku in Indonesia) is Southeast Asia's largest SME digital financing and investment platform, connecting small and medium enterprises seeking working capital with individual and institutional investors. Operating across Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Hong Kong, the platform offers micro loans, business term loans, invoice and accounts-payable/receivable financing, startup financing and property-backed secured lending, alongside investment products for lenders. It is licensed and regulated (Capital Markets Services License, Monetary Authority of Singapore) and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Gamma Technologies
providers.description: Gamma Technologies develops GT-SUITE, the multi-physics system simulation software used by engineers to model, simulate, and optimize complex systems across automotive, HVACR, aerospace, industrial machinery, and shipbuilding. GT-SUITE combines 0D/1D/3D physics-based modeling, prebuilt model libraries, digital-twin workflows, and native AI tooling (GT Intelligence Studio and a Machine Learning Assistant). The company is a desktop/engineering CAE vendor rather than an API-first provider and publishes no public REST API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals that are publicly available.

providers.name: Garmentory
providers.description: Garmentory is a Seattle-based online fashion marketplace that connects shoppers with more than 1,000 independent boutiques and emerging designers across 30+ countries. Backed by Techstars, the platform curates apparel, accessories, and footwear from independent retailers, letting boutiques list inventory manually or sync it through a Shopify integration. Garmentory runs a heavily customized Spree Commerce (Ruby on Rails) storefront and consumes third-party APIs (payments, retail media, and merchant onboarding) rather than publishing a first-party public developer API. This profile tracks Garmentory's identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network; no OpenAPI, developer portal, or API reference is published at this time.

providers.name: Gathern
providers.description: Gathern (جاذر) is the first licensed peer-to-peer vacation-rental marketplace in Saudi Arabia, founded in Riyadh in 2016 and licensed by the Saudi Ministry of Tourism. Through its iOS, Android, and web apps, travelers book short-term private accommodations directly from local hosts — chalets, apartments, villas, farms, resorts, rest houses (istrahat), camps, caravans, and rooms — across more than 200 cities and provinces in the Kingdom, including Riyadh, Jeddah, Taif, Al Khobar, Dammam, Mecca, Medina, and AlUla. The platform lists tens of thousands of units, has served more than five million users, and holds a leading share of the alternative-hospitality sector in Saudi Arabia. Backed by 500 Global, STV, Sanabil Investments (a Public Investment Fund subsidiary), and others, Gathern raised a $72M Series B and is preparing for a Tadawul listing. Gathern operates as a consumer marketplace app and does not currently publish a public developer API surface; this profile tracks its public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: General Services Administration
providers.description: The General Services Administration (GSA) provides workplaces by constructing, managing, and preserving government buildings and by leasing and managing commercial real estate. GSA acquisition solutions offer private sector professional services, equipment, supplies, and IT to government organizations and the military. GSA also promotes management best practices and efficient government operations through the development of governmentwide policies, including a broad portfolio of public APIs.

providers.name: Georama
providers.description: Georama is now QualSights (qualsights.com), a consumer-insights research technology company that helps brands understand human behavior across the product lifecycle. The platform combines Smart Sensors that passively capture product consumption and usage in real time, a participant app that collects video, photo, and survey feedback, and an AI-powered analytics layer that turns that data into actionable insights. Marquee offerings include UseSights (Physical AI for product usage), VoiceSights (AI-moderated conversations), and the moment-based XMOT feedback method, spanning opportunity identification, concept optimization, product development, pre-launch validation, market launch, and acceleration. Georama entered the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead; QualSights publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: GigFinesse
providers.description: GigFinesse is a live-entertainment talent booking platform that connects hospitality venues — hotels, restaurants, bars, and clubs — with musicians, DJs, and performing artists. Venues discover and book vetted talent and manage contracts, insurance, scheduling, and payments through a centralized dashboard, while artists gain access to consistent, recurring gig opportunities. Clients include premium hospitality brands such as St. Regis, The Ritz-Carlton, Fairmont Hotels, and Hard Rock Hotel. GigFinesse is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Glambot
providers.description: Glambot is an online marketplace for buying and selling gently used and new makeup and beauty products. Shoppers can purchase discounted cosmetics from more than 100 brands including MAC, Urban Decay, Charlotte Tilbury, and Chanel across categories such as eyes, lashes, brows, face, cheeks, lips, skincare, palettes, and brushes, while sellers can mail in their unwanted makeup for cash payouts. Glambot operates a two-sided consumer resale platform and was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. The company does not currently publish a public API, SDK, developer portal, or MCP surface.

providers.name: GoWabi
providers.description: GoWabi is a Bangkok-based beauty and wellness booking marketplace serving Thailand and selected markets across Southeast Asia. Consumers use its web and mobile apps to discover and book more than 5,000 spas, massage studios, beauty clinics, nail, hair, dental, fitness, and wellness providers, with discounted deals, cashback rewards, and multiple payment options (credit card, Alipay, BNPL). GoWabi also offers a B2B SaaS/CRM tool integrated with partner point-of-sale systems to help salons, spas, clinics, and studios manage bookings and operations. It is backed by 500 Global. GoWabi operates a private mobile app backend (mobile-api.gowabi.com) but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or portal at this time.

providers.name: GoWork
providers.description: GoWork is Indonesia's largest premium coworking and flexible office space provider, operating more than 25 locations across Jakarta, Tangerang, Surabaya, Bali, and Medan. Formed from the 2018 merger of GoWork and Rework, the company offers private offices, dedicated desks, coworking memberships, virtual offices, meeting and event spaces, plus podcast and live-streaming studios. It also bundles business services such as company incorporation, tax and accounting, visa and work-permit processing, and legal support. Members discover, book, and manage workspace through the GoWork mobile apps and web booking platform. GoWork is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Grove Collaborative
providers.description: Grove Collaborative is a digital-first consumer products company and online marketplace for sustainable everyday household essentials — eco-friendly cleaning supplies, bamboo and recycled paper products, personal care, beauty, pet, and vitamins & supplements from hundreds of vetted brands. Orders meet strict ingredient standards and are carbon neutral, and the company operates as a plastic-neutral, sustainability-focused retailer sold through grove.co (a Shopify-hosted storefront) and retail partners. Grove is a public benefit company (NYSE: GROV) that was an early portfolio company of 500 Global and Bullpen Capital. It publishes no first-party developer API or public developer program; this profile captures its public web, security, and Shopify-platform discovery surface.

providers.name: Gyant
providers.description: Gyant was a San Francisco-based digital health company that built an AI-powered conversational virtual assistant for health systems, guiding patients through symptom checking, care navigation, and triage across web and messaging channels. In 2022 Gyant was acquired by Fabric (fabrichealth.com), and gyant.com now redirects to Fabric's healthcare care-access platform, which combines conversational AI with physician-built clinical protocols for virtual care, patient engagement, and clinical automation. Gyant does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, published legal/compliance surface, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Halara
providers.description: Halara is a direct-to-consumer athleisure and activewear fashion brand for women, best known for its versatile Active Dress and its Halara Flex fabric technology. Its Shopify-based online store sells exercise dresses, leggings, tennis skirts, joggers, pants, sports bras, loungewear, sweaters, and denim under the tagline "Athleisure for 365 Versions of You." Halara runs a mobile shopping app and a customer loyalty program (The Halara Circle), and is backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). Halara publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web, brand, and policy properties for network discovery.

providers.name: Hallow
providers.description: Hallow is the #1 Catholic and Christian prayer, meditation, and Bible app, offering guided daily prayer, the Rosary, Lectio Divina, the Examen, Christian meditation, faith-based sleep stories, Scripture readings, and audio-guided sessions led by well-known voices. Founded in 2018 and based in Chicago, Hallow is a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) with a subscription tier (Hallow Plus), and it runs programs for parishes, families, and gifting. Hallow does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, so this profile captures its public web and product surface. Backed by General Catalyst, Homebrew, and Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Halogen Capital
providers.description: Halogen Capital is Malaysia's first and only licensed digital asset fund manager, regulated by the Securities Commission Malaysia (License eCMSL/A0388/2023) and headquartered in Kuala Lumpur. The firm gives high-net-worth individuals, family offices, corporates, and institutional investors regulated access to cryptocurrency and traditional assets through unit trust structures, offering Shariah-compliant Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Crypto Titans basket funds alongside a MYR liquid fund, a ringgit income fund, and an enhanced income fund, all secured with multi-signature custody. Backed by Kenanga Investment Bank and 500 Global, Halogen manages roughly RM400 million in assets under management and is expanding into real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence and domain-security posture; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Harbor Health
providers.description: Harbor Health is a Central Texas healthcare company building a vertically integrated "pay-vider" model that combines primary care, specialty care, and health coaching clinics with its own commercial and individual health insurance plans, so the same organization both delivers and covers care. Founded in 2022 by Dr. Clay Johnston (founding dean of UT Dell Medical School), Tony Miller, and Eric Scott, the company operates clinics and Express Care walk-in locations across the Austin, Dallas, El Paso, and San Antonio metros, and is pursuing a value-based care model for the commercial market. It is backed by General Catalyst, 8VC, and Alta Partners. Harbor Health publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web properties (member portal, plans, blog, privacy and terms) for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Harbor Lab
providers.description: Harbor Lab is an AI-powered port cost and disbursement account (DA) management platform for the maritime industry, headquartered in Athens, Greece. Its cloud software helps shipowners, ship managers, charterers, and port agents manage port calls, validate and approve disbursement accounts, benchmark and negotiate port service pricing across a marketplace of thousands of port service providers, and automate payment and settlement — improving operational efficiency, digitizing the process, and delivering cost transparency across port cost management. The company is backed by Speedinvest, VentureFriends, Atomico, and others. As of this profile Harbor Lab exposes a web dashboard product only; no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Haz
providers.description: Haz (operated by Vend Solutions Ltd) is a London-based AI social commerce mobile app that connects friends through the things they own and makes it easier to track, buy, and sell second-hand belongings. Its proprietary receipt-reading technology scans digital purchase receipts in a user's email inbox to automatically digitize owned items in real time, removing the manual listing, photography, and description work traditionally required for resale. Users get real-time valuations of everything they own and can offer items to their social circle in a live feed, increasing the liquidity of everyday goods such as clothing and electronics. Haz launched on iOS in March 2024 and raised a $1.4M pre-seed round led by Speedinvest. It is a consumer application and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Health Resources and Services Administration
providers.description: The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) is the primary Federal agency for improving access to health care services for people who are uninsured, isolated, or medically vulnerable. HRSA provides data and web services for healthcare resources, facility locations, and program information.

providers.name: HeavyConnect
providers.description: HeavyConnect is a digital documentation and compliance platform purpose-built for agricultural operations, serving growers, harvesters, shippers, and processors. Its mobile-first, offline-capable modules cover food safety compliance, worker training and certification, time and productivity tracking, quality assurance inspections, end-to-end traceability, and supplier management. The platform replaces paper-based recordkeeping with audit-ready digital documentation and real-time analytics dashboards, helping food and agriculture operations stay inspection-ready. HeavyConnect reports 2,600+ active users across operations including Sysco, Naturipe, Talley, and Empire. It is offered as a month-to-month subscription with a request-a-demo onboarding path. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio-company lead (500 Global, Techstars) and enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: HelloTech
providers.description: HelloTech is a consumer technology-services company providing in-home and online tech support across the United States through a nationwide network of vetted technicians. Services span computer and printer repair, WiFi and home-networking setup, mobile-device support, audio/video and home-theater installation, TV mounting, smart-home device installation, and home-security setup, offered on-demand or through a HelloTech Home membership plan. HelloTech operates as a consumer services brand and does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Highstock
providers.description: Highstock is a private, AI-native wholesale marketplace that connects consumer brands holding excess or unsold inventory with a vetted network of global business buyers. Focused initially on beauty and personal care, the platform lets brands convert surplus stock into cash while protecting brand value and channel privacy, and gives buyers access to authentic inventory directly from brands at exclusive pricing, with centralized order management and flexible payment terms. The company reports 50+ beauty and personal care brands, 100+ wholesale buyers, $100M+ in listed inventory, and more than 1M pounds of product diverted from landfill, with offices in New York (US) and Gurgaon (India). Highstock does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: Hornet
providers.description: Hornet is a queer social networking platform operated by Queer Networks, Inc., serving the global LGBTQ+ community with more than 100 million users worldwide. The Hornet app combines profiles, feeds, live video, one-on-one video chat, messaging, and location-based discovery into a privacy-first digital home for gay men and the broader queer community. Backed by 500 Global (and previously part of BlueCity Holdings), Hornet operates as a consumer social/media company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs — so this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public identity, policy surface, and domain-security posture rather than developer artifacts. Hornet is number one in several key markets including France, Brazil, Turkey, and Taiwan, and monetizes through premium subscriptions and queer-audience advertising.

providers.name: Housable
providers.description: Housable is a California-focused proptech company that helps rental-property owners and operators develop Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) as a portfolio value-add strategy. Its platform manages ADU projects end to end — from concept and financial feasibility analysis through design, permitting, bidding, construction, and lease-up — and lets operators run many parallel developments across their properties at once, converting underused spaces such as leasing offices, garages, and parking areas into new rental units alongside ground-up ADU construction. Housable is an early-stage startup backed by Kindred Ventures and other seed investors. It is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Houst
providers.description: Houst is a global short-term rental and Airbnb management company founded in 2015, operating in 17 cities across 8 countries and managing over 11,650 properties. Houst handles the full hosting lifecycle for homeowners and landlords - multi-platform listing creation and optimization, dynamic pricing, professional photography, 24/7 guest communication and vetting, check-in coordination, cleaning, linen and maintenance - powered by a proprietary host dashboard that tracks earnings, occupancy, bookings and performance. The company operates on a commission model and also runs an operating-partner and affiliate programme. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Hum Capital
providers.description: Hum Capital operates an AI-powered funding marketplace that connects growth companies with the right institutional capital. Through its Intelligent Capital Market platform, companies share their financial and operating data once and are matched to a network of 900+ lenders and investors for non-dilutive and structured financing (typically $1M-$50M), while investors receive curated, data-driven deal flow. Hum reports more than $700M in capital deployed across 6,000+ companies. Headquartered in New York, the company operates in the financial services, capital markets, and alternative-financing sector. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched from the company's public web surface; Hum publishes no public developer API, so this entry is identity- and security-focused.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Imperfect Foods
providers.description: Imperfect Foods is a consumer grocery delivery service focused on reducing food waste. It sources surplus, cosmetically imperfect, and excess-inventory food — produce that is too large or small, packaging overstock, near best-by-date items, and manufacturing byproducts — and delivers them to members at a discount through a weekly, customizable grocery order of produce, meat, seafood, dairy, pantry staples, and snacks. Imperfect Foods was acquired by Misfits Market in 2022 and now operates as part of that company; its consumer web and mobile apps remain live. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface was found during enrichment — this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: INBOTIQA
providers.description: INBOTIQA is a UK-based fintech whose flagship product, YUDOmail, is an Intelligent Business Email and shared-mailbox management platform for high-volume group inboxes at banks, BPOs and financial-services operations teams. YUDOmail layers over Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace to turn incoming emails into assigned, trackable tasks with ownership, due dates, SLA tracking, machine-learning triage and sentiment analysis, audit trails and analytics, without replacing the underlying email platform. It deploys in the cloud or on-premises, integrates with Symphony chat and Microsoft Teams, and is used across KYC, FX, collateral, settlements and trade-support functions. INBOTIQA was a 2019 Barclays Accelerator (powered by Techstars) company.

providers.name: Industrious
providers.description: Industrious is a global flexible workspace provider operating private offices, dedicated and open coworking memberships, and on-demand meeting rooms across hundreds of locations worldwide. Members manage access, bookings, and workspace services through the Industrious member portal and iOS/Android mobile apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Fifth Wall and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Industrious publishes a consumer/member web and mobile experience but no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile therefore captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Inspirato
providers.description: Inspirato is a luxury travel subscription company that gives members access to a curated portfolio of 300+ private branded residences, 200+ five-star hotels, and 170+ destinations worldwide, paired with dedicated concierge care, curated experiences, and signature hotel partnerships. Inspirato does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Instride Health
providers.description: InStride Health is a virtual mental health provider delivering specialized, insurance-based treatment for children, teens, and young adults ages 7 to 24 who struggle with anxiety, OCD, panic, phobias, school avoidance, and related disorders. Its structured four-to-eight month program pairs each patient with a coordinated care team of a therapist, a psychiatric prescriber, and an exposure coach, combining evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy and exposure-and-response prevention delivered over telehealth. The company is backed by General Catalyst and tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a clinical care provider and publishes no public API, developer program, or SDK.

providers.name: Intro

Experts span career and business, interior design and home decor, style and beauty, health and wellness, fitness and nutrition, astrology, and more, with per-session pricing set by each expert. Intro also lets creators and professionals monetize their audience by publishing a bookable profile. The company raised a $10M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from Seven Seven Six. Intro operates as a consumer web and mobile product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: James Webb Space Telescope API

The API provides access to JWST images, observations, and data filterable by program, type, and other parameters. It is built by an independent engineer (not an official NASA, ESA, or CSA service) and data is available under CC-BY 4.0. Authentication is via API key obtained at signup.

providers.name: JAX-WS
providers.description: JAX-WS (Java API for XML Web Services) is a Java standard for building and consuming SOAP-based XML web services. Originally specified as JSR 224 under the Java Community Process, JAX-WS is now part of Jakarta EE as Jakarta XML Web Services. It defines annotations and runtime APIs that allow developers to expose Java methods as SOAP web service operations and to generate Java client stubs from WSDL documents. Reference implementations include the Eclipse Metro project and Apache CXF.

providers.name: Jiraaf
providers.description: Jiraaf (Jiraaf Platform Private Limited, Bangalore, India) is an online fixed-income investment platform that lets retail investors discover, analyze, and invest in listed and secured bonds. Its curated product shelf spans listed corporate bonds, sovereign gold bonds, treasury bills, G-Secs and State Development Loans (SDLs), securitized debt instruments (SDIs), and fixed deposits, each surfaced with transparent yields, credit ratings, and a documented credit-evaluation process. Alongside the investing surface it publishes research reports, a bond analyser, a bond directory, a glossary, calculators, and educational content (Bond Gurukul webinars, blogs, and newsletters). Backed by Accel. Jiraaf is a consumer-facing web and mobile investing product and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: JobToday

JobToday operates across 20+ countries including the UK, US, Spain, Mexico, and France, and reports tens of millions of job seekers and hundreds of thousands of hiring businesses. It is backed by Accel. JobToday is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Josh Wood Colour

providers.name: Juno Chat

It supports conditions including fibromyalgia, long COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, EDS, endometriosis, lupus, and MS, and is informed by research from Oxford and UCL plus 1,000+ patient interviews. Founded in 2025 by Marshall Gould (CEO) and Isaac Tolley (CTO); HIPAA-aligned infrastructure with no health data sold. Juno is a consumer app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Kale
providers.description: Kale (operated by Palette Technologies, Inc., dba Kale) is a creator-rewards and user-generated-content marketplace that connects social-media content creators with brands. Creators join brand challenges and tournaments, post authentic sponsored content about products they use, and earn cash, merchandise, and perks; brands source authentic UGC and micro-influencer marketing at scale. The platform is delivered through the getkale.com and kalecard.com web apps and native iOS/Android apps, with a merchant network spanning consumer brands such as Chili's, Planet Fitness, Urban Outfitters, DoorDash, Southwest, and Starbucks. Kale is backed by Forerunner Ventures. No public developer/API surface is published; this profile captures the company's public identity and security posture.

providers.name: KatalistAI

It targets filmmakers, directors, advertisers, content creators, animators and educators looking to move from concept to visualized story faster. Backed by 500 Global, Katalist is a consumer/creative generative-AI SaaS accessed through its web application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Kibin

Alongside the study app, Kibin also runs its long-standing academic-writing surface — professional essay editing, a paper grader, a thesis-statement generator, essay examples, and a writing blog. Kibin is a B2C, mobile- and web-delivered product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

Products include VR simulators for the Airbus H145, Airbus H125, and Robinson R22 helicopters, with Boeing 737 and eVTOL platforms in development. Customers include Alaska Airlines, the FAA, Airbus Helicopters, the LAPD, and Marshall University. The company operates the LoftHUB customer platform but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Lower publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time; this profile captures its public web, legal, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Luel

Positioned as "the frontier of data," Luel powers the foundations of machine perception through a proprietary, continuous data engine. The company is backed by Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Luel does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Newneek
providers.description: Newneek (뉴닉) is a South Korean knowledge and media platform that makes news and current events easy and fun to follow. Founded by Kim So-yeon and operated by Newneek Co., Ltd. from Seoul's Mapo district, the company is best known for its conversational email newsletter delivered by the mascot "Gosuni," alongside a mobile app, a Slack news bot, and active social channels. Newneek is a consumer content brand rather than an API producer: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. It appears in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company, and this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture. Enrichment probes found no OpenAPI, well-known, OAuth, MCP, or webhook surface to harvest.

providers.name: Nexthop Systems
providers.description: Nexthop AI (Nexthop Systems) builds power-efficient AI networking infrastructure for hyperscalers and NeoClouds — scale-out and scale-across Ethernet switches, a networking software portfolio, and optics and cables engineered to lower the cost per token of training and serving large AI models. Founded and led by CEO Anshul Sadana, the company is backed by Battery Ventures and raised an oversubscribed $500M Series B in 2025 at a $4.2 billion valuation. Nexthop runs a public marketing, blog and news site plus a login-gated customer Support Hub and Learning Hub; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Nixpacks
providers.description: Nixpacks is an open-source build tool that converts application source code into OCI-compliant Docker images by combining language-specific providers, Nix packages, and Buildkit. Originally created by Railway as the build system powering the Railway platform, Nixpacks inspects a project's source, selects one or more providers (Node, Python, Ruby, Go, Java, Rust, PHP, Elixir, Deno, Crystal, .NET, Swift, Scala, Dart, Haskell, Gleam, Zig, Clojure, Lunatic, Cobol, Scheme, F#, Staticfile, and more), and produces a reproducible build plan composed of setup, install, build, and start phases. The plan declares Nix packages, apt packages, environment variables, commands, and cache directories, and can be customized via a `nixpacks.toml` file, CLI flags, or environment variables. Compared with Cloud Native Buildpacks, Nixpacks uses Nix as its package layer, ships as a single Rust CLI, and outputs a plain Dockerfile/OCI image without requiring a buildpack lifecycle. The project is MIT licensed and currently in maintenance mode; Railway recommends Railpack as the actively developed successor.

providers.name: Novee Security
providers.description: Novee Security (Novee) is a cybersecurity company delivering AI-driven penetration testing that finds vulnerabilities faster, validates defenses, and reduces cyber risk. Its autonomous offensive-security platform performs penetration testing at machine speed across web applications and APIs, and spans solutions including DAST, AI red teaming, manual penetration testing, bug bounty, and compliance testing. Backed by Canaan Partners, Novee is building continuous, AI-native security testing as an alternative to traditional DAST scanning and slow, periodic manual pentest cycles. The company publishes a marketing and product site, a vulnerability glossary, and a blog, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Novel Effect
providers.description: Novel Effect is a Techstars-backed interactive read-aloud technology company whose voice-recognition platform listens as a person reads a children's picture book aloud and plays perfectly synchronized music, sound effects, and character voices in response, turning any book into an immersive shared experience. Delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps, Novel Effect is used by families, teachers, and libraries to make reading aloud more engaging for young children. Novel Effect is a consumer and education (EdTech) product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Numerade
providers.description: Numerade is an education technology company that helps students learn STEM subjects through short, expert-created video solutions, step-by-step textbook explanations, and an AI study tutor branded as Ace. Ace responds to typed questions, uploaded notes, quizzes, and worksheets, and can summarize material to help students prepare for exams. The platform spans math, science, and other STEM courses with a large library of instructor-led problem walkthroughs and practice questions. Numerade is a venture-backed consumer learning product and does not currently expose a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of General Catalyst and enriched by probing the public site (2026-07-20).

providers.name: omniX labs
providers.description: omniX labs is a New York-based AI machine-vision analytics company (owned by EverWash) serving car wash, oil-change/lube, and related quick-service automotive businesses. Its platform ingests real-time video of the physical business, applies computer vision and AI to synthesize customer interactions, and returns operational insights that help operators boost throughput, optimize staffing, prevent loss, predict demand, and grow revenue. omniX labs was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. It operates a customer web portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Onze
providers.description: Onze is a Brazilian fintech (São Paulo) focused on corporate private pension (previdência privada) and financial health for companies and their employees. It offers digital management of employer-sponsored pension plans, access to more than 300 investment funds, one-on-one financial consultations with specialists, and financial-education seminars, all delivered as a B2B employee benefits platform. Onze positions itself as the first fintech centered on pension and financial wellness for a company's collaborators, and is backed by Ribbit Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass Onze publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Operon
providers.description: Operon is an AI-powered manufacturing intelligence platform (Y Combinator S2026) that turns P&IDs (Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams), schematics, datasheets, and scanned engineering documents into one structured, queryable model of a plant. Its P&ID Recognition detects equipment, instruments, valves, and piping symbols across ISA, ISO, and proprietary symbology; its P&ID Agent generates standards-compliant diagrams from text, simulation data, or sketches; and Knowledge Chat lets engineers query plant documentation in natural language and build agentic workflows for safety, compliance, HAZOP/PHA, EHS, material take-offs, brownfield digitization, and management-of-change. Operon exports structured DEXPI data and offers cloud and on-premise deployment with encryption, role-based access control, and audit trails. As of July 2026 the product is in private beta (pid.operonsolutions.com) and publishes no public API.

providers.name: Oxyzo
providers.description: Oxyzo Financial Services is an RBI-registered Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) providing customized SME and corporate financing across India. Founded as the lending arm of the OfBusiness group, Oxyzo offers purchase finance, work order finance, invoice discounting, vendor finance, business loans, machinery finance, and loan against property, serving industries such as auto manufacturing, capital goods, e-mobility, logistics, pharmaceuticals, and textiles. The company operates 145+ branches, has powered 10,000+ businesses, disbursed over Rs 77,000 crore, and holds A+ ratings from CRISIL and ICRA. Oxyzo publishes no public developer/API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PadSplit
providers.description: PadSplit is an Atlanta-based co-living marketplace that makes affordable housing accessible by connecting members seeking private rooms in shared homes with property owners who host them. The platform offers flexible weekly payments, fast move-ins, all-inclusive rent (utilities, wifi, and furnishings), member background screening, and a rewards program that helps residents build credit. PadSplit operates across multiple U.S. metros as a two-sided marketplace serving both members (renters) and hosts (property owners), and was backed by Techstars. The company has no public developer program, API, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Pakistan Open Data
providers.description: Pakistan Open Data is a national government open-data portal for Pakistan running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 1,471 datasets.

providers.name: Paladin
providers.description: Paladin is a legal technology company whose software platform connects the pro bono community and empowers legal teams to run pro bono programs more efficiently. The platform provides centralized program management dashboards, volunteer matching that connects attorneys to pro bono opportunities based on interest and expertise, and impact measurement that visualizes and reports on program outcomes across a nationwide network of legal services organizations, law firms, in-house legal teams, law schools, and bar associations. Customers include Clifford Chance, Dentons, Holland & Knight, and Wilson Sonsini. Paladin is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes a customer-facing web application at app.joinpaladin.com but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Paperstack
providers.description: Paperstack is a Canadian fintech operating a private-credit / working-capital financing platform for direct-to-consumer (DTC), e-commerce, and retail consumer brands. It provides non-dilutive, revenue-based funding of up to $5,000,000 that brands can use without restrictions to purchase inventory, invest in advertising, and finance payroll, with transparent flat fees (typically 4-10%) and no origination or late fees. Paperstack couples a network of lending partners with proprietary AI/ML underwriting software that integrates directly into a brand's financial and e-commerce data to assess creditworthiness and project future performance in real time. Founded by Assel Beglinova (CEO) and Vadim Lidich (CTO) and backed by Techstars, the company has processed over 1,500 funding applications. As of this enrichment pass Paperstack publishes a customer-facing product and marketing site only; it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Paraform
providers.description: Paraform is an agentic hiring marketplace where expert recruiters and custom AI agents work together to fill companies' most important roles. Companies post open roles and work with multiple vetted recruiters from a network of 10,000+ professionals in one place, while Paraform's AI toolkit handles sourcing, candidate matching, CRM, notetaking, and scheduling. The platform charges a listing (subscription) fee to publish roles and a success fee when a hire is made. Paraform does not publish a public developer API; instead it integrates into customers' existing ATS and productivity tools (Ashby, Greenhouse, Slack, Gmail, Calendly, Google Calendar) by consuming those partners' APIs and webhooks to keep candidate, role, and interview status in sync bidirectionally.

providers.name: Pebble
providers.description: Pebble is a Silicon Valley electric-vehicle and consumer-hardware company that designs and manufactures the Pebble Flow, an all-electric travel trailer (RV) with an integrated battery, solar, and motor-assist drivetrain. The product line pairs the trailer with the Pebble mobile app for remote control and monitoring, offering features such as autonomous "Magic Hitch" coupling, remote-control positioning, automatic leveling and setup, and up to seven days of off-grid capability. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Pebble sells direct-to-consumer under the tagline "Where Home Meets the Road." As of this enrichment pass Pebble publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; its only software touchpoint is the consumer-facing Pebble Control Center app.

providers.name: Perimeter VRM (formerly ProcessBolt)
providers.description: Perimeter (formerly ProcessBolt) is a vendor risk management (VRM) platform built for regulated industries. It covers the full third-party risk lifecycle through six modules — Monitor (continuous vendor surveillance and alerts), Assess (automated risk assessments with a drag-and-drop template builder), Extract (AI-powered document intelligence), Verify (attack-surface validation), Share (a document management and collaboration hub), and Respond (RFP and assessment response automation). The product centralizes vendor information, scores and reports vendor risk, and supports no-code integration and API-based / CSV vendor imports across US, EU, and Australia data regions. ProcessBolt rebranded to Perimeter and now serves the platform from perimeter.net; processbolt.com redirects there. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs are published — the platform's integration APIs are exposed to customers rather than through an open developer surface.

providers.name: Pernambuco Open Data
providers.description: Pernambuco Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 40 datasets.

providers.name: Photomath
providers.description: Photomath is a mobile math-learning application that lets students scan a printed or handwritten math problem with their phone camera and returns step-by-step explanations, custom visual aids, and animated solving methods across topics from elementary arithmetic through calculus. Originally built by Croatian computer-vision company Microblink and later spun out as an independent education company backed by Menlo Ventures and Goldman Sachs, Photomath was acquired by Google in 2023 and now operates within Google (support is handled through Google's Help Center). It is a consumer subscription product distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish an official public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. The company previously stated it would not release a public Photomath SDK. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio company and enriched to capture the company's public web and domain-security surface; no first-party API surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: Piinpoint
providers.description: PiinPoint is an AI-powered location intelligence and site selection platform for retailers, restaurants, brokers, and commercial real estate teams. The software combines demographic, mobile-location, traffic, and competitive data to help teams validate sites, forecast sales, model cannibalization, run network simulations, and plan expansion. Delivered as a B2B SaaS web application (app.piinpoint.com), PiinPoint does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Pillar
providers.description: Pillar is an Italian construction-technology company, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Milan, building what it calls the operating system for the construction industry (il sistema operativo per l'edilizia). Its cloud platform unifies the back office of building firms (imprese edili) — invoicing (fatturazione), cash-flow management (flussi di cassa), bank reconciliation, quotes and estimates (preventivi), procurement, job and project cost control (gestione commessa), and delivery notes and site work reports (DDT e rapportini) — alongside on-site safety (Pillar Sicurezza) and an AI layer (Pillar AI) that automates data entry in real time, including inputs captured from the job site over WhatsApp. Pillar is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital and today reaches customers through a book-a-demo model rather than a public self-serve signup or a developer-facing API; no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Pine
providers.description: Pine is a Canadian digital-first mortgage lender and real estate brokerage (Pine Canada Financial Corporation / Pine Real Estate Brokerage) that makes home buying more accessible for Canadians through an online platform offering low interest rates, fast pre-approvals, and zero hidden fees. Backed by Greylock, Pine pairs mortgage origination with a REALTOR-affiliated brokerage licensed across multiple provinces (ON, AB, SK, NS, NB, NL), and reports more than $2B in mortgages funded and 100,000+ clients served. Pine is a consumer fintech product with no public developer API; its backend at api.pine.ca is a private, authenticated service.

providers.name: Pintarnya
providers.description: Pintarnya is an Indonesian technology startup, launched in May 2022, that operates an employment and financial-services super-app for the country's blue-collar and entry-level workforce (education levels from elementary school through bachelor's degree, "SD-S1"). The platform aggregates tens of thousands of daily-updated job listings across 300+ Indonesian cities and pairs job search with Cari Cuan side-income tasks, Siap Kerja skill-building video courses, a CV builder, and an employer/recruiter posting product used by tens of thousands of companies. Pintarnya reports more than 10 million registered job seekers and is registered with Indonesia's Ministry of Labor (KEMNAKER). It is a consumer web and mobile product; no public developer API, OpenAPI description, or developer portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Planet FWD
providers.description: Planet FWD is a decarbonization software platform that helps consumer brands measure, reduce, and report their carbon emissions. It provides AI-powered product life cycle assessments (LCAs), corporate greenhouse-gas inventories across Scope 1, 2, and 3, and supply-chain decarbonization scenario planning for food & beverage, retail, and apparel companies. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Playbite
providers.description: Playbite is a free mobile arcade app - "an arcade in your pocket" - built by Digital Media Technology SL and backed by 500 Global. The app offers an ever-expanding library of simple, casual games spanning multiplayer, rhythm, puzzle, matching, relaxing, and racing categories, with over 500,000 players who play games and earn rewards. The service is free to users and monetized through non-intrusive advertising. Playbite is a consumer-facing mobile gaming product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Players Lounge
providers.description: Players' Lounge is a skill-based competitive gaming platform where users win money by completing personalized head-to-head gaming challenges (money matches) or by staking and watching other players compete. The platform supports popular console and PC titles including Madden, NBA 2K, Call of Duty Warzone, Marvel Rivals, and others, and states it has paid out over $200M to players to date. Players' Lounge is a consumer product surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation at this time. This profile captures the company's public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Please
providers.description: Please (Please Platforms) is an AI-powered "thinking" reminders application for iOS that lets people capture a thought, a link, or an image with zero effort, then automatically enriches each reminder with additional context and surfaces intelligent, connected suggestions so nothing gets missed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Please ships a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Plenful
providers.description: Plenful is an AI-powered workflow automation platform for pharmacy and healthcare operations, founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco with an office in New York City. The platform automates complex, high-ROI administrative pharmacy workflows — 340B audit and optimization, 340B referral capture, rebate and Maximum Fair Price (MFP) reconciliation, benefits verification and prior authorization, and infusion order intake — using large language models and machine learning tuned to each organization's data. It ingests PDFs, flat files, APIs, HL7 feeds, and databases, supports unlimited organizational logic rules, and serves 100+ healthcare organizations including Prisma Health, Renown Health, Temple Health, Cencora, and Samaritan Health Services. Plenful is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Notable Capital (formerly GGV Capital), SUSA Ventures, TQ Ventures, and Waterline Ventures. Plenful ships an enterprise SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Plobal Apps
providers.description: Plobal Apps is a no-code mobile app builder for Shopify merchants that turns online stores into native iOS and Android shopping apps without engineering. The platform offers drag-and-drop app design with HTML/CSS/JavaScript code blocks, push-notification marketing campaigns, live selling, AI-powered product recommendations, advanced search and smart filtering, and real-time analytics tracking 60+ in-app actions, plus omnichannel flows such as in-app ordering with in-store pickup. It installs through the Shopify App Store and is used by direct-to-consumer brands to grow mobile commerce revenue and customer retention.

providers.name: Pomelo Care
providers.description: Pomelo Care is a value-based virtual healthcare company delivering 24/7 clinician-led care for women and children across fertility and preconception, prenatal and postpartum, pediatric and NICU, and midlife and menopause health. Operating as a telehealth platform contracted with employers and health plans, Pomelo pairs licensed clinicians, doulas, and care teams with remote monitoring to close the gaps between doctor visits, reduce NICU admissions, and improve maternal and infant outcomes. The company reports covering 25 million lives across all 50 states and raised a $92M Series C at a $1.7B valuation. Pomelo Care is a patient-, employer-, and payer-facing platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and First Round Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network for company-level discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Possible Finance
providers.description: Possible Finance is a consumer fintech company offering small-dollar installment loans and credit-building products through a mobile app. Its core products are the Possible Loan (up to $500 with flexible repayment schedules), the Possible Advance (up to $300 drawn against a future paycheck), and Bill & Rent Reporting that builds credit history by reporting on-time payments to the credit bureaus. The company charges no late fees or penalty charges and uses AI-driven underwriting based on real banking activity rather than FICO scores, serving borrowers who are underserved by traditional credit. Possible Finance operates as a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation and is backed by Union Square Ventures. It is a mobile-app, consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Powerplay
providers.description: Powerplay is a construction project management platform built by Coffer Internet Services Pvt. Ltd. (Bengaluru, India) that gives builders, general contractors, subcontractors, project managers, and site engineers mobile and desktop tools to run construction projects end to end: real-time work and progress tracking, material procurement and inventory management, labor attendance and payroll, issue tracking, petty-cash and expense management, and reporting dashboards. The product is delivered primarily through iOS and Android field apps with a desktop companion. Powerplay does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation, so this profile captures its identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Praktika.ai Company
providers.description: Praktika.ai is an AI-powered language-learning application that lets learners have spoken conversations with lifelike AI avatar tutors and receive instant feedback on pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary. The product spans mobile (iOS and Android) and web, with personalized study plans and speaking, listening, reading, and writing exercises across many languages, plus a B2B offering for organizations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Praktika publishes a consumer product only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation were found — so this profile captures the company identity and web properties rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Projectx
providers.description: ProjectX is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building Infinity (InfinityOS), a cloud operating system designed for AI agents. Infinity lets agents and humans orchestrate GPU workloads through a chat interface rather than traditional APIs, running multiple Windows and Linux applications — such as Blender, VS Code, DaVinci Resolve, Unreal Engine, and Isaac Sim — simultaneously, each on its own independent compute and GPU inside a single shared browser-based workspace with sub-minute cold starts. A public API, developer docs, status page, changelog, and blog are announced as coming soon; no programmatic API surface is published yet.

providers.name: Prolaera
providers.description: Prolaera is a learning and compliance platform built for modern CPAs and accounting firms, combining automated CPE (Continuing Professional Education) tracking, a learning management system (LMS), and a built-in course library so firms can administer training, monitor license and compliance requirements, and manage professional development in one place. Prolaera merged with LCvista and now operates as "Prolaera by LCvista"; the product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application at app.prolaera.com with SSO/SAML 2.0 identity support and SCORM/AICC/xAPI content compatibility. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Prolaera does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Promolta
providers.description: Promolta is a self-service video advertising platform that promotes YouTube and other videos across a network of blogs, websites, mobile apps, and social networks to grow views, subscribers, and engagement. Advertisers fund campaigns and target audiences, while publishers in the Promolta network earn by distributing sponsored video content. Promolta is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or webhook surface — this profile captures its public web, legal, and domain-security footprint.

providers.name: Proudly
providers.description: Proudly is a direct-to-consumer baby care brand, co-founded by Dwyane Wade and Gabrielle Union, that centers the unique skin and hair needs of Black and Brown babies to make products better for all. Its Shopify-hosted storefront sells skincare (balms, washes, oils), hair care, baby wipes, absorbent diapers, bath and body kits, apparel and gift bundles under a "No Sketchy Stuff" ingredient-transparency commitment. Backed by Initialized Capital (via A-Frame Brands), Atacama Ventures and VMG Partners. Proudly is a consumer commerce company with no public developer API or SDK program; the only machine surface is its Shopify Customer Account OpenID/OAuth well-known configuration.

providers.name: Provi
providers.description: Provi is a B2B beverage alcohol marketplace that digitizes procurement across the three-tier distribution system, connecting buyers (bars, restaurants, and retail stores) with distributors, sales representatives, and suppliers/brands. The platform consolidates product discovery across distributor catalogs, direct messaging with sales reps, order management and processing, and brand showcase tools into a single ordering experience. Provi was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Publishizer
providers.description: Publishizer is a book crowdfunding platform and literary agency that connects authors with readers and publishers. Authors create book proposals and run pre-order campaigns; readers pre-order copies to signal demand; and publishers use data such as pre-order volume and proposal quality to discover and acquire promising manuscripts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web platform and blog but no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Qbiq
providers.description: Qbiq is an AI-powered space planning and architectural visualization platform for real estate. It lets brokers, architects, developers, and space planners generate optimized 2D floor plans, photorealistic 3D renderings, virtual tours, Revit/CAD models, and quantity takeoffs from an uploaded space plan (CAD, PDF, or JPEG) in minutes. Qbiq automates test-fits and layout optimization for offices and commercial real estate, comparing multiple design options against program requirements. The company is backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Qbiq operates a hosted web application (plan.qbiq.ai) and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: QiDZ Holding
providers.description: QiDZ Holding operates theQapp (formerly QiDZ), a consumer mobile platform that helps families discover, compare, and book activities, entertainment, and dining experiences across the United Arab Emirates and the wider Middle East (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Jeddah, Eastern Province, Manama, and Cairo). The app curates theme parks, water parks, indoor play areas, sports and creative classes, kid-friendly restaurants, camps, staycations, museums, and birthday and event packages, and offers a Q-Club membership with exclusive promo codes and discounts. Backed by 500 Global, QiDZ is a B2C mobile experience distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine specification, so this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Qwick
providers.description: Qwick is an AI-powered workforce management platform for the hospitality industry, connecting businesses with vetted hospitality professionals ("Pros") for on-demand shifts across 42 states. Its products span the Marketplace (intelligent shift matching), QwickGo (same-day shift posting), Jobs (performance-based hiring with paid working interviews), Compliance (scheduling and time-tracking rules enforcement), and Pay (multi-state W-2 and 1099 payroll). Qwick documents a REST API (v2) plus webhooks for custom integrations exposing shifts, pros, hours, invoices, and compliance data, and pre-built integrations with payroll (ADP, Gusto, Paychex, Paycom), POS (Toast, Square, Lightspeed), HRIS (Workday, BambooHR), scheduling (7shifts, Deputy, When I Work), and SSO (Okta, Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace). It is headquartered in Charleston, SC and backed by Foundry Group.

providers.name: Rally
providers.description: Rally (Rally Rd.) is an alternative-asset investing platform that lets everyday investors buy and sell equity shares in individual collectible assets — classic cars, watches, fine art, wine, sports memorabilia, trading cards, and other rare items. Rally sources and authenticates each item, files it with the SEC as a regulated offering, splits it into shares in an Initial Offering, and then opens a Bid/Ask secondary market roughly 90 days later so shareholders can trade. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York, Rally runs iOS, Android, and web apps and raised a $30M Series B led by Accel in 2021. Rally publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Raydiant
providers.description: Raydiant is a digital signage and in-location experience management platform for brick-and-mortar businesses, now operating under the Displai brand (raydiant.com redirects to displai.ai). The platform lets restaurants, retail stores, hospitality venues, commercial buildings, and schools manage branded content across networks of screens and kiosks from a central cloud dashboard. Core products include Displai Signage (multi-location content management), Displai Engage (employee engagement and gamification), Displai InSight (AI foot traffic and visitor analytics), and self-service ordering kiosks integrated with point-of-sale systems. Customers include Chick-fil-A, Macy's, Toyota, T-Mobile, and Red Bull. It runs a production cloud API at api.raydiant.com / api.displai.ai, but that surface is not publicly documented — there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or API reference. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio lead.

providers.name: ReelData AI
providers.description: ReelData AI builds artificial intelligence software for land-based aquaculture, helping recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) fish farms maximize growth, minimize costs, and reduce risk across smolt, post-smolt, and on-growing production. Its integrated AI suite includes AI Smart Feeding (ReelAppetite), which monitors real-time population appetite to optimize feed and cut waste; AI Biomass Monitoring (ReelWeight), a non-intrusive biomass estimation tool returning results within hours; and AI Cameras (ReelVision), dual-function cameras for fish-behavior monitoring, feed counting, and standard IP camera use. Additional tools cover stress monitoring (ReelStress) and early disease detection (ReelHealth). ReelData is a Techstars portfolio company serving major operators including Samherji, Atlantic Sapphire, Kingfish Company, and Salmon Evolution. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface; its products are delivered as on-site AI hardware and software rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Regular Finance
providers.description: Regular Finance (Regular) is a French fintech offering a consumer digital-asset yield account. Customers deposit euros by bank transfer and earn roughly 5.50% annual interest paid daily, backed by regulated stablecoins such as EURC and USDC placed into on-chain liquidity pools and yield protocols. Withdrawals are free at any time and no crypto knowledge is required. Regular is a Techstars-backed company headquartered in France; the product is entirely consumer-facing (web and mobile app at app.regular.eu) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Retrocausal
providers.description: Retrocausal builds AI-powered copilot software for manufacturing operations, applying patented computer vision and machine learning to manual assembly lines. Its products include Assembly Copilot (real-time AI-tracked work instructions, poka-yoke error prevention, and cycle-level video traceability), Kaizen Copilot (AI-powered time studies, standard work, automatic line balancing, and ergonomic analysis for industrial engineers), and Ergo Copilot (ergonomic risk assessment from smartphone video). The platform runs on AWS, is ISO 27001 certified, and integrates with MES systems, OPC UA for PLCs and smart tools, barcode scanners, torque wrenches, light towers, and projectors, with SSO via Azure Active Directory and Okta. Retrocausal is a Techstars portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API; integrations are delivered as custom MES/OPC UA and identity connections rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Rheaply
providers.description: Rheaply is a circular-economy platform for enterprise asset lifecycle management. It gives organizations real-time inventory visibility, an internal reuse marketplace with approval workflows for reallocating surplus furniture, equipment, IT assets, and lab supplies, and sustainable disposition through a network of 3,400+ verified nonprofit and commercial partners. Rheaply helps companies, universities, and governments cut procurement costs, divert waste from landfill, track embodied-carbon savings, and run decommissioning and office move-outs. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a web application at app.rheaply.com. As of this enrichment pass Rheaply publishes no public developer/API program, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Rondonia Open Data
providers.description: Rondonia Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 14 datasets.

providers.name: Rula
providers.description: Rula is a telehealth mental health platform that connects patients with licensed therapists and psychiatric providers who accept their insurance. Operating as an in-network behavioral health marketplace across all 50 states, Rula matches individuals with more than 23,000 licensed clinicians for individual, couples, family, child, and teen therapy as well as psychiatric medication management, covering 90+ conditions including anxiety, depression, ADHD, PTSD, OCD, and addiction. Rula is in-network with 120+ insurance plans nationwide (Aetna, Cigna, Optum, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross, Kaiser), with patients paying an average of about $15 per session with insurance. Rula publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface as of this profile; care is delivered through its patient and provider web applications.

providers.name: Rwazi
providers.description: Rwazi is a hyper-local market intelligence and Decision AI platform whose product, Sena, combines a company's internal business data with real-world consumer signals from 190+ countries — who is buying what, for how much, from where, when, and why — using consumer activity data, computer vision, zero-party data collection, and 250+ third-party integrations to inform marketing, sales, product, strategy, and growth decisions. Rwazi is a Techstars-backed company added to the API Evangelist network. This profile has been enriched from public web sources; at the time of enrichment Rwazi published no self-service developer API, OpenAPI, or public API reference — onboarding is enterprise, demo-driven, and account-based.

providers.name: Sabbar
providers.description: Sabbar is a leading local employment and recruitment platform in Saudi Arabia that connects job seekers with employers across many sectors. Job seekers search listings, build a free CV, and apply to roles, while employers use subscription-based recruitment packages and candidate matching. The platform reports more than 12,000 companies and over 1 million Saudi and non-Saudi job seekers, with iOS and Android mobile apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Safari Ai
providers.description: Safari AI is a vision-AI company for physical operations, turning an organization's existing camera networks into an automated operational system. Its Action Center platform measures on-site activity (people counts and footfall, occupancy, heatmapping, throughput, queue wait time, dwell time, vehicle counts, and license-plate recognition), raises alerts, recommends and dispatches actions, and attributes outcomes — measurement to action in under 60 seconds. Safari AI serves theme parks and cultural attractions, stadiums and arenas, QSR and drive-thrus, retail and shopping malls, parking, and logistics. Backed by General Catalyst, it exposes no public developer API; customers consume results through a hosted real-time dashboard (Grafana) rather than a self-serve API surface. This profile was surfaced from the VC portfolio graph and enriched from the company's public site.

providers.name: Safqah Holdings Limited
providers.description: Safqah Holdings Limited operates Safqah (Safqah Capital / Safqah Financial), a Saudi Arabian fintech platform headquartered in the Al-Malqa district of Riyadh and regulated by the Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA). Safqah provides Sharia-compliant, debt-based real estate investment opportunities that let qualified individual and institutional investors fund real estate development deals starting from 1,000 SAR, alongside a financing arm that offers land acquisition, residential development, commercial development, raw land, and bridge financing to real estate developers. Investors track deal performance through periodic reporting and live project camera feeds. The platform is a consumer- and investor-facing web application with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Santa Catarina Open Data
providers.description: Santa Catarina Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Brazil running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 112 datasets.

providers.name: Saysh
providers.description: Saysh is a direct-to-consumer athletic footwear and apparel brand founded by Olympic champion sprinter Allyson Felix, designing sneakers engineered specifically for women's biomechanics under the banner "Women Deserve Better." Its lineup spans performance running shoes (the Felix Runner and Evelyn Runner) and the everyday Saysh One, plus apparel, accessories, and the Saysh+ Run Club membership. The saysh.com storefront runs on Shopify, so customer-facing commerce is served through the Shopify platform rather than a first-party Saysh developer API; no public Saysh API program, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal were found. Backed by Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Sciket
providers.description: Sciket (科研市集, operated by STAREK Scientific / 勢得科研股份有限公司) is Taiwan's specialized online marketplace for scientific research and technology procurement.
